title: Falcons average NFL-high 40.0 points with Michael Penix, after NFL-low 8.0 without him
summary: Falcons safety Jessie Bates wasn't exaggerating when he said they're a different team with Michael Penix.
full_text: Falcons safety Jessie Bates wasn't exaggerating when he said they're a different team with Michael Penix . After starting the season 0-2, the Falcons are 2-0 since Penix became the starter in Week 3. But even that doesn't fully display how different things have been with Penix. On average, NFL teams are scoring 23.1 points per game this season. If we considered the Falcons two different teams, with Penix and without him, the version with Penix would rank first in the NFL with an average of 40.0 points per game — more than a touchdown better than the No. 1, the Bills, who average 31.8 points per game. Meanwhile, the version of the Falcons without Penix averaged 8.0 points per game. That ranks dead last, more than a field goal worse than the No. 32 Dolphins, who are averaging 11.5 points per game. Among the 42 quarterbacks who have thrown at least 15 passes this season, Penix ranks fifth with a 113.1 passer rating. The two Falcons quarterbacks who played before Penix are dead last: Rush ranks 41st with a 42.5 passer rating, and Jack Strand ranks 42nd with a 35.1 passer rating. How much better is Penix at avoiding pressure than Rush and Strand? Rush was sacked five times while throwing 39 passes. Strand was sacked twice while throwing 15 passes. Penix has been sacked only once while throwing 45 passes, and Penix played most of the second game after the Falcons lost starting left tackle Jake Matthews to an injury. The effect of Penix on his teammates is notable. In two games with Penix, Falcons running back Bijan Robinson has rushed for 339 yards and four touchdowns. In two games without Penix, Robinson rushed for 155 yards and no touchdowns. Backup running back Brian Robinson has 24 carries for 112 yards and four touchdowns with Penix. He had 20 carries for 82 yards and no touchdowns without Penix. The Falcons' top receiver, Drake London, has 14 catches for 290 yards in two games with Penix. London had six catches for 80 yards in two games without Penix. That stats are a remarkable display of just how well Penix is playing — and just how poorly Rush and Strand played. With a different quarterback, the Falcons are a completely different team.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Klint Kubiak: I put Raiders' problems running the ball on myself
summary: The Raiders opened the season with 130 rushing yards in a win over the Dolphins and that was a welcome development after the team finished dead last in rushing during the 2025 season.
full_text: The Raiders opened the season with 130 rushing yards in a win over the Dolphins and that was a welcome development after the team finished dead last in rushing during the 2025 season. The past three weeks have suggested that might have had more to do with the opponent than anything the Raiders have done to change their scheme or personnel. They've run for 242 yards in those games, which isn't as bad as they were last season but it's also not where head coach Klint Kubiak would like things to be in Las Vegas. Among the issues is that Raiders backs Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington are averaging just 1.8 yards before contact and Kubiak said he isn't looking at anyone else when it comes to finding ways to "scheme them up better." “I put it on myself ," Kubiak said on Monday. "I got to do a lot better job of putting us in better position. We’ve got solid backs, we’ve got a solid offensive line. Myself and the coaching staff, there’s plenty of things we can do better for our players.” A 3-0 start helped downplay any concerns about the way the Raiders have been playing, but Sunday's loss to the Chiefs put the lagging run game in greater focus and it will continue to be one if a three-game run against the Patriots, Bills and Rams does not go well for Kubiak's side.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tyler Shough: Fans are understandably upset, I'd boo too
summary: Monday night's game in New Orleans started with a tribute to a storybook night in Saints history, but there was no happily ever after once the game got underway.
full_text: Monday night's game in New Orleans started with a tribute to a storybook night in Saints history, but there was no happily ever after once the game got underway. Falcons running back Bijan Robinson broke loose for a 59-yard touchdown a few plays into the game that took some life out of the Superdome crowd. The Saints weren't able to stop the bleeding and the Falcons rolled to a 45-24 win that left the Superdome crowd feeling much differently than they did at the outset. Cheers for the 20th anniversary of the Saints' return to New Orleans after Hurricane Katrina were replaced by cascades of boos until enough Saints fans left the building that Falcons supporters had run of the place. The loss dropped the Saints to 1-3 and quarterback Tyler Shough could not take any issue with the way that the home crowd responded to the effort. "Fans understandably are upset ," Shough said. "We had some opportunities that we didn't take advantage of and you're playing the Falcons and you lose like that? I mean, I'd boo, too. That sucks. We want to get everybody going. It’s part of it. You have to have the energy of the crowd and we’re gonna need them next week too against a really good team. That’s the best part about New Orleans. You feel it and we feel it too, and we’re gonna keep going." A 4-1 close to last season with Shough playing well led to hopes of a turnaround for a team that hasn't been to the playoffs since 2020, but the Saints have allowed the most points in the league through four weeks. They have two of their next three games at home before a bye week and they'll need to plug a lot of leaks in order to ensure no one will be considering a return to paper bags on heads later in this year's home schedule.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jessie Bates: We're a different team with Michael Penix in the lineup
summary: During the first two weeks of the 2026 season, the Falcons looked like one of the worst teams in the NFL.
full_text: During the first two weeks of the 2026 season, the Falcons looked like one of the worst teams in the NFL. The last two weeks have been much different. A 35-14 win in Green Bay in Week 3 was followed by Monday night's 45-24 rout of the Saints in New Orleans and it's not hard to notice the biggest difference in the team over the last two games. Quarterback Michael Penix was cleared to return from last season's torn ACL and he's been at the helm of their offensive explosion. Penix is 33-of-45 for 479 yards and two touchdowns in the two wins and combining accuracy with an ability to pick up big chunks of yardage every time the ball is in the air has opened the door for the Falcons to run wild. Bijan Robinson has run for 339 yards and four touchdowns while Brian Robinson has 117 yards to go with four more scores in the back-to-back wins. The change in offense has made a strong impression on safety Jessie Bates. "We just want to show the world who we can be," Bates said, via Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com. "The first two weeks were not up to our standards. Obviously, when you got [Penix] back there dealing, it's a whole different team. So, we're just excited to continue to go with this." The Falcons had a strong collection of skill position players to open the season, but poor quarterback play didn't allow them to take advantage of that talent. The shift with Penix has been clear and it's opened the door to a much brighter future in Atlanta.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jim Harbaugh not happy with reporter for "more insult than question" about Justin Herbert
summary: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh was not happy with a reporter's line of questioning about quarterback Justin Herbert and the Chargers' inability to build a successful offense around him amid the team's 0-4 start.
full_text: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh was not happy with a reporter's line of questioning about quarterback Justin Herbert and the Chargers' inability to build a successful offense around him amid the team's 0-4 start. At his Monday press conference, Harbaugh responded to a question from reporter Kris Rhim of ESPN by saying Rhim had delivered an insult, not asked a question. Harbaugh had previously praised Herbert for how tough he was continuing to play on Sunday after taking some hard hits, and Rhim questioned why the Chargers' offense hasn't been able to better protect Herbert so he doesn't take so many hard hits. That led to this exchange : Rhim: "Jim, when you talk about he's a warrior, he's gritty, part of that is just him taking a ruthless beating because of, I don't know if it's the group in front of him, his protection, what's going on, but when you came here, your charge was to get him protected. Mike's [McDaniel] charge was to make sure he didn't have to be a superhero, but 2.5 years later, like you said, he still has to be a superhero for you guys to have a chance to win the game. Why is that?" Harbaugh: "Yeah, that just sounds more like an insult than it does a question, but if that's the way you look at it. I'm saying that it's the kind of competitor that he is where I've never seen him flinch. I've never seen him rattled. He's an amazing inspiration and that's what we do. We all feed off of that. I know the entire team does. And you ask me what gives me optimism, what gives me hope with this football team, because I see that throughout the entire team. And yeah, we attack, we improve, can't improve everything all at once, but we can improve one thing at a time, all the time. And that's what this team is doing." Rhim: "It wasn't insult. I'm just asking if it's the third season now and he's still among the most pressured and hit quarterbacks. I'm just asking you why that is?" Harbaugh: "I think I answered your question. I can answer it the same way." Rhim: "You can answer it the same way, but I don't think you answered it." Harbaugh: "I think I did." Despite Herbert having his worst statistical season this year, Harbaugh has not wavered in his belief that Herbert is a great quarterback. It's fair to ask why the Chargers can't do more to protect such a great asset, and why this year's Chargers have so far not won any games with him. Even if Harbaugh doesn't like to hear it.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Kellen Moore: Really disappointing how Saints played on an incredible night in New Orleans
summary: On the 20th anniversary of the Saints' return to New Orleans following Hurricane Katrina, it was the Falcons who had a big game.
full_text: The NFL scheduled the Saints to host the Falcons on Monday night to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the Superdome's reopening after Hurricane Katrina. It was a big night in New Orleans, and the Saints did not match the fans' energy. Saints head coach Kellen Moore said after the 45-24 loss that the team came out flat despite the excitement of the moment. "Really disappointing game for us," Moore said. "The dome was an incredible night, incredible energy. I did a poor job preparing our football team. Didn't coach well enough, didn't play well enough. It wasn't good enough. We're at where we're at, a 1-3 football team with some good moments but not enough consistent football to be where we ultimately want to be. We've got a lot of work to do." Moore said he addressed the historical significance of the game with his team and thought they bought into this being a particularly big game. But when it was time to put it all together, they didn't. "We talked about it at the beginning of the week, the guys were fired up," Moore said. "I thought there was good energy, we just didn't execute well enough." The Saints saw the nationally televised, much-discussed game as a big opportunity to show what kind of team they are, and they didn't show much. "Those are big-time opportunities," Moore said. "It's just disappointing for us and I know there's frustration for everyone."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Monday Night Football: Falcons run over Saints 45-24 to ruin New Orleans' celebration
summary: Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson combined for 207 rushing yards and five touchdowns.
full_text: The Saints will always have the Hurricane Katrina game on Sept. 25, 2006. Steve Gleason's block of a Falcons' punt is commemorated in a statue outside the Superdome titled "Rebirth." But Monday night belonged to the Falcons. Atlanta ruined New Orleans' "Domecoming" celebration, routing the Saints 45-24. The Superdome cleared out in the second half as the Falcons ran over the Saints, with 205 of their 420 yards coming on the ground. Bijan Robinson had 19 carries for 145 yards and two touchdowns, and Brian Robinson added 14 carries for 62 yards and three touchdowns. Bijan Robinson went 59 yards for a touchdown on the third play from scrimmage, a foreshadowing of how the night was going to go. The Falcons led 14-0 at the end of the first quarter and 24-7 at halftime before continuing to pour on the points in the second half. The Falcons scored the fewest points in the NFL the first two weeks, with 16. In the past two games, since quarterback Michael Penix returned, the Falcons have an NFL-leading 80 points. The Falcons are 2-2 and tied with the Panthers atop the NFC South. The Saints are 1-3. Penix went 15-of-20 for 223 yards and a touchdown, which was a 31-yard throw to Jahan Dotson. Drake London caught five passes for 96 yards and Dotson had two for 54. Alvin Kamara turned back time in scoring two of the Saints' touchdowns on runs of 3 and 5 yards. He tied Deuce McAllister's franchise record for most multiple-rushing touchdown games with his 14th. Late in the fourth quarter, with the game out of reach, Devaughn Vele made one of the best catches of the season. He got both feet down for a 3-yard touchdown with 1:13 left. Tyler Shough went 30-of-48 for 286 yards and a touchdown despite banging up his left hand. Chris Olave caught eight passes for 116 yards before taking a hard hit on his knee late in the game. The only bad news for the Falcons was the loss of edge rusher Za'Darius Smith (concussion) and left tackle Jake Matthews (groin). They left in the first half with their injuries and now have a short week to try to get back for the Ravens on Sunday Night Football.
author: Charean Williams

title: Seahawks had been planning to use Rashid Shaheed at tailback since training camp
summary: With the Seahawks thin at running back on Sunday, they deployed receiver Rashid Shaheed in the backfield.
full_text: With the Seahawks thin at running back on Sunday, they deployed receiver Rashid Shaheed in the backfield. He got two carries for 33 yards, including a 28-yard touchdown run. It wasn't something the Seahawks cooked up this week, with Jadarian Price on injured reserve and Zach Charbonnet still not all the way back from a torn ACL suffered in January. “We’ve had that in all [training] camp," coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Monday. "This isn’t a quote from [offensive coordinator Brian] Fleury, but felt like it was appropriate because of [Price] going down, he gave us some speed. That was cool.” Indeed it was. Shaheed's scoring play highlighted his speed and agility in the broken field. He's a player who can make things happen with the ball in his hands. The more the Seahawks can make that happen, the better off they'll be. Through four games in 2026, Shaheed has seven catches for 73 yards and three carries for 37 yards, plus Sunday's touchdown. He has returned nine punts for 79 yards and 10 kickoffs for 273 yards. That's fine. But he needs to get the ball more often. With the Seahawks adding veteran running back Joe Mixon to the practice squad and signing running back Robert Henry Jr. from the Commanders' practice squad, Shaheed may not be part of the running game on Sunday against the 49ers — even if he should be.
author: Mike Florio

title: LT Jake Matthews ruled out as Falcons take 31-7 lead
summary: Falcons left tackle Jake Matthews will not return tonight.
full_text: Falcons left tackle Jake Matthews will not return tonight. The Falcons have ruled him out. Now, the question becomes: Will his groin injury keep him out of Sunday night's game against the Ravens on a short week? Matthews has started 199 games in a row, the longest active streak in the NFL. He made his 200th career start on Monday night but left in the first quarter. The Falcons are rolling in the third quarter, holding a 31-10 lead after Brian Robinson's second rushing touchdown. The Falcons have 173 rushing yards, with Bijan Robinson running for 132 yards and two touchdowns on 16 carries. Brian Robinson has 11 carries for 41 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Marcus Davenport will retire from football
summary: Veteran pass rusher Marcus Davenport didn't request his release from the Bears' practice squad so that he could sign with another team's practice squad.
full_text: ' Veteran pass rusher Marcus Davenport didn't request his release from the Bears' practice squad so that he could sign with another team's practice squad. Via NFL Network, the 30-year-old Davenport will retire. He was a first-round pick of the Saints in 2018 (14th overall). He spent five years in New Orleans, one in Minnesota, and two in Detroit before joining the Bears. Davenport has 78 regular-season appearances with 43 starts. He hasn't played much since leaving the Saints — 19 regular-season games and 11 starts in four seasons. He also has four postseason appearances and one start, all of which came with the Saints. Davenport has 25.0 career sacks, with a career-high of 9.0 in 2021.
author: Mike Florio

title: Monday Night Football: Bijan Robinson has Falcons leading 24-7 at halftime
summary: Robinson has 12 carries for 103 yards and two touchdowns.
full_text: Saints fans were ready to party like it's 2006. Bijan Robinson, though, has reigned over their parade. The Falcons running back has 12 carries for 103 yards and two touchdowns, and Atlanta leads 24-7 at halftime. The pregame celebration had barely cleared the field from their "Domecoming" when Robinson broke a 59-yard touchdown run. It came on the third play from scrimmage. He later added a 4-yard touchdown run. The Falcons scored on four of their seven first-half possessions, and they outgained the Saints 255 to 147 yards. Brian Robinson scored the Falcons' third touchdown on a 4-yard run, and he has nine carries for 35 yards. Michael Penix has completed 10 of 15 passes for 125 yards, with Drake London catching four for 82. Saints quarterback Tyler Shough is 12-of-19 for 139 yards, with Chris Olave catching three for 62. The team's only touchdown came on Alvin Kamara's 3-yard run. The Saints, though, have only 15 yards rushing on seven carries.
author: Charean Williams

title: Eagles OL Cam Jurgens enters concussion protocol
summary: Eagles left guard Cam Jurgens self-reported concussion symptoms on Monday and has entered concussion protocol, Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports.
full_text: Eagles left guard Cam Jurgens self-reported concussion symptoms on Monday and has entered concussion protocol, Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports. Jurgens played all 61 snaps in the loss to the Rams on Sunday. Willie Lampkin likely will play against the Jaguars in London if Jurgens can't go. The Friday overseas flight could complicate Jurgens' chances of clearing protocol in time to play. Jurgens moved from center to left guard after Landon Dickerson went on injured reserve with a bone bruise in his knee. Dickerson was injured in the season opener. Drew Kendall replaced Jurgens at center. Jurgens, though, has struggled at guard, prompting a question to coach Nick Sirianni on Monday about whether the Eagles are considering benching Jurgens. “No, I’m pleased with where Cam is ,” Sirianni said, via Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia. “Again, with everybody, obviously we didn't put out there the product that we want to put out there offensively yesterday, and then also combine that with a loss. There's going to be plays he wants back, but there's good moments also. “I think that's the consistency of everybody, from our coaches to our players, has to be the thing that continues to rise. That's Cam; that's everybody. But Cam is definitely doing good things and like us all, got to be more consistent at times as well."
author: Charean Williams

title: Falcons LT Jake Matthews is questionable with groin injury
summary: Falcons left tackle Jake Matthews made his 199th consecutive start on Monday night.
full_text: Falcons left tackle Jake Matthews made his 199th consecutive start on Monday night. But he watched the Falcons' 10-play, 65-yard scoring drive from the sideline. Matthews left in the first quarter with a groin injury that has him questionable to return. He does not look as if he will. Matthews' starting streak is the longest active streak in the NFL. Michael Jerrell has replaced Matthews, and Jerrell helped Brian Robinson score on a 4-yard run. The Falcons lead 21-7. The Falcons have ruled out pass rusher Za'Darius Smith with a concussion. Smith took a knee to the head from a teammate early in the first quarter.
author: Charean Williams

title: Alvin Kamara gets Saints on the scoreboard
summary: The Saints needed a touchdown.
full_text: The Saints needed a touchdown. They got a touchdown. Running back Alvin Kamara scored on a 3-yard run, pulling the Saints to within 14-7 of the Falcons. It was his first rushing touchdown of the season and the 62nd of his career. The Saints started their fourth drive from their own 46 after Falcons cornerback Billy Bowman Jr. was penalized for unnecessary roughness on the kickoff. Tyler Shough then hit Chris Olave for 44 yards to the Atlanta 10 on the first play from scrimmage on the drive. Shough has completed 7 of 10 passes for 100 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bijan Robinson's second TD gives Falcons 14-0 lead
summary: Bijan Robinson has a career-high 78 yards in the first quarter.
full_text: Bijan Robinson has a career-high 78 yards in the first quarter. He also has two touchdowns. The Falcons have a 14-0 lead. Saints running back Kendre Miller fumbled at his own 22, when cornerback C.J. Henderson punched it out. Officials did not rule a fumble on the field, forcing the Falcons to challenge. Replay reversed it to a fumble. The Falcons scored five plays later on Robinson's 4-yard run. The Saints were called for two defensive holding penalties in the drive, including Kool-Aid McKinstry's on Jahan Dotson on fourth-and-4 at the New Orleans 8. Robinson had seven carries in the first quarter, and Michael Penix completed 3 of 6 passes for 30 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley is "week to week" with hamstring injury
summary: The Eagles have a problem at running back.
full_text: The Eagles have a problem at running back. Starting tailback Saquon Barkley suffered a hamstring injury on his first and only carry of Sunday's loss to the Rams. He didn't return. Via NFL Network, Barkley is " week-to-week ." Which is worse than "day-to-day," and implies he'll miss at least one week. There has been no reporting on the degree of the hamstring strain. Whatever the extent of the damage, it's an injury that takes time to heal. Time is of the essence for the Eagles. They play the Jaguars in London on Sunday. And Tank Bigsby is out with core muscle surgery. That leaves Ryan Shipley as the starter, barring a roster move. Jaydon Blue, Dameon Pierce, and Carson Steele are on the practice squad. A trade is possible, in theory. Desperation, however, will drive up the price. The Eagles also could scour the other practice squads in search of someone who may want to make the jump to Philly and fill in while Barkley is out.
author: Mike Florio

title: Falcons DE Za'Darius Smith questionable to return after being kneed in the head
summary: Falcons defensive end Za'Darius Smith took a knee to the head with 12:57 left in the first quarter.
full_text: Falcons defensive end Za'Darius Smith took a knee to the head with 12:57 left in the first quarter. He remained on the ground, and after the Falcons' medical personnel checked him out, they called for a cart. Smith, though, waved it off and walked off the field. Smith is in the training room being evaluated for a concussion and a neck injury and is questionable to return. He was blocked to the ground by Saints left tackle Asim Richards, and while lying on the ground, Falcons defensive end Brandon Dorlus' left knee connected with Smith's helmet. Smith leads the team with 2.5 sacks. Meanwhile, Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts did not start and has played only one snap in two series. The team told ESPN sideline reporter Laura Rutledge that Pitts is healthy. Charlie Woerner, Nick Muse and Austin Hooper have played more snaps and Pitts so far.
author: Charean Williams

title: Matt LaFleur explains his reason for not taking the bait from Ben Johnson
summary: Bears coach Ben Johnson has no qualms about making his disdain for the Packers known.
full_text: ' Bears coach Ben Johnson has no qualms about making his disdain for the Packers known. Green Bay coach Matt LaFleur takes a different approach to the situation. LaFleur explained his decision not to take Ben Johnson's bait to reporters on Monday. “Because this game is about players and so we’ll keep it about the players ," LaFleur said, via Matt Schneidman of The Athletic . "I’m not the one out there they’re playing. . . . Don’t get me wrong. I love the rivalry. It’s awesome. It’s great. It’s intense. You can feel it on gameday. You can feel it throughout the course of the week and also the significance, I mean, they’re the defending [NFC] North champions. So what a great opportunity, great challenge for us in our home stadium to play against the defending champs.” For Johnson's part, he sent a clear message to his players about Sunday's game at Lambeau Field. "He wants to beat them really bad like everyone else in the room, like every Chicago fan. Beat them real bad, and make them quit ," receiver Luther Burden III said, via Cassie Carlson of Fox32. Johnson's anti-Green Bay antics have included declaring in the locker room after a playoff win, "Fuck the Packers! Fuck them!" "The Bears and the Packers, they should not like each othe r," Johnson said in a Scouting Combine-week appearance on PFT Live . "I think it's as simple as that. And I think that's gonna make this rivalry, this game, something that people are going to watch here going forward." For fans, that's absolutely true. Players and coaches are interchangeable. Coaches can be nomads, hopping from job to job regardless of where the job may be. And they generally refrain from making things personal because today's enemy could be tomorrow's employer. Johnson, to his credit, isn't willing to play the game. He earned his stripes with the Packers as a rival (Johnson and the Lions spoiled Aaron Rodgers's last game in Green Bay), and he's in position to be the coach of the Bears for a long time. He could become as beloved as Mike Ditka, in time. He's off to a good start. In part because he says what most Bears fans believe about the Packers. As to this weekend's game, which was moved out of the higher-profile 4:25 p.m. ET window for 1:00 p.m. ET, Johnson surely will say, privately and/or publicly, that the flex didn't happen because of the Bears but because (as Johnson is more likely to say privately but who knows?), "The Packers suck."
author: Mike Florio

title: Monday Night Football: Saints TE Noah Fant is inactive; Falcons LB Samson Ebukam will play
summary: The Saints will not have tight end Noah Fant for Monday Night Football.
full_text: The Saints will not have tight end Noah Fant for Monday Night Football. Fant is among the team's inactives. He was questionable to play with an abdominal injury. Rookie Oscar Delp should see more snaps behind starter Juwan Johnson. The Saints' other inactives are quarterback Zach Wilson, cornerback Decamerion Richardson (shoulder), edge rusher Anfernee Jennings (knee), defensive lineman Christen Miller (toe), linebacker Kaden Elliss (calf) and edge rusher Carl Granderson (ankle). Wilson is the emergency third quarterback. The Falcons will have linebacker Divine Deablo and edge rusher Samson Ebukam. Both were questionable with hamstring injuries. The Falcons' inactives are quarterback Cooper Rush, quarterback Jack Strand, offensive tackle Ethan Onianwa, defensive lineman Jared Ivey, cornerback Robert Longerbeam and cornerback Malcolm DeWalt IV. Rush will serve as the emergency third quarterback.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bijan Robinson puts a damper on Saints' celebration with 59-yard TD run
summary: The Saints are celebrating the 20th anniversary of their Hurricane Katrina return tonight.
full_text: The Saints had barely finished celebrating the 20th anniversary of their emotional post-Katrina return when Bijan Robinson crashed the party. The Falcons running back took the air out of the "Domecoming" game with a 59-yard touchdown run. He followed the hole created by left tackle Jake Matthews on Chase Young and went untouched down the left sideline. Michael Penix completed passes of 12 and 9 yards before Robinson's jaunt. The Falcons lead 7-0 only 1 minute, 26 seconds into Monday Night Football.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bears release DL Marcus Davenport from practice squad at his request
summary: The Bears released veteran defensive end Marcus Davenport from the practice squad at his request, according to multiple reports.
full_text: ' The Bears released veteran defensive end Marcus Davenport from the practice squad at his request, according to multiple reports. He made his season debut on Sunday and totaled one tackle in 12 snaps in the victory over the Jets. Davenport, a 2018 first-round pick of the Saints, signed with the Bears in August. It reunited him with his former Saints defensive coordinator Dennis Allen, who is now the Bears defensive coordinator. Davenport has registered only 24 tackles and 3.5 sacks in 15 games since 2023. Bears second-year defensive lineman Shemar Turner could be close to returning from reserve/PUP. He is working his way back from a torn ACL that ended his rookie season last October.
author: Charean Williams

title: Chargers LT Rashawn Slater is an IR candidate as he will "miss some time"
summary: The Chargers won't have left tackle Rashawn Slater for "some time," coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday.
full_text: The Chargers won't have left tackle Rashawn Slater for "some time," coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday. Harbaugh confirmed Slater has a high-ankle sprain in his right foot. Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Slater is expected to miss 4-6 weeks, making the two-time Pro Bowler an injured- reserve candidate. Harbaugh, though, said the Chargers are still evaluating the prospect of IR. Slater missed all of the 2025 season with a torn patellar tendon and a torn biceps took him out of most of the 2022 season. Right tackle Joe Alt is still undergoing evaluation of a neck injury, Harbaugh said. If Alt can play, the Chargers could move him to left tackle and have rookie Travis Burke play right tackle. Safety Derwin James (hamstring) is week-to-week, and wide receiver Ladd McConkey (foot) and cornerback Donte Jackson (hamstring) are day to day. Tight end Charlie Kolar (forearm), defensive tackle Dalvin Tomlinson (hamstring), wide receiver Brenen Thompson and left guard Kayode Awosika (fibula) are making good progress.
author: Charean Williams

title: Free agent RB Joe Mixon to join Seahawks' practice squad
summary: The Seahawks are signing running back Joe Mixon to their practice squad.
full_text: The Seahawks are signing running back Joe Mixon to their practice squad. Coach Mike Macdonald confirmed the Seahawks worked out Mixon on Monday and are "going through the process" of getting him on the practice squad. The Seahawks placed Jadarian Price on injured reserve last week, and Zach Charbonnet had his 21-day return-to-practice window opened last week after an ACL tear in the playoffs ended his 2025 season. George Holani, Emanuel Wilson and Velus Jones Jr. are the running backs on the active roster. Mixon has not played since January 2025, missing all of last season with a foot injury. The Texans released him in March. In 2024, Mixon rushed for 1,016 yards and 11 touchdowns, earning Pro Bowl honors in his first season with the Texans. A second-round pick of the Bengals in 2017, Mixon has 7,428 rushing yards and five 1,000-yard seasons. He spent his first seven seasons with the Bengals.
author: Charean Williams

title: Sean McVay: Rams coaches will learn from incident with Eagles fans
summary: Some of the Rams assistant coaches did not win gracefully on Sunday.
full_text: Some of the Rams assistant coaches did not win gracefully on Sunday. Videos on social media show coaches in the team's booth taunting Eagles fans, with one assistant banging on a window in the booth before gesturing at them. A cup and a water bottle are thrown from the stands at the glass windows of the booth in retaliation. Rams head coach Sean McVay said he and his assistants have discussed the incident. " We’ll be better in those situations," McVay said, via Sarah Barshop of ESPN. The Rams rallied for a 24-20 victory against the Eagles, scoring two touchdowns in the final 3:59. The Eagles had a 97.4 percent chance of winning with 8 minutes, 17 seconds left. McVay said he understands the excitement and emotion, explaining he was in a similar situation while with Washington calling plays in Philadelphia. "We'll learn from that," McVay said. "We'll be better. Those fans are really into it, but I know that we want to make sure that we're representing the class and just the calm steadiness that we want to have while also being emotionally into it. And there's ways that we can have that reflected. "We did talk about it, and that won't be an issue moving forward."
author: Charean Williams

title: Mike McCarthy, Aaron Rodgers talked "numerous times" after Thursday night's heated exchange
summary: Week 4 began with Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and coach Mike McCarthy exchanging unpleasantries for all the world to see, and hear.
full_text: Week 4 began with Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and coach Mike McCarthy exchanging unpleasantries for all the world to see, and hear. Rodgers looked to McCarthy while waiting for a play call. A Prime Video microphone captured Rodgers angrily yelling, “ What the fuck? Call it!” McCarthy was then seen mouthing his response: “Fucking asshole.” After the game, McCarthy was asked about the interaction ; Rodgers was not. On Monday, the situation came up multiple times again during a McCarthy press conference in advance of the Week 5 game against the Colts. "I wouldn't classify it as normal," McCarthy said of the interaction, "but I think the reality of it is, you know, it's a 20-year relationship. I think the fact that we were able to sit and talk numerous times, you know, over the weekend, about that and a number of things. "As I stated, I'm — hopefully, not to put any pressure on my daughter — I'm getting to grandfather age. You know, I don't want to be saying those type of words. But it's an emotional, competitive environment. I think it's something that we can definitely learn from." McCarthy also was asked whether the game broadcasts have become too intrusive. "Your question's about 15 years too late," McCarthy said. Earlier in the press conference, McCarthy said he had told the team on Thursday morning that it would be important to play the Browns with "more emotion." He wanted it, and he got it. "With that comes the discipline of it," McCarthy said. "So I think those are opportunities for growth. But I'd much rather have too much energy than not enough." Amen to that. It's always easier to try to control enthusiasm than to create it when it's not there. On Thursday night, however, it became a little too unbridled. Come Wednesday, Rodgers will have a chance to respond. Unless he decides to call McAfee's show on Tuesday and air any grievances he may have about the incident, how it was covered by the media, and anything else he chooses to publicly gripe about.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bills CB Maxwell Hairston says he's got to be better in every way
summary: The Bills are not benching cornerback Maxwell Hairston, who has struggled this season.
full_text: The Bills are not benching cornerback Maxwell Hairston, who has struggled this season. Bills coach Joe Brady is already manifesting a bounce-back game for Hairston on Monday Night Football in Week 5. "Max Hairston's going to make a play this week, and you guys are going to be asking me questions like 'Oh man, what was it like seeing him respond from the previous game?'" Brady said, via Nick Suss of ESPN. Hairston, a first-round pick in 2025, was beaten by Patriots receiver Romeo Doubs for two touchdowns in one-on-one coverage in a 29-26 loss to New England. Hairston would not speak to the media after the game, violating the NFL's media access policy. On Monday, Hairston held an impromptu news conference to apologize. " Feeling very emotional ," Hairston said. "I let my emotions get the best of me, and I didn't want to say something I might have regretted. You live and you learn. . . . That's kind of immature, and I'm better than that. So I wanted to get that out of the way." The Bills rank 27th in passing yards allowed, and only the Lions are allowing more first downs. Hairston, though, has drawn the most criticism for his lackluster effort at times. He appeared to have an angle on Patriots tight end Hunter Henry on third-and-10, but didn't go full speed and Henry picked up the first down, denying Josh Allen and the offense another chance with the ball. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said Hairston's effort clearly wasn't good enough. Hairston addressed his play and his allowing his emotions to get the best of him. "I have to be in control of my emotions within the game," Hairston said. "It comes with learning, experiencing certain stuff. I have to be better in that aspect."
author: Charean Williams

title: Cardinals left tackle Paris Johnson out for season with torn biceps
summary: The Cowboys have lost their starting left tackle for the season.
full_text: ' The Cowboys have lost their starting left tackle for the season. Paris Johnson suffered a torn biceps and will miss the rest of the season, coach Mike LaFleur announced today. "I feel for him, obviously," LaFleur said. "It sucks. It sucks for him, first and foremost, it sucks for the Arizona Cardinals, our offense, this team. But NFL football, here we are in October, show goes on." Johnson stayed in the game and played through the injury on Sunday against the Giants, but testing today revealed that it was significant. The Cardinals selected Johnson with the sixth overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft and he's been their starting left tackle since. The Cardinals picked up Johnson's fifth-year option and he is due a guaranteed salary of $19.7 million in 2027.
author: Michael David Smith

title: WR CeeDee Lamb (thigh), CB Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) estimated as full participants

author: Charean Williams

title: Jeremiyah Love says coaches are managing the workload though "longest year of my life"
summary: For first-year players, a 17-game season means eventually hitting the so-called rookie wall.
full_text: ' For first-year players, a 17-game season means eventually hitting the so-called rookie wall. Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love is preparing for that reality. His postgame comments from Sunday suggest it has possibly already happened. Love tiptoed around the question of whether the ankle he sprained in the preseason is still bothering him. On multiple occasions during his session with reporters after the 36-24 loss to the Giants, Love said it isn't. Still, his full remarks (which lasted less than five minutes) oozed with the idea that he's already worn down after only four regular-season games. "Not really bothering me," he said when asked about the ankle, "kind of just a managing because, you know, we got a long season. Coaches don't want to overload me, so not necessarily, like, bothering me to the point where I can't play, because I can go out there and play regardless of whether it's bothering me, like, I gotta go out there and put something on my opportunity to put us in the best position to have success, but it . . . it was all right. It was all right." While he understands the importance of pacing himself, he doesn't like having his workload managed. "It's frustrating because, you know, I'm the type of guy that's going to, you know, do anything for my team to have success," Love said. "Like, so I'm gonna be out there despite, you know, how I'm feeling, but my coaches care about me. They care about everybody on this team. So they're not gonna put you out there if you're not in the best position to go out there and, you know, do what you need to do and be yourself. "So it's frustrating for me personally. I'm not frustrated with the coaches. I'm really frustrated with myself because, you know, like, I just want to be good. I want to be 100 percent, you know, and I want to go out there and do what I need to do. I'm not saying I'm not 100 percent, but, like, I'm not where I want to be. Like, I'm not able to go out there and do spectacular plays every single time, or do stuff like that. So I'm just frustrated with myself, not with the coaches, but they're doing a great job of managing me." Is it because of the ankle? "No, it's not really just my ankle," Love said. "It's more of just the whole thing. It's been a long year for me. Like, [my] body sometimes is down. Somebody [is] sometimes tired. So, like, it's just managing those things. Like, coaches know that. Like, this is probably gonna be the longest year of my life. You know, and I just want to manage that workload. So today, you know, just obviously making sure to keep an eye on me, managing me. But I didn't go out there and hurt anything or anything like that. It's just, you know, they're doing what they need to do to keep me up so that I can finish the season." That included playing only 11 snaps in the second half and not being on the field in crunch time. Instead, Tyler Allgeier was in the backfield. "Then again, like I say, like they even put people in the best position have success," Love said. "You know, me going out there, um, feeling like how I feel, like, you know, I would probably just hamper the team if I'm going out there and I'm not feeling like myself. So why not put somebody else out there? It's, you know, that's playing at a better, just physical, like, physically they're playing better. And I accept that, you know. Like, I'm not gonna go out there and I'm honest with my coaches. Like, they asked me, 'Can you go out there and do this, do this, and that?' And I'd be like, 'I feel pretty good, but I think Tyler can, or Bam [Knight] can do — can exert themselves a little bit more. So that's kind of, you know, how it is. Like I said, my coaches care about me. I'm not hurt or anything like that. It's really just managing me." Love had 30 snaps on Sunday. Allgeier had 36. Love finished with 14 carries for 62 yards; Allgeier had eight for 42. Whatever the reason, Love isn't consistently where he'd like to be. It seems that the ankle is still something of an issue, even if he insists it isn't. Officially, it's not the ankle. Although Love was limited throughout the practice week before the regular-season opener against the Chargers, Love has not appeared on the injury report since then.
author: Mike Florio

title: Nick Sirianni: More answers Wednesday on Saquon Barkley's status
summary: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley's status for Week 5's game against the Jaguars in London is up in the air.
full_text: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley's status for Week 5's game against the Jaguars in London is up in the air. Barkley left Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams with a hamstring injury and head coach Nick Sirianni said the team will have a better idea later this week about whether Barkley is going to miss time. "Yeah, we'll see. These guys are going through different things with treatment and all those different things," Sirianni said, via a transcript from the team. "We'll see how everything responds and then have more answers for you probably Wednesday on that stuff. I know he'll do everything he can do to get himself back, and obviously, he's a great player and a great teammate. We always need him on the field." Barkley had two carries for eight yards on Sunday. He also missed most of Week 2 with a stinger and has 36 carries for 182 yards on the season. Tank Bigsby is set for core muscle surgery after getting hurt against the Rams, so the Eagles are going to be shorthanded at running back even if Barkley is able to go this week. Will Shipley is the only healthy back on the 53-man roster.
author: Josh Alper

title: NFL Week 4 lessons: 49ers look like the league's best while Kirk Cousins proves he still has it
summary: The 49ers are rolling behind Shanahan's creativity, Cousins is thriving at age 38 and Dallas has an offense capable of overcoming its defensive flaws
full_text:
Starting at the bottom, five teams entered the NFL's fourth week winless. All five lost. Sorry, Chargers , Dolphins , Buccaneers , Titans and Texans .
As for the five teams that entered the week undefeated, only three still have a zero in the loss column. The Bills still have legitimate defensive issues, and the Raiders just barely ran out of gas late against the Chiefs . As for the three still-undefeated teams, a perfect record hardly means they're perfect overall.
Well, wait. The 49ers are bucking that trend. They're hardly perfect, but they just continue to look like the league's best team. They've crushed the Rams and the Dolphins, beat a better-than-you-think Cardinals team and just beat the Broncos 24-14.
Last week, I said Brock Purdy is playing as well as he ever has . This week? Let's give a little love to his coach.
Kyle Shanahan receives a lot of praise for what he does for his quarterbacks. But how about some of his run game concepts?
Kyle Shanahan is paying homage to Bill Walsh Shift & Motion to a Split Back Pro Set to run Counter Solid with Deebo Samuel👌 pic.twitter.com/oOaQt8GZGo
The 49ers are fifth in rushing success rate this season, up from 21st last year. It's not all Shanahan, of course, but he has done a lot to free up his injury-battered offense. The 49ers are again one of the most motion-heavy teams in the NFL this season, and their 7.3 yards per play with motion is by far the best in the NFL. They used it on the biggest play of the game Sunday against the Broncos.
THERE HE GOES‼️ 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/QSMFNxWe7L
Shanahan is doing this with no De'Zhaun Stribling , Ricky Pearsall , Demarcus Robinson or Christian Kirk . With such a thin receiver corps, Shanahan is using two-back looks on 49% of his plays -- his highest rate since 2018 -- and using three-receiver looks on a career-low 32% of plays. He's willing to innovate and to adapt.
Then there's the protection: The 49ers haven't allowed a single sack through four games, the first time that's happened since the 2005 Colts , led by Peyton Manning . Add it all together, and you get Shanahan at his best.
The Raiders didn't win as Klint Kubiak pledged they would at halftime , but it's hard to come away from their 30-27 loss to the Chiefs anything but impressed, especially with Kirk Cousins .
The box score stats -- 31 for 52, 365 yards, two touchdowns, one interception, zero sacks -- are strong, and if you take away his desperation end-of-game interception, they look even better. But the best number there is the zero sacks, especially considering he was pressured 21 times!
How rare is that? In the last 10 seasons, this is only the third time a player has been pressured at least 21 times and taken zero sacks. The others? Matthew Stafford vs. the Seahawks last year and Josh Allen vs. Washington in 2021. That's it. Two MVP-level players and ... 38-year-old Kirk Cousins, brought in basically to be a placeholder for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza .
I mean, who does this guy think he is? Josh Allen?
Kirk Cousins yesterday: 21 pressures, ZERO sacks. Only two other players in the last 10 years have faced that many pressures in a game and not been sacked once: Matthew Stafford and Josh Allen. Kirko Chainz was hoopin' pic.twitter.com/TVXEoHQtm9
The fact that we're getting this version of Cousins again is absolutely wild.
Kirk Cousins by team (last three teams)
EPA/dropback under pressure
This looked like Cousins at his best. He was never a bad athlete per se, but he's never been an explosive one, either. Rather, he uses his mobility to avoid negatives. He's smart, he's accurate, and he still has enough arm strength to get the ball into tight windows. He leans on play action. He's kind of Sam Darnold-esque, and Kubiak had terrific success with Darnold last year in Seattle. Give credit to both Cousins and Kubiak, a partnership that has produced results better than anyone could have expected.
This was a great find from Anthony Dabbundo of The Ringer : The Cowboys ' offense is averaging 3.39 points per drive, on pace to be the fifth-highest rate since the turn of the century. Only ahead of them are ...
Sunday's 34-30 win over the Texans showed Dallas' offense can bail out a defense that's a complete mess on the back end.
CeeDee Lamb caught 17 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown against what's supposed to be the best defense in the sport, beating everyone who tried to cover him.
CEEDEE LAMB JUST WENT ABSOLUTELY NUCLEAR. 🤯🔥 🎯 17 RECEPTIONS 🚀 189 RECEIVING YARDS 🏈 1 TOUCHDOWN 📈 41.9 PPR POINTS And his 17th catch was the GAME-WINNING TD with 40 seconds left as Dallas completed the comeback, 34–30. 😭🔥 What a performance from CeeDee. ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/Qf1CT0N5Bn
Dallas showed it can be not only explosive -- usually the one spot Houston can get picked on once or twice -- but efficient, too. Nearly 33% of Dallas' plays went for a first down or a touchdown, the third-highest rate the Texans have allowed in the last three seasons.
Dallas is also fourth in red-zone touchdown rate this season, with Javonte Williams (five touchdowns from 3 yards away or closer) pounding the rock there. This offense is cooking with gas.
Zay Flowers was an advanced-stats darling entering the season after posting 2.53 yards per route run in 2025, only behind Puka Nacua and Jaxon Smith-Njigba . The only problem was that the volume wasn't there. Nacua had 166 targets last year, Smith-Njigba 163. Flowers? 118.
Consider that problem solved. Flowers, freed from the hamstring injury he suffered in Week 1 that kept him out in Week 2 and limited him in Week 3, had eight catches for 118 yards and a touchdown on 10 targets. It would have been an even bigger day if Lamar Jackson hadn't gotten hurt and the weather hadn't been so crummy.
So far this season, Flowers averages a truly preposterous 6.29 yards per route run. For comparison's sake, the highest on record (since 2013) is 3.85 by Tyreek Hill in 2023.
Flowers is lining up in the slot on nearly 60% of his snaps, well up from his previous career rate of about 38%. When he's in the slot, he's averaging 7.61(!) yards per route run. New offensive coordinator Declan Doyle is getting the very best of a superbly talented player.
Zay Flowers makes a great catch and walks into the end zone! TENvsBAL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2AiUAWkXMp
The 2024 NFL Draft class is best remembered for the quarterbacks: Caleb Williams , Jayden Daniels and Drake Maye went 1-2-3, and Michael Penix, J.J. McCarthy and Bo Nix all went in the top 12 picks.
But it was also a huge year for wide receivers: Marvin Harrison Jr. , Malik Nabers and Rome Odunze in the top 10, Brian Thomas Jr. , Xavier Worthy , Ricky Pearsall and Xavier Legette also in the first round, and Keon Coleman and Ladd McConkey as the first two picks of the second round. Like the quarterbacks, there have been some hits, some misses, and some "meh"s.
Week 4, though, wasn't a bad one:
We often have more tolerance for players at other positions starting slow than we do for wide receiver, probably because so many wide receivers start fast. But patience can be a good thing, and just because a player doesn't necessarily live up to his draft hype doesn't mean he's useless.
Coleman's a good example of that first point. He's a huge wide receiver and a big-time athlete. He didn't even focus on football full-time until his sophomore year of college; he played basketball and football at Michigan State in 2021-22. He was always going to be a raw prospect, and some early-career mishaps -- missing meetings, late for practice -- didn't help his development.
Sunday, though, he was excellent in his biggest role of the season, putting his absurd downfield traits on display.
How did Keon Coleman make this catch?? 😱 pic.twitter.com/cjEcjGJvGb
JOSH THROWS A ROPE TO KEON COLEMAN AND THE BILLS HAVE THE LEAD @NEvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LMFJVKt5gT
Odunze, meanwhile, starred in the exact way he can thrive in Ben…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Revisiting the Sauce Gardner trade: Jets sitting pretty as blockbuster blowing up in Colts face
summary: Indianapolis pulled off an in-season blockbuster for Gardner last year, but it hasn't been as big a slam dunk as they hoped
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts put the NFL's collective jaw on the floor last November when they made a deadline day blockbuster, landing All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner . Even at the time, it was a hefty investment — shipping two first-rounders and wideout Adonai Mitchell to the Jets — but it was Indy signaling to the league that it was pushing its chips to the middle of the table and announcing it was a playoff force to be reckoned with.
Fast-forward through the remainder of 2025 and the first few weeks of 2026, however, and that deal doesn't look so rosy for GM Chris Ballard and the Colts.
Since Gardner arrived at Lucas Oil Stadium, the Colts are 3-9 overall, which includes a 2-2 start to the regular season this year. While that win-loss mark isn't entirely on his shoulders, Gardner was brought in to help anchor Indy's defense, and the corner hasn't lived up to those expectations. As a team, the Colts are giving up 261.3 passing yards per game this season and 8.1 yards per attempt, which are both the fourth-highest in the NFL. They also have just one interception this year.
With those struggles in mind, let's revisit the trade that sent shockwaves across the league roughly 11 months ago.
In hindsight, this feels massively lopsided in favor of the New York Jets. They used their 2026 first-rounder to select tight end Kenyon Sadiq , who has already flashed huge pass-catching potential through the first month of the year. That includes a 7-catch, 105-yard performance against the Lions in Week 3, where he made a highlight-reel diving touchdown grab.
Meanwhile, Adonai Mitchell, who was looked at as a throw-in piece to the deal at the time, is a legit factor in New York's passing attack when he's been healthy. In his 10 games played for the Jets, Mitchell has caught 33 balls for 424 yards and two touchdowns. That puts him on a 17-game pace of about 56 receptions for 720 receiving yards. That's a solid No. 2 or No. 3 option behind Garrett Wilson and — when healthy — first-round rookie Omar Cooper Jr .
Most importantly, trading away Gardner has helped springboard their rebuild and puts them in a strong position to potentially secure a franchise quarterback in the 2027 NFL Draft . Along with the Colts' pick they acquired in the Gardner trade, the Jets have their own first-round selection and the better of Dallas's or Green Bay's first-round pick, thanks to last year's Quinnen Williams deal. That creates a ton of flexibility in exchange for a player who no longer matched their timeline.
New York also got out of the four-year, $120.4 million contract extension it inked Gardner to in the summer of 2025, so it cleaned up some of its books as well (albeit by carrying some dead money).
Through the first month of the season in 2026, Gardner has not played particularly well, which only amplifies how much this trade is becoming one-sided. As the primary defender in coverage, Gardner is allowing a 53.3 completion rate against, which falls in line with how he played in his four games with Indy last year (he was in and out of the lineup due to a calf injury). However, his passer rating against has skyrocketed to 120.4. That is essentially double what he did in the Colts secondary last year (63.3) and would be a career high if that holds.
Through four games this season, he's given up four completions of 20-plus yards. Already, that's the third-highest of his five-year career, with seven being his career-high in 15 games played for the Jets in 2024.
During Sunday's matchup against the Commanders in London, Gardner was noticeably torched by the combination of seventh-round rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis and wideout Dyami Brown for a 48-yard gain in the third quarter.
Athan Kaliakmanis is letting it FLY. @INDvsWAS on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GytCPyejQH
This season, Gardner is allowing 12.4 yards per pass attempt as the primary defender in coverage. For reference, last year that figure was 5.8 yards per attempt (between the Jets and Colts). It was 7.4 in 2024, 4.4 in 2023 and 4.8 during his rookie campaign in 2022.
That's a tough look for Gardner and the Colts, especially as the team is paying him as one of the five highest-paid corners in the NFL from an AAV standpoint ($30 million per year).
The biggest reason why the Colts made this move for Gardner in the first place was the emergence of Daniel Jones last year. The veteran quarterback arrived in Indy and resurrected his career, while leading the team to a 7-2 record just before the trade deadline. At the time, Indy felt it had finally secured its quarterback of the future and was thrust into true contention, which gave the Colts the conviction to throw multiple firsts at New York to land Gardner.
The hope was that Jones would be the face of the offense, while Gardner could help anchor the secondary and be a key pillar for the organization for years to come. As we noted, however, the floor fell out from under the Colts down the stretch.
They lost their final seven games of the year, and Jones tore his Achilles in Week 13. Jones returned to the field at the start of the 2026 season, but he hasn't looked like the quarterback we saw in the first half of last year. He's thrown more interceptions than touchdowns so far this season, and the thought of him being a foundational piece under center doesn't feel as rock-solid as it once did.
If Indy got this type of play from Jones in the first half of last year, they probably wouldn't have made the deal for Gardner, which basically says it all.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: AFC team grades: Chiefs among four teams in 'A' range, three teams receive 'F' after four games played
summary: The reigning conference-champion Patriots are off to an uneven start
full_text:
The first month of the NFL season can play tricks on us. Last year, through four games, Baker Mayfield was looking like an MVP candidate, and the Buccaneers were 3-1. The Colts were also 3-1, and Daniel Jones was not only putting up even better numbers than Mayfield, but putting up some of the best numbers in the league -- one of the most out-of-nowhere quarterback surprises in recent memory.
On the other side, the Panthers were 1-3 and coming off a 26-10 shellacking courtesy of the Jaguars . The Texans were also 1-3. Both of those teams made the postseason.
Of course, there are plenty of early signs that prove true, too. The Bills and Eagles were the only undefeated teams through four weeks last year, and both were playoff teams. The Saints , Titans and Jets -- all 0-4 at this point last year -- ended up continuing their poor play and landing top-10 picks.
What we can say for sure is that it's early. The standings of today will look very different one month from now, let alone three months from now when the regular season wraps up. Still, with four games down, we've seen enough to hand out first-quarter grades to every team, taking into account not just their record, but how they've looked getting there and how that projects moving forward.
We'll start with the AFC today and move to the NFC on Wednesday.
The Bills came out gangbusters with wins over the Texans in Houston and against the Lions on a short week, totaling 77 points in the win. But the nagging turnover issues hit the last two weeks -- five in a narrow Week 3 win over the Chargers and two more in a Week 4 loss to the Patriots . Familiar issues on defense are rearing their ugly head, too: Buffalo is 30th in defensive EPA per play and 29th in defensive success rate. This looks like a playoff team once again, but unless the same old issues get fixed, it won't be a Super Bowl team.
Recency bias helps the Patriots here, with a Week 4 win over the Bills propping up what has otherwise been a lackluster start. The Patriots missed a prime opportunity to open the season with a win, but Drake Maye threw three interceptions in a loss to the Drew Lock-led Seahawks that included A.J. Brown suffering a high ankle sprain. Maye's nine turnovers lead the NFL, and his mistakes are shrinking New England's margin for error every week. On a better note, the defense has been solid, especially against the pass.
Through three weeks, the Jets were about what we expected them to be: bad but not embarrassingly bad. They beat the Titans and then played the Packers and Lions close, probably giving away what should have been a win against Green Bay. Then in Week 4, the Bears had more first downs (34) than the Jets had offensive plays (32). It's the first time that's happened in an NFL game since 1999. New York didn't convert a single third down. Still, it's hard to be too harsh here: Garrett Wilson looks great, as do David Bailey and a host of other youngsters. This team has three(!) first-round picks in 2027. The Jets are a low-ceiling operation, but their floor is clearly much better than last year, which was the aim after acquiring a bunch of veterans. It's not a fun outlook, but the fun should start come draft season.
If the Dolphins hadn't lost De'Von Achane to a torn ACL, this grade would likely be a C or C-, similar to the Jets. This is what we thought the Dolphins, bereft of established NFL talent, would look like. But losing a centerpiece, whom you signed to a long-term deal this offseason, to a major injury has to be accounted for here. Otherwise, it's fair to be a bit disappointed about Malik Willis so far, though he really doesn't have much help around him. The Dolphins are getting nice flashes from several of their 13-player rookie class, and that is what matters most. Still, 0-4 is 0-4. The Dolphins haven't led for a single second yet this season. Just one win would boost this grade significantly, but dealing with a 0-17 watch is no fun.
After a 34-10 loss to the Jaguars to open the season, it looked like things could come unglued quickly for Cleveland. Since then, though, the Browns have won three straight games and moved into the AFC North lead. Deshaun Watson has produced solid quarterback play and has been even better late with three straight game-winning drives. The turnovers are still a concern, but considering he was historically bad when he last played -- and tore his Achilles twice since -- this is a stunning comeback. Meanwhile, rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion have impressed at wide receiver, and Spencer Fano and Austin Barber are holding up along the offensive line. Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has had his moments at safety. Mason Graham was taking a huge step (pre-injury) in his second year. GM Andrew Berry and early Coach of the Year frontrunner Todd Monken should be very excited.
This grade would be bumped up to a B+ or A- if Lamar Jackson hadn't suffered an ankle injury against the Titans. It's not believed to be a long-term thing, but his status for Week 5 is up in the air, and Jackson knows all too well how frustrating nagging injuries can be. It's even more of a bummer because he is off to a truly marvelous start this season. He leads the NFL in net yards per attempt and trails only Brock Purdy in EPA per dropback. Declan Doyle has unlocked Zay Flowers , too, and the offense is super explosive. The defense -- new coach Jesse Minter's specialty -- isn't quite there yet, ranking seventh in success rate but 15th in EPA per play. More sacks (Baltimore is 23rd in sack rate) would help.
The Steelers are on pace to do the sort of thing they always do of late: go about .500 with a low-ceiling offense and a playmaking defense and either miss the playoffs or sputter out of it in the first round. The offense is 26th in EPA per play and 25th in success rate, which is actually worse than last year, but it's making up for it with more explosives. The unit as a whole has been better the past couple of weeks, too. Still, it's just so stop-and-start under Aaron Rodgers at this stage in his career. The defense is giving up a ton of big plays and dealing with several injuries, which isn't helping, either.
The Bengals didn't commit tons of resources to the defense and retain Joe Burrow's entire supporting cast this offseason to be at the bottom of the AFC North, yet here they are. Both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are dealing with injuries, which impacts this grade, too. The defense isn't as awesome as it looked early on -- perhaps the Buccaneers and Texans, both 0-4, weren't the perfect barometers -- but it is improved. If it can cut down on the big plays allowed, it's actually been decent down-to-down. The offense has been a bit of a letdown: top five in explosive play rate, but outside the top 10 in success rate and poor in the red zone. The run game is struggling. The move to more under-center snaps was a good idea in theory but has been terrible on the field.
The Jaguars have the best point differential (+51) in the AFC and trail only the 49ers (58) league-wide. The offense is top-10 in both success rate and explosive play rate. Trevor Lawrence picked up right where he left off last season and very much looks like an MVP candidate; he ranks in the top 10 in several statistical categories, including third in touchdown rate, and he's more accurate than ever before. Watching him throw lasers over the middle of the field is about as good of quarterback play as you'll see. Bhayshul Tuten has made a nice Year 2 jump as well. The defense is shaky against the pass but strong against the run. It leads the NFL in turnover rate and is second in red zone efficiency.
The Colts' two wins have come against the Texans without Nico Collins (about as lifeless an offense as there is) and the Commanders without either of their top two quarterbacks. Jayden Daniels (elbow) was already out, and Marcus Mariota (knee) left after two series. But hey, they all count, and after nine straight losses dating back to last…

title: Prisco's NFL Week 5 Power Rankings: Chargers and Texans a disaster, Browns climb up nine spots
summary: Pete Prisco shares his latest Power Rankings for the 2026 NFL season, including some big climbs up the board for some of last week's top teams
full_text:
Our social team at CBS Sports HQ did a video this week asking this question:
Who's the biggest disappointment, the Los Angeles Chargers or the Houston Texans ?
Both teams are 0-4 and look like teams that will be watching come playoff time. Before the season, the Texans were a trendy pick to represent the AFC in the Super Bowl , while many thought the Chargers would be livened up by having Mike McDaniel as their new offensive coordinator.
Instead, the first four weeks have been disasters for both teams. At 0-4, they have big problems.
The Chargers' offensive issues are a concern. The Texans' supposedly dominant defense hasn't been great either. They were being compared to the 1985 Chicago Bears defense before the season, and yet the Dallas Cowboys gutted them in their victory Sunday.
The Chargers face a much tougher schedule the next four weeks — 0-8 is possible, including a game vs. the Texans — while the Texans' schedule does soften some.
Houston is down to No. 26 in my Power Rankings this week, while the Chargers are down to 27, one behind them. The Los Angeles offense is a mess right now. Justin Herbert , who still hasn't won a playoff game, doesn't look right in the McDaniel offense. It's not like there are tons of options in the passing game, but he's making some really bad throws.
As for the Texans, the offense came alive against the Cowboys, but the defense wasn't good. They can't blame that one on C.J. Stroud , who has played well.
If I had to pick one of these two to turn it around, I would go with the Texans. But they are three games behind the Jacksonville Jaguars in the AFC South, which means the wild card is probably the only real playoff path.
Two teams with such high hopes four weeks ago are now floundering and wondering if the season is over.

title: Saquon Barkley injury update: Eagles star considered week-to-week, per report
summary: The star running back seems to have avoided a long-term injury
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles have dealt with a significant number of injuries this season and had another major scare on Sunday when star running back Saquon Barkley exited the game with a hamstring injury. The Eagles and their fans can breathe a sigh of relief, getting good news on Monday that the injury is not considered long-term and that the RB is week-to-week, per the NFL Network.
Barkley went down on a run during the first quarter in their 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams . Before going down with the injury, he had two rushes for eight yards.
Saquon Barkley seemed to have pulled his hamstring on this run He's down on the field #NFL #Rams #RamsHouse #Eagles #FlyEaglesFly #LARvsPHI pic.twitter.com/0xZ1lOGhqi
Barkley immediately exited Sunday's game and was replaced by Tank Bigsby , a 2023 third-round pick who was traded from Jacksonville to Philadelphia last September. After joining the Eagles last season, Bigsby rushed for 344 yards and averaged an impressive 5.9 yards per carry. He had 36 yards and a score on 14 carries this season, entering Sunday's game and added 14 carries for 55 yards in Week 4.
Bigsby suffered an injury in the fourth quarter and is headed to IR for core muscle surgery. Going on IR means Bigsby will be sidelined for at least four weeks, making his earliest return Nov. 8 against the New York Giants. The positive update on Barkley is even more significant, given that the team lost its other top rusher.
If Barkley is sidelined in Week 5, we could see more from Will Shipley, who had the second-most rushing yards at 23 on six carries in Week 4. The 2024 fourth-rounder finished last season with 14 carries for 49 yards in 15 games. Quarterback Jalen Hurts was the team's third-best rusher in Sunday's loss, finishing with five carries for 18 yards on the ground.
Philly is hovering towards the middle of the pack in total rushing yards (436) and is towards the bottom in rushing touchdowns (2).
The offense is dealing with injuries to wide receiver DeVonta Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert, limiting Hurts' options.
Through three games in 2026, Barkley ran for 174 yards with a 5.1 yards-per-carry average. However, he is still in search of his first touchdown run of the season. The 29-year-old rushed for 3,145 yards and 20 touchdowns during his first two seasons with the Eagles, which included a 2,000-yard campaign in 2024. Barkley helped the Eagles win a Super Bowl that season.
The Eagles fell to 2-2 after losing to the Rams, their second straight loss. Philly was blown out by the Chicago Bears 27-7 in Week 3, after starting the season with victories against the Washington Commanders and Tennessee Titans .
Philadelphia will face the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 5, which could be a challenge, especially if they are down their RB1.

title: Sean McVay addresses Rams assistant coaches' viral interaction with Eagles fans
summary: McVay said he addressed the fourth-quarter exchange with Philadelphia fans and promised the coaching staff will handle high-emotion moments with more composure moving forward
full_text:
During a wild week in the NFL, which saw two officials suspended for unprofessional conduct and a head coach penalized for using profanity on the field , we also witnessed assistant coaches and fans go at it in Philly.
During the Los Angeles Rams ' thrilling, 24-20 comeback victory over the Philadelphia Eagles , some Rams assistant coaches got a little excited in their box and started banging on the glass while also trading some obscene hand gestures with the Philly faithful. At one point, an Eagles fan even threw a drink at the coaches' box.
The now-viral interaction allegedly took place after Kyren Williams ' game-winning touchdown late in the fourth quarter. Check out what happened here:
Here’s a video I took of the Rams coaching staff taunting Eagles fans after the game-winning touchdown. The Rams coaches started to bang on the windows and flip off Eagles fans which caused retaliation (which also isn’t right). pic.twitter.com/BzpSckDvJL
Here’s another video where you can clearly hear the Rams coaches continuing to bang on the windows during the Eagles final drive https://t.co/NDBCpUWILK pic.twitter.com/CH8a1plMiM
Omg caught in the crossfire of LA Rams OC cursing out fans and almost got hit while someone threw a beer can at the OC window @RamsNFL @Eagles #rams #eagles pic.twitter.com/rgAWXNdIxD
Rams head coach Sean McVay addressed the incident on Monday, saying, "We'll be better in those situations," per ESPN .
"We'll learn from that," McVay said. "We'll be better. Those fans are really into it, but I know that we want to make sure that we're representing the class and just the calm steadiness that we want to have while also being emotionally into it. And there's ways that we can have that reflected.
"We did talk about it, and that won't be an issue moving forward."
McVay said he had been in a similar situation earlier in his career, back when he was calling plays for Washington as an assistant coach.
"You get excited and emotional," McVay siad.
There was plenty of emotion to be found at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday. The Eagles held a 10-point lead in the fourth quarter, but Nick Sirianni's failed decision to go for the touchdown on a fourth-and-goal from the two-yard line opened the door for a dramatic Rams comeback. Los Angeles then put together two straight 10-play scoring drives, both capped by Williams' touchdowns, to escape Philadelphia with the win.
This marked Jalen Hurts ' first career loss when leading by double digits with five minutes remaining in the game, and Matthew Stafford's first such win with the Rams. It also marked the third time in the Sirianni era where the Eagles blew a 10-point lead at home.

title: Fueled by Sean Payton's 'disrespect,' 49ers' Dre Greenlaw dominates Broncos and lets former coach know
summary: The linebacker led San Francisco with 12 tackles in Sunday's win before opening up about feeling ignored and disrespected during his lone season in Denver
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw faced his former team, the Denver Broncos , on Sunday and used it as a chance to make his feelings on his old coach known. Greenlaw played for the Broncos, and head coach Sean Payton, last season. While his time there was short, it was impactful, just not for the right ways if you ask the LB.
Greenlaw said something to Payton during the game and appeared to tell the head coach, "Hey! You get the f-ck off my field!" after San Fran's 24-14 home victory over Denver. The 29-year-old didn't try to backtrack, later confirming his comments while speaking to the media.
"I told him to get the f--k off the field," Greenlaw said of his postgame comments, per the San Francisco Chronicle . "That's it: 'Get the f--k off the field.'"
He signed a three-year, $35 million contract with the Broncos ahead of the 2025 season and in his one year in Denver, Greenlaw played in eight games, starting seven. His missed time was due to a one-game suspension and injuries, something Greenlaw credits for the downfall of his relationship with his HC. Greenlaw said Payton stopped talking to him in Week 12, believing it was over the lingering injury.
"He definitely was, for sure," Greenlaw said, when asked if he thought Payton was ignoring him because the head coach was frustrated on Denver's return on their investment. "He would walk by - I would walk by - and he wouldn't even look at me because of my injury. So I just knew what it was (with him) there."
After Sunday's win, Greenlaw said he hadn't talked to Payton "in months" adding it dates back to when he was on the team.
"It's just a lot," Greenlaw said.
"I mean I just haven't talked to him in months. Even since I was on the team. It's just a lot." Dre Greenlaw when asked about his brief exchange with Sean Payton on the sidelines after making a tackle today. pic.twitter.com/96ZIe5D2HJ
Greenlaw had 43 total tackles, a sack and a forced fumble and an interception in 2025. He finished with four tackles in their divisional win over the Buffalo Bills and and six tackles in their AFC Championship loss to the New England Patriots , which would end up being his last game in orange.
The premature release was another thing Greenlaw was upset about.
"The disrespect," Greenlaw said regarding his motivation was for Sunday comments. "He couldn't be man-to-man and call my phone and say, 'We're going to cut you.'"
Payton was asked about the two exchanges and kept his answer politically correct.
"I think the world of him. I love everything about him," Payton said. "He plays with that emotion and so, all good."
Greenlaw seemed to use the motivation for his own good, leading the team with 12 tackles, marking his most so far this season.
The 49ers now sit at 4-0 and will face the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field next week. The Broncos are 2-2 and will face the winless Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium next week.
