title: Saints vs. Falcons prediction: Michael Penix Jr. leads Atlanta into New Orleans
summary: The NFC South rivals meet Monday night in New Orleans as Michael Penix Jr. and the Falcons look to build on their first win of the season
full_text:
In the Week 4 edition of "Monday Night Football," the New Orleans Saints host the Atlanta Falcons .
New Orleans is coming off a loss to the Las Vegas Raiders last week that dropped the Saints to 1-2. The Saints turned the ball over four times in the game and were carved up by Kirk Cousins and Brock Bowers on the other side of the ball. New Orleans lost running back Travis Etienne to injured reserve in that game as well. The Saints are now looking to rebound at home.
Atlanta is coming off its first win of the season, a destruction of the Green Bay Packers in Michael Penix Jr.'s first start of the year. Both Bijan Robinson and Drake London went completely berserk in Green Bay, with 194 yards on the ground and through the air, respectively. The Falcons are looking to get back to .500 after a dreadful start to the year with Cooper Rush filling in under center.
Will the Saints bounce back, or will the Falcons make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
The Falcons didn't make a single trip into the red zone in their first two games of the season, and they totaled just 524 yards in those two contests. They then came out in Week 3 and absolutely stomped on the Green Bay defense, piling up 498 yards on "Thursday Night Football" -- 256 through the air and 242 on the ground. They did all that while bouncing back from a game-opening interception by Michael Penix Jr., who was making his first start of the year after returning from his latest knee injury.
The New Orleans defense, meanwhile, has been lit up for over 30 points in two of its three games this season -- 31 by the Lions and 35 by the Raiders. The Saints, though, held the Ravens to 17 points in the other game and have dealt with poor opponents' field position in the two games where they got tagged, thanks to a combined seven turnovers by the offense. New Orleans' opponents have begun their average drive on the 34.8-yard line, the third-closest to the end zone of any team in the league.
The most fascinating matchup to watch in this one might be the one between Falcons wideout Drake London and Saints cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry . London had just six catches for 80 yards through the first two games of the season with Cooper Rush under center, but he went off for nine catches and 194 yards against Green Bay last week. London has a monster target share in games where Penix has started, and he is clearly the top target for the lefty signal-caller.
McKinstry isn't a corner who just plays one side of the field; his snaps have been split just about equally between left and right cornerback, and I'd probably expect him to follow London whenever he lines up on the perimeter. The Falcons would do well to get London lined up in the slot more often than usual, because McKinstry has yet to play a snap in the slot this season, per Pro Football Focus. Shifting London inside would yield more advantageous matchups.
Of course, Atlanta's offense is still based around Bijan Robinson in the backfield. Robinson is averaging a career-best 5.3 yards per carry this season, thanks in large part to his 29 carries for 194 yards and two touchdowns a week ago. The Falcons have been clocked for an average of 4.7 yards per carry on running-back runs, according to Tru Media, the fourth-worst mark in the NFL.
Tyler Shough led the NFL in completions through the first three weeks of the year. Shough is 91 of 132 (68.9%) for 917 yards (6.9 per attempt), eight touchdowns and three interceptions so far. He's done most of his work in second halves as the Saints have worked to come back from deficits: he's just 32 of 53 for 278 yards, two touchdowns and an interception before the break, while he's 59 of 79 for 639 yards, six touchdowns and two picks after it.
The Falcons rank a surprising first in the league in pressure rate so far this season, generating a sack, hit or hurry on 45.2% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media. They were expected to have one of the worst pass rushes in the NFL coming into the year in the absence of both Jalon Walker (injury) and James Pearce Jr . (suspension), but instead, guys like Gervon Dexter (10), Brandon Dorlus (eight), Cameron Thomas (eight) and Samson Ebukam (seven) have been getting after it up front.
The Saints haven't had much in the way of success running the ball, and will be without Travis Etienne hereafter, as he went on injured reserve. Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller are expected to share the load in the backfield with Etienne out, though CJ Donaldson could mix in as well. Kamara has been extremely inefficient on the ground for several years now, but he's at least a threat as a pass-catcher. Miller has only 140 carries in his career and has averaged south of 4.0 yards per attempt.
The Falcons looked much improved last week against the Packers, thanks in large part to the return of Michael Penix Jr. They hadn't even entered the red zone through the first two weeks of the season, then dropped 35 points on the Packers in Week 3. The Saints, meanwhile, could conceivably be 3-0 right now if not for backbreaking turnovers. They have two one-possession losses, both in games where they turned it over at least three times. If they can avoid giving the ball to the Falcons, I think they can win a close one here. Prediction: Saints 23, Falcons 20

title: NFL just doled out a punishment it hasn't used in 8 years -- to two separate offenders
summary: A look at how rare it is for an NFL official to be punished by the league
full_text:
The National Football League hands out punishments, in the form of fines and suspensions, to players and coaches often. Certain celebrations, hits, comments and actions off the field will have the shield knocking on the door. The one group that is hardly ever punished, though, is the officials.
The last time an official was suspended was in 2018. At least that was until today. The league announced on Monday that line judge Jeff Seeman will be suspended for two games and referee Adrian Hill for one game for "an instance of unprofessional conduct toward a player." The suspensions were issued by NFL Vice President of Officiating Ramon George.
Seeman, who has served as an official for 20 years, was seen appearing to swear at Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride in their game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium. It looked like Seeman was yelling, "F-- you" to McBride. That incident prompted a response from NFL Players Association President JC Tretter .
"This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter said. "Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."
Hill appeared to yell at Minnesota Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson after the player accidentally collided with the official. The incident took place at U.S. Bank Stadium in the Vikings' home game against the Miami Dolphins .
It's rare for one official to be suspended in a season, and even more rare for two officials to be suspended through the course of a year. But for two to be suspended in the same week is almost unheard of.
The last time an official was suspended was eight years ago.
In December of 2018, umpire Roy Ellison was placed on administrative leave for one game and fined one game check for a confrontation with a Bills player. Before that, the last suspension was handed to side judge Rob Vernatchi for a game clock error, as he failed to recognize an errant 18-second runoff during a Steelers-Chargers game in 2015. Two years before that, Ellison was also suspended in 2013 for using profanity against a player.
The last time multiple officials were suspended in the same season was 58 years ago, in 1968. Six officials were suspended for one game and were considered ineligible to officiate the postseason after losing track of downs at the end of a game between the Bears and Rams .
Other suspensions have come by way of an official failing to allow the game's final play to be set in motion, allowing a fumble to stand despite a penalty called during the play, conduct toward fans, failing to review a safety that should have been called a touchback and use of profanity towards players.
Scrutiny on the officials has increased so far in 2026, especially after a Week 4 Sunday that saw 235 total penalties called, according to NFLPenalties.com. New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel also had a heated moment with an official over a pass interference situation. Vrabel was said to have told a down judge that he made "a f---ing terrible call," which drew an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. Vrabel called the official "a little sensitive" for issuing the flag.
Carter Bahns also contributed to this report.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: NFL suspends official Jeff Seeman for incident with Cardinals' Trey McBride
summary: The altercation between the two went viral following New York's win over Arizona
full_text:
The NFL suspended line judge Jeff Seeman two games for "unprofessional conduct" toward Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride in Week 4. The league reviewed an exchange between the two in the Cardinals' 36-24 loss to the New York Giants wherein Seeman appeared to use vulgar language against McBride.
McBride initially voiced his displeasure after he thought pass interference should have been called on a third-down incompletion, and the referee seemed to respond with an expletive. Cameras caught the official's response to McBride, which quickly went viral.
The NFL said it is reviewing the situation in which an official appears to use profanity at Cardinals TE Trey McBride. The NFLPA Executive Director JC Tretter called for the NFL to hold the official accountable. pic.twitter.com/NuueChAmrx
The altercation caught the attention of JC Tretter , the president of the NFL Players Association.
"This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter wrote on X . "Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."
CBS Sports sideline reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala was in close proximity to the incident. She shared her observations on X.
"What's wild is that it all started with Trey McBride saying 'please' when pleading his case for a PI flag," she wrote . "He was heated for sure, but I never heard a curse from him. The harshest he got was, 'You're ruining the game.'"
Ironically, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was penalized after saying something similar to an official during New England's win over the Buffalo Bills . The penalty helped set up a Buffalo touchdown.
"I've said that 87 times since I've been a head coach," Vrabel said afterward. "There's nothing derogatory. You know, you'd have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive. ... I probably shouldn't have sworn, but I can tell you that in my history of being on the sidelines as a head coach, I've said that, and I apologized to him."
The NFL also suspended referee Adrian Hill one game for an interaction in Week 4 with Minnesota Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson .

title: Tyquan Thornton to have surgery after ankle injury; 'chance' Chiefs WR could return this season, per insider
summary: Thornton had already established career highs in receiving yards and touchdowns before exiting late in Week 4 vs. the Raiders
full_text:
Tests on Monday revealed that Chiefs receiver Tyquan Thornton will need surgery after dislocating his ankle during Kansas City's Week 4 game against the Raiders, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. The expected time for recovery is between three and four months, but there is a "small chance" of a late-season return, Zenitz reports .
The Chiefs ' wideout suffered a left ankle injury after making a 55-yard catch late in the fourth quarter on Sunday. Thornton initially didn't know that he had suffered an injury after making the catch. He began celebrating his big play before he realized what had happened. Cameras initially showed the severity of Thornton's injury, but then immediately stopped showing any replays. Thornton received an air cast to get off the field.
It was later revealed that Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle that was put back into place by doctors. A full evaluation on Monday morning revealed surgery is necessary.
While the injury is tough news for the 4-0 Chiefs, Zenitz added that "it's a relatively positive outlook" for Kansas City. A return toward the end of the season or during the playoffs is still possible.
Tyquan Thornton didn’t even know he was seriously hurt. He tried to stand on his bad ankle. pic.twitter.com/RGRWtHxexc
Tyquan Thornton didn’t even know he was seriously hurt. He tried to stand on his bad ankle. pic.twitter.com/RGRWtHxexc
Thornton's injury occurred after he had a monster day. He caught five passes for 111 yards and two scores. Thornton entered the game with six catches for 108 yards.
The 50th overall pick in the 2022 draft, Thornton spent his first three seasons with the Patriots before joining the Chiefs in 2025. He set career highs last season with 438 yards and three touchdowns while averaging 23.1 yards per catch.
Thornton's teammates made sure that his 55-yard catch would not go in vain. Kenneth Walker III scored one play later and scored again less than 20 seconds later after the Raiders fumbled the ensuing kickoff.
Kansas City prevailed, 30-27, improving to 4-0 and handing the Raiders their first loss of the season.
Walker rumbled for 177 yards and two scores and was again a key contributor in a Chiefs win. The Chiefs wouldn't have beaten the Raiders without Thornton, however.
"First off, I'm just praying for him," Patrick Mahomes told CBS Sports lead sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson afterward. "You never want anyone to get injured, and you're hoping it's better than it looked out there. Praying for him, and hopefully he comes back healthy."
"First off, I'm just praying for him ... Hopefully he comes back healthy." Patrick Mahomes shows love to Tyquan Thornton, who suffered a major ankle injury making a huge play for the @Chiefs 🎙️ @tracywolfson pic.twitter.com/Zpa4gc5vE4
With Thornton injured, the Chiefs will have to lean more on their other playmakers, which include Walker, Xavier Worthy , Travis Kelce , and Rashee Rice , who missed the majority of Sunday's game after injuring his hamstring in the second quarter.
The Chiefs will have time to rest and recover during their Week 5 bye before hosting the winless Chargers in Week 6.

title: Steve Gleason opens up on how Saints' 'Rebirth' game has kept him alive through ALS battle 20 years later
summary: Gleason's blocked punt was a pivotal moment for both the city of New Orleans and himself. Now, 20 years later, he opened up on 'Good Morning America' about his own 'rebirth'
full_text:
The parallels between Steve Gleason's legendary blocked punt, what it meant for the city of New Orleans and how it resembles his own personal struggle are chilling. A play on the football field that will forever be known as the "rebirth" of New Orleans was, in many ways, a "rebirth" for Gleason. He just did not know it at the time.
Almost exactly 20 years ago, the New Orleans Saints returned to the Superdome for the first time since Hurricane Katrina devastated the city. The venue that served as a shelter for thousands during and after the storm became, once again, the home of a proud football team. A minute and a half after the opening kickoff of the Sept. 25, 2006, game against the rival Atlanta Falcons , Gleason made the most memorable play in franchise history, blocking a punt that was scooped up in the end zone. It was a play that gave the Saints and the city of New Orleans hope once again.
20 years ago, the @Saints player their first game back in The Superdome after Hurricane Katrina. The Steve Gleason blocked punt will live on forever. 💛 ATLvsNO – 8:15pm ET on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/BUyftIq5D3
On Monday, the Falcons return to the Superdome to face the Saints in Week 4 of the 2026 season.  The team will honor Gleason and that 2006 squad in a 20th anniversary celebration.
It will undoubtedly be a meaningful return to the Superdome for Gleason.
"When I roll back into that stadium, I will not only be revisiting a monument of 2006, but I will be walking into a mirror — a place that had to learn how to rise," Gleason said on "Good Morning America" on Monday. "I had to learn the same thing."
Five years after he made an indelible mark on New Orleans with his blocked punt, in 2011, Gleason revealed that he was diagnosed with ALS. The average life expectancy after diagnosis is about three to five years, yet Gleason is among the 10-20% of those who survive for 10 years or more.
"I'm still here," Gleason said on GMA. "That still surprises some people. It does not surprise me as much as it used to."
Gleason uses speech synthesis technology to communicate and requires assistance to move and breathe. Still, he relishes in a "miraculous, wonderful life" and remains an active contributor to the ALS awareness movement. He became the first NFL player to win a Congressional Gold Medal in 2019 for his activism.
NFL players represent one of the populations that is at higher risk of developing ALS than the general public, Gleason said. He found community with other football players who battled or are currently battling the disease, including Chris Johnson , Tim Shaw , O.J. Brigance, Eric Stevens, and Steve Smith .
That game 20 years ago did not just revive the city of New Orleans. In hindsight, it was a pivotal moment in Gleason's life. It just took a few years for him to fully realize what it would mean to be a central figure in a defining moment in the city's and the football team's history.
"If I do not block that punt, I am another former special teams player, a has-been football guy," Gleason said. "When ALS came, I probably fade away quietly and die anonymously. That play made me visible at the exact moment this city needed a symbol. Years later, that visibility became a lifeline. So many people have told us our foundation's work saved their lives."
Last week, Gleason announced that he will release a musical album. The project combines his poetry with the instrumental talent of local musicians in New Orleans. He has already released two tracks and will continue to unveil more throughout the month of October. The songs are largely influenced by Gleason's life since his ALS diagnosis.
Fittingly, the album is titled "Rebirth."
"The truth I have to live with is this: The same play that helped New Orleans breathe again," Gleason said, "is a big reason I'm still breathing now."
Gleason, a special teams stalwart, ran unblocked to deflect the Falcons' punt into the end zone, where Curtis Deloatch recovered the loose ball for a touchdown. The crowd popped when Gleason made contact with the ball, rivaling that of any big play in football history. It was a cathartic moment for a city that, over the previous year, had been through misery.
For the first time in a year, New Orleans had something to cheer about.
"During the Falcons' first two games of the year, we noticed a lot of confusion and errors on their punt team, so we wanted to exploit that," Gleason said , recounting the preparation for that contest. "The scheme is an interior stunt where I cross from the right A gap to the left A gap. Sure enough, the Falcons had some confusion on their assignments. Because they used the slide technique, I ended up unblocked and the B gap opened up for me.
"At that point, there wasn't much thinking. All the film study, repetition and technique took over. The gap opened, and I knew I had a real chance. Then the ball hit my hands."
The Saints had spent the past year bouncing from stadium to stadium because of the damage Hurricane Katrina had done to the Superdome. They went 3-13 in that adversity-filled campaign. Questions arose about whether the franchise would return to the Superdome or to New Orleans in general.
But after a year of repairs to the facility, the Saints made their way back to the Superdome and dominated their division rival. The blocked punt helped the Saints down the Falcons 23-3 in a game that was symbolic of New Orleans' revival as a city.
In turn, a statue of that blocked punt stands outside the Superdome.

title: Caleb Williams to miss Bears' Week 5 rivalry game against Packers, Tyson Bagent set for second start
summary: The Bears are unbeaten without Williams in the starting lineup
full_text:
The Chicago Bears will be without quarterback Caleb Williams for at least one more game. Coach Ben Johnson said Monday on ESPN Chicago that Tyson Bagent "will be the guy" for the Week 5 rivalry game against the Green Bay Packers , which sets him up for his second consecutive start after he guided the Bears to a 23-12 win over the New York Jets on Sunday.
Williams remains on the mend from a hamstring strain and is poised to miss his third consecutive game. He suffered that injury in the Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , and in his absence, both Bagent and third-string quarterback Case Keenum stepped up to keep the offense rolling. They orchestrated plenty of success in back-to-back victories.
Bagent would have been in line to start against the Philadelphia Eagles in the first Williams-less game, but he spent most of Week 3 in the NFL's concussion protocol, which prompted Johnson to turn to Keenum. Now that Bagent is cleared, though, this is his offense until Williams returns. Chicago signed him to a two-year, $10 million contract extension in the offseason and regards him as a premier backup, so it was unsurprising that Johnson called his name even though Keenum was highly effective starting two games ago.
Bagent completed 25 of 34 passes against the Jets and amassed 268 yards through the air. He did not account for either of the Bears' touchdowns, though, and he threw one interception. Running back Kyle Monangai did the majority of the scoring with his two trips to the end zone on the ground.
"Some good and some that I think he wants back," Johnson said of Bagent's first start of 2026. "It's a little bit of a mixed bag. The best part is how he controlled the operation. I thought we had good tempo in and out of the huddle. I thought our guys played with a lot of confidence because of how he conducted himself. He found completions. I thought he played an efficient football game."
The hamstring strain Williams sustained in the Week 2 loss reportedly comes with a three-to-four-week recovery timeline , so even though the Bears initially labeled him as "week to week," there was always a real chance he would be unavailable for the NFC North battle against the Packers.
If Williams misses the full four weeks, he will also sit against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 6. That would set him up for a potential prime-time return against the New England Patriots on the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football."
author: Carter Bahns

title: NFL Week 4 injury panic meter: Concern for Ja'Marr Chase as Lamar Jackson gets good news
summary: We assess the latest injury news surrounding Lamar Jackson, Ja'Marr Chase, Saquon Barkley and the other prominent players hurt in Week 4
full_text:
Throughout the first month of the 2026 regular season, we were reminded not once, not twice, but by what felt like an avalanche of injuries sweeping over the league. And it's not just the number of injuries that have popped up over the opening month, but it's also been inflicted on some of the biggest names in the league at the most important positions in the sport.
For instance, leading up to Week 4, the NFL had already seen young phenoms like Caleb Williams (hamstring), Jayden Daniels (elbow) and Jaxson Dart (knee) suffer varying degrees of injuries. Meanwhile, Myles Garrett , the defending NFL Defensive Player of the Year and the centerpiece of arguably the biggest trade of the offseason, has yet to play for the Rams on American soil, landing on short-term IR after the opener in Australia due to a knee ailment. Then, there's Baker Mayfield (thumb), Justin Jefferson (ankle), Breece Hall (quad) and De'Von Achane (season-ending ACL tear), among other stars, dealing with injuries as well.
It's truly a who's who when they step into the NFL infirmary, and Week 4 only added to that total.
Below, we're going to highlight some of the biggest names in the NFL who went down with an injury in Week 4, assess their status, and give them a rating on our panic meter.
Panic meter barometer: 🔥🔥🔥 = Fears of a season-ender 🔥🔥 = Could miss a chunk of time 😬😬 = Could miss some time 😅 = Should be fine
The Ravens quarterback left Sunday's win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury sustained just before halftime and was seen leaving M&T Bank Stadium in a walking boot. While Jackson being in a boot isn't exactly ideal for the two-time NFL MVP, it does sound more like a precaution than anything else. NFL Network reported on Monday morning that Jackson will undergo tests late today, but the initial thought is that he's day-to-day, signaling that the ailment doesn't appear to be too serious. Coach Jesse Minter also said that "there were some talks about that," referring to Jackson possibly reentering the game. The fact that it was a discussion about him going back in (even though he didn't) is another signal that Jackson avoided anything substantial.
Week 5 opponent : at Atlanta Falcons
Chase suffered a concussion in the second quarter of Sunday's loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars . After making a catch, the wideout was brought to the ground by his facemask by Jaguars corner Jarrian Jones (which drew a penalty), and he was hit again while being taken down. After sitting on the turf for a moment and being evaluated by the training staff, he was taken into the locker room and did not return. Chase is now in the league's concussion protocol, so he'll have to get over several hurdles this week to play next Sunday. Typically, it's a tight turnaround for a player to suffer a concussion and be back the next week, so there's a chance Chase misses at least a week.
Week 5 opponent : at Miami Dolphins
Higgins suffered an adductor injury during Cincinnati's final drive of the game after making a leaping catch. He stayed on the field for one snap after being hobbled on the reception before exiting. With this being a soft-tissue injury, it does feel like there's a possibility Higgins could miss some time. That said, there's no definitive word on the severity of the injury yet.
Week 5 opponent : at Miami Dolphins
It's been tough sledding for Barkley on the injury front this season. After already dealing with a stinger, the Eagles running back left Sunday's loss to the Rams due to a hamstring injury he suffered in the first quarter. Barkley seemed to pull up after running out of bounds on a carry during Philly's second possession. NFL Network reports that Barkley will undergo testing on Monday, but added that it doesn't appear to be overly serious. That said, as is the case with all soft tissue injuries, they won't know the full extent until they do testing.
Week 5 opponent : vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (in London)
The injuries continued to pile up for Philadelphia. On top of Barkley, All-Pro corner Quinyon Mitchell left the game in the third quarter on Sunday due to a knee injury. Mitchell got tangled up on the sideline while tackling Rams running back Blake Corum and appears to have taken a helmet to the knee. NFL Network reports that the hope is Mitchell hyperextended his knee and may have suffered a bone bruise, but testing on Monday will reveal the severity.
Week 5 opponent : vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (in London)
Mariota has been starting for Washington in place of the injured Jayden Daniels (left elbow), but he couldn't finish Sunday's loss to the Colts in London. The veteran reportedly aggravated his MCL injury and is now undergoing further testing, but he is expected to miss time. There's hope that Daniels will be back next week, but if he's unable to go, it could thrust rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis , who came in under duress for Mariota, into the starter role.
Week 5 opponent : vs. New York Giants
Moore aggravated his shoulder injury in Sunday's loss to the Patriots , but ESPN reports that the injury is not considered to be a long-term issue right now. Head coach Joe Brady didn't give an update on Moore's injury postgame. The wideout, who initially injured the shoulder in Week 2 against the Lions ,  went down in the second quarter during Sunday's matchup. Before this aggravation, Moore didn't miss any time, but has been limited in practice. He'll have some extra time to recuperate as Buffalo plays on Monday night in Week 5.
Week 5 opponent : at Los Angeles Rams
The Packers fear Cooper, their standout linebacker, sustained a torn Achilles in the win over the Buccaneers . Coach Matt LaFleur acknowledged that the injury is "not good" and he'd "suspect" it will be a season-ending injury.
Week 5 opponent : vs. Chicago Bears
The Chiefs receiver was having the game of his life on Sunday against the Raiders , catching five passes for 111 yards and two touchdowns. Unfortunately, he suffered a gruesome ankle injury after making a sensational 55-yard catch and was carted off. Specifically, Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle. They were able to put the ankle back into place, and he did fly back with the team, but he is now out indefinitely. He will undergo an MRI on Monday to see if there is further damage.
Head coach Andy Reid said that Rice tweaked his hamstring in the first quarter and did not return. While the wideout did not get back into the game in Week 4, the injury doesn't sound too severe, with NFL Network characterizing it as a very minor hamstring injury. With Kansas City on the bye in Week 5, it appears that Rice may not miss much, if any, time.
Denver's star corner is expected to miss time with an ankle injury and will undergo further evaluation on Monday, according to NFL Network . At the time when Surtain went down in the second quarter with a non-contact injury, fears of a season-ender were hard to ignore. However, the injury is not as severe as it initially appeared. Surtian is still expected to be sidelined for a period of time -- NFL Network floated a couple of weeks or an IR stint -- but it is not expected to be season-ending, which is good news for the Broncos .
Week 5 opponent : at Los Angeles Chargers
Rashawn Slater left Los Angeles' Week 4 loss to the Seahawks in the fourth quarter due to an ankle injury and did not return. NFL Network reports that the Chargers' star left tackle is believed to have suffered a high ankle sprain based on initial exams. He's slated to undergo an MRI, but this is the type of injury that could leave a player out for several weeks and possibly place them on short-term IR.

title: Patriots' Mike Vrabel fires back at Bills' C.J. Gardner-Johnson for jab at Efton Chism III
summary: Gardner-Johnson called Chism a 'practice squad player' and suggested the Patriots receiver could not replicate his spectacular game-winning catch
full_text:
The New England Patriots upset the Buffalo Bills in a key early-season divisional showdown on Sunday and got over the top in the close battle with help from an unlikely source. Wide receiver Efton Chism III secured the game-winning touchdown in the Patriots' 29-26 victory on the biggest play of his young career: A diving, one-handed catch in the end zone with 1:50 to play.
Bills cornerback C.J. Gardner-Johnson brushed off the highlight reception as a fluke. He called Chism a "practice squad player" and said that if the teams were to run that play over again, the wide receiver would not be able to replicate his stellar catch. It should be noted that Chism has been on the Patriots' 53-man roster since signing as an undrafted free agent in 2025.
"We're not going to get into no bulletin board material," Gardner-Johnson said postgame before promptly giving the Patriots plenty of bulletin board material. "An elevated guy made a hell of a catch. Probably won't hear from him again, respectfully. I say that with a lot of confidence, because it's like, he didn't put his confidence in his best player. If that was it, he would've threw it to Doubs or somebody. They won the game. Whatever. They ain't do s--- better than us. We gotta play better."
Patriots coach Mike Vrabel came to Chism's defense with his reaction to Gardner-Johnson's jab. He had a day to concoct the perfect response and delivered it Monday on his weekly radio appearance on WEEI.
"For a guy that's been on eight teams in four years? I guess he knows the drill," Vrabel said of the Bills defender . (For the record, Gardner-Johnson has been with seven teams in his eight-year NFL career, including spending time on the Bears and Ravens practice squads).
New England, for now, has the last laugh thanks to its coach's "mic drop" of a reply. The teams will meet again in Week 13, and Chism will have an opportunity to show Gardner-Johnson that he, in fact, can replicate the dazzling catch.
TOUCHDOWN PATRIOTS. What a catch by Efton Chism III to take the lead! @NEvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DtIZoenYNL
Chism is a second-year professional out of Eastern Washington, where he broke Cooper Kupp's school record for single-season receptions and earned FCS first-team All-American honors as a senior. The Patriots were one of multiple teams to target him as an undrafted free agent, and they kept him around on their active roster following an impressive rookie preseason. Chism made only a couple of appearances in 2025 but displayed his potential in Week 17 when he hauled in his first two career receptions.
With No. 1 receiver A.J. Brown out due to a high ankle sprain, Chism saw action in each of the last three games and made one start. He has four catches on the year for 41 yards and the highlight-reel touchdown.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Dan Campbell 'not talking about' defensive overhaul. Without one Lions are wasting their Super Bowl window
summary: With the defense bottoming out in 2026, Campbell needs to make changes in order to take his team back to the championship conversation
full_text:
Pull a random defensive statistic out of a hat, and there is a solid chance the Detroit Lions rank dead last in the NFL in that metric. Through Week 4, no team surrendered more points or yards than the Lions. This is now the second consecutive year in which Detroit's defense has been a liability, yet coach Dan Campbell is hesitant to make any significant changes to the unit's structure or leadership.
Following the 32-26 loss to the Carolina Panthers on "Sunday Night Football," Campbell admitted that the defense is a glaring issue. But instead of firing second-year coordinator Kelvin Sheppard , shaking up the play-calling duties or doing anything else to reconstruct the defense's framework, Campbell said he wants to "exhaust everything" with the players and coaches he has by his side.
"I'm not talking about all that," Campbell said after the game of a potential leadership change. "I'm talking about getting better right now with what we've got. That's what we're going to do. We're going to find a way to get better with what we've got. There are other things that we can do. We've tweaked a little bit every week here. There's still some things that we can try that we haven't yet to try to settle some things down and see if we can help. It's a work in progress."
None of the adjustments Campbell and his staff have made on the fly over the last year have produced the desired results. Sunday night was just the latest example. Carolina quarterback Bryce Young entered the game as the NFL's leading passer and only padded his advantage over the rest of the league's signal-callers with a 329-yard outing. Wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan enjoyed a career night with 14 catches, 192 yards and two touchdowns. On the ground, Chuba Hubbard racked up 122 yards and a pair of scores.
With each passing week, Detroit shows that no matter how excellent its offense may be, it is always in grave danger of losing. The Panthers, New York Jets , Buffalo Bills and New Orleans Saints each posted at least 24 points against this team. New Orleans tallied 30 in the second half and overtime of the season opener. Still, Campbell and his players stand up for Sheppard.
#Lions LB Jack Campbell on DC Kelvin Sheppard: “Shep works hard. Dan believes in him, I believe in him. He's made of the right stuff. We're going to get this figured out. We've just got to stay the course, stick together. Right now, it's us versus everybody.”
In Sheppard's defense, his personnel is less than fully stocked. The absences of Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch from the safety unit, plus Terrion Arnold's late-offseason departure, are undoubtedly key reasons why the Lions' secondary cannot get off the field. But the front is still full of Pro Bowl talent like Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell .
The issues date back to before those defensive backfield personnel deficiencies, so it is clear that the troubles go much deeper.
Detroit has not been a defensive juggernaut at any point during the Campbell era, but there was a brief period at the height of his tenure where the Lions were nearly as effective at preventing opponents from scoring as they were at putting points on the board themselves. Former defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn built the group from the ground up and turned it into a top-10 unit before his departure to take the Jets' head coaching job.
Since then, it has been nothing but regression. The team as a whole suffered in turn. During Glenn's tenure, the Lions improved their win total every year. In his final season, they went 15-2 and reached the divisional round of the playoffs. Once Sheppard took over, Detroit instantly regressed to 9-8 and missed the postseason, and it is off to a mediocre start to 2026.
The Lions' offense is championship material. A few of the best players in the NFL at their respective positions reside on this unit. Jahmyr Gibbs is perhaps the top running back in the league. Penei Sewell might be the league's most elite tackle. Amon-Ra St. Brown is a top-flight wide receiver. Sam LaPorta is off to a tremendous start to his career at tight end. Holding the unit together is a commendable quarterback in Jared Goff , who logged the seventh 400-yard game of his career and the third of his Lions tenure in Week 4.
Winning shootouts is not a sustainable model, though. That was evident a year ago when the Lions finished just one game above .500. It is clear in 2026 as they open the campaign at 2-2. The offense can keep pace with nearly anyone, but the group on the other side of the ball is putting too much of the burden on Goff and his supporting cast.
There is foundational talent on the defense, too. Hutchinson and Campbell are the kinds of pieces that can anchor a formidable group. They just need more help on the back end and a play-caller who utilizes them more effectively.
Unless the Lions shake up their defensive leadership or make a splash personnel move, the group will continue to weigh down a team that, for so many reasons, should be in the Super Bowl conversation.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Travis Kelce closing in on NFL history, could climb to No. 5 on all-time receptions list in coming weeks
summary: Kelce is tied with Tim Brown for seventh in NFL history and needs nine catches to take sole possession of fifth place
full_text:
Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce is already among the greatest tight ends in NFL history, and this week, he made his already impressive resume that much more convincing. Kelce came into Week 4 tied with wideout Tim Brown for the seventh-most receptions in NFL history with 1,094, meaning one catch from quarterback Patrick Mahomes and he would have sole possession of that mark.
Kelce finished with two receptions in their 30-27 win against the Las Vegas Raiders, meaning he claimed sole possession of that seventh spot.
Cris Carter is No. 6 on the all-time list with 1,101 receptions, just five more than Kelce. Marvin Harrison is at No. 5 with 1,102, six more than Kelce. When he hits seven more catches, Kelce will be at No. 5 on his own. He could move multiple spots in the coming weeks and has the chance to move up to No. 5.
In Week 1 against the Miami Dolphins , Kelce recorded two receptions on two targets. He registered nine receptions on 11 targets in Week 2 against the Indianapolis Colts, and caught three more balls on five targets in Week 3 against the Denver Broncos . He has 16 receptions total in the four wins, for an average of 4 catches per game.
If Kelce continues his trend of average receptions per game, he will pass Carter in Week 6 and will pass Harrison in Week 7. That said, the veteran always has a chance to have a big game and get those would-be historic receptions earlier.
If Kelce continues to average 4 receptions per game, he will finish the year with 68 catches if he plays all 17 games at the average. That would put him at 1,148 all-time, which would still put him at No. 5, as Jason Witten has 1,228 at No. 4.
To reach No. 4, Kelce needs 132 catches. The most receptions he has recorded in a single year is 110, and his 17-game average is 95 a year. If he plays in 2027 and continues at a similar level, he would likely pass Witten sometime next season.
At 36, Kelce will be hanging up the cleats sooner rather than later. While he hasn't announced whether he will retire after this year, after 14 seasons, it wouldn't come as a shock.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Jim Harbaugh defends Mike McDaniel despite 0-4 start, Justin Herbert earns ugly Chargers honor
summary: Los Angeles is struggling on offense and its franchise quarterback is a shell of himself
full_text:
Offensive execution continues to lack for the winless Los Angeles Chargers , partly due to schematic changes following the offseason hiring of former Miami Dolphins coach Mike McDaniel.
After Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Seattle Seahawks , coach Jim Harbaugh was peppered with questions about his team's struggles on that side of the football and whether he thought the Chargers could turn things around, with McDaniel calling plays.
Los Angeles has the fourth-worst scoring offense (16.8 points per game) in the NFL , and its passing offense (185.3 YPG) is on pace for its lowest full-season per game average since 1998.
"No, his job is not in jeopardy," Harbaugh said of the OC, via the Associated Press. "He's a skilled coach, and we're going to keep growing.
According to the NFL's stats department , Justin Herbert is the first Chargers quarterback with at least six interceptions and 10 sacks through the team's first four games since Ryan Leaf in 2000.
Herbert's never thrown six interceptions in his career this early in the season, and he's already been sacked 12 times, tied for the second-most in the league.
Like Harbaugh, however, Herbert's not putting the onus on his play-caller.
"I think (McDaniel) is the greatest and I want to make him proud and do everything I can to pick up the offense and do exactly what he asks," Herbert said. "But I think we've just got to go make plays. I've got to make plays out there and haven't done that, but I know we'll get it next time."
Last month, after a Week 3 loss to the Buffalo Bills , Harbaugh encouraged Herbert to "be better" as the orchestrator of McDaniel's offense. The former first-round pick acknowledged he needed to perform at a higher level.
But so much for Harbaugh attempting to energize his franchise player. Herbert turned it over three times in Sunday's loss, including a loss-clinching fumble after a sack on his team's final possession.
Herbert's QBR is a career-worst 27.9 through four starts, alarming for a signal caller whose efficiency usually rests in the 60s. He's only completing passes at a 59.7% clip, and two first-half interceptions against the Seahawks led to an early 17-point deficit.
McDaniel said after the Chargers' struggles against the Bills that the team's personnel was failing to do their "jobs" on offense and admitted he was part of the problem.
"I'm fully responsible," McDaniel said prior to his team's fourth straight setback, via ESPN . "I spend zero time trying to avoid blame. It's quite the opposite."
Harbaugh has a mess on his hands offensively if Herbert and McDaniel fail to get this ship turned in the right direction before the midseason mark in a couple of weeks.
author: Brad Crawford

title: Bryce Young shines again: How former No. 1 pick went from benched to leading NFL in passing
summary: Down two of his top wide receivers, Young threw for 329 yards and two scores on 'Sunday Night Football' vs. the Lions
full_text:
Sunday night, "MVP" chants rained down on Bryce Young as he led the Panthers to a 32-26 win over the Lions , his first prime-time win. It was both fitting -- Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns -- and a reminder of how far he has come. Just two years earlier, he wasn't even playing in games, let alone starring in them. He had been benched for Andy Dalton , with his chances of being an NFL starter seemingly in the balance.
How quickly things can change.
Young currently leads the NFL in passing yards and passing first downs. He's tied for third in passing touchdowns and seventh in yards per attempt. For a quarterback who doesn't have a rocket arm, he sure is making the most of it: He leads the NFL in completions of 10+ yards (55) and is tied for second in completions of 20+ yards (17).
And he's doing it all in far from ideal circumstances. The Panthers were without their No. 2 ( Jalen Coker ) and No. 3 ( Xavier Legette ) wide receivers Sunday. Rookie field stretcher Chris Brazzell suffered a season-ending injury in training camp. The offensive line, also battered by injury, is giving up pressure at a 46.3% rate -- only Justin Herbert is pressured at a higher rate.
So, what's working for Young? And more importantly, is it sustainable as the 2-2 Panthers look to make consecutive playoff trips for the first time in more than a decade?
This offseason, Dave Canales handed play-calling duties to offensive coordinator Brad Idzik. Idzik and Canales go back to 2019, when they were both with Seattle, but this is Idzik's first time calling plays. Still, one could have assumed it would look similar to Canales.
That's where assuming can be erroneous. The Panthers currently lead the NFL in pass rate over expected and are fifth in pass percentage. And they're not just passing a lot, but being aggressive doing so: Young is 12th in deep pass rate, ninth in air yards per attempt and sixth in explosives per dropback. It's a wild departure from Young's earlier career, even excluding his disastrous rookie season.

Furthermore, Young is using play action on 31.5% of his dropbacks, the highest rate of his career. He's averaging 8.1 yards per play on those passes, also a career high. Here's one of his best throws from Sunday night:
Bryce Young is feelin' it @DETvsCAR on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/eJVA9QoIv2
Young not only makes a terrific throw, but he does so with a defender right in his face. Which leads us to ...
Young's superpower -- the thing that made him a Heisman Trophy winner at Alabama, the thing that made him the No. 1 pick despite his underwhelming physical profile -- is his ability to make the right reads and get the ball there on time. But the jump from being excellent at that in college and being excellent at that in the NFL is a huge one. Young appears to be making that jump.
Young is currently third in EPA per dropback on quick-game throws (thrown in 2.5 seconds or faster). That's an absurd jump.
Bryce Young EPA per dropback on quick throws
Here's one such throw from Sunday night: Young initially gets a Cover-2 look, but it's just a disguise, and the Lions end up playing Cover 3 with a deep safety. Young shreds it immediately with a dart to John Metchie III .
Young darts keep flyin' @DETvsCAR on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Yf2CbrL9oX
Furthermore, Idzik is implementing many different ways to attack. Sunday, for example, Young had three run/pass option throws, which resulted in three completions for 35 yards. It was Young's most RPO throws in a game since his rookie year. He had only three all season entering the game. Three isn't a big number, but adding wrinkles is crucial every week. Idzik clearly saw an area he wanted to attack and exploited it.
The game "slowing down" is a cliche, but it can be true. Young has just two interceptions, and his 1.2% turnover-worthy throw rate is sixth-lowest in the NFL. He's simply not putting the ball in harm's way as much. He's hitting first reads with confidence, and when things get mucked up, he's more composed.
EPA/dropback when pressured
Negative play rate when pressured
<< Ranks top 10 this season
It's not just negative play mitigation. How about this one from last night, in the biggest of moments?
T-MAC ARE YOU SERIOUS! @DETvsCAR on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/uIhOgbACgr
( Tetairoa McMillan rocks, by the way.)
Simply put, Young is playing on time. When it's not on time, it's not the disaster it was before. The biggest strengths of his game are shining, and the weaknesses are becoming either less weak or less important.
As fun as this excellent start has been, it's a very small sample size against a less-than-inspiring bunch of opponents. You can only play who's on your schedule, yes, but there's little doubt a start of Bears , Falcons , Browns and Lions is hardly Murderers' Row when it comes to pass defense.
The Browns were by far the best of that bunch, and Young struggled in that loss. He was inaccurate, took three sacks and couldn't produce explosive plays against a Cleveland defense heavy on press coverage. Young was under pressure all afternoon, and that's going to be an issue, too. The offensive line is without tackles Ikem Ekwonu and Taylor Moton and guards Brady Christensen and Damien Lewis . First-round rookie tackle Monroe Freeling left Sunday night's game and didn't return.
Carolina is currently 26th in PFF's pass blocking grades, and Young has faced 49 quick pressures this season, six more than anyone else.
It makes sense that Young has made strides against pressure, but making such a gigantic leap for an entire season seems unlikely -- especially as he faces some better secondaries, starting with the Eagles in Week 6 after the bye. Can the Panthers keep him clean (enough)? Can he continue to play this well under pressure? Will the wear and tear of a season begin to take its toll?
That's still to be determined. Still, Young has shown major strides. He might not play like a top-five or even a top-10 quarterback the rest of the season like he is now, but it's still trending toward making a very important step for both himself and the organization. Young didn't sign an extension this offseason and will enter the fifth-year option year of his rookie deal. Should he continue to play well -- even at a slightly lower clip than what he's currently doing -- Carolina will have much more confidence believing it's found its long-term answer at quarterback after nearly a decade of searching.

title: NFL Week 5 early odds: Bears favorites at Lambeau, Bills underdogs to Rams

full_text:
Now that the first month of the season is in the books, it's time for the true contenders to begin separating themselves from the pack. That could happen as soon as Week 5, as there are several high-profile matchups on the docket.
Once again, Sunday's action starts a little early with the Eagles and Jaguars playing in London. Jacksonville travels to its home away from home as a favorite, while Philly will look to get its offense back on track after collapsing against the Rams in Week 4. After that, we have five divisional matchups, including Bears-Packers, with Chicago entering Lambeau Field as a road favorite. We then wrap up the entire slate on Monday for what could be a Super Bowl preview between the Bills and Rams from SoFi Stadium, so this slate packs quite the punch.
As we begin to turn our attention to Week 5, let's jump into the odds and see who the oddsmakers have coming out on top and which games could be high-scoring affairs.
Note : Kansas City and Carolina are on the bye in Week 5
All lines via DraftKings ; all games on Sunday unless noted
Buccaneers at Cowboys (Thursday)
Buccaneers +425, Cowboys -575
Eagles at Jaguars (in London)
Bengals -360, Dolphins +285
Raiders +154, Patriots -185
Giants +142, Commanders -170
Broncos -185, Chargers +154
Lions -250, Cardinals +205
Dallas is now a double-digit favorite over the Buccaneers, laying 10 points after the line initially opened at Coboys -9.5. This comes after we got our first glimpse of Jalon Daniels for Tampa Bay, and the undrafted rookie quarterback managed just two scoring drives in a loss to Green Bay. With Baker Mayfield still out, the Cowboys are rightfully being looked at as a heavy favorite, and they are riding high after a road win in Houston. Dallas is 3-1 ATS this season, including a cover in their home opener. The Bucs are 0-4 ATS through the first month.
Jacksonville has jumped out to a 4.5-point favorite over the Eagles, which is up from the 3-point spread they were laying at the open. The Jaguars are one of the more underrated teams in the NFL through the first three weeks, owning a 3-1 SU and ATS record with an average margin of victory of 12.8 points (second-highest in the NFL). They take on an Eagles team that has been banged up with injuries and saw Saquon Barkley leave Sunday's loss to the Rams with a hamstring injury. So far, the Eagles are 0-4 ATS. Because of the questions surrounding Philadelphia's offense, the total has dropped from 44.5 to 43.5.
Chicago opened as a 1.5-point road favorite over the Packers and that has since bumped up to -2.5. The Bears are both 3-1 straight-up and against the spread this season, and that's in spite of Caleb Williams suffering a hamstring injury. As for the Packefs, they've continued to look sluggish this season and, while they were able to beat the Bucs, it was hardly an inspiring victory and are 1-3 ATS this sesaon. If you're looking for a silver lining, however, Green Bay is 6-2 ATS as a home underdog under Matt LaFleur. That 75% cover rate is the highest in the NFL over that span.
Cincinnati is a 7.5-point road favorite on the road as they gear up to face the Dolphins. That's down from the 8.5-point spread at the open, which may be attributed to injuries plaguing the Bengals offense in Week 4. They lost Ja'Marr Chase due to a concussion, while Tee Higgins exited with an adductor injury. That leaves their availability for Week 5 in doubt, and the total has sunk to 42.5 (opened at 46.5) as a result. The Bengals are 1-1 on the road this season, while Miami is 0-1 ATS at home.
New York is 1-3 on the season, but they've been pesky. They're 2-1-1 ATS and now take on a Browns team that has been one of the surprises of the first month. They'll do so as a 2.5-point favorite, which is up from -1.5 at the open. They're 3-1 (SU and ATS) and are coming off a win against the Steelers on Thursday, so they'll have the rest advantage of New York. The Jets covered their lone game at MetLife Stadium this season, while Cleveland is 1-1 ATS on the road.
Las Vegas suffered its first loss of the season in Week 4 against the Chiefs and will look to rebound when they travel to Foxborough to face the Patriots. They'll enter Gillette Stadium as a 3.5-point underdog, however. New England got its season back on track with a last-minute win over the Bills in Buffalo to move them to 2-2 on the season. Since the start of last season, the Patriots are 7-4-1 ATS at home (1-0 ATS in 2026). The Raiders have covered both of their road games this season.
Houston is a 6.5-point road favorite in this AFC South matchup in Tennessee, but this may say more about the 0-4 Titans than the Texans. That said, Tennessee is 2-2 ATS on the season and 1-1 at Nissan Stadium, while the Texans are 0-4 ATS on the season. Under head coach DeMeco Ryans , the Texans are 5-6-1 ATS as a road favorite. Looking at the totals, the Under is a combined 5-3 between them this season.
This is quite the mismatch in terms of rest. Indy is coming back stateside after playing in London and will then have to travel to Pittsburgh to face a Steelers team that'll be on extended rest after playing last Thursday. That makes this 2.5-point spread in favor of Pittsburgh pretty interesting, especially considering they are 2-0 ATS at home this season. Indy is 1-0 ATS on the road this season.
The Commanders are a 3-point favorite over New York, but this line will be worth monitoring throughout the week. It's unclear if Jayden Daniels will make his return this week. If he doesn't, seventhr ound rookie Athan Kaliakmanis could get the nod after he relieved Marcus Mariota in London on Sunday due to a knee injury. If that proves to be the case, we could see more movement here. The Giants are 0-1 ATS on the road this season, while Washington is 1-0 ATS at home.
Minnesota is a 1.5-point road favorite over the Saints, who still have their Week 4 matchup on deck on Monday night. That said, the line does seem to be moving towards New Orleans as it originally opened at Vikings -2.5. Minnesota is 2-0 ATS on the road this season, but neither of those covers came with them as a road favorite. Before Monday's matchup, the Saints are 0-1 ATS at home and 2-1 ATS on the season.
Denver is a 3.5-point road favorite over the Chargers, who continue to struggle this season. On top of being 0-4 coming out of the first month, Los Angeles is still searching for its first ATS win (0-3-1). The Broncos are 2-2 ATS so far this season, but have yet to cover on the road. The total for this matchup sits at 43.5 and the Under could be in play as it's 6-2 between these teams this season.
Detroit has moved out to a 3.5-point road favorite over Arizona, which is up from the field goal spread at the open. They'll be looking to rebound after a loss in Carolina, where they were road favorites. The Cardinals have lost three straight after upsetting the Chargers in the season opener, but are 2-2 ATS entering Week 5. In their lone game as a home underdog, Arizona is 0-1 ATS.
The Seahawks are a field goal favorite at home as they host the undefeated 49ers in what is a key NFC West matchup. On top of being 4-0, San Francisco is 3-1 ATS and has an NFL-best 14.5 average margin of victory. On the road, they are 1-0 ATS. Meanwhile, Seattle is 1-1-2 ATS so far this season.
This line could change dramatically for a couple of different reasons. For one, the Falcons still have to play their Week 4 matchup on Monday night. Second, Lamar Jackson left Sunday's win over the Titans with an injury. If that causes him to miss time, you can almost guarantee this line won't continue to sit at Ravens -3.5 as it has since the open. The 44.5-point total will also move. This season, the Ravens are 1-3 ATS.
The Rams are a slim 2.5-point favorite as they gear up to host the Bills in a heavyweight matchup next Monday night. This line is down from the full field goal L.A. was laying at the open. The Rams are coming off a comeback win over the Eagles, while the Bills lost at home…

title: Cover 32: Packers don't instill any faith on possible playoff run, plus game balls, biggest gaffes from Week 4
summary: Tyler Sullivan dives into all the biggest items from Week 4 in the NFL, including CeeDee Lamb's historic day and Mike Vrabel's bizarre tiff
full_text:
With the first month of the season in the books, there are a few teams that haven't exactly lived up to the hype. Sure, you can look at teams like the Los Angeles Chargers and Houston Texans -- who are both still winless this year -- as some of the biggest disappointments through the early stages of the 2026 season, but don't sleep on the Green Bay Packers either. Despite emerging from the first month at 2-2, these Cheeseheads don't exactly pass the smell test.
It's been a slog for the Packers, and they haven't instilled much confidence as far as any serious threat in the NFC North. After coming into the year with the second-best odds to win the division and favored to reach double-digit wins on the year, their .500 record feels hollow, with their 17-14 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 4 serving as the latest piece of evidence pointing to that fact.
They nearly let undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels -- who started in place of the injured Baker Mayfield -- beat them at the last minute because of self-inflicted wounds. For instance, they committed two fourth-quarter turnovers with a mere field goal lead, basically daring Tampa Bay to pull off the upset. The first was a fumble by Kaleb Johnson , and then, on the very next possession, Jordan Love needlessly tossed the ball into a high-traffic area, and the pass was picked off by Bucs corner Jacob Parish.
ANOTHER TAMPA BAY TAKEAWAY 🔥 @GBvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/VVfqSCPHii
Despite those golden opportunities, Daniels and company couldn't capitalize, first punting, then turning the ball over on downs after those two turnovers. Had they been facing a more capable quarterback instead of a UDFA, we could be looking at a different result.
As has been the case throughout the year to this point, the Packers have had two adversaries every week: the opposition and themselves. On Sunday, they committed 10 total penalties, bringing their total to 42 infractions for the year (second-most in the NFL ). Their 344 total penalty yards also lead the league. That's not a characteristic of a true playoff contender.
When they're not having laundry thrown at them, the offense hasn't inspired much fear in opposing defenses. They average just 18.3 points per game, which is their lowest through the first four weeks of the season since 2006. They're also last in the NFL with a 26.1% conversion rate on third down, while their rushing yards per game average (3.2) is near the bottom of the barrel as well. Their defense is allowing a 48.2% conversion rate on third down (fourth-highest in the NFL), so it's not great on either side of the ball right now.
Yes, external circumstances are contributing to this lackluster beginning. They don't have Micah Parsons as he's continuing to rehab his season-ending ACL tear from last year, Josh Jacobs is on the commissioner's exempt list, and they continue to be inundated with injuries. After losing Jayden Reed and Zach Bako-Bewele in previous weeks, they also just saw linebacker Edgerrin Cooper go down in Week 4. It's been brutal from that front.
Even with that in mind, this team has enough talent that it shouldn't be this anemic, yet they're barely getting by despite facing backup and/or bottom-tier starting quarterbacks.
So far this season, Green Bay's two victories have come against the Buccaneers and Jets , who are a combined 1-7 through four weeks. As we mentioned, Tampa Bay started an undrafted free agent, while the Jets had Geno Smith (who nearly beat them in overtime). Meanwhile, their losses have come against the Carson Wentz-led Vikings and the Falcons, with Michael Penix Jr . making his first start since suffering his third career ACL tear.
Looking at their upcoming schedule, the offenses that they're set to face aren't going to give them much reprieve. Over the next three weeks, they'll face the Bears in Week 5, the Cowboys in Week 6, and the Lions in Week 7. At the rate at which they're going currently, it feels like an uphill climb for them to stay at or get over .500 on the season over that stretch.
Right now, the Packers are +225 to make the playoffs at DraftKings Sportsbook, which is a far cry from -146 odds they were before the season. I think that number will only continue to inflate as Green Bay moves forward throughout the rest of the year.
How Game Balls work: Six are awarded to standout players from the slate of teams that won their contests, and only one player on a team can get a game ball.
It was a monster day for the Cowboys receiver as Dallas went into Houston and pulled off a 34-30 win. Lamb was the straw that stirred the drink of the entire offense, and his 12-yard touchdown with 40 seconds left in regulation proved to be the game-winning score. Lamb is the first player in Cowboys history with at least 15 catches and 175 receiving yards in a game. He's also just the fourth player in NFL history to have a game with at least 17 catches, 180 receiving yards, and a touchdown.
WHO ELSE BUTE CEEDEE?!?! @DALvsHOU on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ODeK70fSFH
The Giants defense generated three turnovers in the 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals , and rookie linebacker Arvell Reese was at the center of most of the action. The No. 5 overall pick at the 2026 NFL Draft was everywhere in Week 4, leading the Giants with nine total tackles and also breaking up three passes. One of which was an interception in the closing minutes of the first half. That runover helped springboard a touchdown by the offense two plays later.
ARVELL REESE TAKES IT🔥 📺: CBS/Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/vm6RQr629J
Monangai saw a massive increase in attempts during Chicago's Week 4 win over the Jets, particularly after D'Andre Swift fumbled on the first possession of the third quarter. The second-year back took the ball on 30 of Chicago's 54 rushing attempts on the day. Those attempts set a new career high, while his 146 yards rushing were the second-most of his career. This was also Monangai's first game with multiple touchdowns.
Not many are running it better than Kyle Monangai today 😤 NYJvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/aOzQXt1CM5
Williams was instrumental for the Rams , who rallied from a 10-point deficit in Philadelphia to beat the Eagles . The veteran back scored both of the Los Angeles' fourth-quarter touchdowns, each of which came inside five minutes remaining in regulation. This was Williams' ninth-career multi-touchdown game and his 10 receptions set a new career high.
Kyren Williams POWERS IT IN FOR THE LEAD!! @LARvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LW85llHviL
Kenneth Walker III continues to dazzle this season and put on a show in Las Vegas as Kansas City remains perfect at 4-0. Walker set a new career high with 177 yards rushing and scored two touchdowns in the span of 20 seconds. He's the first Chiefs player to have at least 175 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns in a game since Jamaal Charles in 2009.
K9 GOES 77 YARDS 🔥 @KCvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1d8jxbAU0C
It was a career night for the Panthers receiver as he helped lead Carolina to a 32-26 win over the Lions. He set new career highs in both receptions and receiving yards. McMillan is also just the second player in franchise history with at least 10 catches, 150 receiving yards, and two receiving touchdowns in a game, joining Steve Smith Sr. in 2005.
BRYCE TO MCMILLAN FOR 6️⃣ @DETvsCAR on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7Owb2F0Uni
After lobbying for a pass interference call on a third-down incompletion, one of the officials in the Cardinals-Giants matchup appears to use a profanity towards Arizona tight end Trey McBride . Various clips on social media appear to show the official saying "[expletive] you" to McBride, which was caught on camera during the broadcast.
This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable. Players are consistently held accountable when the roles…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Eagles' offense completely collapses vs. Rams: Who's to blame and what needs to change
summary: The offensive meltdown after having the chance to deliver the knockout punch to Los Angeles highlights an uncomfortable truth in Philadelphia
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles ' 24-20 collapse at home against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4 on Sunday is a five-alarm fire for the back-to-back NFC East division champions.
Philadelphia had Los Angeles on the proverbial ropes. The Eagles led 20-10, and they had the ball on the two, just a couple of yards from scoring a touchdown that would land the knockout punch and put the game entirely out of reach with under eight minutes to play. At that moment, the NFL's Next Gen Stats assessed the Rams had a win probability as minuscule as 3.2%.
But Los Angeles stuffed quarterback Jalen Hurts on Philadelphia's famed "Tush Push" play before he threw incomplete on fourth-and-goal to force a turnover on downs. From that moment on, on their final two drives, the Eagles' offense lost a combined 14 yards. The Rams mounted consecutive, 10-play touchdown drives capped by rushing touchdowns from running back Kyren Williams .
The Eagles lost for the first time with Hurts when up double-digit points in a game's final five minutes, per CBS Sports Research. They were previously a perfect 41-0 in such situations (including the playoffs). The last time the Eagles lost in regulation when leading by at least 10 in the final five minutes was all the way back in a 2018 game against the Carolina Panthers , with Carson Wentz starting at quarterback.
So how did we get here? Let's take a look.
What killed the Eagles was a couple of things, starting with injuries and head coach Nick Sirianni's inability to assemble an offense that provides easy answers for Hurts. Running back Saquon Barkley , the player Philadelphia built its offense around, exited the game with a hamstring injury. Even before kickoff, the Eagles knew they would be without top wide receiver DeVonta Smith , tight end Dallas Goedert , offensive guard Landon Dickerson and right tackle Lane Johnson .
With all those players sidelined, Sirianni and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion couldn't build a game plan that provided Hurts and Co. with easy answers in high-leverage situations, particularly third down. The Eagles didn't convert on any of their 12 third downs, which is Philadelphia's most third-down attempts in a game without a conversion in the past 35 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. It's also the most third-down attempts without a conversion by any team in a game this decade, per NFL Media Research .
"Oh-for on third down, it hurts your drives. It hurts your being able to do the things you want to do on offense," head coach Nick Sirianni said postgame . "It can put you in a pressing situation at times. ... That to me is where we had our biggest issues here today was there."
How much did the Eagles' third-down inefficiency kill the offense? According to The Ringer , Philadelphia's 172 total yards of offense ranked as its lowest in a game in the last 12 years, while its 68 net passing yards are its lowest in a regular-season game in 23 years. On all of Philadelphia's third-down plays, it's clear Hurts didn't have the opportunity to execute key plays. He chalked it up to execution by the players, not an issue with the coaching staff.
"Poor execution. I don't think there's any other way to put it. ... I have to be better. I have to figure it out. However it looks, whatever that means," Hurts said postgame .
We'll save you the trouble of digging into every third-down play from the Eagles because it was ugly. But on third-down attempts, they had:
The most glaring execution issue came on the third-and-goal from the 2-yard line, in which the Eagles had a chance to put the game out of reach for good. Left guard Cam Jurgens, being too early coming off the line of scrimmage, threw off the timing of the Eagles' quarterback run play, and the Rams stuffed it for no gain. A play later, a Hurts incompletion led to a turnover on downs before Philadelphia netted minus-14 yards across their final two possessions.
Found it. Went through all the camera angles. The reason why the Eagles run failed on 3rd and goal from the 2 (which likely would have scored) is because Cam Jurgens slightly false started, but it wasn't called. He was on top of Hurts too quickly as he pulled, and his hand hit… pic.twitter.com/FnecKiGg2G
Including the goal-line miscue, the Eagles had six offensive possessions in the second half, and they ended as follows: punt, punt, turnover on downs, turnover on downs, punt, and turnover on downs.
However, Sunday afternoon's offensive woes after halftime weren't unique to Week 4. In their 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders , they scored 10 points. In their 24-20 Week 2 win at the Tennessee Titans , they scored 10 points. Across the last two weeks, a blowout "Monday Night Football" loss vs. the Chicago Bears and the loss against the Rams, Philadelphia went scoreless after halftime. The Eagles are now the league's worst second-half offense as a result.
Expected points added (EPA) per play
New offensive coordinator Sean Mannion came to Philadelphia after spending last season as the Green Bay Packers quarterbacks coach under Matt LaFleur. He also played for Sean McVay and the Rams and Kevin O'Connell and the Minnesota Vikings across his nine-season playing career.
He is a branch off the Shanahan-McVay coaching tree, which tends to have offenses that display heavy doses of motion, quarterbacks lining up under center and play-action passing. The scheme wants the looks for runs and passes to appear the same to defenses. That way, the quarterback should be able to easily run a given play as called and then take advantage of a defense that can't tell what's coming.
In Mannion's offense under Sirianni, the Eagles are just average in motion rate (45.2%, 15th in the NFL) while ranking bottom-five in under-center rate (31.3%, 28th) and dead last in play-action rate (14.5%). Running the Shanahan-McVay offense without its core staples is like trying to win the lottery: The odds are that it isn't going to work out for you.
In addition to needing better health across the board, the Eagles need Sirianni to let Mannion fully incorporate every element of his playbook that he would like. Otherwise, the easy answers won't be present in Philadelphia.
"I have a ton of confidence in Sean [Mannion]. He's going to wear a lot of this, no doubt. I'm going to wear a lot of this," Sirianni said postgame . "Our offense is going to wear a lot of this. You win together, you lose together. I have no complaints with what happened there today. There's opportunity for us to grow."
Sirianni's confidence in Mannion and what he wants to do needs to be more than lip service going forward. Otherwise, he'll have to explain why the Eagles missed the playoffs for the first time in his tenure come January.

title: NFL investigating referee cursing at Cardinals’ TE McBride
summary: The NFL has begun an investigation regarding a sideline referee cursing at Arizona Cardinals TE Trey McBride during the 36-24 loss to the New York Football Giants in New Jersey. The NFL Players Association, plus the NFL Referees Association, have gotten involved. RELATED: BEAKS & GEEKS CARDINALS VS. GIANTS If you watched the game, you […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Trey McBride #85 of the Arizona Cardinals takes a drink of water during warm ups (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL has begun an investigation regarding a sideline referee cursing at Arizona Cardinals TE Trey McBride during the 36-24 loss to the New York Football Giants in New Jersey. The NFL Players Association, plus the NFL Referees Association, have gotten involved. RELATED: BEAKS & GEEKS CARDINALS VS. GIANTS If you watched the game, you know what this moment was. The fourth quarter was winding down, and the Giants were clinging to a 27-24 lead, but had to punt. The kick was signaled a fair catch by KR Devin Duvernay at the 13-yard line, but instead, he let it hit the turf at the 15-yard line, and it was downed at the three-yard line. Now, the Cardinals had to drive the field in the hopes of getting into field goal range. QB Jacoby Brissett gained seven yards after being flushed from the pocket. On second down, RB Tyler Allgeier was tackled by NT DJ Reader after just a one-yard gain. This brought up third-and-two from the 11-yard line. Brissett dropped back to pass, and flung it in the direction of McBride just past the first down marker on the left side. Giants nickelback Dru Phillips picked up McBride off the line, grabbed his jersey, released, and was able to bat away the pass. He was obviously all over McBride and made physical contact without the tight end catching the ball. Before the ball even arrived, McBride was falling. Editor’s note: This play begins at the 13:07 mark McBride got to his knees while on the turf with his arms up at the 19-yard line, waiting for a pass interference call. None was thrown. McBride got to his feet and started barking at the line judge, Jeff Seeman, who was stationed at the 13-yard line in perfect view of the play. McBride then began to walk towards the line judge, jawing the entire time. The referee, who is situated behind the offense, also had a good view and did not throw his flag either. In the live feed, McBride was livid. Cardinals personnel had to pull him away from the line judge. Arizona was forced to punt. Since the conclusion of the Giants game, the NFL is in full review of the official’s apparent use of profanity directed at McBride in their little back-and-forth. Seeman was caught on camera cussing out McBride, who most likely was cussing out Seeman. It appears Seeman yelled out “F*** you” twice. Seeman is wearing a microphone. The NFLPA is asking the NFL to hold Seeman accountable for the verbal tirade. This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable. Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard. pic.twitter.com/vawHA8Jrlt — JC Tretter (@JCTretter) October 4, 2026 NFL players go through similar situations and suffer the consequences. The incompletion to McBride was obvious as Phillips pulled the tight end down as the ball approached. McBride normally has a pretty calm and cool demeanor during games, but it was evident what had happened with Seeman only six yards away from the action. The NFL Referees Association has not responded to any inquiries regarding this incident.
