title: Intriguing players to watch in Falcons vs. Saints
summary: A victory for the Atlanta Falcons in a high-stakes divisional clash against the New Orleans Saints will help strengthen the former’s position in the NFC South divisional race. That creates plenty of intrigue as five Falcons face critical questions in this Week 4 rivalry. QB Michael Penix Last week’s win over the Green Bay Packers […]
full_text: Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson (7) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Green Bay Packers on Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Falcons won the game, 35-14. Tork Mason/Green Bay Press-Gazette | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co A victory for the Atlanta Falcons in a high-stakes divisional clash against the New Orleans Saints will help strengthen the former’s position in the NFC South divisional race. That creates plenty of intrigue as five Falcons face critical questions in this Week 4 rivalry. QB Michael Penix Last week’s win over the Green Bay Packers was an impressive debut for Penix, but the Falcons still have 14 more starts to answer the big question facing them this year: Is Penix their long-term answer at quarterback ? That may take years to answer definitively, but Penix can steadily prove each week that he should remain the guy at present. Right now, he has an opportunity to lead the Falcons to another impressive road win in a hostile environment. Last week’s win in Lambeau increases hopes that Penix’s road woes are behind him. He and the rest of the Falcons offense have a great opportunity to pummel the Saints because of several favorable matchups. RB Bijan Robinson The most favorable matchup centers on Atlanta’s best player: Bijan Robinson, raising the question of whether Bijan can continue to dominate . Fresh off a 213-yard performance against the Packers, Robinson can keep shining against the Saints defense battling critical injuries to linebackers Kaden Elliss and Pete Werner. With Elliss’s blitzing abilities sidelined, Bijan should have more opportunities as a pass-catcher instead of being stuck in pass protection. With Werner’s injury making the Saints more vulnerable in coverage, Robinson can have another superhuman performance in primetime . OT Jake Matthews Given the positive outlook for the offense, the only thing that might derail Atlanta’s hopes is losing the battle in the trenches. Left tackle Jake Matthews’ battle against Chase Young will become pivotal to deciding the outcome of that battle. Matthews is making his 200th career start on Monday night , a remarkable achievement and the epitome of durability, reliability, and stability at a cornerstone position. However, Matthews has had a few too many uncharacteristic, unsightly losses to start in 2026, prompting questions over whether his trademark consistency remains. Young has been a difficult challenge for Matthews over the past few years, pressuring the latter and the rest of the Falcons offensive line to rise once more and win the battle up front. CB Avieon Terrell Rookie cornerback Avieon Terrell is another who must rise to the challenge, alongside the rest of the secondary against Saints wideout Chris Olave. For Terrell, the intriguing question is whether he will get more snaps playing outside cornerback against one of the league’s most productive pass-catchers . Terrell deserves more than the 13 snaps he got against the Packers, rotating with Mike Hughes and C.J. Henderson. While we can debate whether the Falcons’ trust in the Hughes-Henderson tandem is prudent, the veteran duo certainly brings value now, but Terrell’s youth and upside offer more for the future . Finding out whether Avieon can pick up the slack left by his injured elder sibling A.J.’s absence could pay off both on Monday night and in many games beyond. DT Gervon Dexter Speaking of paying off, Falcons defensive tackle Gervon Dexter just signed a very lucrative extension, leaving some to question if it’s premature. Despite Dexter’s brilliant start to the season, the raise puts more pressure on him to keep showing why he earned it . Dexter can do so by continuing to lead a surprising, impressive Falcons pass rush . If Dexter continues to be a force along the interior and put the quarterback on his back, it makes things easier for Terrell and others on the back end of the defense. A win in the Superdome will not only boost the Falcons’ divisional momentum but also keep building their confidence. Can you name other Falcons who excite and intrigue you in this primetime battle?

title: Falcons vs. Saints: What will Week 4’s win or loss mean for Atlanta?
summary: The Falcons may have stumbled out of the starting of the 2026 season, but they regained their footing in a major way on the national stage, against the Green Bay Packers. Behind the heroics of Bijan Robinson and Drake London, Atlanta declassed the hosts in their home opener and really gave the early portion of […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - DECEMBER 24: Mohamed Sanu #12 of the Atlanta Falcons catches the ball as Marshon Lattimore #23 of the New Orleans Saints defends during the second half of a game at the Mercedes-Benz Superdome on December 24, 2017 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Sean Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons may have stumbled out of the starting of the 2026 season, but they regained their footing in a major way on the national stage, against the Green Bay Packers. Behind the heroics of Bijan Robinson and Drake London, Atlanta declassed the hosts in their home opener and really gave the early portion of this season a much needed shot in the arm. Next, the prime time festivities continue as the Birds head into the most hostile of environments with a game against the New Orleans Saints, on what will be the 20th anniversary of the re-opening of the Superdome following Hurricane Katrina, on Monday Night Football. For those who remember, the Falcons spoiled the festivities on the 10th such anniversary on Monday night exactly a decade ago. Following the short week, Atlanta has the longest possible rest that’s not a bye week, with a full 11 days between their game in Green Bay and the one upcoming in New Orleans. Here is the scenario the Falcons face if they beat the New Orleans Saints in Week 3, as well as if they lose. If the Falcons win They will essentially pull a lot of the fanbase back in and regain a lot of trust, especially playing in what increasingly continues to look like a pathetic division. Kevin Stefanski will pass a major early test in the consistency department after we witnessed this team routinely lay an egg after nearly ever huge win last season. Speaking of that division, the Falcons will move to 2-2 overall as well as 1-1 in the NFC South. If the Carolina Panthers lose a game they are not favored in against the Detroit Lions on Sunday Night Football that would give the Birds sole possession of first place. With the Bucs and Panthers struggling and the Saints at that point already once vanquished, Atlanta would emerge as an early favorite to win their first division title since 2016. They would also win their third consecutive win head to head against New Orleans, the first such instance of that occurring since 2017, which is also the last time we watched Atlanta compete in the playoffs. This will also be the first time they have won four games in five tries head to head over the Saints since the turn of the millennia. If the Falcons lose Despite the coaching and front office turnover, this will just feel like another case of it being the “same old Falcons.” While this regime has nothing to do with the failures of their predecessors, the stigma and stench of this organization over the past decade of losing is hard to wipe away. It would be New Orleans who would have the early inside track in the division, going 2-2 and likely taking over first place. If Carolina were to also win their game, Atlanta would be trailing two separate teams in the standings while already possessing a worrisome 0-2 record against the NFC South. A Tampa victory puts the Birds in the cellar. New Orleans would put a stop to the modest two game losing streak they have over the Falcons and once again pull within one game of the all time head to head mark, making their new record against Atlanta 57-58, and putting them in position to tie things up with another win later in the season. The meat of the schedule comes right after this game, with Baltimore, Chicago and San Francisco coming to town. Going into that run of games at 1-3 and the arrow pointing down feels like it could be catastrophic before we even hit November.
author: Adnan Ikic

title: NFL predictions: Can the Falcons continue their winning streak against the Saints?
summary: There’s a very special matchup on Monday Night Football, as the Atlanta Falcons travel to take on the New Orleans Saints in Week 4. This is a heated rivalry between two teams that truly seem to loathe each other, and things only get more intense when both teams are in the thick of the NFC […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - JANUARY 04: Atlanta running back Bijan Robinson (7) runs the ball during the NFL game between the New Orleans Saints and the Atlanta Falcons on January 4th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There’s a very special matchup on Monday Night Football, as the Atlanta Falcons travel to take on the New Orleans Saints in Week 4. This is a heated rivalry between two teams that truly seem to loathe each other, and things only get more intense when both teams are in the thick of the NFC South race. That’s the case as we reach the start of October, as the Falcons and Saints both sit at 1-2 with an opportunity to take at least a share of the lead on Monday night. While the Falcons started out playing abysmal football with third-string quarterback Cooper Rush, they looked like a completely different offense with Michael Penix Jr. against the Green Bay Packers in Week 3. Meanwhile, the Saints have played pretty great offensive football, but dropped two games thanks to inconsistency and turnovers. FanDuel currently has Atlanta as 2.5-point road underdogs , showing how close this game is projected to be. This is a tough game to get a read on for a number of reasons. For one, we only have a one-game sample size of Atlanta with a real quarterback in 2026. Not exactly much to base opinions on, although the fact that it was a great game certainly bodes well. New Orleans also can’t seem to play a consistent game, as their 1-2 record and massive point swings from quarter to quarter suggest. There’s also the matter of a pretty large injury report for the Saints, who could be down multiple major contributors on Monday night. Falcons vs Saints Week 4 predictions There are a few reasons why I’m bullish on the Falcons to win this game. For one, Atlanta already took down Tyler Shough and a very similar Saints team twice in 2025—and I’d argue that the 2025 Falcons were not as well coached as this year’s iteration. The Falcons defense found ways to stymie Shough and the passing game, and that will be critical once again in this matchup. Second, Atlanta has been downright dominant in primetime. The Falcons are 8-3 on all primetime games going back through the 2024 season, and they’ve been particularly good on Monday Night Football. Atlanta is 4-0 on MNF since 2024, including two away games. If you take it back even further to 2015, the Falcons are a startling 9-1 (including a road win against the Saints in 2016). This team plays its best football under the bright lights, and I’d expect that to continue this week. Getting to the game itself, the Falcons match up well with the Saints in a number of key areas. Even though the passing game is coming along with Penix at the helm, the is still a team that wants to run the ball as much as possible with Bijan Robinson. Atlanta is second in rushing yards and seventh in yards per carry, and they did all that with no passing game to speak of in the first two weeks. Meanwhile, the Saints are a poor run defense, ranking 27th in rushing yards allowed and 27th in yards per carry allowed. This could be a recipe for disaster, particularly with a banged up front seven in New Orleans. On the other side, the Saints are very inconsistent running the football. New Orleans is league average in rushing yardage, but 21st in yards per carry at just 3.8. The Falcons hold the league’s best run defense, allowing the fewest rushing yards, yards per carry, and zero rushing TDs allowed. The Saints also just lost major free agent addition Travis Etienne Jr. to IR, putting everything on the plate of an aging Alvin Kamara. I wouldn’t rule out Kamara having one last big game against Atlanta, but it’s a very tough matchup. The Saints might be forced into a very one-dimensional game script on offense, which could lead to futher issues. Those issues start with the offensive line, which lost left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. for the season last week. The Raiders took advantage of his replacement, Asim Richards, particularly late in the game. Atlanta somehow possesses one of the league’s best pass rushes, and could feast on an undermanned Saints line—particularly if the run game is nonexistent. This is a key matchup for both sides: the Saints have thrived throwing the ball with Tyler Shough, and Atlanta is a bit undermanned in the secondary. There could be big play opportunities for New Orleans if they can protect the QB, but that might be a difficult task. I do expect New Orleans to put up quite a fight, but I think the culmination of injuries and a one-dimensional offense ultimately lead to more turnovers for Tyler Shough and the Saints offense. The Falcons manage to steal a hard-fought divisional matchup on Monday Night Football, thanks to dominance from Bijan Robinson and some clutch plays by the defense. I’m predicting the Falcons to emerge victorious, 27-24. Rise up with Falcons fans on the SB Nation app! title: Falcons-Saints MNF discussion: scouting the Ravens’ next opponent
summary: The Ravens are traveling to Atlanta next Sunday night, so tonight’s matchup between the Falcons and the Saints is a perfect opportunity for some early advance scouting. Here’s what I’ll be watching on Monday Night Football: Is Michael Penix really back? Michael Penix did not just have a solid 2026 debut against the Packers last […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - SEPTEMBER 24: Michael Penix Jr. #9 and Bijan Robinson #7 of the Atlanta Falcons looks on during a game at Lambeau Field on September 24, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Ravens are traveling to Atlanta next Sunday night, so tonight’s matchup between the Falcons and the Saints is a perfect opportunity for some early advance scouting. Here’s what I’ll be watching on Monday Night Football: Is Michael Penix really back? Michael Penix did not just have a solid 2026 debut against the Packers last week. He had one of the better performances of his young NFL career, averaging +0.24 EPA/dropback on his way to a 35-14 win. The Falcons’ offensive line is healthy, and their run game is absolutely humming (more on that later). But Penix’s individual play has been a rollercoaster over the last few years. Can he keep it up against a Ravens defense that, for all of their faults recently, has still played well against subpar quarterbacks. I just don’t know if Penix still belongs in that group. The Saints’ pass defense has been efficient this year, though they did hold the Ravens to just 233 yards through the air in Week 2. Tonight will be a solid test for his prospects against Baltimore next week. How is the Falcons run defense this good? The Falcons have absolutely demolished opposing rushing offenses so far this season. They have allowed just 47.7 yards per game, 2.8 yards per attempt, and two explosive rushes, all league-bests, along with a 21.2% stuff rate and -0.22 EPA/rush that rank among the NFL’s top three defenses. This is a wholesale reversal from last year’s bottom-10 unit. The reasons for the improvements are not fully clear. Kevin Stefanski retained defensive coordintor Jeff Ulbrich when he arrived in Atlanta this offseason, and the team did not heavily invest in their front-seven personnel. Acquiring Gervon Dexter Sr. from the Bears certainly upgraded the offensive line, but he has not been a dominant run defender to start his career. The Ravens will need to lean on their run game if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is sidelined next week. But their offensive line injures could put them at a significant disadvantage. Dwayne Ledford needs to be watching his former team closely tonight for any weaknesses he can exploit next week. Will Bijan Robinson force Jesse Minter to play more base defense? Jesse Minter’s defensive philosophy is built around stopping the run out of nickel (and even dime) personnel. In order to keep at least five defensive backs on the field as often as possible to slow opposing passing games, he relies on his safeties and linebackers to step up in run support. So far, the results have been mixed. The Ravens’ -0.09 EPA/rush allowed is the sixth-best mark in the league, but they rank eighth-worst with +0.55 rush yards over expected/attempt. That may not cut it against a Falcons offense that is averaging 5.0 yards per carry, -0.01 EPA/rush, and +0.70 RYOE/attempt, all among the best numbers in the NFL. Bijan Robinson has been a force of nature behind Ledford’s former offensive line, and Stefanski’s diverse run scheme has given opposing defenses nightmares. Atlanta will try to bully the Ravens out of their nickel/dime looks, so Minter and defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver will need to study tonight’s game to get their run defense on point for next Sunday night. title: Ravens enter Week 5 shrouded in injury uncertainty
summary: Seriously, did someone pay one of those Etsy witches to curse the Ravens again? Is there a new electric substation near The Castle? What is going on? For years, fans blamed Steve Saunders, the team’s former and oft-criticized strength and conditioning coach, for the injuries that seemed to crop up in Baltimore annually. He was […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 04: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens looks on during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Tennessee Titans at M&T Bank Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Seriously, did someone pay one of those Etsy witches to curse the Ravens again? Is there a new electric substation near The Castle? What is going on? For years, fans blamed Steve Saunders, the team’s former and oft-criticized strength and conditioning coach, for the injuries that seemed to crop up in Baltimore annually. He was dismissed before the 2024 season, and the Ravens were one of the healthiest teams in the league. Problem solved, right? Not so much. In 2025, the Ravens were battered by injuries, often with multiple affecting the same position group. At various times, the defensive line, tight end/fullback, inside linebacker, and cornerback rooms were all missing at least two players – not to mention Lamar Jackson’s four absences that effectively doomed the team’s playoff hopes. This season is off to a similar start. The Ravens are already selling with a slew of injuries, especially along their offensive line. By the start of Week 4, all three of the team’s preseason starting center candidates are on injured reserve, along with rookie receiver Ja’Kobi Lane and third-year cornerback T.J. Tampa. Left tackle Ronnie Stanley and left guard John Simpson have both been playing through injuries, and edge rusher Trey Hendrickson did the same with a fractured finger for two games before opting for surgery this week. Then, on Sunday, three more starters went down, including two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson with an ankle injury. Andrew Vorhees, who stepped in at right guard with Vega Ioane sliding to center, went down with a foot injury, and Marlon Humphrey hurt his calf. Tight end Durham Smythe, who has been a key blocker to start the year, also suffered an Achilles injury. Head coach Jesse Minter declined to offer any real updates on Sunday’s injuries outside of saying that Jackson would not be out “crazy long-term.” He has clearly embraced the team’s (understandable) desire to play injuries close to the chest. The team’s first Week 5 injury report will be posted on Wednesday and should provide more concrete information, along with any roster moves in the next 48 hours.

(Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images Offense QB: Lamar Jackson 33, Tyler Huntley 31 RB: Derrick Henry 40, Justice Hill 24 WR: Zay Flowers 47, Devontez Walker 44, Rashod Bateman 30, Elijah Sarratt 23, LaJohntay Wester 2 TE: Mark Andrews 37, Matthew Hibner 37, Durham Smythe 18, Josh Cuevas 18 OL: John Simpson 64, Vega Ioane 64, Roger Rosengarten 64, Ronnie Stanley 62, Emery Jones Jr. 36, Andrew Vorhees 28, Carson Vinson 2 Jackson played all 33 snaps in the first half but did not return after halftime with an ankle injury. Backup quarterback Tyler Huntley (31 snaps) played the final two quarters. The Ravens suffered another offensive line injury as Andrew Vorhees exited after 28 snaps with a foot ailment and did not return. That forced Emery Jones to plug in at right guard, where he played 36 snaps. Carson Vinson played two snaps as an extra blocker upon Ronnie Stanley’s return to the starting lineup. After playing limited snaps in Week 3, Zay Flowers’ workload increased as he led all wide receivers in playing time (47 snaps). Devontez Walker saw a big jump in playing time with 44 snaps, 14 more than Rashod Bateman (30 snaps). Bateman got shaken up at one point in the game. Rookie Elijah Sarratt played a season-high 23 snaps and made his first NFL catch for 13 yards. Chris Moore was inactive for this game. Matthew Hibner’s 37 snaps were a season-high at tight end and he matched Mark Andrews in playing time. The latter caught five passes with a touchdown grab, while Hibner recorded 34 receiving yards. Durham Smythe suffered an achilles injury after 18 snaps and did not return. If Smythe is out long-term, expect Hibner and Josh Cuevas to quickly take on larger roles. Defense DL: Nnamdi Madubuike 46, Travis Jones 33, Calais Campbell 31, Broderick Washington Jr. 19, John Jenkins 9 EDGE: Tavius Robinson 46, Mike Green 41, Zion Young 25, Ethan Burke 16 ILB: Roquan Smith 64, Trenton Simpson 36, Teddye Buchanan 11 CB: Nate Wiggins 64, Chidobe Awuzie 56, Chandler Rivers 29, Marlon Humphrey 8 S: Kyle Hamilton 64, Malaki Starks 59, Jaylinn Hawks 45, K’Von Wallace 2 In his second game back from injury, Madubuike again led the defensive line group in snaps (46). title: Winners and Losers from the Ravens’ Week 4 win over the Titans
summary: The Baltimore Ravens defeated the Tennessee Titans in Week 4, 24-18, but face a litany of injury questions in the aftermath of the game. There was far more good than bad for the Ravens in their win on Sunday, including a solid performance from a reshuffled offensive line. Winners Lamar Jackson: Jackson’s stellar game was […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 04: Mark Andrews #89 of the Baltimore Ravens celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Tennessee Titans during the first half at M&T Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens defeated the Tennessee Titans in Week 4, 24-18, but face a litany of injury questions in the aftermath of the game. There was far more good than bad for the Ravens in their win on Sunday, including a solid performance from a reshuffled offensive line. Winners Lamar Jackson: Jackson’s stellar game was ended early when an ankle injury sidelined him for the second half. Jackson completed 15 of 20 pass attempts for 222 yards and two touchdowns through the first two quarters. Zay Flowers: Flowers’ ascendance into the top tier of NFL receivers continued this week with another monstrous first half prior to Jackson’s injury. Flowers finished the game with 118 receiving yards and a touchdown on eight catches, including a 52-yard reception. Mark Andrews: Jackson’s old reliable tight end was just that on Sunday. Andrews finished the game with just 27 yards on five catches, but one of those was a touchdown catch, while another one came on a third down earlier in that same drive. Vega Ioane: The rookie first-rounder made his first start at center after desperation forced him there from right guard a week ago. Ioane was solid in the middle of the offensive line, helping to hold superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to a quiet day. According to PFF, Ioane allowed zero pressures on the day. Mike Green : The Ravens entered the game without Trey Hendrickson to rush the passer. Mike Green stepped up in his absence with six pressures on Cam Ward, according to PFF. While Green did not record a sack, he was close on several occasions, and a quick pressure on the first drive of the game led to a Trenton Simpson interception. Trenton Simpson: Simpson had one of two turnovers forced by Baltimore’s defense when he picked off Ward on the opening drive of the game. He also led the team in total tackles with nine. The fourth-year linebacker is earning himself a nice contract with his play so far this season. Nnamdi Madubuike: Madubuike looked like his old self in just his second game back, recording five pressures and two quarterback hits, according to PFF. Madubuike also had a drive-ending tackle on a fourth-down run at the goal line. Ethan Burke : The undrafted rookie got his first NFL start on Sunday and made the most of it with the team’s only sack of Ward. Malaki Starks: Starks has been a polarizing subject to start the season, but a strong game against Tennessee will hopefully quiet some of the noise. Starks recovered a forced fumble by Kyle Hamilton and recovered the Titans’ onside kick to end the game. He finished with six total tackles. Kyle Hamilton: After being on the receiving end of a questionable unnecessary roughness penalty, Hamilton bounced back to force a fumble on rookie first-round receiver Carnell Tate after a 33-yard catch-and-run. The do-it-all safety continues to be the best player on the Ravens’ defense. Tyler Loop: Loop followed up his late-game heroics in Brazil with the longest field goal of his career in Week 4, nailing a 64-yarder before halftime to give Baltimore a 24-7 lead. Loop later missed a field goal from 40 yards, but the main culprit seemed to be the hold by Ryan Eckley. The second-year kicker appears to have his confidence back after a difficult end to last season and a shaky preseason. Losers Elijah Sarratt: The rookie fourth-round receiver got his first catch of the regular season on Sunday with a 13-yard reception, but a handful of mistakes brought his day down. First, Sarratt was flagged for holding, wiping out a 29-yard scramble for Jackson. Next, Sarratt attempted and failed to catch a pass that was intended for Flowers on a route behind him in the two-minute drill before halftime. Lastly, Sarratt was involved in an illegal shift penalty as both he and Justice Hill were moving at the time of the snap. Devontez Walker: Walker had a holding penalty that brought back a successful third-down run by Derrick Henry. He also failed to haul in a catchable pass earlier in the game. Walker finished with one catch for 19 yards.
author: Dustin Cox

title: Ravens Report Card, Week 4: Imperfect performance in a gritty win
summary: The Baltimore Ravens improved to 3-1 with a six-point win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 4. After leading by 17 points at halftime, the Ravens were outscored 11-0 in the second half without their starting quarterback but hung on to emerge victorious for a second straight week. Here are report card grades for each […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 04: Zay Flowers #4 of the Baltimore Ravens rushes for a second quarter touchdown during the game against the Tennessee Titans at M&T Bank Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens improved to 3-1 with a six-point win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 4. After leading by 17 points at halftime, the Ravens were outscored 11-0 in the second half without their starting quarterback but hung on to emerge victorious for a second straight week. Here are report card grades for each position group from yesterday’s game. Quarterback: A- Lamar Jackson was in the midst of another heater in the first half of this game, completing 15-of-20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns. His completions and attempts were the exact same as last week, which he matched in just two quarters, and his passer rating was 144.2. In relief of Jackson after his ankle injury, Tyler Huntley completed eight passes for 63 yards. Huntley had one long first down pass to Rashod Bateman but otherwise his throws were screen-heavy and mostly around the line of scrimmage. Jackson’s performance before leaving the game was good enough to carry the grade for this group. Running Back: C+ The Ravens found running room hard to come by against the Titans’ defensive front. Derrick Henry was featured heavily against his former team with 23 carries but mustered only 73 rushing yards (3.2 yards per carry). His longest run went for 14 yards, and it was Henry’s second straight game averaging 3.4 yards per carry or less. The Ravens were able to convert some short yardage rushes with better efficiency in this game than last week. Justice Hill had two catches for 22 yards out of the backfield as a dump-off screen option. Wide Receiver: B + Zay Flowers had another dynamic performance with 118 receiving yards and a touchdown, reeling in a season-high eight catches. Flowers had a long reception of 52 yards on a sideline grab from Jackson. His effort carries the grade for this group, as has been the case so far this year. Rashod Bateman caught two passes for 46 yards but no other wideout made a substantial impact. Devontez Walker and Elijah Sarratt each had one first-down catch but also a miscue. Walker dropped a would-be long catch that was nearly intercepted as a result, and Sarratt committed a costly holding penalty that negated a big first-down scramble by Jackson scramble. Tight End: B- Mark Andrews had the second most catches of any Raven pass-catcher with five. While he gained only 27 yards, he made some nice short grabs over the middle of the field and also had a touchdown grab. Andrews appears to be in better athletic form than he was last year. Matthew Hibner recorded a season-high 34 receiving yards on two catches with a long gain of 25 yards. Veteran Durham Smythe exited the game early with an achilles injury that appeared to be serious and did not return. Offensive Line: C+ The Ravens’ mixed-and-matched offensive line had their best pass protection performance of the season. While the Titans did record a couple sacks and five quarterback hits, the impact of star defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons was limited. Vega Ioane held up well in his first start at center. The unit overall was not able to replicate a successful run blocking showing to match an improved pass blocking game. The Ravens were stuffed for minimal gain on rushing attempts repeatedly and weren’t able to open up significant holes for Henry. False starts and other penalties continue to be an issue from the offensive line as well. Defensive Line: B Nnamdi Madubuike had four tackles, two quarterback hits and a handful of pressures in his second game back, making strong plays at the line of scrimmage. Madubuike had one of the defensive plays of the game with a fourth-down run stuff at the team’s own goal line. Travis Jones surprisingly was blanked in the box score and Calais Campbell had just one tackle. The Ravens were stout against the run after the first couple drives of the game. They allowed just 85 rushing yards and 3.3 yards per carry. Edge Rusher: B He may not have finished plays with sacks, but Mike Green had an impactful performance. Green led the team with three quarterback hits and was charted for the most pressures as well. He flushed Cam Ward out of the pocket on multiple occasions and came up just short of bringing him down. Tavius Robinson and Zion Young had quiet showings, but undrafted rookie Ethan Burke picked up the slack. Burke recorded a sack, quarterback hit and tackle for loss. Linebacker: B+ A breakout season for Trenton Simpson continued in this game, as he recorded a team-high nine tackles and his first career interception. Simpson picked off an errant shovel pass on the opening drive of the game and returned it 24 yards. Roquan Smith had six total tackles but only one of which was solo. The Ravens’ linebackers were strong against the run, stuffing most attempts by Tony Pollard for minimal gain. Cornerback: C+ Marlon Humphrey exited the game early, on the second drive in the first quarter, with a calf injury and did not return. That left Chidobe Awuzie to slide into his starting role. Awuzie and nickel corner Chandler Rivers each had a pass breakup. The Ravens had some challenges defending rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate, who had a a career-best performance with nine catches for 145 yards. No other Titans’ wideout made a significant impact but Wan’Dale Robinson caught a late touchdown in the fourth quarter. Safety: B- Kyle Hamilton had another impactful all-around game with six solo tackles, one tackle for loss and a pass breakup. Hamilton forced a fumble against Tate to prevent a long reception and give the Ravens the chance to add three more points before halftime. Malaki Starks and Jaylinn Hawkins were more sturdy with open-field tackling, although Starks did have one notable whiff late in the fourth quarter. The Titans were not successful generating explosive plays for most of the game. Special Teams: C+ Tyler Loop’s confidence carried over from Brazil last week, nailing a career-best 64-yard field goal at the end of the second quarter. It was the longest field goal ever made at M&T Bank Stadium. Unfortunately, Loop later badly missed a 40-yard attempt in the fourth quarter that would have given the Ravens’ a 27-10 lead. Ryan Eckley had a busy day with six punts, four of which landed inside the 20 yard line with a longest punt of 56 yards.

title: Carolina Panthers 2027 NFL Draft Prospect Profile: Zabien Brown
summary: The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the […]
full_text: Nov 30, 2024; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide defensive back Zabien Brown (2) intercepts a pass intended for Auburn Tigers tight end Rivaldo Fairweather (13) during second half at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Alabama won 28-14. Mandatory Credit: Gary Cosby Jr.-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the Draft. In this series, we’ll only be looking at prospects the Panthers could seriously consider. This week our profile will focus on Alabama Crimson Tide cornerback Zabien Brown Bio Brown (6’0”, 192 lbs.) has the rare achievement of starting at Alabama as a true freshman. The former five star recruit from Santa Ana, CA really took over on the boundary last season, snagging a couple interceptions and providing elite run support for the position. The preseason First Team All-American and team captain has started out his true junior campaign with his usual dependability, with opposing teams avoiding his side of the field whenever possible. Strengths/Weaknesses Brown has the size and athleticism to stick on the boundary in the NFL, running a sub 4.4 forty yard dash at just under 200 lbs. Perhaps his biggest strength is his willingness and dependability against the run. He crashes without hesitation, more than willing to mix it up even against larger blockers. He’s also a very reliable tackler for a corner, making him great at setting the edge and forcing runs back inside. He has the press man skills to cover well enough, with both of his interceptions last year coming in press man (both of which he returned for touchdowns). Brown does get beat on occasion, often erased by his elite recovery speed. He can get a little handsy at the top of routes, especially against vertical threats. He’ll need to tighten up his technique in order to stick at the next level. While many scouts agree that Brown has a high ceiling, he is a bit of a project to truly reach that high potential. Projection Brown has the size, athleticism, and production to be a quality NFL corner. His elite potential will need some time and coaching to come to fruition, which is why he’s often mocked in the late first to mid second round at the moment. If he can show a little more consistency with his technique this year, his measurables could push him comfortably into the first. With Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson both on IR, and with Jackson’s contract expiring this year, the Panthers would be wise to invest a high pick in the cornerback position. Brown has a similar fearlessness to Jackson in the run game, which is important to have in your corners. If Will Lee III can grow and if Jaycee Horn can come back healthy, Brown could be a great addition to the cornerback room. What do you think, Panthers fans? If Zabien Brown is available when the Panthers select in the 2027 NFL Draft, should they take him? Sound off in the comments!

title: The Optimist: A statement win and a much needed rest
summary: The Carolina Panthers have had a long, heavy hangover since their triumphant, 15-1 2015 season. The 11 years since then have seen some of the most pitiful play, coaching, and management that this franchise has ever known. A lot of us were holding our breath entering the 2026 season, waiting to see if the career […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 4: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers looks to pass against the Detroit Lions prior to an NFL football game at Bank of America Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers have had a long, heavy hangover since their triumphant, 15-1 2015 season. The 11 years since then have seen some of the most pitiful play, coaching, and management that this franchise has ever known. A lot of us were holding our breath entering the 2026 season, waiting to see if the career of Bryce Young was going to take an incremental step forward—as he had managed each of the past two season—or if Young was simply going to take his place as one more sad chapter of the last decade. Instead, he may finally have found the first steps on the path to being the Panthers’ next franchise quarterback. 2026 may be the year of putting to rest all the sad streaks and facts of the last decade. January saw the first playoff game in over a decade. Last night was Charlotte’s first time hosting Sunday Night Football in over a decade. Now, after four games, Young leads the league with 1,268 yards passing, nine touchdowns, and only two interceptions. He is one of the top passers in the league right now and will, for the first time in over a decade for a Panthers quarterback, legitimately be in MVP conversations for at least the next two weeks. As we have said with every benchmark he has met thusfar in his career, what happens next is on him. Beating the Lions to pull up to 2-2 feels like a season-saving moment. 1-3 with more holes due to injury than a screen porch—even in light of three stellar offensive performances—would have felt defeating. Instead, Ejiro Evero’s defense used a preseason roster to hold off one of the best offenses in the NFL. They held the Lions to just 19 points before losing Jaelan Phillips to a concussion. The offense put up 22 points before 2026 first round pick and second string right tackle Monroe Freeling went down with an unspecified knee injury, leaving third stringer Stone Forsythe to match up against one of the best defensive linemen in the NFL in Aidan Hutchinson. They gutted out the rest of the game with a 10-7 margin to keep the win. In a game where they came in with two hands behind their backs, they lost another leg, shot themselves in the remaining foot with two missed extra points, and still won. What’s not to be optimistic about? There is no break down of what I did and didn’t like this week. Let’s just celebrate. We’ll dig into injury timelines and updates more during the bye, but the bottom line is that the Panthers are poised to get healthier and be a stronger team when they come back to face the Eagles in Week 6 and the rest of their schedule beyond. Almost all of us predicted the team would be 2-2 heading into the bye, but I guarantee that none of you predicted it would look like this—or that it would feel so promising.

full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Marcus Davenport #52 of the Chicago Bears arrives prior to the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Defensive end Marcus Davenport made his Chicago Bears debut yesterday after being elevated from the practice squad, and today he requested to be released. The Bears granted the wish, and with the release official, Davenport intends to retire, per a report from Ian Rapoport. Against the Jets, the 30-year-old Davenport logged 12 snaps on defense, making a tackle, and he played 1 snap on special teams. The Bears signed him in August and brought him along slowly to ensure he had his conditioning right after battling injuries over the previous few years. He was among their final roster cuts and signed to the practice squad before the season. Davenport also played for the New Orleans Saints, the Minnesota Vikings, and the Detroit Lions. The Bears now have an opening on their 16-man practice squad, and one opening on their 53-man roster after placing Braxton Jones on injured reserve last week. The Bears have three potential options for the active roster this week: defensive end Shemar Turner, linebacker Noah Sewell, and defensive back Kyler Gordon are all eligible to come off the PUP list. All three players participated fully in practice last Friday.

title: Bears offense among NFL’s best despite red zone issues
summary: That’s three weeks in a row the Chicago Bears have stumbled in the red zone, and it’s something head coach Ben Johnson recognized and addressed in his opening remarks at his postgame press conference before he even fielded any questions about their win over the New York Jets. “Obviously, we got to get better in […]
full_text: Oct 4, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III (10) makes a catch for a first down against New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick (29) during the first quarter at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect That’s three weeks in a row the Chicago Bears have stumbled in the red zone, and it’s something head coach Ben Johnson recognized and addressed in his opening remarks at his postgame press conference before he even fielded any questions about their win over the New York Jets. “Obviously, we got to get better in the red zone,” he said. “It’s been really three weeks in a row that we’ve left points out there. So that’ll be a major emphasis for us going forward, as well as the turnovers. We can’t have those on offense, but overall, like I said, great job finding a way to get to three and one.” The Bears gave the ball away twice, once on a Tyson Bagent interception, and once on a D’Andre Swift fumble. Swift seemed to be sidelined after that, and I’d imagine Bagent’s film session will be ugly, because he had a couple of other poor decisions. But all in all, it was a solid performance for Chicago’s number two QB. The Bears have one of the best offenses in the NFL, and each week they’ve made mistakes that cost them points. Whether that be penalties, execution, or bad play calls, they need to self-scout, clean some stuff up, and take the offense to the next level. And considering no team in the NFL has more yards than they do through 4 games, what would that next level look like? Check out our latest Bear & Balanced right here (or on YouTube), live at 6:00 p.m. CT as we talk through the game. The 3 Bears: You all know the story of the Three Bears, don’t you? title: Bears vs. Jets Game Balls: Monangai Shines, D-Line Creates Havoc
summary: Despite starting their third quarterback of the young season, the Chicago Bears defeated the New York Jets on Sunday afternoon at Soldier Field in dominating fashion. By now, you’ve probably heard the insane stats. The Bears ran 89 plays on offense, the most by a Bears team since 1997. And the team’s 34 first downs […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 4: Kyle Monangai #25 of the Chicago Bears reacts during the fourth quarter against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 4, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Despite starting their third quarterback of the young season, the Chicago Bears defeated the New York Jets on Sunday afternoon at Soldier Field in dominating fashion. By now, you’ve probably heard the insane stats. The Bears ran 89 plays on offense, the most by a Bears team since 1997. And the team’s 34 first downs (most in franchise history) exceeded the amount of total plays run by the Jets (32). While Tyson Bagent was more than adequate under center, it was the Bears’ run game that continued to dominate. And on the other side of the ball, the Bears defense continued their ascent to the top of the league rankings in shutting down a Jets offense that had previously shown flashes under the command of QB Geno Smith and star receiver Garrett Wilson. Let’s get to the game balls. Offense Game Ball: RB Kyle Monangai It simply couldn’t go to anyone else. Monangai was the Bears’ work horse in this one, carrying the ball 30 times for 146 yards and two touchdowns. He also had one catch for four yards. Importantly, Monangai was able to come through in short yardage situations, something that D’Andre Swift failed to do on the team’s first possession when the Bears were marked short of the goal line on two running attempts from inside the 3 yard line, turning the ball over on downs. Kyle Monangai delivers for the @ChicagoBears 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/R8oOsg2tyl — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) October 4, 2026 Kyle Monangai is bullying my Jets. He’s a freight train. Ben Johnson outclassing Aaron Glenn. pic.twitter.com/gR49TWvcKI — John Frascella (Football) (@NFLFrascella) October 4, 2026 KYLE MONANGAI IS NOT REAL😱🤯 pic.twitter.com/lipokFp5Cy — CHGO Bears (@CHGO_Bears) October 4, 2026 Monangai runs with intensity and a low center of gravity, which should make him the team’s go-to in short yardage situations. It was clear as the game wore on, Monangai was the most-trusted running back on the field for head coach Ben Johnson. Monangai did exit the game with a thumb injury late in the game. The team is currently classifying it as a day-to-day injury. Honorable mention to Darnell Wright and Jonah Jackson, both of whom who were obliterating the Jets defense throughout the day. Defense Game Ball: DE Dayo Odeyingbo This was a tough one given the fact that the Bears defense was only on the field for 32 plays on Sunday. LB Devin Bush even called the game “boring” for that reason. A good problem to have, to be sure! If we’re being honest, rookie Dillon Thieneman could win this award almost every week. He led the team in tackles (7) this week. Devin Bush received a game ball from Ben Johnson after the game, deservedly so. He had a sack, a tackle for loss, a QB hit, and four tackles total. But I’m going to look to the defensive line, where Dayo Odeyingbo has indeed been motivated. Coming off of last year’s Achilles injury, he’s made a noticeable impact throughout the early part of the season. Against the Jets, he had a sack, a tackle for loss, a pass defended, and two tackles. On the play where Austin Booker had the sack after jumping high into the air, Dayo commanded the attention of three members of the New York offensive line as he pushed into the backfield. #Bears have unlocked Dayo on the inside on passing downs. He chased down Geno Smith to the sideline and is credited with a sack. According to PFF, Odeyingbo leads the team with 12 total pressures and 3 sacks. #MOTIVATED pic.twitter.com/jXRRklua0r — Nicholas Moreano (@NicholasMoreano) October 5, 2026 Speaking of Booker, I’d throw an honorable mention to him this week. title: 10 Bears Takes: Ben Johnson beats Aaron Glenn, Soldier Field Domination, and More
summary: Following another dominant win at Soldier Field, the Chicago Bears exit the first quarter of their regular season at 3-1. Although many will look at the box score and see a 23-12 final score, make no mistake: the Bears dominated this game from start to finish. If anything, they were their own worst enemy on […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 4: Kyle Monangai #25 of the Chicago Bears celebrates with teammates after scoring a touchdown during the second quarter against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 4, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following another dominant win at Soldier Field, the Chicago Bears exit the first quarter of their regular season at 3-1. Although many will look at the box score and see a 23-12 final score, make no mistake: the Bears dominated this game from start to finish. If anything, they were their own worst enemy on Sunday. With a quality start to the season locked in, all eyes will turn to the health of their starting quarterback heading into a big Week 5 matchup against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Before we turn the page on their second-straight win, let’s take a deeper dive into Sunday’s game and what to expect next in Week 4’s edition of 10 Bears Takes. 1. After coaching on the same staff for four years in Detroit, the first matchup goes to Ben Johnson, and it wasn’t really that close. It’s always hard to label an 11-point win as “dominant,” but that’s exactly what this team did on Sunday. From the opening whistle until the final kneel-down, the Bears dominated this game, and despite the score, it never felt relatively close. Much was made about this matchup coming into the weekend, especially on a short week for Chicago. Conventional wisdom would have said that two head coaches who spent four years together on the same team would have made for a much closer matchup. Even if these two teams are in different spots at this juncture of this season, Johnson owned the matchup of his offense versus Glenn’s defense. Still, Dennis Allen also schooled Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich, despite some advantageous field position for the Jets coming off their two takeaways. As I wrote about last week, it’s time for fans to ignore past troubles and embrace the fact that this is a very good football team. Even more encouraging, they’ve yet to come close to reaching their ceiling. Penalties, self-inflicted mistakes, and injuries have held this group back from playing their best football. All things considered, that’s pretty impressive considering they are 3-1 and exit Week 4 with a +47 point differential. Maybe that’s why many, including myself, came away from Sunday’s game wanting more. Despite having more rush attempts (54) than the Jets had plays run (32), an 11-point margin of victory feels light. It took the Jets until the third quarter to break the 100-yard threshold, and outside of Geno Smith’s 58-yard bomb to Isaiah Williams late in the fourth quarter, the Jets offense managed just 109 yards on 31 plays. Let that sink in for a minute- the Bears had 153 yards over their first two possessions in the first quarter. Simply put, the Bears controlled every aspect of this game (outside of the turnover margin), including 345 more yards and 57 more plays, to go with a heavily lopsided 25:30 time of possession advantage. Considering the dominance displayed on Sunday, it’s only a matter of time before the scores start reflecting it. For now, Johnson will gladly take Round 1 against his former coaching mate. Now, we wait to see if there will ever be a Round 2. 2. With Caleb Williams’ status still up in the air for the next few games, Ben Johnson might want to reevaluate the quarterbacking situation heading into a crucial Week 5 matchup in Green Bay. If you look at the box score, you might have come away impressed with Tyson Bagent’s overall numbers. After all, he finished the game 25-of-34 (73.5%) for 268 passing yards, a 7.9 yards-per-attempt average, and the lone interception. That said, what didn’t show up on the stat sheet might warrant a more extensive conversation about who should start in Week 5, assuming Williams isn’t ready to go. I don’t want this to sound like I’m dumping on Bagent, but evaluating his overall performance needs nuance. On the plus side, when Bagent was accurate and on time, he was responsible for multiple big plays downfield. Aside from the one sack he took earlier in the game, his protection was fantastic, and for the most part, Bagent’s footwork and overall mechanics looked good. The bigger issue is that because of his lack of arm strength, when he doesn’t play on time or isn’t pinpoint accurate with his throws, the margin for error is much thinner than it would be with most starting-caliber quarterbacks in the league. Bagent had three interceptions that penalties would have wiped out, though one came on a “free play”. The issue is that he had a few other close throws that could have gone the other way, too. Now, don’t get me wrong- Case Keenum was far from perfect last Monday night, and had a few passes that should have gone for interceptions as well. The difference is that, for the rest of the time, Keenum was extremely accurate and rarely late to his reads. Aside from age, Bagent and Keenum play similarly. They must have good protection, must play on time, and must be more accurate than most quarterbacks because of their lack of natural arm strength. If the Bears decide to give Bagent another look in Green Bay, it’s best to trust the head coach. So far, he’s 2-0 in games started with backups, which is something he had yet to experience coming into the season. That said, it’s worth wondering if a veteran like Keenum would give them a better chance to win, especially in a big game on the road against their most-hated rival. My hunch is it’ll be Bagent again (assuming Williams still isn’t ready), but I hope there are at least some honest conversations at Halas Hall this week before they decide. 3. After back-to-back games without a consistent run game, Johnson made a concerted effort to get things back on track. I’d say- mission successful. Unlike Week 3, Johnson leaned on his run game early and often on Sunday afternoon. In fact, they ended up with a 54-36 run-pass split when the clock struck zero. Since 2025, the Bears have four games with 230-plus rushing yards, according to an NFL Researcher on X. No other team has more than two in that same time span. Last week, it felt like the Eagles were able to key in on their run game without a mobile quarterback under center. This week, Bagent’s athleticism and early success allowed Johnson more freedom to grind the clock and bludgeon the opposing defense. In total, four runners combined for 232 yards on the ground, two touchdowns, and a 4.3-yard-per-carry average. Even with D’Andre Swift being benched for his second-half fumble, the Bears’ two-headed monster combined for 204 yards and a quality 4.5 yards per carry average. Heck, even Roschon Johnson factored in on the 232-yard total. Both Swift and Monangai have proven to be very good players, but this scheme lends itself to maximizing opportunities, which is promising for this season’s prospects. Even once Williams is back under center, expect this team to keep establishing the run and not get away from it. That’s not something we have been able to say in the past, but as we’re learning, Ben Johnson isn’t your typical offensive mind. 4. Despite dominating all but one series, their goal-line struggles and turnovers made this game look a whole lot closer than it was. The “record” numbers have kept pouring in since the game ended, and they all heavily favor the Bears. Some of those examples: The Bears didn’t punt in a game for the first time since 2014. The play differential (+57) was the fourth biggest in a game since 1970. Their 89 plays were the most in a single game since 199,7 when they ran 90 plays against… You guessed it- the Jets. The Jets’ 32-play run was the fourth-fewest run by a team, according to Pro-Football-Reference. The Bears had more first downs (34) than the Jets had plays (32). This is just the second time this has happened in the Super Bowl era. The Jets had just 45 seconds of time of possession in the fourth quarter. Although I’m…

title: Bears vs. Jets: Inside the Snap Counts, Stats, and Chasing Records
summary: The Chicago Bears entered Week 3 against the New York Jets as the NFL’s number one ranked rushing team, averaging 184.3 yards per game. Chicago’s offensive line paved the way for 232 yards on the ground, bringing their average up to 196 this year. They still have a long way to go in the 2026 […]
full_text: Oct 4, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai (25) runs with the ball against the New York Jets during the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Mike Dinovo-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Chicago Bears entered Week 3 against the New York Jets as the NFL’s number one ranked rushing team, averaging 184.3 yards per game. Chicago’s offensive line paved the way for 232 yards on the ground, bringing their average up to 196 this year. They still have a long way to go in the 2026 season, but they are on pace to break the franchise record for rushing yards in a season set in 2022: 3,014 yards (177 per game). I’ll have more on this tonight on Bear & Balanced, so join us at 6 ! Speaking of records, the Bears set a franchise record with 34 first downs. Those 34 first downs were more than the 32 total offensive plays the Jets ran, making this the second game in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) in which a team had more first downs than its opponent had offensive plays. The Bears may have won by only 11 (23 to 12), but it was a dominant performance by the Navy and Orange. They had more yards (492 to 157), more plays (89 to 32), and had the time-of-possession edge (42:45 to 17:15), while holding the Jets to only 7 first downs. The 7 first downs are the fewest a Bears team has allowed since December 14, 1991, when they allowed 7 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Jets only had the ball in the fourth quarter for 45 seconds. Chicago had fewer penalties, with just 4 for 29 yards (both season lows), compared to New York’s 12 for 76. The Bears were 7 for 15 (46.7%) on third downs, and 2 of 3 on fourth downs. The only place the Jets had the edge was the turnover margin, which they won 2-0. Let’s look at the Bears’ playing time breakdowns and a few individual stats from the game. OFFENSE This was Tyson Bagent’s first *start in over a thousand days, but unlike Case Keenum, who also went over a thousand days between starts, Bagent didn’t have over a decade and 81 games of experience to pull from. This was just Bagent’s fifth career start, so I’ll judge his performance accordingly. Bagent was fine, but he was also lucky he didn’t throw multiple interceptions. One of his could-have-been-interceptions came off a free play that he went deep on, and the other was a direct result of a defensive penalty that let the defender get in position. But he had two others that were awful decisions, negated by penalties. His actual pick was on a throw he was a bit late and behind on. But he also had some really nice moments working his progressions. The throw down the seam to Rome Odunze got them points before the half. The aforementioned deep shot on a free play is a veteran move. He worked his cadence well. His timing on screens was good. All in all, this game is a good learning experience for him and the Bears. The running game was brilliant, led by Kyle Monangai’s career-high 30 carries, which came after Swift was seemingly pulled after his fumble. When asked if Swift was shaken up on the play he fumbled on — he seemed to get up slowly, and he had a knee issue earlier in the week — head coach Ben Johnson said, “No, no, nothing, nothing like that.” *The record books will technically list Case Keenum as the starter at quarterback for this game, unless they asterisk it at some point because Bagent also started the game. Also, how great is it that Ben Johnson basically started Keenum just to troll the insiders who reported that Bagent would start? DEFENSE Rookie safety Dillon Thieneman has either led or tied for the team lead in total tackles in every game of his young NFL career. That’s not necessarily a good stat for a safety, but he’s been used up close to the line of scrimmage plenty, and he’s flying up in run support while rallying to the ball in the secondary. I’ve been pleasantly surprised at Dayo Odeyingbo this season. While his sack was a gift this week because Geno Smith ran out of bounds, Dayo was in hot pursuit. It also gives him a team-leading 3 sacks in 4 games. Chicago held the Jets to 0-8 on third-down tries, and The Athletic’s Kevin Fishbain shared that this was the first time since October 5, 1997, that they didn’t allow a single third-down conversion. They held Jets QB Geno Smith to just 8 of 15 (53.3%) passing for 119 yards. Before Sunday, he was leading the NFL with a 75.5% completion percentage. Marcus Davenport got a stat in his season debut! I wasn’t expecting much, but I thought he looked decent out there. SPECIAL TEAMS* *The above image has players who only played in the third phase. Cairo Santos hit 3 field goals and both extra points. Tory Taylor did nothing but hold for field goals and extra points. The Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs had this interesting nugget: This is just the fourth time in the Super Bowl era that the Bears have gone through a game without punting, and the first time since September 28, 2014, against the Green Bay Packers. Zavion Thomas had 4 kickoff returns for 70 yards, and Kalif Raymond had 16 yards on 2 punt returns. Daniel Hardy had 2 special teams tackles. Rookie tight end Sam Roush had a holding penalty on a kickoff, and he had a tackle on the Bagent interception. To check out the complete Bears vs. Jets box score, I find ESPN’s site is easy to navigate. All statistics and snap counts, as well as the accompanying pictures, are taken directly from the NFL’s Game Statistic and Information System.

title: Bears lay the smack down on Jets, take control on both sides of the ball
summary: Coming out of Week 4, the Chicago Bears have a 3-1 record in the 2026 season. Each of those three wins has come with a different quarterback at the helm. On Sunday, Tyson Bagent was the one who got the job done in their 23-12 victory over the New York Jets. The Bears utterly dominated […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 4: Rome Odunze #15 of the Chicago Bears runs with the ball during the second quarter against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 4, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming out of Week 4, the Chicago Bears have a 3-1 record in the 2026 season. Each of those three wins has come with a different quarterback at the helm. On Sunday, Tyson Bagent was the one who got the job done in their 23-12 victory over the New York Jets. The Bears utterly dominated the time-of-possession battle, squeezing out 42 minutes and 45 seconds of the 60-minute period to give the Jets very little time to get anything going on offense. It helped that Chicago’s defense held New York to just 157 yards and stopped the offense on each of its seven third-down conversion opportunities. Though the offense had its flaws, there was still more than enough firepower to make up for the absence of Caleb Williams in the lineup. As of this writing, the Bears ranked No. 4 among 28 NFL offenses in PFN Offense Impact grading in Week 4, and they ranked No. 6 in PFN Defense Impact grading. These are some of my takeaways from Sunday’s win, which match up with what the analytics have to say. Ben Johnson is a wizard, and Tyson Bagent is good enough The efficiency of the Bears’ offense on Sunday was commendable. The team certainly took a run-heavy approach against the Jets, rushing the ball 54 times against 35 dropbacks to pass. Ben Johnson did a fantastic job of realizing where he had the leverage, and utilizing his athletic offensive line and impressive running back tandem to run it down New York’s throats. That helped Chicago dominate the time of possession battle, but when Bagent did drop back to pass, he was effective in moving the ball down the field. Bagent completed 73.5% of his passing attempts on Sunday, throwing for 268 yards in the process. Of his 34 passing attempts, ten of them went more than 10 air yards past the line of scrimmage, and he completed seven of them. I’d argue that Case Keenum’s performance in Week 3 was slightly better from a decision-making perspective, but Bagent was tested with more opportunities to move the ball down the field, especially in the first half of the game. In all, Bagent was perfectly serviceable. He wasn’t great, as made evident by his lack of passing touchdowns and his interception (a total which would have been four if three of them hadn’t been called back for penalties). There is no quarterback controversy in Chicago, and Bagent is a backup-caliber quarterback. And that’s perfectly fine. There’s a lot of value in a solid backup, especially one who understands Ben Johnson’s offense like Bagent does. The Kyle Monangai showcase Kyle Monangai out-carried D’Andre Swift 30 carries to 15 on Sunday, which is the largest gap Monangai has ever taken ahead of Swift in a single game. Once Swift coughed up a fumble in the third quarter — his second in three weeks — he didn’t touch the ball once for the remainder of the game. Monangai handled the load as the running back chosen to wind the clock down for the Bears, and he executed. On his 30 carries, Monangai finished with 146 rushing yards, two rushing touchdowns, and an average of 4.9 yards per carry. He was decisive running in between the tackles, he was powerful bouncing off of defenders, and he showed off his trademark determination to battle for every yard he got. He already had an impressive performance before the Bears pulled Swift from the game, but from that point on, his consistency helped Chicago squeeze out the clock and put the game on ice. Rome Odunze makes a statement There’s admittedly very little to take away from the Bears’ defensive performance compared to most weeks, though credit belongs to the secondary for shutting down the Jets’ passing attack for much of the afternoon. Instead, I wanted to give a shoutout to Rome Odunze, who put together one of his best career performances to date on Sunday. Odunze finished the game with six catches for 94 yards, hauling in all but one of his seven targets and averaging 15.7 yards per reception. His fluidity shined across the middle of the field, and he demonstrated his underrated ability to create separation pretty consistently. The big difference was his hands, as he’s had issues with drops over the course of his NFL career. Drops were not an issue for him on Sunday, and he put up legitimate WR1 production as a result. With how many mouths the Bears have to feed in their offense, it can be easy to overlook Odunze sometimes, but do so at your own risk. He showed improvement in his biggest weakness this week, which allowed him to maximize his existing strengths.

title: More proof Amarius Mims is having an elite season for the Cincinnati Bengals
summary: Cincinnati Bengals offensive tackle Amarius Mims was already an ascending player last year, but he has taken it to another level in 2026. Against the Jaguars, Mims continued his elite play, allowing no pressures on 58 dropbacks. According to Next Gen Stats, Mims has allowed a 3% pressure rate this season, the lowest of any […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals offensive tackle Amarius Mims was already an ascending player last year, but he has taken it to another level in 2026. Against the Jaguars, Mims continued his elite play, allowing no pressures on 58 dropbacks. According to Next Gen Stats, Mims has allowed a 3% pressure rate this season, the lowest of any offensive tackle with 100+ pass blocks. The Bengals should be very glad entering Week 5 with what seems to be an elite offensive tackle on the right side. He still needs to do a bit of work in the run game to reach the rank of the truly top-tier offensive tackles, but he clearly is on the way to getting there. The Bengals offensive line is looking good with Dylan Fairchild and Mims both looking good and having a couple of years of team control, along with Orlando Brown Jr., who has been a decent left tackle and is on a modest deal. There will be questions about replacing or extending Dalton Risner and Ted Karras in the offseason, but the Bengals have a good group of young offensive linemen to build off of. The key for the long term is keeping Joe Burrow healthy. Mims is a good start for that, and the Bengals have shown improvement in their ability to draft offensive linemen after struggling for a while. Another strong draft could set up the Bengals’ offensive line for years after their big hit with Mims. Amarius Mims did not allow a single pressure on 58 pass blocks against the Jaguars, the most pass blocks without pressure in a game in seven seasons. Mims has allowed a 3.0% pressure rate this season, the lowest of any tackle with 100+ pass blocks. #WhoDey pic.twitter.com/VaoROD4ZTh — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) October 5, 2026

title: 3 things we learned from the Bengals’ wild loss to the Jaguars
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals (2-2) are nowhere near a finished product, but they might not have enough time to figure out some of their persistent problems. Here’s what we learned from their second straight loss, a wild 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The lack of a running game has made this team rely on hero […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - OCTOBER 04: Chase Brown #30 of the Cincinnati Bengals is tackled by Rayuan Lane III #25 and Branson Combs #50 of the Jacksonville Jaguars during the game at Paycor Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals (2-2) are nowhere near a finished product, but they might not have enough time to figure out some of their persistent problems. Here’s what we learned from their second straight loss, a wild 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The lack of a running game has made this team rely on hero ball At first, it was fun to watch Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins make toe-dragging sideline grabs. But then, after watching the Bengals rely on similarly athletic sideline catches from Higgins, Mike Gesicki, and Mitch Tinsley just to create any semblance of an offense against the Jaguars, something became clear: that’s the only way they know how to score points. Whether you want to blame Chase Brown, his blocking, or both, the running game is doing next to nothing. Brown got just 10 yards on nine carries against Jacksonville. Though he’s known as a speedy, dual-threat back, his longest run of the year is 13 yards and his longest catch is 12 yards. There is no way you’re going to consistently be able to score points with such a lack of explosion at the RB position. Turnovers at the worst possible moments are tanking the season In Week 3, it was the muffed punt and the Joe Burrow fumble that ended the game. In Week 4, it was a bizarre fourth-quarter Burrow interception. Yes, mistakes happen, and even the best quarterbacks misfire on occasion. But these seem to be an indication of a sort of nervousness or lack of preparation for the moment. Something is going on with the Bengals mentally, and they need to get more confident in what they’re doing on the field so that they can make level-headed decisions in the clutch. The tackling issue isn’t going away The Bengals’ front office did a nice job of fixing the defensive line. Dexter Lawrence, Boye Mafe, and others are consistently getting into the backfield to make plays and create pressure. The problem is everything after that. Dax Hill and DJ Turner are doing their part, but outside of them, the Bengals can’t seem to stop pass catchers. The strength of the Bengals' defensive back 7 is DJ Turner and Dax Hill, right? They got targeted 3 times in this game. The Jags just threw the ball at everyone else. Linebackers: 8 targets Safeties: 6 targets Edges dropping into Cov: 3 targets The other CBs: 2 targets — Goodberry (@JoeGoodberry) October 5, 2026 Most significantly, the Bengals still can’t stop tight ends or get guys down on the first attempt. Tight ends, in particular, have posed a problem. Dalton Schultz had 140 yards against Cincinnati in Week 2. Darnell Washington had a 47 yard catch and run down the sideline where he evaded four tacklers to set up the game-winning field goal in Week 3. And then Brenton Strange put up 95 yards for the Jaguars in Week 4. Giving up easy yards to opponents while not being able to get them for yourself is a bad recipe in the NFL. Zac Taylor and the coaches have to figure out how to make things easier on their players quickly for this team to stay in contention.

Gesicki owned up to the mistake after the game: “It was a […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) and tight end Mike Gesicki (88) celebrate a Burrow touchdown rush in the fourth quarter of the NFL Week 4 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Jacksonville Jaguars at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. The Bengals fell to 2-2 on the season with a 22-17 loss at home. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co One of the big things to happen at the end of the end of the Cincinnati Bengals loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars was what appeared to be a miscommunication between Joe Burrow and tight end Mike Gesicki on the final series of downs. Gesicki owned up to the mistake after the game : “It was a play that, because of personnel shuffling, normally that’s Tee (Higgins) running that. So then, I went we moved to Tee’s spot. I felt the corner heavy inside. I’m supposed to cross his face. I didn’t. I learned that one on the sideline. It just is what it is. There’s no excuse for things like that. I was just trying to make a play.” Unfortunately, these are the kinds of things that can happen when you are shuffling so much due to injuries. It is bad enough to be without Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, but when they both go down in a game things can be hectic. Bengals News Postgame Quick Hits | Ja’Marr’s Injury, Jags Defense Beat Joe Burrow’s Big Passing Day The Bengals may have an issue at wide receiver next week against the Miami Dolphins. We will have to see how Ja’Marr Chase progresses through concussion protocol over the week. We will also have to monitor an injury to Tee Higgins (adductor) as well. Burrow could be without his top two wide receivers on a week that seems crucial going into their Bye Week after. Bengals Big Betting Favorites Against Dolphins in Latest AFC Battle During 2026 Season Cincinnati opens as a full touchdown favorite on the road against Miami. That is pretty significant amount of points for a team to be spotted on the road. It really feels like the odds makers are expecting a bounce back game a la what college teams get. Joe Burrow on lack of offensive balance: My response is “throw it more” On a day when the running game clearly had issues and the team fell behind while also having troubles stopping the Jaguars, it made sense to let Burrow do his thing a bit more throwing the ball. Chase Brown also ended up with 11 receptions, and the team had several wide receiver screens to keep the defense on its toes. NFL News Jim Harbaugh backs Mike McDaniel after Chargers fall to 0-4: ‘His job is not in jeopardy’ The Los Angeles Chargers were expected to take a big step forward with McDaniel’s offense, but that hasn’t exactly transpired on their way to 0-4. This past week was their first time crossing 20 points in a game. Not a good look for the Justin Herbert truthers Jets end 20-game interceptionless streak with Minkah Fitzpatrick’s pick vs. Bears One of the crazier stats in the NFL was the Jets not having an interception since the 2024 season. Seems almost impossible with things like tipped balls and such. Yet here we are. Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson exits win over Titans early due to ankle injury Jackson left the stadium in a walking boot after the game. Things are sounding positive, but it is definitely worth monitoring as Baltimore goes as Jackson does.
