title: Best available NFL free agent wide receivers the Bengals could target following injuries
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals came into their Week 4 game against the Jaguars boasting the best wide receiver duo in the NFL. They finished the game with both of those wide receivers injured and on the sidelines. Ja’Marr Chase was lost in the first half after a brutal helmet-to-helmet hit from linebacker Ventrell Miller while the […]
full_text: Sep 29, 2025; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Miami Dolphins wide receiver Tyreek Hill (10) practices before the game against the New York Jets at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rich Storry-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cincinnati Bengals came into their Week 4 game against the Jaguars boasting the best wide receiver duo in the NFL. They finished the game with both of those wide receivers injured and on the sidelines. Ja’Marr Chase was lost in the first half after a brutal helmet-to-helmet hit from linebacker Ventrell Miller while the wide receiver’s facemask was being held by cornerback Jarrian Jones. Then, in the second half, Higgins was lost to an adductor injury. He tried to come back but eventually was forced to turn over his helmet. That left the Bengals with Dohnte Meyers and Mitchell Tinsley, who was signed off the Texans’ practice squad earlier this week. It’s currently unclear as to how much time Chase and Higgins will miss, if they miss any time at all, but the Bengals are going to at least need to kick the tires on bringing in help at the wide receiver position. If they do, they’re most likely to pluck someone from one of the league’s practice squads, but here’s who’s available if they decide to bring a free agent in. Curtis Samuel Samuel suffered an elbow injury that ended his 2025 season, but he has since recovered and is an unrestricted free agent after being cut from the Bills in March. The former second-round pick and Buckeye could find himself in need as injuries mount up this season. DeAndre Hopkins Hopkins is 34 years old, and he may be an assistant wide receivers coach for Georgia Tech, but he’s not retired. He played in 17 games for the Ravens in 2025. Even though he didn’t do too much with Baltimore, the future Hall of Fame wide receiver should still command enough respect that it could open things up for others. Zay Jones Jones suffered a torn Achilles in Week 10 of the 2025 season and was placed on IR, but has since recovered. He was signed by the Houston Texans before the 2026 season. He was cut in August and is still awaiting a phone call from a receiver-needy team. Tyreek Hill Hill has been around the league for a long time. He suffered a nasty knee injury in Week 4 of the 2025 season, and he’s not completely cleared for action, but his team is eyeing a possible November return. Considering the injury and the fact that he’s lost a step, this one’s not realistic. Trenton Irwin Hey, here’s a guy you may remember. Irwin was signed off the Dolphins’ practice squad in 2019 and stayed on the team until December of the 2024 season when he was waived. Since then, he bounced around the league. He was most recently with the 49ers, where he was cut at the end of August. Hopefully both Higgins and Chase don’t miss any time, and the Bengals won’t need to bring in any outside help at wide receiver. If they have to, though, who would you like them to sign? Would you take someone from this list or someone else not mentioned? Sound off!

full_text: The goodwill the Cincinnati Bengals bought with their 2-0 start has been wasted on the two losses that see them going into Week 5 with a 2-2 record. After such a great start to the season, the Bengals dropped a winnable game in Pittsburgh in Week 3 and then did everything they could to ensure they’d lose in Week 4. Now the Bengals travel to Miami to face the 0-4 Dolphins before they head into their Week 5 bye. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Bengals are opening as 7.5-point favorites for their game in Hard Rock Stadium. The Bengals will definitely want to head into their bye week with a winning record because they travel to Baltimore for their first of two division games against the Ravens. The Bengals are definitely banged up as they head into Week 5. They came into Week 4 missing safeties Bryan Cook and Kyle Dugger, and they came out of their loss to the Jaguars without wide receivers Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor). It’s currently unclear as to what the status of the best wide receiver duo in the league will be, but their impact on a defense can’t be overstated. title: Browns: There is more to playing defense than just sacks
summary: The NFL is a league that loves to celebrate the big moments in a game. Watch any highlight reel, and you will see: Those are all important, of course, but the game is made up of more than just big moments, especially when it comes to sacks. Consider the following scenario. The offense is facing […]
full_text: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL is a league that loves to celebrate the big moments in a game. Watch any highlight reel, and you will see: A long touchdown pass or run A big kickoff or punt return A quarterback sack late in the game Those are all important, of course, but the game is made up of more than just big moments, especially when it comes to sacks. Consider the following scenario. The offense is facing a third-and-long, and the quarterback drops back to pass. The defense doesn’t get a sack, but pressures the quarterback into either an incompletion or a pass that falls well short of the first-down line. The defense jogs off the field, mission accomplished, even if the play never makes the highlight reel. This is a timely discussion when looking at the impact that Cleveland Browns defensive end Jared Verse has made during Cleveland’s 3-1 start to the season. The Browns have tallied 12 sacks this season, with eight different players recording at least one sack. But Verse is not one of them. The easy (and lazy) way to look at that is to conclude that Verse is not carrying his weight and the Browns will soon have buyer’s remorse. But remember the earlier point about sacks not being the only defining stat? Well, it turns out that Verse, who came into the season with the fifth-most quarterback pressures among defensive ends since 2024, is the poster child for impacting a game without registering a sack. Robert Mays and Derrick Klassen, co-hosts of The Athletic Football Show, made that argument in a recent video segment , comparing Verse to Jadeveon Clowney (who played for the Browns in 2021 and 2022) at his peak: Jared Verse is just an awesome player. You are never going to fully understand his value by how many sacks he gets over the course of a season. This feels a lot like the way that we had to talk about Jadeveon Clowney when he was at his peak, where it’s like the sack numbers are just never really quite there. But he is always just around the quarterback and always pushing a tackle into the quarterback, and a good run defender who can take back space in that way. He does feel very similar to Clowney at his peak. OK, you might be saying, “What do a couple of guys on a podcast know about rushing the quarterback? I want sacks!” Fair enough. But what about Hall of Fame offensive tackle Joe Thomas? Seems like he might know a thing or two about line play in the NFL. “Jared Verse has been a bust since the Garrett trade.” That's what the outside world is saying…. Zero sacks through four games. But he leads the Browns in pressures, and six of them came against Carolina, where his rush helped Mason Graham and Isaiah McGuire get home. Sacks… pic.twitter.com/gQxvJHWbsk — Joe Thomas (@joethomas73) October 2, 2026 And Thomas echoes the thoughts on Verse in a recent video clip showing the impact that Verse had in Cleveland’s Week 3 win against the Carolina Panthers: “Jared Verse has been a bust since the Garrett trade. That’s what the outside world is saying…. Zero sacks through four games. But he leads the Browns in pressures, and six of them came against Carolina, where his rush helped Mason Graham and Isaiah McGuire get home. Sacks are the receipt. The pressure is the purchase. We rolled the tape. Coaching point for every young lineman: a rush that moves the quarterback is a win, even when somebody else makes the tackle.‘ Verse and the Browns will certainly not be unhappy if he starts stacking sacks, and they will likely come as he is too talented not to get to the quarterback at some point. But no one will be complaining if he keeps disrupting quarterbacks and helping the defense get off the field in a big spot. Even if it means he is not making the weekly highlight film. title: Browns Shedeur Sanders trade rumors: Logical, but unlikely based on Monday report
summary: The NFL schedule seems to always be in warp drive. With the first quarter of the season over (technically, that will not come until the end of the first quarter of Week 5), the Cleveland Browns are in first place in the AFC North and have the fourth seed in the current AFC playoff picture. […]
full_text: The NFL schedule seems to always be in warp drive. With the first quarter of the season over (technically, that will not come until the end of the first quarter of Week 5), the Cleveland Browns are in first place in the AFC North and have the fourth seed in the current AFC playoff picture . The return of QB Dillon Gabriel also leads to questions about how the team will handle their roster and potentially four quarterbacks. The Browns also still have two first-round picks, but the Los Angeles Rams also winning kept both of those picks far away from the Top 10 . For now, the focus is on the current season mostly. Besides a somewhat easy schedule for Cleveland , the second quarter of the NFL season leads into the NFL trade deadline on November 10th. If the Browns continue their winning ways, GM Andrew Berry could be apt to be a buyer at the deadline. Berry is also creative in his process, so Cleveland could also be a seller if offers make sense. As we’ve already seen in the NFL, the deadline isn’t the only thing that has spurred trade action. For the Browns, Gabriel’s pending return could lead to fellow QB Shedeur Sanders being on the move. Rumors kicked off once Sanders lost the quarterback battle with starting QB Deshaun Watson . This week, Dan Graziano of ESPN fueled those rumors a bit more : Young guys such as Anthony Richardson Sr., Stetson Bennett IV or, yes, even Shedeur Sanders could be interesting to teams looking for a developmental QB who needs a change of scenery. Always watch for under-the-radar QB trades at this time of year. Again, we’ve already had one. With Watson playing well and Gabriel returning, Berry could find a trade he finds acceptable for Sanders. There has been some conversation that Watson’s positive, not perfect, performance could be a positive indication for Sanders’ development. Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com threw cold water on the embers of the Sanders rumors: Amid national and local speculation that the #Browns might trade Shedeur Sanders, throwing this report from last week out there again: #Browns have no plans to trade Shedeur Sanders or Dillon Gabriel. Same goes for WR Jerry Jeudy: –> https://t.co/1XlNTrTdAV — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) October 5, 2026 As always, if someone makes them an offer they can't refuse, they'll pivot. But they currently don't intend to trade these 3. — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) October 5, 2026 Astute Browns fans have already noted the similarity between this “no plans” language and that which was used surrounding DE Myles Garrett in the months prior to him being dealt. As always, it takes two to tango. While Sanders had his moments in 2025, his overall performance has been ranked at the bottom of the league multiple times . Sanders completed 57% of his passes last year as a rookie, for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions. The surrounding cast and offensive system did not help any of Cleveland’s quaterbacks last year, including Sanders. HC Todd Monken’s work with Watson, and Sanders pushing the veteran throughout training camp, could raise his stock in the league. The NFL has also seen injuries to quarterbacks each week, which could create an opening for a team to see what they have with Sanders. For now, Sanders rumors are smoldering and could heat up at any moment, especially whenever Gabriel is cleared to return to practice with his 21-day window opened. summary: After a 3-1 start, the Cleveland Browns have an opportunity to extend their win streak over the next several weeks. full_text: After a 3-1 start , the Cleveland Browns have an opportunity to extend their win streak over the next several weeks. Looking at the next four weeks of the Browns’ schedule , can they win three of their next four games to bring their record to 6-2? Duplicating the results from the first quarter of the season would certainly multiply the excitement around Northeast Ohio heading into the holiday season. This stretch of games kicks off with an away game against the 1-3 New York Jets. Although playing on the road can be challenging, this should be a winnable game for Cleveland. The Jets’ offense struggled in their most recent matchup against the Chicago Bears, managing just 12 points. The Browns defense should look to make some big plays. The next game is a home game against the Baltimore Ravens. Cleveland is 3-2 against the Ravens at home over the last five seasons. Baltimore is also sitting at 3-1 right now, so this will certainly be a challenging matchup, but a win is not out of the question. The Tennessee Titans have yet to record a win this season, so the Browns should certainly be looking to get that win on the road. The Cleveland defense will give them a lot of problems. The final matchup in this stretch is a road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Playing in Pittsburgh is always a challenging environment. The Browns already have one win against the Steelers this season, so they will have a level of confidence going into this game. A win in Pittsburgh would be a massive accomplishment for this team. “The 6-2 (or 7-1) Cleveland Browns” on November 1st has a nice ring to it. The team will take the “one game at a time” moniker, but we get to look ahead and imagine what could be. Let me know what you think in the comments – Can the Browns win 3 of their next 4 games? title: Jake Ferguson’s fourth-down catch kept Dallas’ comeback alive
summary: Football is all about momentum. Sometimes those shifts happen quickly and unexpectedly. It was CeeDee Lamb who delivered the winning touchdown, but it was Jake Ferguson’s crucial catch that made sure the Cowboys still had a chance to score it. It was a real turning point in the game. With Dallas trailing Houston 30-27 late […]
full_text: Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images | Getty Images Football is all about momentum. Sometimes those shifts happen quickly and unexpectedly. It was CeeDee Lamb who delivered the winning touchdown, but it was Jake Ferguson’s crucial catch that made sure the Cowboys still had a chance to score it. It was a real turning point in the game. With Dallas trailing Houston 30-27 late in the fourth quarter, the comeback was hanging by the smallest of threads. The Cowboys faced fourth-and-4 at their own 32-yard line with 1:34 remaining. Dak Prescott found Ferguson over the middle for seven yards, moving the chains and keeping alive the possession that would decide Sunday’s 34-30 victory. Dak Prescott connects with Jake Ferguson for the 4th down conversion #DallasCowboys #DALvsHOU pic.twitter.com/D7tL9x2r3E — False Finish (@FalseFinishHQ) October 4, 2026 It was a modest gain at the time but as it turned out it held enormous importance. Dallas needed four yards to continue fighting, and Dak trusted his tight end to deliver. Ferguson secured the pass with a sliding catch, giving the offense another set of downs when an incompletion would have handed Houston possession deep in Cowboys territory to kill the game. That is the moment that stands out in a game filled with swings. Houston had an opportunity to take control of the closing stages. Instead, Dallas kept the ball and could continue attacking. The Cowboys still had plenty of work ahead, but Ferguson’s catch allowed everything that followed to happen. Earlier, there had been little suggestion that Dallas would win. The Cowboys trailed 16-6 at halftime after a frustrating first two quarters. However, KaVontae Turpin’s 48-yard return at the start of the second half lifted the team, and Javonte Williams scored an eight-yard touchdown to finish the possession. Houston responded, forcing Dallas to keep chasing. The Cowboys’ offense eventually found consistency, scoring three rushing touchdowns from Williams. Prescott continued to find success with Lamb, leading Dallas to take the lead. However, Houston responded with Woody Marks’ late touchdown run, forcing the Cowboys to respond once again. This time, they delivered, securing the victory. After Ferguson extended the final possession, Prescott advanced Dallas downfield. Completions of 15 yards to Lamb and 22 yards to George Pickens positioned the Cowboys for a scoring opportunity. With 40 seconds left, Prescott connected with Lamb for the winning touchdown, capping off an impressive afternoon for the receiver, who caught 17 passes for 189 yards. The winning drive covered 74 yards in just 11 plays, showcasing the significant improvement in the offense after halftime. Quarterback Prescott completed 20 of his 25 second-half attempts for 248 yards and a touchdown, providing Brian Schottenheimer’s team with the production they needed to overcome their poor start. Schottenheimer should be commended for assisting the offense in discovering solutions after halftime, and the players should be acknowledged for performing under pressure. A comeback involves more than just a successful adjustment or a motivational talk at halftime. Ultimately, someone must make a crucial play when there’s no margin for error, and Ferguson did precisely that. summary: Four games into the season, the Cowboys stand at a slightly disappointing 2-2, but with the hope that the addition of Joey Porter Jr. will be the start of a defensive turnaround. Since the league moved to a 17-game schedule in 2020, 63 teams started the season 2-2, and 25 of those teams (40%) eventually […]
full_text: Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Four games into the season, the Cowboys stand at a slightly disappointing 2-2, but with the hope that the addition of Joey Porter Jr. will be the start of a defensive turnaround. Since the league moved to a 17-game schedule in 2020, 63 teams started the season 2-2, and 25 of those teams (40%) eventually made the playoffs. The table below shows what the playoff chances have looked like over the last six seasons by W/L after the fourth game of the season. body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 0px 6px !important; } Playoff chances based on Week 4 W/L records, since 2020 Record after Week 4 4-0 3-1 2-2 1-3 0-4 Total Teams 14 49 63 53 13 Playoff Teams 14 38 25 7 0 Percentage 100% 78% 40% 13% 0% But how good are the 2-2 Cowboys really, and more importantly, can they start stacking some wins soon? To understand where the Cowboys currently stand and what their chances look like going forward, we turn once again to the trusted Pythagorean Formula. We’ve used the formula often before (for more details, go here ) to measure overall team strength, on the hypothesis that a team’s true strength could be measured more accurately by looking at points scored and points allowed, rather than by looking at wins and losses. After four weeks of play, there is already quite a strong correlation between the win-projection and the actual season-ending W/L record. Of course, with every additional week of data, the formula gets better, but after about Week 4 the improvements are gradual, and not as steep as in the first few weeks. To illustrate that, let’s look at the four teams in the NFC East and how their Pythagorean Wins developed week by week last season: Notice how the Pythagorean Formula last year was already projecting the Eagles, Cowboys, and Giants pretty accurately after Week 4: The Eagles were already looking like 11-game winners, the Cowboys were projected for six wins, one shy of their eventual win total, and the Giants were slightly ahead of their eventual four-win total. The Commanders started out strong, but then multiple injuries to Jayden Daniels derailed their season. The point here is that barring a meltdown like the Commanders had last season, or a surge later in the season, a couple of weeks worth of data can provide an early indication of where the train might be headed. In four games so far this season, the Cowboys have scored 122 points (T2nd) and allowed 112 (29th). The Pythagorean projected wins for this stat line: 9.4 wins, and adjusted for the games already played: 9.2 wins. Even outside of the historic playoff chances, that win total suggests it’ll be tight for the Cowboys to make the playoffs, barring a significant improvement on defense. Using the Pythagorean formula for the remaining 31 teams, we get a good idea of the emerging 2026 playoff picture. For the Cowboys, the safest way to the playoffs is by winning the NFC East. Over the course of a season, most football fans construct a mental map of the NFL teams. After last season, for example, most football fans would have considered the Texans contenders heading into this year. Yet after just four weeks, the Texans’ playoff margin for error has effectively disappeared at 0-4. Like every season, the NFL landscape is changing, and with it fans have to readjust their mental map of NFL teams. The reality of the 2026 season is taking shape right before our eyes, and that reality doesn’t necessarily have much to do with the 2025 season. title: Cowboys perfect red zone day enough to even record in Houston
summary: The 0-3 Houston Texans may have been the team carrying the “desperate” label into Sunday’s early kickoff against the Dallas Cowboys, but after the first 30 minutes of play, the visiting Cowboys at 1-2 sure found themselves in a desperate spot as well. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s team was back on the field for the […]
full_text: Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images | Getty Images The 0-3 Houston Texans may have been the team carrying the “desperate” label into Sunday’s early kickoff against the Dallas Cowboys, but after the first 30 minutes of play, the visiting Cowboys at 1-2 sure found themselves in a desperate spot as well. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s team was back on the field for the first time since that loss in Brazil, one that fell in the lap of coaching at large, the offense squandering a great opportunity to take a late lead, and defense giving up one too many gash plays. Through 30 minutes in Houston, it looked like the Cowboys hadn’t learned any lessons in any of these areas, and trailed 16-6 to a Texans team that was never going to flinch at being 0-3, having been in this spot a year ago. There were also few indicators from the first half that the Cowboys would fight back into a very similar position from the Ravens game, the ball in Dak Prescott and the offense’s hands in the red zone with a chance to take the lead at the end. The Cowboys did play themselves into this spot though, and this time got the go-ahead touchdown on CeeDee Lamb’s 17th catch of the game, plus the stop to follow to win 34-30. From ESPN Research: The Cowboys had lost 32 straight road games when trailing by double digits in the second half, which was the longest active streak of its kind in the NFL. — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) October 4, 2026 Let’s get to our notes on how it happened, with the Cowboys now facing a short week to prepare for another winless team – the now 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Corner Up, Corner Down The Cowboys were very depleted in the secondary coming into this game, and to make matters worse for them the Texans welcomed their star wide receiver Nico Collins back to the lineup to face this banged up pass defense. This mismatch showed itself very early, in fact as early as possible with Collins making a 45-yard catch on the first play from scrimmage. Houston caught Reddy Steward lined up against Collins for this big play, and then hit Collins again in the red zone against DaRon Bland to cap off the drive with seven points. Bland did not have his best game, but part of the reason why is actually encouraging in an overall sense for Christian Parker’s defense. The higher volume of throws that Bland faced was partly a result of the newly traded for Joey Porter Jr. inserting himself into the lineup and having a great debut. There were questions about how Porter would fit this scheme, but he came in and played well immediately. This shifts some of those scheme fit concerns to the veteran Bland, who has battled through injury to be part of multiple scheme changes defensively in Dallas. Joey Porter Jr. in his Cowboys debut, per @SumerSports : 24 snaps 0 targets 0 receptions allowed 0 yards allowed — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) October 5, 2026 There have been multiple big plays allowed by Bland this season where he appeared not on the same page with the rest of the coverage, or playing the wrong leverage. This happened on Collins’ touchdown, where Bland and rookie Caleb Downs were out of sync. The Cowboys defense is still searching for it’s first interception of the season, and teams being forced to throw near Bland more can bring takeaways in bunches, but right now his inconsistencies on a down-to-down basis paired with an inconsistent pass rush are worrisome for how well this defense can hold up for long stretches. Defending Long Fields Speaking of the defense holding up, the Cowboys defense was handed multiple gifts early in this game via Texans special teams penalties that backed them up and gave them long fields. If there was any doubt about it before this game, there should be zero now that this Cowboys team is again built to play through their offense. The defense supporting this by flipping some of these long fields into short fields for Dak Prescott would be a very welcome sight, but also for the second week in a row they had trouble doing so. The Texans got points on their first two drives of the game that started at their own 15- and 8-yard lines, as well as the fourth quarter touchdown to put them up 30-27, starting at their 13. The splash negative plays from this defense are coming in later downs or short-yardage situations, which is still a very good thing, but opposing offenses are leaning on this defense with their run games in early downs and getting them off-balance in manageable down and distances. The drive that started at the eight-yard line for Houston and ended in a field goal had a field-flipping play against Bland, when Jaylin Noel beat him on an out and up route for 52 yards. The Cowboys had Von Miller and Malachi Lawrence on the field for this play as their edge rushers, and neither got remotely close to Stroud, allowing the double move deep route to develop. Not Picking up the Defense The counterpoint to this is that the Cowboys offense continued on a concerning trend carrying over from the Ravens game as well. In that loss, the defense forced three separate three and outs. The offense got the ball back in these spots and kicked a field goal in the red zone, missed a field goal, and went three and out themselves. In Houston, the Dallas defense got back-to-back three and outs in the second quarter, and the offense punted after the first one and missed a field goal after the second on Will Anderson’s block. The Cowboys would miss another long range field goal on their next drive following this sequence too, and to the defense’s credit they bowed up and held Houston to six points out of the two drives where the Texans had their best starting field position of the game. The Cowboys punt would come even after they escaped a 3rd-and-22 and intentional grounding penalty thanks to a Texans penalty. Schottenheimer getting too cute with the play calls again would pop up at an inopportune time, losing five yards on first down to a CeeDee Lamb reverse, then asking Jake Ferguson to block Will Anderson on second down – another incomplete pass to Lamb. Ferguson’s blocking at the point of attack has been a major red flag within the heavier personnel sets the Cowboys have still been at their best offensively in. Ferguson needs to be included in the downfield passing concepts, but defenses should continue to force him to block out of these looks after seeing the Texans tape. Late in the fourth quarter, the Cowboys offense had the ball back with a four point lead and chance to really seize control of the game by at least chewing some more clock. They possessed it for only 1:45 on a three and out of their own, after Ferguson had a terrible chip block against Anderson on third down. All his block did was give Anderson more of a direct rush past Terence Steele and into Prescott’s lap, deflecting Dak’s pass incomplete. Red Zone Excellence The Cowboys immediately cut into the Texans lead coming out of the locker room with a four-play touchdown drive, and the play sequencing was a thing of beauty – starting with a nice return by KaVontae Turpin as well. A play-action pass to Lamb got them into the red zone, and Javonte Williams finished it off with his first of three touchdowns. We already mentioned Steele’s inconsistency at right tackle, and on the left side Tyler Guyton had a plus game, but it was the Cowboys interior offensive line that struggled most often in this game. Instead of bashing their head against the wall in the red area where things are condensed, the Cowboys pulled guard T.J. Bass and center Cooper Beebe to take the Texans interior defenders out of the play by design. These two linemen paved the way on a toss for Williams to score. Dallas would need more of these scores from Williams after the Texans got a big kick return of their own and answered back with another Nico Collins touchdown, and his second touchdown took the Cowboys off the hook a little bit for not-as-great sequencing in the red zone this time. George Pickens had the 54-yard catch to get…

title: Cowboys at Texans: CeeDee Lamb is currently the NFL’s best wide receiver
summary: After a demoralizing loss in Brazil to the Baltimore Ravens, the Dallas Cowboys came into Sunday’s matchup against the Houston Texans as a desperate team. Since the 2015 season, 14.9% of teams have made the playoffs after starting 1-3 (13 of 87) versus 43.3% of teams that started 2-2 (45 of 104).  If Dallas lost […]
full_text: (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After a demoralizing loss in Brazil to the Baltimore Ravens, the Dallas Cowboys came into Sunday’s matchup against the Houston Texans as a desperate team. Since the 2015 season, 14.9% of teams have made the playoffs after starting 1-3 (13 of 87) versus 43.3% of teams that started 2-2 (45 of 104). If Dallas lost this game and fell to 1-3, their playoff hopes would start to slip away just four weeks into the regular season. Thankfully, the Cowboys bounced back in a big way from the heartbreaking loss last Sunday, delivering a 34-30 victory over the Texans. Dallas’ offense was the star of the show in the second half of Sunday, led by five-time Pro Bowl receiver CeeDee Lamb. The seven-year pro put the Cowboys on his back, posting a career day and earning this week’s game ball award. Lamb put together one of the best receiver performances of the past decade in Houston. The 27-year-old caught a career-high 17 passes for 189 yards to go with scoring the game-winning touchdown late in the fourth quarter. HUGE CEEDEE TD 🔥 #DallasCowboys | @_CeeDeeThree 📺: #DALvsHOU on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/pQcMzqN4BZ — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) October 4, 2026 While this was undoubtedly his best performance of the year, Lamb’s performance on Sunday was a continuation of an unbelievable start to his 2026 campaign. Four games in, Lamb has recorded 37 receptions for 498 yards, both the most in the NFL, to go with four receiving touchdowns. Lamb’s has already surpassed his previous career-high of 332 receiving yards through four regular-season games from last season. CeeDee Lamb's first four games: 2020 – 21 Rec, 309 Yds, 2 TD 2021 – 20 Rec, 264 Yds, 1 TD 2022 – 23 Rec, 288 Yds, 2 TD 2023 – 23 Rec, 309 Yds, 1 TD 2024 – 20 Rec, 316 Yds, 2 TD 2025 – 21 Rec, 332 Yds, 1 TD 2026 – 37 Rec, 498 Yds, 4 TD pic.twitter.com/NpejrEvtYH — Bobby Belt (@BobbyBeltTX) October 4, 2026 There is no denying that Lamb looked like the best receiver in the National Football League on Sunday in Houston. He did everything a true generational receiver is supposed to do, including taking over the game when his team needed him most. There is some hope that the Cowboys will figure things out defensively as the season unfolds, but it is becoming increasingly clear that this team is going to have to be carried by its offense. That may seem like a tall task, but if Lamb continues to play at this level, he has the ability to make up for the team’s shortcomings on defense and help lead Dallas to a historic season on the offensive side of the ball. For now, the message is simple: CeeDee Lamb is playing on a different level, and the Cowboys are going to go as far as he can carry them. Right now, it’s CeeDee Lamb’s world—and everyone else is just living in it.

title: Cowboys at Texans Stock Report: CeeDee Lamb leads the way
summary: The Dallas Cowboys won the Texas State Championship on Sunday, and whether or not beating the in-state Houston Texans means anything extra to you, it stands to reason that wins in general do. Sunday’s victory was very needed for the Cowboys to stop the bleeding that began down in Rio when they lost to the […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys won the Texas State Championship on Sunday, and whether or not beating the in-state Houston Texans means anything extra to you, it stands to reason that wins in general do. Sunday’s victory was very needed for the Cowboys to stop the bleeding that began down in Rio when they lost to the Baltimore Ravens. There is no rest for the weary though as they are back in action just a few days from now on Thursday night against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Before we fully shift focus to Tampa Bay, we need to properly tie a bow on the win in Houston. Several players really shined where others left us wanting more. Here is our stock report from Sunday’s win. Let’s begin. Stock Up: CeeDee Lamb What can you really say at this point? CeeDee Lamb was a true and total alpha in Houston. He did whatever he wanted, and Next Gen Stats noted that he recorded multiple receptions against six different Texans defenders . Think about how absurd that is. Lamb was entrusted with the game on the line, and well before it, to deliver and he absolutely did. He is living up to all hype and fanfare that people have had around him, and it feels like we are seeing the best version he has ever offered throughout his Cowboys career which is really saying something. Stock Up: Joey Porter Jr. It took all of five seconds for everyone involved to realize/remember that JPJ is the best cornerback on the Cowboys roster. All told it was still a wading in for Porter as he was just acquired by the Cowboys this past week, but he played 19 snaps while in coverage and did not allow a single reception against a single target. It was evident that Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud was avoiding him at all costs. That is what the Cowboys paid for. They went out to get someone to neutralize one side of the field, and they have it now. Stock Up: Tyler Guyton There really was a time, not too long ago, when we doubted whether or not Tyler Guyton would actually be the left tackle on this team. Heck, head coach Brian Schottenheimer openly declared in the offseason that Nate Thomas was competing with Guyton for the job. That is the same Nate Thomas who got traded to the Texans in roster cutdowns and was inactive for this game. Having the left side of the offensive line so stable is such a peaceful thing. It will improve even more when Tyler Smith returns to the lineup. Don’t forget about that. Stock Up: George Pickens Four games into this season we have yet to see George Pickens have the exact same impact that CeeDee Lamb has, but he is easily making his mark. Consider that the Cowboys’ game-winning drive would not have happened to the extent that it did without a huge gain from Pickens. Heck, consider that his 53-yard reception early in the second half was part of what woke the offense up at large. Pickens is giving the Cowboys his all and delivering when called upon. Stock Up: Ryan Flournoy This was arguably Ryan Flournoy’s best game since joining the Cowboys. The sample size there isn’t exactly large, but we have long believed that he could/should exist as a proper third option in the passing game and that’s exactly what he was in Houston. Sometimes the opposing defense is taking so many things away and wreaking havoc in a number of different directions. You have to have that person who helps keep things moving right along, and that’s what Flo was in this game. Stock Up: Quinnen Williams The last two games have shown the Quinnen Williams who the Cowboys traded for and extended. He is turning into the defensive game-wrecker that his reputation said he was with the New York Jets. Maybe it was a matter of gelling across time, but it feels fair to assume that this is the player who is here to stay. Clearly we hope that. is the case. Williams kept things in check, especially as the second half wore on and the game got tight. That’s his job and he did it very well. Static Stock: Brian Schottenheimer It has been a while since I handed out a static stock, but I believe Brian Schottenheimer is deserving in this instance. The first half was pretty terrible. Specifically, the sequence at the end of it. Schottenheimer gambled in letting Brandon Aubrey attempt a 65-yard field goal right after having a 62-yard one blocked, and the miss gave Houston short field position that they converted into a field goal to send everyone to their respective locker rooms. But Schotty locked in as the game wore on. He pledged all week to not let last week, as in the Ravens loss, define him. He said he would not hold the team back the way that he believed he did against Baltimore in Rio. Eerily, the Cowboys faced almost an identical situation as the game wore on. Their offense went three and out when they could have iced the game with a four-point lead, and they took over with around two minutes left down by three. This time, unlike last, Schotty entrusted and enabled his superstars and the Cowboys won as a result. That is legitimate growth. So the beginning was rough, but the end was great. So long as they are in that order and lead to a win, that’s what matters. Stock Down: DaRon Bland This is another instance where there really isn’t a ton to say. Joey Porter Jr. is incredible, but his incredible-ness means that opposing quarterbacks are going to attack DaRon Bland early and often. C.J. Stroud did so and was highly successful as a result of it. There is no question that Bland is among the weaker points of the Cowboys roster at the moment. That is a huge issue that they are going to have to address if they don’t want to be in similar circumstances moving forward. Stock Down: Brandon Aubrey You can certainly argue that his 62-yard field goal was blocked because Will Anderson Jr. is incredible, and you can similarly claim that a 65-yard field goal is difficult to pull off and that being asked to do it right after a block is not ideal. But it feels like we move the goalposts a lot for Aubrey, no pun intended. It feels like we let his reputation tell us we are being too harsh when moments of constructive criticism come up. It can be true that those circumstances were not ideal and that as the NFL’s highest-paid kicker he should be successful nonetheless. He wasn’t and that’s a problem. Stock Down: Nick Sorensen At the moment the Cowboys have one of the worst and least efficient special teams operations across the NFL. Nick Sorensen has been under fire even dating back to last year, and that temperature is only rising as a result of the messes we are seeing. We regard the Cowboys’ special teams as great because of the visible pieces in the aforementioned Aubrey, KaVontae Turpin, and even Bryan Anger. But the operation is clunky. How? How can this really be possible? Are they missing a veteran on the field in C.J. Goodwin? Does Nick Sorensen need to do more? Whatever the answer is, they have to find it immediately.

title: With injuries, Broncos need to quickly shift gears
summary: Overshadowing the loss on Sunday to the San Francisco 49ers, the Denver Broncos lost a great deal more to injury. Pat Surtain II (ankle), Riley Moss (ribs), and Pat Bryant (leg/ankle) all left the game and it looks like all could miss more than a little time, if not the whole season. While I appreciate […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 4: Pat Surtain II #2 of the Denver Broncos stretches on the field prior to an NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Overshadowing the loss on Sunday to the San Francisco 49ers, the Denver Broncos lost a great deal more to injury. Pat Surtain II (ankle), Riley Moss (ribs), and Pat Bryant (leg/ankle) all left the game and it looks like all could miss more than a little time, if not the whole season. Non-contact injury for Pat Surtain. A closer look pic.twitter.com/p0Pmy0qXRv — Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) October 4, 2026 🚨🚨HEARTBREAKING🚨🚨 #Broncos WR Pat Bryant was carted off the field after this ankle injury. This is GRUESOME… watch with caution. 😬😬 pic.twitter.com/LNMJEUTHBm — MLFootball (@MLFootball) October 4, 2026 While I appreciate the Klis report late Sunday night of Broncos brain-trust optimism regarding the extent of Surtain and Bryant’s injuries, there’s not much of a silver lining. No matter how you look at it, the Surtain injury has all the hallmarks of what’s tipically a season-ending Achilles injury. Pat Bryant’s ankle was wrenched the wrong way and, while it may not be a season-ender, he will most certainly miss more than a few weeks. Riley Moss’ previous rib injury took him out of action in the preseason for a couple weeks and it’s possible this could be more of the same (best case scenario)… but it’s also possible there is a bone fracture or cartilage damage, which could mean 3-6+ weeks of recovery. What do you do when you lose both your starting corners and a reliable offensive contributor at wide receiver? First of all, the defense can no longer be counted on to keep games close. For the first time in Bo Nix’s career, the defense is no longer the security blanket that will allow Davis Webb to fart around with the offense for 3 quarters. The offense now has to lock in when the game starts and get off to fast starts. The run game, and sustaining drives, has never been more important. This affinity for wasting downs in 3 and out possessions is only going to stress a depleted secondary and will most certainly yield horrific results. Sure, Davis Webb is finding his way as a play caller and it’s been a neat little adventure, watching him wobble and stumble like a toddler learning to walk. With the injuries on Sunday, the time for stumbling is over. The Broncos offense has got to strike first and strike hard to cover for a defense that suddenly finds itself without their starting cornerbacks. Sustaining offensive pressure through 4 quarters of football has never been more crucial than it suddenly is for the Denver Broncos. While these injuries don’t necessarily signal the end of the Broncos Super Bowl dreams in 2026, they absolutely don’t help. It’s time for the Broncos offense to show up when the game starts and not when they’re behind in the 4th quarter. In order for Bo Nix to ascend to the legendary echelon of Broncos quarterbacks, he’s going to need to put this team on his back and will them to victory, injuries be damned. …and so begins the next chapter of Bo Nix’s story.
author: Jess Place

title: Lions injury updates: Brian Branch return imminent, but 2 other defenders hurt
summary: It appears Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch will return to practice this week. Lions coach Dan Campbell said on Monday afternoon that the Lions’ Pro Bowl safety still needs to clear final medical tests, but the expectation is for him to return to practice on Wednesday, starting his 21-day evaluation window. “We have not gotten […]
full_text: Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch (32) practices during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, August 21, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co It appears Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch will return to practice this week. Lions coach Dan Campbell said on Monday afternoon that the Lions’ Pro Bowl safety still needs to clear final medical tests, but the expectation is for him to return to practice on Wednesday, starting his 21-day evaluation window. “We have not gotten confirmation from the doctor yet. That’s the only thing we’re waiting for on Branch,” Campbell said. “I think it looks really good that he’s going to practice this week.” Branch suffered a torn Achilles in early December and has slowly been rehabbing his way back onto the field. While gone, Detroit has struggled a ton in the secondary. At safety specifically, they’re already down Avonte Maddox (season-ending IR), Thomas Harper (IR), and Kerby Joseph (PUP). That has left them starting 31-year-old Chuck Clark and Christian Izien, who spent most of training camp repping at nickel cornerback. So Branch’s return would be more than welcome, although it seems unlikely he’ll play this Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals. Detroit typically likes players coming off long-term injuries to get at least a couple of weeks of practice in before playing them. That would mean Branch’s debut is more likely to come out of Detroit’s bye against the Packers in Week 7. Campbell had less positive updates on two other Lions defenders. Rock Ya-Sin, who left Sunday’s game with a hamstring injury, is not trending in the right direction. “I don’t think Rock looks good right now,” Campbell said. Ya-Sin has been demoted to CB4 or CB5, and only played nine special teams snaps on Sunday. However, that leaves Detroit even thinner at the cornerback position—a position that already had questionable depth. This could be an opportunity to bring someone like Nick Whiteside up from the practice squad. Campbell also provided an update on Lions defensive tackle Tyleik Williams, who was spotted in a walking boot after the game. Williams told reporters he’s fine , but Campbell was a little more cautious. “Tyleik is touch-and-go. He’ll be day-to-day,” Campbell said. Williams is off to a strong start to his second NFL season, both as a run defender and pass rusher. Through four games, Williams has 14 tackles, 1 QB hit, and eight pressures (per PFF). We’ll know more about the injury status of these players when the team returns to practice on Wednesday.

summary: The Detroit Lions suffered yet another disappointing loss on national television, their second of the season, this time falling to the Carolina Panthers 32-26 on “Sunday Night Football.” Let’s look at the snap counts from this game and see what they mean for the depth chart hierarchy and what we can ascertain moving forward. full_text: Oct 4, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Carolina Panthers wide receiver Ja'seem Reed (86) is unable to make a catch defended by Detroit Lions cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (2) during the fourth quarter at Bank of America Stadicompetes. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions suffered yet another disappointing loss on national television, their second of the season, this time falling to the Carolina Panthers 32-26 on “Sunday Night Football.” Let’s look at the snap counts from this game and see what they mean for the depth chart hierarchy and what we can ascertain moving forward. Quarterback Jared Goff: 71 (100%) Josh Dobbs: Did Not Play Goff threw for 412 yards in this game, but like several other players on this roster, came up short in some critical moments. In a game where the defense was so bad that he needed to be near perfect to keep the Lions competitive, this time he came up just a bit short. title: Detroit Lions grades: Defense is beyond embarrassing vs. Panthers
summary: The Detroit Lions fell to the Carolina Panthers 32-26 on Sunday night in a particularly disheartening game. The team does not look like it has evolved or improved from week to week. The offense, while still a clear strength, is dealing with bouts of self-inflicted mistakes, leading to consistenetly inconsistent play. The defense is a […]
full_text: Oct 4, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan (4) makes a catch defended by Detroit Lions cornerback D.J. Reed (4) during the second quarter at Bank of America Stadium. McMillan scored a touchdown on the play. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions fell to the Carolina Panthers 32-26 on Sunday night in a particularly disheartening game. The team does not look like it has evolved or improved from week to week. The offense, while still a clear strength, is dealing with bouts of self-inflicted mistakes, leading to consistenetly inconsistent play. The defense is a complete disaster with no end in sight. Here are my positional grades for the Lions’ Week 4 report card. Quarterback: B Jared Goff was fine for most of the night. There was obviously a lot of pressure on his shoulders for most of the second half with the Lions down two scores, and he kept them competitive with steady plays and a couple of deep shots. However, his operation on the final drive was a disaster. He can’t take a coverage sack, he can’t miss Sam LaPorta by five feet, and it wasn’t much help to throw short of the sticks on fourth down either. Unfortunately, Goff is in a position where he needs to play near-perfect ball to win the game, and on Sunday night, he didn’t. Running backs: C- Jahmyr Gibbs had his least effective game of the season, rushing for just 46 yards on 15 carries. He also had a critical drop on third down forced Detroit to settle for a field goal—something they just couldn’t afford to do in the middle of a shootout. Gibbs did find the end zone once, but he was more of a non-factor than expected against a Panthers defense that had struggled to stop the run. Wide receivers: B- Jameson Williams and Isaac TeSlaa had some huge plays in this game to help the Lions keep it close. However, Williams had a weird drop(?) early in the game, then had another critical drop that could’ve gotten the Lions out of a second-and-14 situation. It felt like a night of two steps forward, one step back for this unit. More good than bad, but some critical mistakes in critical moments. Tight ends: B Sam LaPorta was one of Detroit’s most potent weapons in this game, finishing with eight catches, 84 yards and a touchdown. Unfortunately, Brock Wright brings the unit’s grade down for his two penalties—a personal foul leg whip and a false start. Offensive line: C Pass protection was pretty solid, in general. Although, I thought the Lions could’ve handled blitzes a little better. What was more concerning was Detroit’s run blocking, which provided almost zero daylight for Gibbs. On top of that, the line was called for three false starts and two holding penalties (one declined). Defensive line: B Perhaps the most frustrating part of Sunday night’s defensive performance is that the defensive front didn’t let Bryce Young get comfortable all night. In total, they tallied 11 quarterback hits (all but one from the DL), three sacks, and a handful of TFLs. When it comes to the pass game, they held up their part of the bargain and more, but Bryce Young had the back seven in the palm of his hand. The Lions defense produced a 40.0% pressure rate (ninth best of the week) despite only blitzing 26.7% of the time (21st). Unfortunately, I can’t even give the defensive line an A because the run defense completely fell apart in the second half. In the final two quarters alone, the Panthers tallied 93 rushing yards on just 18 carries (5.2 YPC). Linebackers: F Young’s use of RPO concepts had the Lions’ linebacker room in a tizzy all night. Their zone discipline was a disaster, their tackling was not on point, and the amount of wide open field over the middle was significantly the fault of poor depth from the linebackers. Just look at how much Young attacked the middle of the field: Per @NextGenStats : Bryce Young’s 14 completions on in-breakers tied his career-high, and he totaled 160 yards and a touchdown on such throws. pic.twitter.com/7eOkEq6VxJ — John Ellis (@1PantherPlace) October 5, 2026 Detroit tried to switch up personnel again, using rookie Jimmy Rolder a few times early in the game before realizing he wasn’t ready. But no one else stepped up, either. Defensive backs: F When the Lions play zone, the safeties are too late to break on the ball and the corners aren’t playing disciplined ball. When the Lions play man-coverage, the cornerbacks are getting toasted. Detroit is shuffling through schemes, personnel, and trying several different things, but when it comes to the question: what does this Lions secondary do well? I’m afraid the answer right now is nothing. Special teams: B Jake Bates was a perfect 4-for-4 on field goals and 2-for-2 on extra points. He was also excellent on kickoffs, landing every single one of them inside the 8-yard line and none in the end zone. However, the Lions coverage and return units weren’t particularly good. Both Tom Kennedy and Jacob Saylors averaged less than 22 yards per kick return. Meanwhile, the Panthers averaged 25.5 on theirs. Coaching: F Let’s start with in-game management. Detroit had to burn a timeout early in the game after having too many men on the field. Then they burned a second timeout on a challenge that had little chance of succeeding. Late in the game, a delay of game (then false start) doomed a fourth down attempt. Not a terrible list of transgressions, but not great, either. No, the coaching gets an ‘F’ this week for preparation and game-planning. On defense, I don’t know if there’s anything left to say. The team is far, far, far less than the sum of their parts on that side of the ball, and that falls directly on Kelvin Sheppard’s shoulders. And what’s particularly concerning is that coach Dan Campbell openly admitted they weren’t prepared for all the RPO looks they got early. “To start the game, we didn’t do well enough in the coverage aspect. They had a couple of things in there, the RPOs that got us,” Campbell said. “They put your run-pass-hook defender in conflict there a little bit and he’s got such a quick release. That got us a little bit early.” Detroit’s adjustment there was far too late, and as Campbell then pointed out, once they settled that down, the run defense levee broke. By now, the Lions defense should have an identity, an area of strength, or some sort of “bread and butter” concept they can fall back on. Instead, Lions defenders look as lost as ever, and I can’t point to a single thing the back seven is doing well consistently. Then there’s the discipline on offense. Detroit racked up another nine penalties on Sunday night, most of which were of the pre-snap variety. Campbell took complete ownership of those mistakes after the game. “The bottom line is I’m not getting that across. I’m not getting it done right now because it’s still happening, so I put that squarely on my shoulders—that I’m not getting it coached properly,” Campbell said. “I’m the one who’s going to get this fixed. I’m the one who is going to fix this whole discipline thing, whatever it takes.” And if I can get a little nitpicky, offensive coordinator Drew Petzing deserves some heat for the final drive of the game. Detroit had plenty of time to mount a game-winning drive, but he got greedy. On second-and-7, Petzing dialed up a long-developing double-move to Jameson Williams—hoping to get a big chunk play. Instead, the Lions got the one thing they couldn’t afford: a sack. I know the Lions had hit on some deep shots earlier in the game, but that play reeked of desperation when they didn’t need to be in desperation mode. Detroit had plenty of time for some easier, shorter passes to methodically move down the field and get their late shots at the end zone.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Detroit’s defense comes face-to-face with its ugly past selves
summary: The sports teams in the city of Detroit had a weekend. The Detroit Red Wings kicked things off on Friday, and before the season even started, the fans voiced their frustration with Dylan Larkin, mercilessly booing the former captain. Within five minutes of the puck dropping, the Hockeytown faithful summed up their thoughts on ownership […]
full_text: Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell watches a play against Kansas City Chiefs next to defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard during the second half at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri on Sunday, Oct. 12, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The sports teams in the city of Detroit had a weekend . The Detroit Red Wings kicked things off on Friday, and before the season even started, the fans voiced their frustration with Dylan Larkin, mercilessly booing the former captain. Within five minutes of the puck dropping, the Hockeytown faithful summed up their thoughts on ownership in just three words . Less than 24 hours later, Simon Edvinsson, the team’s young and promising defenseman—think Year 2 Jack Campbell—informed the team he’d prefer to be traded than sign another contract. Signs sat outside on the porch of one condo on Woodward facing LCA: “Sell the team, Chris.” “Red Wings fans deserve better.” The scene in Detroit Sunday, when I went down there for the Red Wings game against the Winnipeg Jets, it reminded me of that era of Lions football. The “Millen Man March” in December of 2005 came after the Lions went an abysmal 20-57 over a stretch of football games from 2001 to 2005. It was the lowest of lows for Lions fans both young and old. “Sunday Night Football” was an opportunity to wipe away the bewilderment brought on by the 2026 Detroit Red Wings. Their season was over before it began because of poor direction from leadership. Here’s to hoping this 2026 Detroit Lions team doesn’t fall victim to the same pitfalls. Because point blank, Detroit needs to do something to improve their secondary. Additional help at safety and a cornerback could both be used back there, but it isn’t going to mean a single thing if the person pulling the levers and pushing the buttons wants to spam Cover 0. Carolina ran the RPO so effective because Bryce Young could identify the pressure and get the ball into the space the defender had vacated. The Panthers ran the football on the Lions: Chuba Hubbard averaged 6.1 yards per carry across 20 carries but had a long of just 32. Sunday night’s takeaway is that the leadership on the defensive ball needs to be better. It needs to be built to cater and accentuate the strengths of its current personnel, not who they want to be when they’re at “full health.” The former linebackers coach has got to get those guys back on track. Jack Campbell looks like he’s playing not to make a mistake—and in turn, making mistakes. The vibes are way off. This defense is historically bad through four games . Detroit has allowed the third-most points per game (31.8) in the last 40 years, only outdone by… the Lions in 2008 (32.3) and 2020 (32.4). It’s hard on a weekend like this to see this defensive performance and not think about some of the other dysfunctional moments when this defense was absolutely dreadful. To think this team could be 3-1, maybe even 4-0 if they had a defense that wouldn’t let a team score 21-unanswered points on three straight drives to start a game, it’s remarkable. Not world beaters. Not Brian Flores and what he’s doing with much, much less—they rank 28th in spending on defensive players in the NFL, and only one player makes north of $10 million (Andrew Van Ginkel). If Kelvin Sheppard could even get this defense to be slightly below average , it’d help me forget about the territory this defense is headed toward. And after missing out on Joey Porter Jr., is Brad Holmes going to keep checking in with teams ahead of November’s trade deadline? Do the Lions have that much time to wait around and see if Brian Branch makes the difference? What’s going to happen during that upcoming bye week after the team travels to the desert to play a beatable Arizona Cardinals team? Do the Lions have time to wait around and see if the defense can avoid being as porous as its been? Only two people could answer these questions, and they’re the two leaders of this football team in Holmes and Dan Campbell. It’s more than just cleaning up and fixing a few things here or there for Campbell. He isn’t worried about being 2-2 with a 17-game schedule, and he isn’t going into “panic mode,” but I’d be lying if I think Brian Branch is going to make all the difference. It’s going to take Holmes digging into his draft day bag and getting talent in the building. It’s going to take Campbell entrusting the right person to lead that defense. If that person is indeed Kelvin Sheppard, it better happen soon. Another performance like this against the Arizona Cardinals could have the boo birds fly back north for a long Week 6 of restlessness.
author: Ryan Mathews

title: Dan Campbell refuses to talk about Kelvin Sheppard’s job security
summary: The Detroit Lions are four games into the 2026 season, and the defensive performance is reaching historically bad levels. Through four games, the Lions have allowed a league-high 1,695 yards (423.75 per game)—which is the second-most the Lions have ever given up through Week 4. Their 127 points allowed (31.75 per game) is, again, league-high, […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard, left, shakes hands with Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) after 32-26 loss to Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions are four games into the 2026 season, and the defensive performance is reaching historically bad levels. Through four games, the Lions have allowed a league-high 1,695 yards (423.75 per game)— which is the second-most the Lions have ever given up through Week 4 . Their 127 points allowed (31.75 per game) is, again, league-high, and it’s fourth-worst in franchise history . Naturally, the topic of firing defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard has come up publicly. Given the perceived talent on the team and the pretty significant spending on that side of the ball , the performance of the defense has been less than acceptable. It’s been atrocious, particularly with a back-seven of the defense that leaves acres of open grass for the opposing quarterbacks to attack. After Sunday night’s 32-26 loss to the Carolina Panthers, Lions coach Dan Campbell was not ready to talk about the future of Sheppard’s employment. He was asked how many of these bad performances he needs to see before he considers a change at defensive coordinator. His answer: “Yeah, I’m not talking about all that, man,” Campbell said. “I’m talking about getting better right now with what we got, and that’s what we’re going to do. We’re going to find a way to get better with what we got.” No one should expect Campbell to talk publicly about the job security of someone on his coaching staff, particularly in the minutes after a particularly humiliating loss. And Campbell was at least cognizant enough to point out that significant changes need to be made on that side of the ball. Campbell said he believes they have players who can play. They just need to start putting them in better positions to win. “We’ve got guys on the back end that can cover. We’ve got guys that can hit. We got to pull this thing together and find the right combination of coverage versus pressure and job responsibility, putting guys in the right spot to do what they do,” Campbell said. “And so this is a work in progress. We’re four games in. There again, we just have to find a way to get better. I thought we would play better than we did last week, and as a whole, we didn’t.” But at the same time, Campbell warned about overreacting too early. The team is still 2-2 with everything in front of them. The last thing he wants to do is go into “panic mode” with 13 games left. And he believes there are still plenty of things the team can try to pull themselves out of this defensive rut. “There’s some things we can mix in here that we haven’t done a ton of this year, and that’s next step. Let’s see what we can do,” Campbell said. “I want to exhaust everything here. Let’s exhaust everything we have.” While Campbell didn’t say it, “exhausting everything they have” should certainly involve entertaining the idea of some coaching changes. Whether it means shifting responsibilities or making some tough staff decisions, the Lions truly need to have everything on the table, because they won’t go far with the worst defense in football.

The Cardinals fired head coach Jonathan Gannon and his staff after the conclusion of the […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 22: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions looks to pass during an NFL football game between the Arizona Cardinals and the Detroit Lions at State Farm Stadium on September 22, 2024 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions (2-2) will stay on the road in Week 5, traveling to the desert to take on the Arizona Cardinals (1-3), and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -4.5 points . The Cardinals fired head coach Jonathan Gannon and his staff after the conclusion of the 2025 season—creating an opportunity for the Lions to hire offensive coordinator Drew Petzing—and hired former Rams offensive coordinator Mike LaFleur (brother of Packers HC Matt LaFleur). LaFleur retained Nick Rallis as defensive coordinator, brought in veteran playcaller Nathaniel Hackett as offensive coordinator, and went to work overhauling the roster. The Cardinals kicked their offseason off by releasing QB Kyler Murray and promoting Jacoby Brissett to their starting role, then drafted RB Jeremiyah Love with the third overall pick and signed Tyler Allgeier to bolster their running backs room while James Conner recovers from a 2025 foot injury on injured reserve. Additionally, they also signed WR Kendrick Bourne, LG Isaac Seumalo, and RT Elijah Wilkinson to starting roles. On defense, they re-signed DT Roy Lopez (who spent last season in Detroit) and gave him a starting role, then added LB Jack Gibbens and S Andrew Wingard as additional starters. As with most new regimes, things have started off bumpy. While the Cardinals pulled off a Week 1 win, it was over the 0-4 Chargers, who have struggled all season. Since then, the Cardinals have given up at least 31 points in all three games, losing 31-7 to the Seahawks, 36-30 to the 49ers, and 36-24 to a Jameis Winston-led Giants this past Sunday. Against New York, it was a back-and-forth game that came down to the wire, as the Cardinals got themselves in position to win the game, but Brissett threw his third interception of the contest, a pick-six that put the game out of reach. With all the problems the Lions are having on the defensive side of the ball right now, they’ll likely need to continue the trend of putting up 31+ points against the Cardinals if they want to win this game.
