title: Jaguars Winners And Losers From Week 4: Defense Leads In Tough Road Win
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars might have something cooking. On a Sunday where the Jags had to not only beat the Cincinnati Bengals but the NFL Zebras, they did so anyway, defeating Cincy on the road 22-17. It wasn’t pretty, but it was gritty, proving the Jags aren’t only capable of winning on the road but winning […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - OCTOBER 04: Defensive end Myles Murphy #99 of the Cincinnati Bengals is penalized for a face mask on running back Bhayshul Tuten #33 of the Jacksonville Jaguars during the second quarter of an NFL game at Paycor Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars might have something cooking. On a Sunday where the Jags had to not only beat the Cincinnati Bengals but the NFL Zebras, they did so anyway, defeating Cincy on the road 22-17 . It wasn’t pretty, but it was gritty, proving the Jags aren’t only capable of winning on the road but winning when things are not going 100% their way. There is no denying that this defense is legit after four games this season. And this offense is extremely effective when given the chance. Beating the Bengals doesn’t mean Jacksonville has the automatic path to the Super Bowl, but teams have to win those types of games if they are to have a legit chance at winning it all. The Jags now seem like they have the mettle to do it. WINNERS Mentality Sometimes you just need to get the monkey off your back. For some reason, the Bengals have been a thorn in the side of Jacksonville for a handful of years. Whenever these two teams meet all hell just breaks loose for some reason. While this matchup was no different, the score was in favor of the Jags this time. Losing to the Broncos stung. It stung even more when the team came home and pummeled the Patriots. I think Jacksonville needed a bit of a “prove it” road win to really put a stamp on the front part of the year and make it known far and wide this team can travel. The Jags don’t play in Jacksonville for quite some time now as they prepare to ship off to London. Earning a win like that could be an excellent boost as they embark overseas. Just listen to how head coach Liam Coen talks about this one. You need wins like this to really bring it all together. Tough team. Tough win. pic.twitter.com/ydMV36wo8c — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) October 4, 2026 Travis Hunter, Jourdan Lewis and Jarrian Jones It’s not often cornerbacks are winners when facing a Cincy offense featuring Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Despite what the stats may say, these guys played lights out. Hunter is now stacking consecutive great games on defense after ripping down his first pick last week. He had an athletic pick called back Sunday, but did only allow three catches for 21 yards to go with two pass breakups and a huge hit along the sideline. The second-year corner was the second highest graded player on the team according to PFF. Travis Hunter with a big hit, he's fired up! pic.twitter.com/yEWpTbNa9W — Fitz (@LaurieFitzptrck) October 4, 2026 As for the others, Jarrian Jones was second on the team in tackles (seven) and had a tackle for loss and this nice PBU . Jourdan Lewis took down a pick and almost housed it. This cornerback room rose to the challenge in a difficult circumstance, especially considering Higgins and Chase were catching a lot of balls for a lot of yards. That never broke the confidence in the corners and it was a humongous factor in why Jacksonville won. A big shoutout also goes to safety Rayuan Lane, who not only led the team in tackles but made the game-ending over field tackle to seal it. Ray Lane with the stop that wins the game for the Jaguars on 4th and 10 pic.twitter.com/iBYb7HTUoy — Fitz (@LaurieFitzptrck) October 4, 2026 Running The ball On the offensive side, Jacksonville had a solid time running the rock against Cincy’s pretty solid defensive line. Jacksonville rushed for 111 total yards and one ground score from Chris Rodriguez. Bhayshul Tuten led the game in rushing with 73 yards on 17 carries. Speaking of PFF grades, Tuten ended up being the highest graded player when all was said and done. Tuten now has back to back games over 70 yards rushing and three straight games with two catches. This running back core is coming together quite nicely after a bit of a quiet start. Chris Rodriguez makes it a two-score game with a 25-yard TD! JAXvsCIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/EocORsZ5jR — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Jacksonville needs to be able to run the ball effectively to set up its huge passing game. Conversely, the team needs to be able to stop the run in order to sell out to stop the pass which… Stopping The Run Jacksonville did that on Sunday! Cincinnati had absolutely nothing going on the ground, finishing the game with just 23 combined yards rushing. Cincy had just one run over four yards, the second time in franchise history the team was able to limit a rushing attack in such a manner. Arik Armstead had a big game. DaVon Hamilton had another bulldozing afternoon. Those guys sold out to stop the run and in turn were in the lap of Burrow all day. Again, the stats may not jump off the page because Burrow passed for over 400, but he had to because the Jags were not going to allow any run game to beat them. Bend but don’t break. Mission accomplished. Cam Little Obligatory Cam Little appreciation section. Little nailed three field goals with a long of 55. He is 4-6 on the year on kicks and perfect under 50 yards. Little’s leg was integral to victory on Sunday and he deserves a little bit of praise, like always. Al’s Pizza For the second straight week, the defense triggered the Al’s Pizza and Big Cat Country promo. Courtesy of interceptions by both Foye Oluokun and Lewis, customers can get 50% off their Al’s Pizza order through Oct. 6. Get some pizza and watch whatever the hell unfolds between the Saints and the Falcons on Monday night. Please forgive me for interrupting, but the defense has made two interceptions, so Al’s Pizza is offering 50% off pizza! Offer code “PIZZAPICKOFF” is valid for 48 hours after the game on https://t.co/VQgsy0KG5d 🐆 pic.twitter.com/XXlQ6qJiww — Big Cat Country (@BigCatCountry) October 4, 2026 The Pass Catchers In a game with some of the biggest wide receivers in football, it’s funny to me that Parker Washington didn’t have a bigger game. Instead, it was Brenton Strange who led the pass catchers. Strange had 95 yards on seven catches. It was a Strange catch that set up Rodriguez’s score and a Strange catch that extended Jacksonville’s last drive to eat up more clock. Lo’ and behold, it was Josh Cameron who was second on the team in receiving with 42 yards, coming ever so close to scoring yet again. Even Brian Thomas Jr. (yes, him!) scored on Sunday. It was an everybody eats type of afternoon for the pass catchers and it was exactly what Jacksonville needed. Josh Cameron gets inside the 5 on a catch-and-run 😤 JAXvsCIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CmTUPhSj6A — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 LOSERS Penalties Holy shit was a showing from the NFL referees. There were 24 accepted penalties in that game, 13 of which going against the Jags. Multiple touchdowns were called back. A Hunter interception was called back. Years of our lives were taken away because of how many flags made it to the ground. And we were not even the only game to have trouble with the refs . The damn cover photo for this article features a penalty by the way. It was all just so unreal to watch, even the penalties that actually were really penalties. Good on Coen for being diplomatic after the game because he could have exploded. At least the Jags won. Imagine if we lost AND had 13 penalties. Liam Coen didn’t want to get fined commenting about penalties in the first half 🤣 “I’m not going to say anything to get fined. That was just mental. I’ve just never seen something quite that much in the first half of a football game.” #Jaguars #DUUUVAL pic.twitter.com/MgJVds9JyW — Action Sports Jax (@ActionSportsJax) October 4, 2026 The Rest Of The AFC South There is no reason to really pile on the rest of the AFC South after four weeks but I’m going to anyway. Houston is winless, losing three games at home already. Thankfully for them, they have to…

title: Chiefs skill-position players were heroic in win over Raiders
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs had a roller-coaster game, and that was especially true for their wide receivers. The group’s peak performance came from a duo of speedsters: wide receivers Xavier Worthy and Tyquan Thornton combined for 181 receiving yards on nine catches. Worthy fought off tight coverage to secure a jump-ball pass for 41 yards, […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs had a roller-coaster game, and that was especially true for their wide receivers. The group’s peak performance came from a duo of speedsters: wide receivers Xavier Worthy and Tyquan Thornton combined for 181 receiving yards on nine catches. Worthy fought off tight coverage to secure a jump-ball pass for 41 yards, while Thornton caught passes for 41 and 55 yards along with two red-zone touchdowns. Unfortunately, the dips were extreme: Thornton suffered a serious ankle injury at the conclusion of the 55-yard bomb in the fourth quarter. That came after wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring) left the game in the first quarter after coming up limp after a catch-and-run. Thornton’s injury unfairly overshadows what can be considered his career-best performance. Thornton scored on third-and-goal to open the scoring, then caught a beautiful pass down the left sideline from quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the two-minute drill before halftime. To start the fourth quarter, Thornton caught another great throw from Mahomes, this time off a well-executed shoulder fake in the red zone. If his day wasn’t already heroic enough, he made arguably the most important play of the entire game seconds before suffering a brutal injury. Tyquan Thornton went down after this play pic.twitter.com/oRrUsDxfQ7 https://t.co/mZ6TjUmnI1 — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) October 4, 2026 While Thronton’s heroic effort unfortunately became sacrificial, it was immediately followed up by two touchdown runs from running back Ken Walker, the two deciding scores of the game. Walker acknowledged some motivation stemming from an awful moment for his teammate during his post-game press conference. “You never want to see that happen to anybody,” Walker began. “It’s kind of motivating in a sense where you have to play for your brother that much harder.” Walker was heroic himself; he finished with 177 rushing yards — and 76 of them came on a game-changing play at the end of the third quarter. An off-tackle run to the right produced a massive hole, and Walker wasted no time bursting through it into the third level of Las Vegas’ defense. He flew down the sideline for the longest run by any Chiefs player in seven years. He broke through after a first half that offered less open space for Kansas City’s offense. Walker was stuffed on a fourth-and-short run in the first quarter, ending an opening drive where the Chiefs failed on third down twice. The team kept handing off to Walker, who finished with 22 carries, and that commitment was crucial to the Chiefs’ pass catchers having one-on-one opportunities downfield. On Worthy’s big play, Mahomes purposefully put air under the ball, valuing the chance for Worthy to strong-arm a defensive back for the completion rather than potentially overshooting a deeper pass on the run. “The one early to Xavier, I probably could have tried to throw it further,” Mahomes recalled. “But I was just trying to give him a chance to make a play versus another cover zero-type look, and he went up and made a big play. “It doesn’t always have to be perfect thrown by me,” Mahomes noted. ”It’s about giving guys chances to make plays.” Worthy could see the play coming and knew his quarterback would give him the chance to complete the explosive play. “Everybody blitzed,” Worthy recalled at the podium. “I knew Pat was going to put it up and we went up and made a play.” Whether it was Thornton, Walker, Worthy, or any of the other seven Chiefs who touched the ball on offense, it was an outstanding performance by Mahomes’ supporting cast in Las Vegas.

title: Chiefs’ Tyquan Thornton to have surgery with ‘12 to 16-week’ recovery timeline
summary: An extreme high turned into an extreme low when Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton crumpled into the grass after attempting to celebrate a 55-yard completion late in the Chiefs’ 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Fortunately (as much as the news around this kind of injury can be), Thornton cleanly dislocated his ankle, by […]
full_text: (Photo by Steve Marcus/Getty Images) | Getty Images An extreme high turned into an extreme low when Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton crumpled into the grass after attempting to celebrate a 55-yard completion late in the Chiefs’ 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders . Fortunately (as much as the news around this kind of injury can be), Thornton cleanly dislocated his ankle, by all accounts, and is set for surgery this week. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported the dislocated ankle on Sunday evening, then followed up with more information on Monday. After extensive tests today, Tyquan Thornton is expected back within 12 to 16 weeks, sources say. He’ll have surgery within the week and there is a real chance at a late-season or playoff return. https://t.co/AgiJI94AzJ — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 5, 2026 Rapoport reported that after extensive tests on Monday, Thornton is preparing for surgery this week and has “a real chance at a late-season or playoff return.” He set the timeline at 12 to 16 weeks. Cameron Wolfe, a national NFL reporter for NFL Network , is reporting that the surgery is expected to be performed by Dr. Norman Waldrop , “a top foot and ankle specialist who works on many NFL stars.” 12 weeks from today is December 28, the day after a home game against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 16. Four weeks later would be the NFL’s Divisional Round weekend of postseason games. While it is not the same injury, the timeline recalls former Chiefs wide receiver Hollywood Brown’s saga during the 2024 season after he suffered a dislocated clavicle in the preseason. He returned in Week 16 and became an impactful player on the way to Super Bowl LIX. At the time of his injury, Thornton led the team in yards per reception (19.9) and ranked second in yards (219). He is the only wide receiver with multiple touchdowns this season, both coming in Las Vegas. There’s reason to believe Thornton could step back into the lineup and be a very impactful player during the course of a potential playoff run.

title: A comeback to Kansas City feels inevitable in the receiving corps
summary: There have been eight months of lead-up to the current rumors swirling around the Kansas City Chiefs and five-time All-Pro wide receiver Tyreek Hill. When Hill was released in mid-February while recovering from a severe knee injury, many in Chiefs Kingdom immediately thought to re-sign him, once he’s fully healthy or before. Now, it feels […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images There have been eight months of lead-up to the current rumors swirling around the Kansas City Chiefs and five-time All-Pro wide receiver Tyreek Hill. When Hill was released in mid-February while recovering from a severe knee injury, many in Chiefs Kingdom immediately thought to re-sign him, once he’s fully healthy or before. Now, it feels inevitable that the Cheetah will be returning to Kansas City. After the Chiefs’ 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders that featured injuries to wide receivers Tyquan Thornton (ankle) and Rashee Rice (hamstring), Michael Silver of The Athletic reported that the team is “very interested” in signing Hill . Silver writes the team was “already interested in a reunion before Sunday.” Then, Monday morning, ESPN’s Adam Schefter shared a developing story about Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus expressing plans to “begin negotiating a deal” for Hill on Monday. Schefter’s Twitter post mentioned “multiple teams,” but the Chiefs were the only team named. Through Schefter, Rosenhaus relayed a timeline to the public. “I would anticipate Tyreek potentially signing with a team over the next few days,” During “The Aftermath,” an NFL Network show airing Monday, insider Ian Rapoport said, “it would be a surprise if he does not sign back with the Kansas City Chiefs.” Based on these high-level sources, Chiefs fans should expect Hill back in Kansas City. But when will he actually be able to don the red and gold again? I expect the Chiefs to have strong interest in a Tyreek Hill reunion when the free agent receiver is healthy enough to play. He's believed to be targeting a November return. Players I talked to in the locker room (Mahomes, Kelce, Chris Jones & others) are all for it. @TheAthletic — Michael Silver (@MikeSilver) October 5, 2026 Silver mentioned that Hill is “targeting a November return” to the field. The Chiefs are on a bye this week, but the team will play the Los Angeles Chargers and then face the Seattle Seahawks on the road before November begins with a battle against the Denver Broncos at Mile High on the first of the month. With that in mind, could another reunion be in play for Kansas City? The expectation is that Thornton will be placed on the Reserve/Injured list, though that doesn’t mean his season is over, and Rice could be back quickly from his hamstring, based on insight from Rapoport. The team could feel the need for immediate help in the receiving room. Former Chiefs wideout Justin Watson is a free agent and preceded Thornton as a downfield target in the Chiefs’ offense, although Thornton clearly upgraded the position from 2024 to 2025. Juju Smith-Schuster is available after the New York Giants cut him during the preseason. Mecole Hardman was also released before the regular season began after a stint with the Buffalo Bills . It feels like the Chiefs and Hill will reunite soon — so now the question is: will there be two comebacks to Kansas City over the bye week? Bonus question: will rookie running back Emmett Johnson surrender the No. 10 jersey to arguably the franchise’s all-time wide receiver?
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Andy Reid says special teams was Chiefs’ best phase in win over Raiders
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs needed a full-game effort to outlast the Las Vegas Raiders in the Week 4 bout that finished 30-27. The offense came alive in the fourth quarter with 20 points while the defense made enough stops to hold the Raiders down. However, head coach Andy Reid called the third phase of the […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs needed a full-game effort to outlast the Las Vegas Raiders in the Week 4 bout that finished 30-27. The offense came alive in the fourth quarter with 20 points while the defense made enough stops to hold the Raiders down. However, head coach Andy Reid called the third phase of the game “the best” in his opening statement after the game. At the podium, Reid detailed the impact of special teams coordinator Dave Toub’s unit. “I think special teams was the best part of the three phases today,” Reid said. “(Punter) [Matt] Araiza with the fake punt did a nice job there. We didn’t capitalize on it offensively, but what a job he did there, and then the punt down there at the end, I thought, was nice.“ Araiza was locked in from the jump, which included the fake, where he sprinted to the right with the ball and took a big hit after moving the chains. After that, he punted five times; the Raiders produced only four yards off those kicks, which averaged nearly 47 yards. Rookies finishing off a masterpiece by Araiza 💣 pic.twitter.com/2uHPFiaDH4 — Arrowhead Pride (@ArrowheadPride) October 4, 2026 The last of his five punts seemingly iced the game, pinning the Raiders’ offense at their own one-yard line with only 1:16 of game time and no timeouts to move down the field for a game-tying field goal. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson made an athletic play to toss the ball back to rookie safety Xavier Nwankpa in order to finish off the on-target punt by Araiza. Reid noted Johnson’s “great instincts” and pointed out that he is still learning and growing as a special-teams player, benefiting from Toub’s and assistant special teams coach Porter Ellett’s direction. “Emmett is doing running back, and he’s working the special teams, which he hasn’t done a lot of in his career,” Reid said. “But Dave has been teaching him and pushing him along there; he and Porter.” It wasn’t just punt coverage; the team also made plays on kickoffs. Reid pointed out the forced fumble by second-year linebacker Jeffrey Bassa in the fourth quarter as a pivotal play. Veteran linebacker Jack Cochrane secured the turnover. “The play of the game was Bassa punching the kickoff out,” Reid noted. “Then Cochrane getting it back there. What a great job he did on that with the forced fumble, and like I said, probably the biggest play of the game.” In a road divisional matchup, the little things matter in a game of inches. Kansas City’s young special teams unit has plenty to clean up with penalties, but the third phase of the game made a difference in the close win on Sunday.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Who gets your game ball from the Chiefs’ win over the Raiders?
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are 4-0 after a 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4! Wide receiver Tyquan Thornton currently leads the poll for his heroic effort on Sunday, totaling 111 yards on five catches with two red-zone touchdowns. He gained 42 yards on a second-quarter play that set up a field […]
full_text: (Photo by Steve Marcus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs are 4-0 after a 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4! Wide receiver Tyquan Thornton currently leads the poll for his heroic effort on Sunday, totaling 111 yards on five catches with two red-zone touchdowns. He gained 42 yards on a second-quarter play that set up a field goal before halftime, then caught and ran for 55 yards on a third-down play in the fourth quarter that ended with a very unfortunate injury. However, defensive end George Karlaftis was a menace for the Raiders’ offensive line. He finished with five total tackles — including a tackle for loss — a pass defended and six quarterback hits! He accounted for more than half of the team’s hits on Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins. Running back Kenneth Walker’s 76-yard run was just one of his difference-making plays in Las Vegas. He finished with 177 rushing yards over 22 attempts and scored two touchdowns. The team’s commitment to the run game allowed Walker to break loose and virtually put the game away in the fourth quarter. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane finished as the team’s leading tackler (10) while also breaking up a pass and making one tackle behind the line of scrimmage. Here are the top comments from the post-game poll: NCRaiderHater I know you can’t give Delane the nod here, but it turns out this young man is really, really good at football. Sticky in coverage and great at the run D as well. I have a feeling he’s going to be viewed as one of the best corners in football very soon. Steve Soper Bassa. I feel like he made the play of the game that won it for KC. afflatusmisery Even if he hadn’t gotten hurt, Thornton was making clutch play after clutch play. I would say he had a slight edge over K9, but the injury while making a game changing play seals it for me imo. RunningFree Hard to hand it to anyone but the guy who had a career day before disaster struck. 138 of Mahomes 225 total passing yards were the 3 long completions to Thornton and Worthy. With some time to sleep on it, who gets your game ball from Week 4?

title: Chiefs Week 4 snap count analysis: Chamarri Conner returns as starter
summary: Welcome to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! Let’s take a closer look at the Kansas City Chiefs’ playing time in the 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes from Pro Football Focus’ premium stats. Starters (offensive): LT Kahlil […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Arrowhead Pride’s weekly snap-count analysis! Let’s take a closer look at the Kansas City Chiefs ’ playing time in the 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4. The starting lineups are courtesy of NFL Game Stats and Information, and the snap-count data comes from Pro Football Focus’ premium stats. Starters (offensive): LT Kahlil Benson, LG Mike Caliendo, C Creed Humphrey, RG Trey Smith, RT Jaylon Moore, QB Patrick Mahomes, WR Tyquan Thornton, WR Rashee Rice, WR Xavier Worthy, RB Kenneth Walker and TE Travis Kelce Starters (defensive): DE George Karlaftis, DT Chris Jones, DT Khyiris Tonga, DE Felix Anudike-Uzomah, LB Nick Bolton, LB Drue Tranquill, LB Jack Cochrane, CB Mansoor Delane, CB L’Jarius Sneed, S Alohi Gilman and S Chamarri Conner Did not play: LG Kingsley Suamataia, QB Justin Fields Inactive: TE Jared Wiley, QB Garrett Nussmeier (Emergency third QB), DB Jadon Canady, DE Jack Pyburn, OT Diego Pounds, LT Josh Simmons (Back) The big takeaway: Jalen Royals, not Cyrus Allen, steps up With the injuries of two starting receivers, second-year wide receiver Jalen Royals stepped up and played the second-most snaps of his career (38), only behind the season finale last season in Las Vegas (43). Royals didn’t record a catch over two targets (and 22 pass plays), but he was the next man up over rookie wideout Cyrus Allen, who only played five snaps. Allen saw one target, but it came on a drawn-out play that felt closer to a desperation heave from quarterback Patrick Mahomes than an in-rhythm play. Without Rashee Rice, Royals’ ability to gain yards after catch with physical running will continue to be utilized, but it will be worth monitoring how Royals and Allen’s role change with the absence of Tyquan Thornton now factored in. The Offensive takeaway: Emmett Johnson is the pass-down back Rookie running back Emmett Johnson played the second-most snaps (17) of his career and the most pass-play snaps (12) of the season. Johnson did not receive a handoff over his time on the field, but did catch a screen pass that gained 10 yards at one point. In the shadows of lead back Ken Walker’s 177 yards on the ground, Johnson is settling more into a pass-down role and is hogging the playing time from second-year back Brashard Smith, who only played two snaps on offense in Las Vegas. Smith has only played six snaps on offense this season. The Defensive takeaway: Chamarri Conner returns as primary starter In his season debut, safety Chamarri Conner played 75% of the team’s defensive snaps and played the same amount of snaps as starting slot defender L’Jarius Sneed (63). He was one of the two starting safeties, along with Alohi Gilman, taking over the role of third-year safety Jaden Hicks, who only played 29 snaps in Week 4. However, Hicks (13) nearly played the same amount of run-defense snaps as Conner (18), which shows that the Chiefs’ defense still values Hicks’ skills in certain situations. In previous seasons, Conner has been an every-down starter. Safety Christian Roland-Wallace (29 snaps) also saw a good amount of playing time, speaking to the team’s reliance on Dime personnel (six defensive backs in formation) against the Raiders. Before Week 4, Roland-Wallace’s season-high snap-count total was 12. Offensive Snaps Defensive Snaps Special teams snaps

title: Chargers-Seahawks Winners/Losers: A tale of 2 halves for Justin Herbert
summary: The Chargers really had a shot at getting their first win of the season against the reigning Super Bowl champs. They really did. Even after two bad first half interceptions from Justin Herbert, it all came down to one final drive for the Chargers. But alas, it wasn’t meant to be. There was a lot […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 04: Khalil Mack #52 of the Los Angeles Chargers sacks Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter at Lumen Field on October 04, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers really had a shot at getting their first win of the season against the reigning Super Bowl champs. They really did. Even after two bad first half interceptions from Justin Herbert, it all came down to one final drive for the Chargers. But alas, it wasn’t meant to be. There was a lot of bad during Sunday’s loss. We’ve come to expect that throughout a very frustrating first month of the season. There was also some good that needs to be celebrated, but it’s unfortunate that it wasn’t enough to finally get this team over the hump. Let’s talk about it. Winners QB Justin Herbert (Second Half) It really was a tale of two halves for Herbert. In the first half, he completed less than half his passes and did not break 40 passing yards. In the second half, he topped 150 yards and a touchdown, including a few clutch throws in the fourth quarter to Quentin Johnston and Tre’ Harris. It also wasn’t a surprise that when the offense simplified itself and went into full two-minute mode, Herbert looked much more comfortable running the offense. From a down-to-down basis in the final 15 minutes, it truly looked like the Herbert of old. He looked COMFORTABLE. He looked POISED. If Mike McDaniel and Jim Harbaugh do not make a note of that going forward, then shame on them because it was night and day. EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu On the second play of the entire game, Tuli picked off Sam Darnold to get the ball right back after Herbert’s opening play turnover. Tuli followed the running back to the sideline on a swing route and when Darnold pulled the trigger, the back slipped and was not in a position to contest at the catch point. While Tuli did not record a sack, he helped bottle up the run game and created pressure to keep Darnold jittery in the pocket. His 91.6 overall game grade from PFF was also his highest grade of the young season. EDGE Khalil Mack Mack recorded his third sack of the season and is currently on pace to record his second double-digit sack season since being traded from the Bears during the Brandon Staley era. In a very disapponting season thus far, especially for all the veterans that continue to put their bodies on the line and put off their eventual retirement, Mack has been an all-around difference-maker up front. If the postseason isn’t ever going to bounce his way, then he can at least pad his career stats on the way out the door. Losers QB Justin Herbert (First Half) As mentioned above, Herbert’s first half was a far cry from his second half performance. Herbert began the game with an ugly interception where he targeted tight end Oronde Gadsden over the middle. I gave Herbert the benefit of the doubt initially because it looked like linebacker Drake Thomas was covered in his line of sight by the offensive line before showing up just after Herbert pulled the trigger. However, a Seahakws safety was also right there to undercut the pass if Thomas did not make the play. Either way you looked at that one, it was going to end up being a concerning decision. Then there was the second interception. This one looked even more concerning. After watching the replauy numerous times, there’s not reason Herbert should have thrown the pass. It was on a double slant concept and Herbert was looking to hit Ladd McConkey on the second slant. The thing is, linebacker Ernest Jones dropped back into the window of the slants and even with him sitting squarely in the passing window, Herbert threw it anyway. It could not have been an easier pick for Jones. Herbert now has six interceptions in four games played this season. DT Justin Eboigbe Eboige has been a bright spot on this defense for most of the this young season but his decision to fall on top of Darnold after he slid was nearly more catastrophic than it ended up being. With a few seconds left before the two-minute warning, Darnold was flushed from the pocket and headed towards the sideline. It was third down and the Chargers needed to get a stop to have enough time to put together a final drive to tie the game. Darnold’s slide sealed the Chargers’ chances of getting the ball back to run a two-minute drill. However, Eboigbe didn’t just touch Darnold down, he fell entirely on his head. He was then flagged for unnecessary roughness and gave Seattle a fresh set of down. The Seahawks ultimately did punt back to the Chargers with a little over 90 seconds left in the game so they had a shot nonetheless, but for Eboigbe to be that undisciplined and lack that awareness in the moment was a really bad look.
author: Michael Peterson

title: Chargers Week 4 PFF Grades: Tuli Tuipulotu, Khalil Mack ravaged the Seahawks OL
summary: In a game where the defense still played well despite the 30 points put up by the Seahawks, it was edge rushers Tuli Tuipulotu and Khalil Mack that shined the brightest. Tuli was the team’s highest-graded player with an elite 91.7 game grade, followed by Mack’s 86.1. Offensively — and you’re not going to believe […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 27: Tuli Tuipulotu #45 of the Los Angeles Chargers on the field before a game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images In a game where the defense still played well despite the 30 points put up by the Seahawks, it was edge rushers Tuli Tuipulotu and Khalil Mack that shined the brightest. Tuli was the team’s highest-graded player with an elite 91.7 game grade, followed by Mack’s 86.1. Offensively — and you’re not going to believe this — but right guard Cole Strange was that unit’s highest-graded player at 75.5. That’s surprising and also not surprising given that he was one of two healthy starters to begin and end the game. In a very up-and-down game for the Chargers, it’s a positive to see them hang around the reigning Super Bowl champs long enough to actually threaten them with a loss on the very last drive. Is that enough for fans to calm down in any sense of the word? My guess is no. Alright, let’s take a look at this week’s grades. Offense Best RG Cole Strange – 75.5 OT Joe Alt – 74.7 LT Logan Taylor – 74.6 TE Oronde Gadsden – 71.7 RB Omarion Hampton – 65.5 Strange went from being the offense’s worst-graded player to their highest-graded player in the span of a week. His 75.5 was tops among the unit and his run block grade was an elite 90.8. Alt’s 77.3 in run blocking was second best while his pass block grade of 66.3 was fifth best. Taylor’s first 28 snaps of his career ended in him earning a near-elite 86.6 pass block grade. His 66.9 run block grade was good for fourth. Hampton saw a season-low 25 snaps but looked great when he was leaned upon in the second half. The Chargers would be wise to not overthink his fumbles and continue to ride their first-round pick. Omarion Hampton finds the hole for the touchdown! pic.twitter.com/OG7eBXlegu — TSN (@TSN_Sports) October 4, 2026 Worst C Jacob Spomer – 42.2 QB Justin Herbert – 43.8 WR Ladd McConkey – 44.0 TE Hayden Rucci – 50.7 TE Patrick Herbert – 52.0 Spomer’s first 11 career snaps came against the likes of Leonard Williams and Byron Murphy. That’s a real “Welcome to the NFL” moment for the undrafted rookie. He’ll be better for being thrown to the wolves like this and I’m not too worried about how he looked in that small sample size against elite competition. Herbert had two egregious interceptions, both of which were thrown directly into the arms of a linebacker standing in front of his intended receiver. Both were indefensible. I’m not sure what he was looking at nor what McDaniel coaches him to do on those particular plays but it was really, really bad on the live broadcast. McConey dropped his first pass of the season and it happened third down to kill a promising drive. Looks like the bad vibes have now extended to the team’s best wideout. Patrick Herbert, Justin’s brother, recorded a higher grade but still wound up in the bottom five with a terrible 22.0 in pass blocking. Defense Best EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu – 91.7 EDGE Khalil Mack – 86.1 LB Troy Dye – 74.7 S Elijah Molden – 66.0 LB Marlowe Wax – 65.9 Tuli’s grade was pushed into elite territory due to high grades in every area other than pass rush. His interception gave him an elite coverage grade of 93.8 to go with an 82.0 in run defense and a 75.6 in tackling. Mack produced one sack and four pressures while leading the team with four stops. He also posted an 82.0 in run defense and a 69.6 in pass rush (second best on the team). Dye posted a team-high 72.7 pass rush grade that was reinforced with a sack on third down to force a punt by Seattle during their final drive of the game. The huge play gave the Chargers a shot at tying it up in the final 90 seconds. Tuli Tuipulotu chega na luta contra os atuais campeões! 📺: #LACvsSEA – ao vivo no SporTV2 e GE TV pic.twitter.com/tcU4LkibXb — NFL Brasil (@NFLBrasil) October 4, 2026 Worst DT Justin Eboigbe – 37.0 EDGE Bud Dupree – 37.5 S Tony Jefferson – 40.2 DT Teair Tart – 40.5 LB Del’Shawn Phillips – 41.7 Eboigbe’s unnecessary roughness penalty late in the fourth quarter almost erased any chance the Chargers had at a final drive to tie it up. His run defense of 47.0 was fourth worst on the team, as well. Jefferson’s 33.4 coverage grade was tied for worst on the team with Phillips. Phillips’ 28.5 in tackling was fourth worst on the team and his 54.3 run defense grade was middle of the pack. Tart posted a 40.5 in tackling (fifth worst) and a 51.6 in run defense (sixth worst). He had two pressures but a missed tackle.

title: Los Angeles Chargers news: A positive takeaway from the loss to the Seahawks
summary: The Chargers lost a close one against the Seahawks on Sunday and wouldn’t you know it, but we got a little glimpse of the old Justin Herbert during the second half comeback attempt. Once the Chargers offense was pressed for time and needed multiple scores, the whole system looked to be simplified by Mike McDaniel […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 04: Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers reacts after a touchdown against the Seattle Seahawks during the fourth quarter at Lumen Field on October 04, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers lost a close one against the Seahawks on Sunday and wouldn’t you know it, but we got a little glimpse of the old Justin Herbert during the second half comeback attempt. Once the Chargers offense was pressed for time and needed multiple scores, the whole system looked to be simplified by Mike McDaniel at the drop of a hat. No more motions. No more unique handoff techniques. It simply became Herbert sitting in the shotgun dissecting the defense while STILL being chased around on every play (some things never change!). The wildest thing was that the offense looked even better once it was just a bunch of backups in the game protecting him. I can’t put my finger on it, but it just felt…normal? And that’s probably a terrible thing but it certainly looked like Herbert was able to find a groove from play to play. After suffering through the better part of the first month of the season while watching this offense, Sunday’s second half really did feel like a return to home. Herbert made hero plays, his receivers were coming through for him (even Quentin Johnston!) and they were able to move the ball consistently down the field. That’s a silver lining if there ever was one. And now for today’s links. title: Rams Injury Report: Mumpfield, Forbes suffer minor injuries
summary: The Los Angeles Rams left Philadelphia with a much-needed 24-20 victory over the Eagles, but the team did pick up a couple of minor injuries along the way during their east coast trip. Wide receiver Konata Mumpfield suffered a rotator cuff contusion, while cornerback Emmanuel Forbes sustained a knee contusion during Sunday’s victory. Head coach […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 4: Konata Mumpfield #4 of the Los Angeles Rams attempts to catch a pass during an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on October 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams left Philadelphia with a much-needed 24-20 victory over the Eagles, but the team did pick up a couple of minor injuries along the way during their east coast trip. Rams WR Konata Mumpfield has a rotator cuff contusion, Sean McVay says. Doesn't sound like something Rams are worried about. Same with Emmanuel Forbes (knee contusion) — Adam Grosbard (@AdamGrosbard) October 5, 2026 Wide receiver Konata Mumpfield suffered a rotator cuff contusion, while cornerback Emmanuel Forbes sustained a knee contusion during Sunday’s victory. Head coach Sean McVay indicated Monday that he was not particularly concerned about either injury, suggesting both players have a chance to avoid a significant absence. Mumpfield played 23 offensive snaps against Philadelphia, catching one pass for seven yards on three targets. Forbes stepped into a larger defensive role because of Jaylen Watson’s absence, playing 21 snaps and recording one tackle. Their availability will nevertheless be worth monitoring as the Rams prepare for a Week 5 matchup with the Buffalo Bills. The bigger picture is more encouraging for Los Angeles, as several important reinforcements are on the horizon. Myles Garrett remains on injured reserve following his knee injury, but he is eligible to return following the Bills game. That means the Rams could potentially have their prized defensive addition back on the field beginning in Week 6. Garrett’s eventual return remains one of the biggest storylines surrounding the team, particularly with the possibility of pairing him with Aaron Donald. And that pairing could finally become a reality soon. Aaron Donald missed the Week 4 victory over Philadelphia because of back soreness, but McVay said Monday that the veteran defensive lineman is trending toward a return for Week 5 against Buffalo. Donald’s return would provide an enormous boost to a defensive front that has had to operate without both Donald and Garrett for stretches of the season. The secondary remains a concern, however. Jaylen Watson is still dealing with his shoulder injury and remains essentially week-to-week. McVay expressed optimism that Watson could potentially return against Buffalo if he responds well during the week of practice, but his status will need to be monitored closely. The Rams also suffered a significant loss at tight end when Terrance Ferguson was placed on injured reserve because of his medial ankle sprain. Ferguson had emerged as an important part of the passing game early this season, so his absence creates another opportunity for Colby Parkinson and rookie Max Klare to take on increased responsibilities. Ferguson is expected to return later this season rather than miss the entire year. Parkinson’s own status is also worth watching. He has dealt with a knee/shoulder issue and was questionable heading into the Eagles game. He remains on the injury report entering Week 5, meaning the Rams could potentially have some uncertainty at tight end despite the return of other injured players. Ultimately, the Rams appear to be getting healthier at precisely the right time. Mumpfield and Forbes’ injuries do not currently appear serious, Donald could return against Buffalo, Watson has a chance to return, and Garrett could be back beginning in Week 6. If Los Angeles can navigate the next couple of weeks without suffering additional significant injuries, the defense could look dramatically different by the middle of October. A healthy Donald followed by the return of Garrett would give the Rams a defensive front capable of changing games, while Watson’s eventual return would further stabilize a secondary that has already performed well despite the injuries. After a 2-2 start, the Rams may finally be approaching the point where their preseason expectations begin to meet their actual roster.

title: Rams snap count review: L.A. defense puts the pressure on Philly
summary: For the first 53 minutes of Sunday’s game, the Los Angles Rams offense matched the Philadelphia weather, dank, damp and heavy-footed, they did just about everything in their power to lose the game. But on their final two drives, they found some dry gun powder and shot down the Eagles 24-20 on Lincoln Financial Field […]
full_text: Los Angeles Rams running back Kyren Williams celebrate a come back win (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images For the first 53 minutes of Sunday’s game, the Los Angles Rams offense matched the Philadelphia weather, dank, damp and heavy-footed, they did just about everything in their power to lose the game. But on their final two drives, they found some dry gun powder and shot down the Eagles 24-20 on Lincoln Financial Field in Philly. While the offense was all smiles and got the post-game accolades and interviews, it was the defense that kept L.A. within striking distance, turning in, for all intents and purpose, a smothering effort. The Rams used a myriad of pre-snap looks, often mixing and matching seven different players in the box and on the line of scrimmage, all designed to keep Eagle QB Jalen Hurts off balance. It worked. In all the Rams blitzed on 60+ percent of snaps and created pressure on 13 of 18 of them, allowing just five completions of 16 passes. Overall, Hurts was 12 of 27 passing for 93 yards gross and only two completions and 10 yards in the second half. L.A. blitzed on every third down, until the Eagles final possession. Philly did not convert a single third down in the game (0-12). Here the snap count review from Sunday, players their snap counts and percentage of play time in bold. Defensive line Kobie Turner ( 48, 79%) Turner is consistently solid, against both run and pass. Hustles constantly and wins a lot of battles. Got back to his 70+ percent play rate and was handful all game for the Eagles offensive line. Maybe he needs more snaps to get a lather up and less rotation. Braden Fiske ( 44, 72%) Fiske came back a after a tough game against Denver and had seven pressures by my count and a QB hit. He’s a bit under-sized, but plays with maximum effort. His highest snap count since the middle of last season. Poona Ford ( 26, 43%), Tyler Davis ( 22, 36%) While not outstanding individually, they combined for five tackles and played as part of a front line that held a good running team to 104 rushing yards on 27 attempts. Larrell Murchison (12, 20%), Ty Hamilton ( 11, 18%) A package deal, the two were inserted into the game together. Not just mop-up, they could be seen on the field as early as the first quarter. Edge Byron Young ( 54, 89%) Young stacked another fine performance. He was in on six tackles, two of those for loss, had 2.5 sacks, three QB hits, and forced a fumble. He passed Leonard Floyd (29) and James Hall (30) and on the Rams all-time sack list and is now tied for with Reggie Doss at 31. Also passed Ryan Pickett and tied London Fletcher (35) for 12th in all-time tackles for loss. Josaiah Stewart ( 32, 52%) Not sure if he’s nicked up, but Stewart has not been playing with his usual edge. Wesley Bailey ( 29, 48%), Desjuan Johnson ( 7, 11%) Bailey has taken over E#3, his snaps are trending up while Johnson falls back. Two words: Byron. Young. 😤 🎥 more highlights on https://t.co/d9sXTdTW10 pic.twitter.com/vTruKPvecU — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) October 5, 2026 Off-ball linebacker Nate Landman ( 57, 93%) Good game for Landman. Two plays stood out, a wrenching headlock on the Eagles QB when attempting a tush push (don’t think they tried another) and a hustle play where he navigated through traffic to make a tackle near the sideline. Omar Speights ( 18, 30%) His lowest play count since early 2024, his rookie season. Not sure if moving Lake into his position will be a trend or was a one-off. He did get a couple of nice tackles on special teams. Safety Quentin Lake ( 61, 100%) Almost made the finger tip interception that the Eagle receiver was able to juggle in for a score. Lake has played in every defensive snap in 2026 and been lined up all over the formation. After playing predominantly in the “STAR” hybrid position last year, he’s gone back to his base safety roots, 49.6% percent of snaps. He plays less slot this year and replaced it with off-ball linebacker duties (35.2%). Kamren Curl ( 61, 100%) Played deep safety on a lot of reps and the Eagles could not get the downfield passing game off the ground. He did, however lose track of his man in end zone coverage and allowed a Philly TD pass. Kamren Kinchens ( 43, 70%) L.A. has used dime personnel over 36 percent this season and Kinchens was a welcome addition. He was used as a blitzer numerous time on Sunday and got half a sack, a QB hit, and batted down a pass. He helped set the defensive tone early in the game, triggering downhill and laying the wood to an Eagle receiver on a short completion. Jaylen McCollough ( 3, 5%) The Rams didn’t get McCollough involved in the action, instead moving Lake to the second level when Speights subbed out. Cornerback Trent McDuffie ( 61, 100%) McDuffie has accrued more passes defended than he has completions allowed. I love the way he plays the game, vs pass or in run fits. Money well spent. Josh Wallace ( 61, 100%), Emmanuel Forbes ( 21, 34%) It’s good news when you hear little about your cornerbacks. The Rams pass rush pressure kept the Eagle pass game underneath, so neither were challenged much deep. While Forbes isn’t much of a tackler, Wallace appears willing and able to stick his nose in on run defense Special teams Another game, another poor performance. Punt coverage was drek, kickoff coverage was saved by a couple of shoestring tackles, and returns, both kickoff and punt were sluggish at best. Place kicker Harrison Meevis missed another field goal and made an egregious error sending a fourth quarter kickoff out of bounds. Quarterback Matthew Stafford ( 84, 100%) Another Jekyll and Hyde display from the Rams quarterback. “Bad” Stafford looked unsure and off-target throwing a pair of interceptions and 12 of 21 for 120 yards in the first half. He started to warm up a little in Quarter 3, but had nothing to show for it. “Good” Stafford finally made his presence in the Rams final two drives. cocksure and on target, going 10 for 14 and leading the Rams to the come from behind win. Staff worked out of the shot gun over 2/3 of snaps, lessening the effect of and reliance on play action. Running back Kyren Williams ( 70, 83%) Gutty effort, so fun to watch. Not a true power back nor speedster, Williams has the innate ability to make tacklers miss and sniff out the end zone. His two touchdowns brought him to 48 and tied with Henry Ellard for 8th place on Rams all-time list. For the future, the fact of his 10 catches looms as his most important accomplishment. Blake Corum ( 13, 15%) Since joining the Rams, Stafford hasn’t been one to check down or target his running backs, just 11.9%. This year that number is up to 20.4%. To that point, Corum has again lost ground in the snap count. If the Rams offense is going to settle in at 50 pass attempts per game, his dropping check down passes will keep him limited. Wide receiver Davante Adams ( 80, 95%) Hot and cold is the best descriptor for Adams’ performance. For all his time on field, his added value was measured. Broke free for big plays on a couple of reps, but Stafford missed him. On the other hand he had a couple of big drops and ran a half-assed effort route on the Rams final drive that was almost intercepted. Puka Nacua ( 76, 90%) How much does the Rams offense miss him? After a relatively quiet first half, he took over in the second, hauling in eight of nine passes. The importance of his strength at catch point and ability to roughhouse for extra yards after the catch cannot be understated. Jordan Whittington ( 42, 50%) With all the tight end injuries, the Rams leaned into three wide receiver sets at at an 87 percent clip. While Whittington doubled his season snap average, the role has been as a blocker, not an offensive target. On special teams, he hustles down as a gunner, but needs to get himself under control when approaching the returner. The Eagles kickoff team appeared content to stay away from him and allow Alex Bachman to…

title: Rams boast elite defensive stats even without Myles Garrett
summary: The addition of Trent McDuffie in the offseason is already paying off dividends for the L.A. Rams defense, as they rank second in passing yards allowed, second in yards per pass allowed, and third in EPA per pass allowed through four weeks. Even with no contributions yet from Myles Garrett, or practically Aaron Donald, the […]
full_text: The addition of Trent McDuffie in the offseason is already paying off dividends for the L.A. Rams defense, as they rank second in passing yards allowed, second in yards per pass allowed, and third in EPA per pass allowed through four weeks. Even with no contributions yet from Myles Garrett, or practically Aaron Donald, the Rams have received the pass defensive improvements that they desperately wanted to see from last season. Now imagine how the defense could do with Garrett, Donald, and Jaylen Watson. Trent McDuffie is worth it The Rams traded a late first-round pick in 2026 for McDuffie and then paid him over $30 million per season. This was all in an effort to replace the likes of Darious Williams and company and it’s paying off. McDuffie is arguably the best cornerback in the NFL this season. Trent McDuffie has allowed a 26.7% completion percentage in coverage this season, the lowest of any cornerback to face at least 10 targets. McDuffie has recorded seven passes defensed, the most among cornerbacks, while allowing just four receptions. #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/Meaivcw2pt — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) October 1, 2026 The Rams wanted to pair McDuffie with former Chiefs teammate Jaylen Watson, but Watson missed Week 4’s win over the Eagles with a shoulder injury. And the Rams held Philadelphia to 68 net passing yards. TRENT MCDUFFIE IS ONE OF THE BEST CORNERBACKS IN THE #NFL : Trent continues to make ridiculous plays look routine and completely LOCK DOWN opposing receivers — every week since arriving in LA. One of the most dominant defensive backs in football. 🔒🔒🔒 pic.twitter.com/qr1PNmGoJ3 — MLFootball (@MLFootball) October 5, 2026 It certainly helps that Jalen Hurts didn’t have Devonta Smith to throw to this week, but Darius Cooper certainly earned some respect with his two touchdown catches against L.A.‘s defense. It took practically all he had for the first one to be completed, so credit to him for that. Only TWO cornerbacks have been targeted multiple times in man coverage and allowed a 0.0 passer rating this season. – Trent McDuffie – Travis Hunter 🤯🤯🤯 pic.twitter.com/Q4t4j6Nary — Dov Kleiman (@NFL_DovKleiman) October 4, 2026 But even so, the Rams held the Eagles to 68 passing yards with Josh Wallace starting and playing the entire game. Wallace certainly deserves more credit too: Going into Week 4, Wallace has been allowing a passer rating of 34.8 on throws in his direction. 4 games, 582 passing yards The Rams have only allowed 582 passing yards in four games, including a season-worst 205 passing yards against the 49ers in Week 1. Only the Seahawks and Rams have held all four opponents to 205 passing yards or fewer this season. L.A.’s defense is second in total yards per play allowed at 4.2, also behind Seattle. One area the Rams would like to improve is forcing more turnovers, as they only have three takeaways and have yet to recover a fumble. This is at least partly related to L.A. only having three sacks and a 19% pressure rate. By comparison, the Vikings have a 36% pressure rate. This is what Garrett was traded to help with and he has missed the last three games. He didn’t do anything in Week 1. But nobody expects Garrett to miss the entire season and his presence will change everything about the Rams’ front seven. Per Next Gen Stats, the Rams are averaging 3.1 yards of separation between the defense and the intended receivers of the offense. That ranks as the third-best in the NFL. Again, this highlights how sticky McDuffie and company have been in coverage this season, a major improvement from 2025. Rams have more on the way Garrett has to miss at least this week’s game against the Bills, and then he will be eligible to come off of IR in Week 6. However, the Rams have not indicated that they expect Garrett to return that soon . If Garrett misses the Cardinals and Raiders games, which would mean six weeks off, he’d return against the Chargers on November 1. Week 4 Defensive EPA per Play pic.twitter.com/upOftpHVWh — Gridiron Stats and Info (@GridironInfo_) October 5, 2026 Watson missed this week’s game, but McVay said that it wasn’t even up for discussion that Watson would go on IR, implying that he could return in the next two weeks. The Rams are reportedly “optimistic” that Donald will return from a back injury in Week 5, according to Mike Garafolo. Aaron Donald (back) is out for Sunday's game against the Eagles, but the Rams are "optimistic" that he'll be able to play Week 5 versus the Bills. Via @MikeGarafolo pic.twitter.com/hhDmeMUkDb — RotoWire Fantasy Football (@RotoWireNFL) October 4, 2026 Kam Kinchens returned from a hamstring injury in Week 4 and played in 70% of the snaps. This is actually typical for Kinchens, but perhaps he’d be even better next week. Overall, if the Rams had this defense and only this defense, their prospects for the upcoming schedule would already be fairly good relative to other teams. However, imagine if this was the Rams defense and then they traded for Myles Garrett, Jaylen Watson, and Aaron Donald between Weeks 5-8. That’s kind of what could happen. And as long as the rest of the team, and McDuffie, stays on track, that could mean that the L.A. Rams’ defense is as good as we thought it could be after the offseason they used toiling to make it better.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: The Rams need to beat the Bills
summary: The NFL is only entering Week 5, but the October stakes couldn’t be higher for the NFC West based on next weekend’s games. The Los Angeles Rams salvaged potential disaster by coming back to beat the Philadelphia Eagles and setting their record at 2-2, and they’re within striking distance of the 4-0 San Francisco 49ers […]
full_text: The NFL is only entering Week 5, but the October stakes couldn’t be higher for the NFC West based on next weekend’s games. The Los Angeles Rams salvaged potential disaster by coming back to beat the Philadelphia Eagles and setting their record at 2-2 , and they’re within striking distance of the 4-0 San Francisco 49ers and 3-1 Seattle Seahawks. However, that slim margin could become a chasm if the Rams lose to the Buffalo Bills in Week 5. Worst Case: 49ers 5-0, Rams 2-3 The 49ers already have a head-to-head advantage by beating the Rams 27-7 in Week 1. So already the Rams are in a position where they are in a must-win situation when they face San Francisco in Week 14 — but a lot could change by then. Either in L.A.’s favor or against it. Starting this weekend . Week 5: 49ers at Seahawks Week 5: Bills at Rams If the 49ers beat the Seahawks, and the Bills beat the Rams, then L.A. will essentially already be four games back of first place in the NFC West. Four, not three. That’s 3 games back in the win-loss column + a head-to-head loss. Things get really, really ugly when a team is that far behind another team at any point in the season. The good news about it being early in the season is that there’s a lot of time for things to change. The bad news is that it could get that bad this early in the season? The Rams are not in must-win territory, especially when it comes to simply making the playoffs (and it should NOT be the goal for L.A. to only make the playoffs, they must do much better than that), but Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford are pushing the envelope if they lose to the Bills. And the Bills are not going to be easy to beat. Odds to NFC West if this happens: 8.5% If the 49ers end up 5-0 and the Rams 2-3, then L.A.’s odds to win the NFC West drop to approximately 8.5%. This isn’t easy to calculate because a lot depends on whether or not the Rams win the rematch. Even if the Rams win that game, the odds only go up to about 12%. If the Rams lose the rematch, then their odds to win the NFC West are almost 0 . But think of it like this based on the 5-0 vs. 2-3 scenario: If the 49ers go 10-2 the rest of the way, the Rams can’t win the division If the 49ers go 9-3 the rest of the way, the Rams have to go 12-0 If the 49ers go 8-4 the rest of the way, the Rams have to go 11-1 If the 49ers go 7-5 the rest of the way, the Rams have to go 10-2 It becomes a situation where the Rams have to be almost perfect and they need the 49ers to play significantly worse than they’ve already played this season. And that’s just looking at ONE team. The Rams also have to be better than the Seahawks to win the division. “So what? Just win a wild card!” Here we go again: The “All-In” Rams going for…a wild card? Wild Card teams don’t win The Rams haven’t won or reached the Super Bowl since 2021, when they won the division and were the number four seed. That team also had two home games in the playoffs, including the NFC Championship against the 49ers. L.A. can’t count on getting a home game if they are a wild card, and it’s exceedingly rare for teams to go 3-0 on the road in the playoffs. Like it just doesn’t happen. Since 2021’s 7-team playoff expansion, a wild card has NOT made the Super Bowl. From 2002-2020, wild card teams reached the Super Bowl only 4 times (05 PIT, 07 NYG, 10 GB, 20 TB) . So since 2002 realignment, only four wild card teams have reached the Super Bowl. And since expanding the schedule to include an extra wild card, a wild card teams has not even reached the Super Bowl. The goal NEEDS to be winning the NFC West. If the Rams lose to the Bills, that becomes extremely difficult to do. Especially if the 49ers beat the Seahawks. Bills 3-1 Buffalo dropped to 3-1 after losing to the Patriots 29-26 on Sunday. It was a close game, obviously, and needed an exceptional catch by New England’s rookie receiver to win the game in the final minute. TOUCHDOWN PATRIOTS. What a catch by Efton Chism III to take the lead! @NEvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DtIZoenYNL — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 On offense, the Bills have Josh Allen and James Cook and they lead the NFL in points per game. On defense, the Bills are 25th in points allowed per game. Buffalo has allowed at least 29 points in three of four games, with the only exception being the hapless L.A. Chargers. The Bills are hard to beat. The Rams need to beat them. If McVay and Stafford L.A. to a win, then the Rams will be a threat to win the NFC West regardless of how Seattle vs. San Francisco goes because then we’ll know that the team is waking up. However, if they sleep through this week and lose, the odds of getting the rebound that they need to have will be dramatically deflated.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: With Sunday’s win, Rams put themselves back in the playoff picture
summary: It’s early in the season, but the Los Angeles Rams maybe, kinda, sorta just saved their season by beating the Philadelphia Eagles and rising to 2-2 instead of falling to 1-3. Look, it’s a 17-game season, the Rams maybe, kinda, sorta could’ve come back from a 1-3 reord, but 2-2 is so much better. It’s […]
full_text: It’s early in the season, but the Los Angeles Rams maybe, kinda, sorta just saved their season by beating the Philadelphia Eagles and rising to 2-2 instead of falling to 1-3. Look, it’s a 17-game season, the Rams maybe, kinda, sorta could’ve come back from a 1-3 reord, but 2-2 is so much better. It’s gives them some breathing room. Now, there’s a lot of games to go, the Rams could falter over the next few weeks, but this win, for now, puts the Rams firmly back in the playoff conversation in a real way. It’s a week-to-week league, the Rams can be happy for this week, but they need to keep winning. That’s the trick. Happy victory Monday. Monday night game in Week 5 incoming. 2026 NFL season, Week 4: What We Learned from Sunday’s games (nfl.clom) “ Rams finally finish. Los Angeles thoroughly outplayed the banged-up Eagles at a soggy Linc on Sunday, but found itself down 10 points midway through the fourth quarter. Matthew Stafford interceptions, special teams snafus and fourth-down follies were to blame. But one week after blowing multiple leads against the Broncos, the Rams took control of the proceedings in eastern Pennsylvania and changed the narrative. After L.A. stuffed Philly at the 2-yard line as the Eagles attempted to go up three scores, Stafford led the Rams on their best drive of the day, finding Puka Nacua (who is absolutely back from injury, finishing with nine catches for 125 yards) and Tyler Higbee on the boundary to get L.A. into Philly territory. An Eagles late hit penalty and Kyren Williams TD later, the Rams were within striking distance. L.A. then stopped Philadelphia on their 11th straight third down of the day and got the ball back. The recipe was the same: Nacua and Higbee into Eagles territory, then Williams (147 total yards on 26 touches) to salt away the drive. The box score will say L.A. should have run away with this one (414 yards to 172), and perhaps Sean McVay’s side should have. But the mettle shown against a franchise that has had their number has to be rewarding for the Rams, as they avoid a 1-3 start and keep pace with the rival 49ers and Seahawks in the NFC West. This team can finish — at times, in spite of itself.“ The Los Angeles Rams saved their season with a last-minute comeback (nbcnews) “After having blown a 16-0 lead to the Denver Broncos a week ago, the Los Angeles Rams — a preseason Super Bowl favorite — looked well on their way to another dispiriting loss Sunday. The Rams were trailing 20-10 and had the ball 98 yards away from the end zone with less than eight minutes to go in the fourth quarter on a day they had already committed several mistakes against an opponent they had not beaten since 2020. Staring a 1-3 record in the face, Los Angeles instead stepped up and saved its season.“ Watch: Rams coaches and Eagles fans flip each other off at end of game (ramswire) “The Los Angeles Rams pulled off a dramatic comeback win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday afternoon, taking down a team that has had their number for years. Sean McVay was fired up after the win, as were his assistant coaches up in the booth. A video was taken in the stands at the end of the game showing Rams coaches and Eagles fans flipping each other off. Eagles fans could be seen shouting at the Rams’ coaches, who allegedly were banging on the window after Kyren Williams’ go-ahead touchdown. A beer was then thrown by a fan at the glass where the Rams’ coaches were sitting.“ Notable injuries, news from Sunday’s Week 4 games: Saquon Barkley (hamstring), Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) exit (nfl.com) “ Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring) was injured in the first quarter and did not return to Sunday’s win over the Raiders. Head coach Andy Reid described Rice’s injury as a tweak. Wide receiver Tyquan Thornton ‘s ankle injury “doesn’t look good,” according to Reid, who said that Thornton would travel back to Kansas City with the team. Thornton was carted off in the fourth quarter and ruled out shortly after. Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Jalen Nailor (concussion) was ruled out of Sunday’s loss to the Chiefs. Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey (foot) and offensive tackle Joe Alt (neck) were ruled out of Sunday’s loss to the Seahawks. Offensive tackle Rashawn Slater (ankle) and cornerback Donte Jackson (hamstring) did not return. Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Konata Mumpfield (shoulder) did not return to Sunday’s win over Philadelphia.“ Rams Beat Eagles, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Stafford, Hurts, Saquon, Puka, Top Players (bleacherreport) “Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams are magicians. Or the Philadelphia Eagles snatched defeat from the jaws of victory. Depends on your perspective. Los Angeles overcame a 10-point deficit in the fourth quarter for a dramatic 24-20 victory over the Eagles on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field. Kyren Williams scored the two fourth-quarter touchdowns for the victors, while the Rams defense didn’t allow Jalen Hurts and Co. to score a single point in the second half.“ Game Recap: Rams rally for 24-20 road win over Eagles in Philadelphia (therams.com) “Trailing 20-17 with 3:59 to go in the fourth quarter after a four-yard touchdown run by running back Kyren Williams , the Rams defense had to dig in after kicker Harrison Mevis received a kickoff out of bounds penalty, spotting the ball at the Eagles’ own 40-yard line. Still, the Rams defense got the stop and forced the Eagles (2-2) to punt, putting the ball back in the hands of quarterback Matthew Stafford with just under three minutes remaining. Stafford then marched the Rams downfield on a go-ahead scoring drive punctuated by a seven-yard touchdown run by Williams to give the Rams the lead 24-20 with 1:10 remaining. Outside linebacker Byron Young ‘s two sacks on the final drive clinched the victory for Los Angeles. Williams finished with 16 carries for 80 yards and two touchdowns, plus 10 catches for 67 yards in the victory.“ Eagles vs. Rams: Philadelphia blows a ten-point lead in Week 4 loss (eagleswire) “The Philadelphia Eagles squandered a 10-point halftime lead and fell to the Los Angeles Rams , 24-20, on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field. Philadelphia failed to convert any of its 12 third-down opportunities and did not score after halftime. Jalen Hurts threw two touchdown passes to Darius Cooper, but the Eagles finished with just 172 total yards. Kyren Williams scored twice in the fourth quarter as Los Angeles completed its comeback, dropping Philadelphia to 2-2. Andrew Mukuba and Cooper DeJean recorded the Eagles’ first two takeaways of the season, but those early defensive contributions were not enough. Saquon Barkley was ruled out with a hamstring injury, and Jonathan Greenard left with an ankle injury and did not return. Philadelphia now heads to London to face Jacksonville on Oct. 11, with an expanding injury list and major questions about its protection and second-half offense. Eagles Wire brought you live updates, scores, and highlights from the game. Check out the key moments below.“ Williams helps Rams stage comeback win over Eagles (nbcsports) “Mike Florio unpacks the Rams improbable win over the “hamstrung” Eagles, where Sean McVay got his first win over Nick Sirianni in comeback fashion thanks to a stellar showing from Kyren Williams.“ Eagles-Rams Week 4 report card: Beat-up Birds let double-digit lead – and history – slip away (phillyvoice) “The Eagles were threatening to become the first team in NFL history to win a game despite failing to convert at least one of 12 third-down attempts before predictably imploding in the fourth as the their injury situation became untenable. Had the Eagles been able to punch in a touchdown at the LA 6 with 8:57 to play, they would’ve have won the game. But they were stopped on three straight tries, including a bold 4th-and-2 pass, and then watched the Rams score go on two TD drives to win.“ NFL says it is looking into an official cursing at Cardinals TE Trey McBride…

title: Las Vegas Raiders lose in trenches against Kansas City Chiefs to fall short in Week 4
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders entered Week 4 with a chance to take command of the AFC West, but fell three points short, squandering the opportunity with the 30-27 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. The difference came down to the trenches, as both teams ran the ball 26 times, but the Chiefs turned that into […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders entered Week 4 with a chance to take command of the AFC West, but fell three points short, squandering the opportunity with the 30-27 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs . The difference came down to the trenches, as both teams ran the ball 26 times, but the Chiefs turned that into 189 rushing yards (7.3 ypc) and the Raiders managed just 72 yards on the ground (2.8 ypc). That’s a big point of emphasis in this week’s winners and losers. LOSER: Klint Kubiak Kubiak drew plenty of praise for starting his career 3-0, but the other end of that is that he has to shoulder the blame when his team loses. Also, while it can be debatable whether or not the decision to take the field goal off the board was the right decision, the NFL is a results business at the end of the day and Kubiak’s call didn’t work out. To the coach’s credit, he took accountability for the loss after the game and admitted that he “blew it” on the final drive. There’s still plenty of reason to believe in the first-time head coach. One loss doesn’t erase how the Raiders have already exceeded expectations with a hot start to the season. However, Kubiak certainly has to figure out the offense’s running game woes since his unit hasn’t had success on the ground since Week 1. LOSER: Kolton Miller While Miller has been a steadying presence on Las Vegas’ offensive line for several years, including the beginning of the 2026 campaign, he was anything but that on Sunday. According to Pro Football Focus , the nine-year veteran had only given up five pressures in the first three games combined but more than doubled his season total by giving up six to the Chiefs. Miller struggled to handle George Karlaftis’ power in the passing game, and he had issues in the running game, getting beaten several times to log a 51.2 run-blocking grade from PFF. Again, the Raiders’ left tackle and longest-tenured offensive lineman has been playing well for most of the season. But he certainly wasn’t at his best in Week 4. LOSER: Caleb Rogers To be fair, lining up against Chris Jones in your first start of the season isn’t an easy task. However, the Raiders needed Rogers to provide more resistance than giving up five pressures and an ugly 7.6 PFF pass-blocking grade . On top of that, this was an opportunity for the second-year pro to establish himself as a regular starter moving forward with Jackson Powers-Johnson out of the lineup. But Rogers didn’t rise to the occasion, likely giving Powers-Johnson his spot back if he can return from injury next week. WINNER: Michael Mayer If you’re looking for silver linings from the Silver and Black’s tough loss, Kubiak’s ability to use the team’s tight ends is one of them. Fighting an illness, Brock Bowers did his thing by being the team’s leading receiver with six catches for 86 yards and a touchdown, while Kubiak had a great play design for Ian Thomas to score a 27-yard touchdown. On top of that, Mayer had one of the best games of his career, hauling in eight passes for 82 yards. Both of those figures are the second-most he’s had in a single game . The fourth-year pro did exactly what is expected of him in the Raiders’ passing attack: serve as a check-down option by getting yards after the catch and moving the chains (37 YAC and five first downs, per PFF ), in addition to making contested catches (three-for-three on such targets). That’s the type of performance the Raiders have been looking for since giving Mayer a contract extension right before the season. LOSER: Rob Leonard Of course, the defensive front seven shoulders some of the blame for Kenneth Walker collecting 177 rushing yards and 8.0 yards per carry, but so does the defensive play caller. Also, Leonard got burned when trying to dial up the heat on Patrick Mahomes, as three Cover 0 calls resulted in the Chiefs adding over 50% win probability, according to former director of analytics Ryan Paganetti on X/Twitter . Additionally, Mahomes was seven-of-11 for 120 yards with one “big time throw” and no “turnover-worthy plays” when the Raiders blitzed on Sunday, per PFF , and Vegas’ fourth-quarter defensive magic ran out. The Chiefs scored 20 of their 30 points in the final frame and weren’t forced into any turnovers throughout the game. Leonard did a great job of creating havoc in the first three weeks of the year, but not so much against Kansas City. The Raiders may have wished they could get some of their Cover 0 calls back against Mahomes. Three pivotal Cover 0 moments in the game: 41 yard completion to Worthy (10.6% win probability added) 2 yard TD to Thornton (5.6% win probability added) 55 yard completion to Thornton… — Ryan Paganetti (@RyanPaganetti) October 5, 2026 WINNER: Kirk Cousins Cousins certainly isn’t to blame for the loss, throwing for a season-high 365 passing yards and a pair of touchdowns. Granted, 52 attempts definitely helps with that. But the quarterback has been playing pretty well over the last three weeks. He’s tied with Brock Purdy for the most passing touchdowns in the NFL (11) so far this season, and has posted a solid 71.8 PFF passing grade . There’s no need for the Raiders to put Fernando Mendoza on the field right now because Cousins is playing well enough to keep the team in the playoff conversation through the first quarter of the season. LOSER: Kwity Paye After a solid performance in the season opener, Paye has been pretty quiet. He had six tackles, two TFLs, two sacks and four quarterback hits against the Miami Dolphins, but has five, zero, zero and one in the three games combined since then. Paye’s outing on Sunday was especially underwhelming, failing to show up on the box score while also recording zero pressures on 18 pass rushes, a missed tackle and a 43.8 run defense grade, per PFF . That’s not what the organization had in mind when it signed the free agent to a three-year, $48 million contract in the offseason. LOSER: Mike Washington Jr. Kubiak mentioned that Washington had earned more touches with his play during the first three games of the season, and the rookie received the most carries he’s had with nine against the Chiefs. However, that resulted in the second-lowest rushing yards (18) and worst yards per carry (2.0) of his young career. On top of that, Washington struggled in the passing game with one drop on two targets and was beaten for a pressure in pass protection . The Raiders may have issues in the running game, but it’s pretty clear who their top back is right now.
