title: Explosive plays, special teams miscue Raiders’ undoing in loss to Chiefs
summary: When CBS Sports play-by-play man Jim Nantz called out Kansas City had generated just 18 total yards of offense with 30 seconds left in the third quarter, it was fortuitous foreshadowing for the Chiefs. What ensued was an explosive play netting a touchdown and four series later, the visiting Chiefs got another chunk play resulting […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images) | Getty Images When CBS Sports play-by-play man Jim Nantz called out Kansas City had generated just 18 total yards of offense with 30 seconds left in the third quarter, it was fortuitous foreshadowing for the Chiefs. What ensued was an explosive play netting a touchdown and four series later, the visiting Chiefs got another chunk play resulting in another end zone visit. And after punching the ball out of Las Vegas Raiders kick returner Dareke Young, Kansas City found the end zone one play later. Yielding the two explosive plays and the special teams gaffe sunk the home Raiders and the Chiefs reign supreme in the AFC West at 4-0 after a tightly contest 30-27 win this past Sunday.4 What could’ve been a runaway win Kansas City was thwarted by Las Vegas trailing 30-19 in the fourth quarter, but unlike the previous two matchups where takeaways powered the Silver & Black, it was the opposition that showcased more complementary football. It’s the first defeat for Raiders rookie head coach Klint Kubiak — who proclaimed on the broadcast his team would win the game in a half time interview before the two teams went into the locker rooms at half time — and how his team develops and grows after this stinging loss will say a lot about this team going forward. Especially with his football team having a difficult schedule ahead of them. "[The Raiders] are going to be a pain in the butt for every team out there." @PriscoCBS #NFLPostgame pic.twitter.com/J0vgmZ2NqC — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 5, 2026 As longtime NFL analyst Pete Prisco noted above, this isn’t a fugazi football team and what Kubiak is doing is not fluke. How he and his coaching staff pivot after film review from the loss is something many will be watching closely — under a microscope even. Because yielding explosive plays on defense while not generating more of their own on offense can’t continue to happen, especially for a tough stretch of upcoming games that feature the New England Patriots (road), Buffalo Bills (home), Los Angeles Rams (home), and New York Jets (road) in the next four games. Las Vegas will also need to rejuvenate a run game that’s been stymied. Perhaps watching the tape of how Walker carved up the defense will provide not only answers for Rob Leonard’s defense, but Kubiak’s offense? Immediately after Nantz made note of the lack of offensive production, Walker took the hand off on the 1st-and-10 play from the Chiefs’ 11-yard line sprinted through a gaping hole for a 76-yard run. The reason it wasn’t a home run break away touchdown was because of the hustle from Raiders nickel cornerback Taron Johnson, who ran the tailback down. K9 GOES 77 YARDS 🔥 @KCvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1d8jxbAU0C — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 Two plays later, quarterback Patrick Mahomes threw a dime to wide open wide receiver Tyquan Thornton to boost the Chiefs momentarily lead to 17-13. But Thornton wasn’t done there as he hauled in a 55-yard dime from Mahomes to set up a go-ahead two-yard touchdown run from Walker, 23-19 Chiefs. Walker hit pay dirt again after the forced fumble and recovery on the ensuing kick off going around the Raiders defense for a 22-yard score and with 30-19 lead in hand and 3:02 left to play, Kansas City was comfortable. Kubiak and his Raiders weren’t going to go away quietly and made it a game again after quarterback Kirk Cousins escaped a sack and lofted a 20-yard touchdown to tight end Brock Bowers to slash the deficit to 30-27. The Las Vegas defense rose to the occasion to force a punt but the Raiders’ last gasp on offense ended with Cousins firing an interception on a play that Kubiak admitted he didn’t get quickly enough to his quarterback, hence its haphazard nature and turnover. Let’s hit the quick slants as fast as both Walker and Thornton torched the Raiders defense on their respective big-play efforts: —Losing by three points put Kubiak’s decision to go for it on 4th-and-2 instead of keeping the made field goal on the board in the third quarter under the spotlight. To his credit, the rookie’s aggressive decision is something to be done against the high-powered Chiefs, and Kubiak noted he didn’t regret the decision, just regretted the team couldn’t convert and turned the ball over. —Bowers and fellow tight end Michael Mayer paced the Raiders air attack with six catches for 86 yards and a touchdown and eight receptions for 82 yards, respectively. Reserve tight end Ian Thomas hauled in the other touchdown — a beauty of a 27-yard pass from Cousins where Kubiak schemed the tight end wide open. KIRK COUSINS MAGIC FOR THE TOUCHDOWN! @KCvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ADaylXSjLZ — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 —While the tight ends produced 200 yards and two touchdowns on 16 receptions, the wide receivers didn’t produce as much. Tre Tucker had four grabs for 44 yards while Cody White had two receptions for 32 yards. Jeanty did haul in six passes for 68 yards, but the lack of a standout wideout is glaring. —In the battle of quality punters, the Chiefs’ southpaw Matt Araiza outperformed the Raiders’ AJ Cole III with five boots for 238 yards and all five landing or downed inside Las Vegas’ 20-yard line. Cole had three punts for 142 yards with only one being downed or landing inside the Chiefs’ 20-yard line. —Walker’s impressive 2026 season continued as he churned out 177 yards on 22 carries (8.0 yards per carry average) with two touchdowns. —CBS Sports color analyst and likely future hall of fame defensive end J.J. Watt called out that Crosby was on the sideline during Walker’s long 76-yard run for a breather. And just like Watt noted, giving up that kind of explosive play with your best defender taking a rest likely is the catalyst for Crosby to once again play near 100 percent of snaps. —In comparison, the Raiders’ entire run game rushed for 72 yards on 26 carries (2.8 yards per carry) with Ashton Jeanty leading the group with 58 yards on 15 carries. Rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. added 18 yards on 9 totes while fullback Connor Heyward had two carries for negative four yards. Ashton Jeanty talks about how he is feeling health wise and what the #Raiders offense needs to do in order to get the run game going again pic.twitter.com/qh3XqgFVsI — Raider Nation Radio (@RNR920AM) October 5, 2026 Quotes of Note “I took three points off the board, and we were going to be aggressive going into the game. I don’t regret it. I regret not getting it.” —Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak on going for it on 4th-and-2 in the third quarter instead of taking the made field goal. “That’s a good football team. You know they had a few people defensively come over for them. They added to the talent they had. The D line and secondary were playing together. That’s a good team. When Kirk’s dealing like that it’s hard to stop. And they have a guy like Brock Bowers. We have to keep getting better but I’m sure they will do the same.” —Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes on the Las Vegas Raiders after the win. Up Next Las Vegas (3-1) preps for an East Coast trip to face New England (2-2) next Sunday. The Patriots head into Week 5 after a big win over the Buffalo Bills in their AFC East clash. The Raiders are 2-0 on the road so far this season and will need similar strong performances the team had at the Los Angeles Chargers and New Orleans Saints. Unlike the two previous away games, however, this is the first for the Silver & Black that’s an early 10 a.m. (Pacific Standard Time) matchup.

full_text: (Photo by Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) While the Las Vegas Raiders came up three points short in the Week 4 battle for first place in the AFC West against the Kansas City Chiefs, the Raiders are still in good standing when it comes to the division standings since the Denver Broncos and Los Angeles Chargers also suffered defeats. Broncos vs. 49ers Score: 24-14 Broncos lose Key Stats: QB Bo Nix: 25/42 (59.5%), 214 yards, 1 TD, 0 INTs, 2 carries, 10 yards RB RJ Harvey: 7 carries, 25 yards, 10 catches, 68 receiving yards WR Jaylen Waddle: 5 catches, 35 yards, 1 TD LB Alex Singleton: 14 tackles, 1 TFL DT Zach Allen: 5 tackles, 3 QB hits Denver’s offense is becoming an issue. While the Broncos scored 30 points in Week 3, one of their touchdowns was via a pick-six, and they’ve been held under 21 points in the three other games of the season. Also, Nix and Co. have become known for slow starts, and the Ponies didn’t find the end zone until there were four minutes left in the game. This is a team that was a quarterback injury away from playing in the Super Bowl last season, but the 2-2 club needs a major turnaround to be a legitimate contender this year. The Seattle Seahawks had a 21-point lead after the first possession of the third quarter and seemingly took their foot off the gas. To the Chargers’ credit, they fought until the end and scored 10 fourth-quarter points to make it more respectable, but the hole was just too big to dig out of. At 0-4, it’s looking like Los Angeles will be picking toward the top of the draft this spring, and it wouldn’t be surprising if the organization hits the reset button in the offseason. title: Fins Up, Fins Down | Winners and losers from Miami Dolphins week four loss
summary: The Miami Dolphins fell to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday by a score of 15-10. While keeping it close only really counts in horseshoes and hand-grenades, as they say, it was Miami’s narrowest defeat of the season through four tough contests. This team is getting better, despite the considerable limitations they are under regarding the […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Miami Dolphins defensive tackle Zach Sieler (92) tackles Minnesota Vikings running back Demond Claiborne (21) during the second half of the NFL game between the Miami Dolphins and the Minnesota Vikings on October 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins fell to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday by a score of 15-10. While keeping it close only really counts in horseshoes and hand-grenades, as they say, it was Miami’s narrowest defeat of the season through four tough contests. This team is getting better, despite the considerable limitations they are under regarding the mammoth amount of dead cap they are currently dealing with, and I don’t think it’s long before they steal a victory to finally get into the win column this year. Of course there are still glaring problems on this team — covering tight ends has been one of those problems. T.J. Hockenson was targeted 13 times yesterday — he caught all 13 passes for a game high 119 yards receiving. Special teams is another — with multiple errors leading to fantastic starting field position for the Vikings on numerous occasions. FINS UP Our Fins Up player from Miami’s week three loss is defensive tackle Zach Sieler. It had been a rough start to the season for Miami’s veteran defender, however, on Sunday against the Vikings, Sieler unleashed his frustrations on Minnesota quarterback Kyler Murray — sacking the diminutive passer twice on the afternoon to account for half of Miami’s four sacks on the day. Sieler hadn’t sacked an opposing quarterback since Week 16 of last season. He finished last season with just 5.5 sacks after having 10 sacks in both the 2023 and 2024 seasons. If he can continue the momentum he began building on Sunday, Miami’s monster in the middle could easily surpass last year’s sack total in short order. FINS DOWN This week’s Fins Down personality is once again special teams coordinator Chris Tabor. Tabor, a respected coach in the National Football League, has now been named in our Fins Down section twice this season — also earning the dubious distinction after week one’s dismal performance from his unit. All afternoon long, Minnesota’s offense was treated to great starting field position due to Miami’s inability to cover kick returns with any competency. Tabor is working with what he has — and what he has is a bunch of young, inexperienced football players trying to make their mark on an undermanned Dolphins squad. However, it is his job to coach them up and maximize their abilities. Unfortunately, he isn’t doing such a great job at that just yet… His next opportunity to show that he should remain on Miami’s staff will come this Sunday when the Dolphins host the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium.

title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 4 loss to the Minnesota Vikings
summary: The Miami Dolphins traveled to Minnesota to take on Kyler Murray, Aaron Jones Sr., T.J. Hockenson and the rest of the Vikings in week four of the 2026 season. Jeff Hafley’s bunch once again battled hard throughout the entire contest — but ultimately fell to the undefeated Minnesota squad by a score of 15-10. Without […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Jacob Rodriguez #10 of the Miami Dolphins warms up before kickoff against the Minnesota Vikings during an NFL football game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins traveled to Minnesota to take on Kyler Murray, Aaron Jones Sr., T.J. Hockenson and the rest of the Vikings in week four of the 2026 season. Jeff Hafley’s bunch once again battled hard throughout the entire contest — but ultimately fell to the undefeated Minnesota squad by a score of 15-10. Without their top weapon, running back De’Von Achane, and rookie standout receiver, Caleb Douglas, Miami’s offense was stagnant for most of the afternoon. Their defense, however, played their best game all season. The Dolphins may be 0-4 in the standings, but they are getting better each week. It won’t be long until they claim their first victory of the year. But, before we look too far into the future, let’s take a look back at the good, bad and ugly from Miami’s week four loss to the Minnesota Vikings. GOOD Dolphins keep Vikings out of endzone; hold Minnesota offense to nothing but field goals If there was one positive to take away from Sunday’s loss, it was the performance of Miami’s defense. For a team that entered Week 4 searching for answers, holding a 3-0 Minnesota Vikings team without a touchdown is no small accomplishment. Sure, they were without stud receiver Justin Jefferson, but the Dolphins limited Minnesota to just 15 points, forcing kicker Will Reichard to account for every single point on the Vikings’ scoreboard via five field goals. Miami’s defensive front deserves plenty of credit for making life uncomfortable for quarterback Kyler Murray. The Dolphins generated four sacks and consistently applied pressure — preventing Minnesota from finding the rhythm it wanted offensively. Rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez finished the tilt with 18 total tackles! Miami’s pass rush was particularly encouraging, with Zach Sieler, Josh Uche and Chop Robinson contributing to a defensive effort that looked considerably more disruptive than what we had seen through the first three weeks — repeatedly finding ways to make Minnesota scrap and claw for its points. The defense gave Miami a legitimate opportunity to steal a road victory. It created stops, generated pressure, and kept the opposing offense out of the end zone for four quarters. Unfortunately, the offense couldn’t return the favor. BAD Miami’s passing offense nearly nonexistent in loss The Dolphins’ passing offense was simply not good enough on Sunday. Malik Willis finished the afternoon completing 9 of 17 passes for just 85 yards, with no touchdowns — accumulating a paltry 67.0 passer rating. Throughout the entire game, Miami struggled to generate anything resembling a legitimate passing attack. That effort is not going to cut it. Miami’s inability to consistently threaten Minnesota through the air allowed the Vikings to remain comfortable defensively. The Dolphins struggled to sustain drives, failed to capitalize on opportunities, and ultimately put far too much responsibility on a defense that was doing everything it could to keep the game within reach. There was a moment when it appeared Miami had finally found the explosive play it desperately needed. Willis connected with rookie wide receiver Chris Bell for what looked like a dazzling 68-yard touchdown. Unfortunately, the play was erased by an illegal-touching penalty after Bell was ruled to have stepped out of bounds (by a toenail) before making the catch. It was a devastating, yet appropriate moment for a Dolphins offense that seemed incapable of getting out of its own way all game. The Dolphins cannot expect to win football games while producing fewer than 200 total yards — they had 198 yards on Sunday. At some point, the offense has to become part of the solution rather than another problem for the coaching staff to address. UGLY Both teams combined for 20 total penalties; 15 in the first half alone If you enjoy watching football games interrupted by yellow flags, Sunday’s first half was practically your Super Bowl. For everyone else, it was an unmitigated nightmare. The Dolphins and Vikings combined for 15 penalties before halftime, turning what should have been a competitive NFL contest into an exercise in frustration. That’s an astonishing amount of self-inflicted nonsense, particularly for two teams attempting to establish offensive rhythm and control the game. False starts, holding calls, and other costly infractions repeatedly disrupted the flow of the afternoon. Drives became longer than necessary, promising situations disappeared, and both teams struggled to establish any kind of consistency. There is a difference between playing aggressively and playing undisciplined football. Sunday’s first half featured far too much of the latter. The final penalty totals told the story. Miami finished with nine penalties for 55 yards, while Minnesota was flagged 11 times for 85 yards — 20 combined penalties for 140 yards over the course of the afternoon. Let’s hope the Dolphins can clean things up on the penalty front when they take on the Cincinnati Bengals next Sunday. __ The Dolphins find themselves sitting at 0-4 to begin the Jeff Hafley era in Miami , but they are showing improvements in certain areas. Do you think a victory is on the horizon for the boys in aqua and orange? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up.

title: NFL Suspends Referee Adrian Hill for Eric Wilson Confrontation
summary: One of the more surreal moments of yesterday’s 15-10 Minnesota Vikings’ victory over the Miami Dolphins involved a play that, technically, didn’t even count. With about five and a half minutes left in the first quarter, a third-down play for the Dolphins had been blown dead because of a neutral zone infraction on Dallas Turner. […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Minnesota Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson (55) talks with referee Adrian Hill (29) during the first half of the NFL game between the Miami Dolphins and the Minnesota Vikings on October 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images One of the more surreal moments of yesterday’s 15-10 Minnesota Vikings’ victory over the Miami Dolphins involved a play that, technically, didn’t even count. With about five and a half minutes left in the first quarter, a third-down play for the Dolphins had been blown dead because of a neutral zone infraction on Dallas Turner. Before the action could be stopped, Dolphins’ running back Ollie Gordon pushed Vikings’ linebacker Eric Wilson into referee Adrian Hill. Wilson appeared to be trying to go over and help Hill get up off the ground, but Hill got to his feet and immediately started screaming in Wilson’s face as if he thought Wilson had knocked him down intentionally. To Wilson’s credit, it appears that he remained calm and walked away without escalating things any further. It seems pretty obvious to pretty much everyone that Wilson had no intention of knocking Hill over and that he was, in fact, pushed into him by Gordon. Hill, apparently, was not interested in such details and decided he wanted to yell at Wilson instead. The league was not impressed with Hill’s reaction and has decided to suspend him for a week because of it. The league also suspended a line judge from the Arizona Cardinals/New York Giants game for two games for a confrontation that he got into with Cardinals’ tight end Trey McBride that you’ve probably seen around the internet at some point today. Everyone knows that making contact with the referees is wrong, but that implies intentional contact with the officials. In this case, Wilson was clearly not intending anything malicious, and Hill’s reaction to what happened was completely out of line. The suspension is completely deserved and, hopefully, Hill will think twice before the next time he decides to get up in the face of a player who had not done anything wrong in the first place.

title: A Couple Doses of Bad News for the Vikings’ Offensive Line
summary: Despite their 4-0 record, the Minnesota Vikings have had their share of issues on offense in the early phases of this 2026 NFL season, and they’ve gotten a couple of doses of bad news on this Monday morning that could, somehow, make things a little bit worse. Both members of the left side of the […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Donovan Jackson #74 of the Minnesota Vikings lines up against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Despite their 4-0 record, the Minnesota Vikings have had their share of issues on offense in the early phases of this 2026 NFL season, and they’ve gotten a couple of doses of bad news on this Monday morning that could, somehow, make things a little bit worse. Both members of the left side of the Vikings’ offensive line are now dealing with injuries, and one could be out for an extended length of time. We’ll start with left tackle Christian Darrisaw, who had a couple of different issues in Sunday’s victory over the Miami Dolphins. Darrisaw left early in Sunday’s game with a neck issue and was listed as questionable to return, but did come back into the game. Later on, he left the game again and was replaced by Ryan Van Demark, who finished things out in Darrisaw’s spot. In his press conference today, Kevin O’Connell told reporters that Darrisaw is now in the league’s concussion protocol, putting his status for Sunday’s game in New Orleans in doubt. That’s, obviously, something that we’ll be monitoring throughout the course of this week. Unfortunately, the news is much worse for his tag team partner, guard Donovan Jackson. Jackson has a torn meniscus that will require surgery and, in all likelihood, end his sophomore season after just four games. Jackson went out in the first quarter of Sunday’s game and went to the locker room, where he was ruled out for the afternoon relatively quickly. He was replaced by Joe Huber at the left guard spot. Jackson, the Vikings’ first-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, had really come on strong in the early portion of this season, and his absence is definitely one that is going to be felt for a Vikings’ offense that is already having problems getting points on the board. The week is already not off to a great start on the injury front for a Vikings team that is already wondering about Justin Jefferson’s status as they head into their Week 5 matchup in New Orleans. We’ll have more news on Christian Darrisaw’s status as the injury reports come out through the week, and here’s hoping that Donovan Jackson’s upcoming surgery is a successful one and he comes back fully ready to go for 2027.

title: Patriots playoff picture: What Bills win means for AFC standings
summary: Coming off a blowout loss and going up against an unbeaten division rival on the road, the New England Patriots celebrated a big win in Week 4. Playing their most complete game of the season, especially on the offensive side of the ball, they beat the Buffalo Bills 29-26 to, in the words of their […]
full_text: Coming off a blowout loss and going up against an unbeaten division rival on the road, the New England Patriots celebrated a big win in Week 4. Playing their most complete game of the season, especially on the offensive side of the ball, they beat the Buffalo Bills 29-26 to, in the words of their head coach, get “back in the race.” Let’s find out what the victory means for Mike Vrabel’s team. AFC East standings Buffalo Bills (3-1) New England Patriots (2-2) New York Jets (1-3) Miami Dolphins (0-4) Just like last year, the AFC East is shaping up to be a two-class society. The Bills remain on top despite losing to the Patriots, but what could have been a decisive win for them decreased their lead to just one game with New England now holding the ever-important head-to-head tiebreaker. Behind the two playoff aspirants, the Jets and Dolphins are reeling. The former dropped their third straight game after starting the season with a win, while the latter have an argument as the worst team in football right now: not only is Miami 0-4 under new head coach Jeff Hafley, their -55 scoring differential ranks 32nd in the NFL. AFC playoff standings Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1) Buffalo Bills (3-1) Cleveland Browns (3-1) Baltimore Ravens (3-1) Las Vegas Raiders (3-1) New England Patriots (2-2) On the bubble: 8. Denver Broncos (2-2), 9. Pittsburgh Steelers (2-2), 10. Indianapolis Colts (2-2), 11. Cincinnati Bengals (2-2), 12. New York Jets (1-3), 13. Miami Dolphins (0-4) , 14. Los Angeles Chargers (0-4) , 15. Tennessee Titans (0-4) , 16. Houston Texans (0-4) Their win over the Bills propelled the Patriots’ back into the playoff picture as the current No. 7 seed and the best-ranked of the 2-2 teams. Why? Because their wins over Pittsburgh and Buffalo gives them a 2-1 conference record, best among their peers at .500. New England will be in a position to add to it this week. Hosting the Raiders at Gillette Stadium on Sunday, they can get to a winning record for the first time all season and further put the pressure on the Bills and the rest of the AFC. And, yes, we know Las Vegas started 3-0 before a close loss to the Chiefs, but those victories came against the winless Dolphins, winless Chargers, and one-win New Orleans Saints.

title: Kindle Vildor, Mike Brown revert to Patriots’ practice squad following Week 4
summary: Kindle Vildor and Mike Brown reverted to the New England Patriots’ practice squad on Monday after serving as standard elevations at Highmark Stadium. Both veteran defensive backs had a hand in what became a 29-26 AFC East upset over the Buffalo Bills. Vildor, 28, got the call at cornerback after the 2025 division winners ruled […]
full_text: Oct 4, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) comes under pressure from New England Patriots cornerback Kindle Vildor (28) during the fourth quarter at New Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kindle Vildor and Mike Brown reverted to the New England Patriots’ practice squad on Monday after serving as standard elevations at Highmark Stadium. Both veteran defensive backs had a hand in what became a 29-26 AFC East upset over the Buffalo Bills. Vildor, 28, got the call at cornerback after the 2025 division winners ruled out All-Pro Christian Gonzalez due to a shoulder injury and later downgraded undrafted rookie Channing Canada due to a hamstring injury. He stepped in to play eight snaps on defense and five snaps on special teams during the visit to Orchard Park. With No. 3 option Charles Woods also missing time on the sideline, his Sunday brought a pair of tackles, including one for a loss of three yards on a shotgun run by former NFL MVP Josh Allen. Signed by the Patriots as an unrestricted free agent in March, the 5-foot-11, 189-pound Vildor recorded an interception in August preseason action and joined the practice squad at its formation after being released at the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline. Originally entering the league with the Chicago Bears in the fifth round of the 2020 draft at No. 163 overall, the Georgia Southern product made additional stops with the Tennessee Titans, Philadelphia Eagles, Detroit Lions and Tampa Bay Buccaneers before arriving in Foxborough. Through 81 appearances, including 27 starts, Vildor has had a hand in 142 tackles, one sack, one forced fumble and two interceptions across 2,113 snaps on defense and 578 snaps in the kicking game. Brown, 27, stands as a back-to-back elevation after previously taking the field against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium. The 6-foot-1, 218-pound safety has seen 12 snaps on defense and 42 snaps on special teams over the past pair of weeks and notched a pair of tackles. He tied for the team lead with 88 percent of the workload in the kicking game on Sunday. That was with former special teams captain Brenden Schooler on the non-football injury list and fellow core defensive back Dell Pettus on injured reserve . Undrafted in 2022, Brown spent time on the practice squads of the Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings and Cleveland Browns before heading to Tennessee’s 53-man roster late in his rookie season. The Miami of Ohio product remained with the Titans until being non-tendered as a restricted free agent ahead of the 2026 league year. He signed with the Patriots in March and was retained on the initial practice squad after being released at the cutdown deadline. Now 37 games into his career, including five starts, Brown has totaled 61 tackles and two passes defensed over the course of 515 snaps on defense and 802 snaps on special teams. Three standard elevations are permitted under NFL rules before requiring 53-man contracts to suit up. Two call-ups remain for the corner this regular season, while one remains for the safety. Head coach Mike Vrabel’s 2-2 Patriots move forward with an open spot on the active roster while awaiting returns from the reserve lists. The Las Vegas Raiders visit Gillette Stadium next Sunday. Kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET.

title: Mack Hollins injury set to open door for more Efton Chism III
summary: The New England Patriots saw wide receiver Mack Hollins depart Sunday’s game early with a calf injury.  While the Patriots await more information to determine the severity of the injury, head coach Mike Vrabel is preparing to potentially be without the veteran in the short term. “I think we’ll probably know more here in a […]
full_text: The New England Patriots saw wide receiver Mack Hollins depart Sunday’s game early with a calf injury. While the Patriots await more information to determine the severity of the injury, head coach Mike Vrabel is preparing to potentially be without the veteran in the short term. “I think we’ll probably know more here in a little bit,” Vrabel said Monday morning. “I don’t know if he’ll be able to practice here for a couple days. But again, I don’t have every detail. I’ll get in there with [the training staff] afterwards and kinda see where we are, and make sure we have guys that are ready to go and everybody is preparing as a starter. We know the energy that Mack brings. The next guy has to be ready to go.” In Hollins’ absence Sunday, wide receiver Efton Chism III played a season-high 34 offensive snaps in relief. Chism made the most of the opportunity, hauling in two catches for 42 yards and the game-winning touchdown. The performance could set Chism up for a larger role moving forward. “Of course. That’s what happens. Guys continue to take advantage of their opportunities, they get more opportunities,” Vrabel said. “We’ve been finding ways to work Chiz in there previously. It’s a balance, but certainly did a lot of things well and I know that he’ll continue to do things well for us and continue to know a bunch of different spots.” The Patriots are already without A.J. Brown in the wide receiver room, as the veteran remains on injured reserve through at least next week. Hollins’ absence would leave just Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Chism on the active roster. Undrafted rookies Cameron Dorner and Kyle Dixon, in addition to Chandler Brayboy, are currently on the practice squad. Vrabel did not rule out the Patriots searching for external additions at the position. “Sure. Anybody that can help us, we’ll go exploring here shortly,” Vrabel said.

title: Patriots vs. Bills: Fan observations from Week 4 win
summary: Covering the NFL, in any capacity, is like being a weatherman. You don’t know a damn thing and you’re wrong more often than you’re right. But since nobody else knows anything either, you get a pass each and every week. The New England Patriots, who have been struggling all season and were without their best […]
full_text: Covering the NFL, in any capacity, is like being a weatherman. You don’t know a damn thing and you’re wrong more often than you’re right. But since nobody else knows anything either, you get a pass each and every week. The New England Patriots, who have been struggling all season and were without their best cornerback and best interior linemen on both sides of the ball, took the best team in the AFC to the wire yesterday in a game that should give us all a lot of optimism going forward. It’s kind of fitting that Buffalo’s first-ever loss in their new stadium came at the hands of the Patriots, the team that won the most games ever at the old Bills stadium. I feel like everyone, yours truly included, had the Patriots sitting at 2-2 through four weeks. Lo and behold, here we find ourselves. Did I think New England would get slapped around by Jacksonville only to beat Buffalo on the road? Of course not. But that’s why we watch this nonsensical sport. If there’s a larger chasm that separates a 2-2 team from a 1-3 team, I don’t know what it is. It’s technically only one game, but teams sitting at 1-3 this morning are taking a long, unshaven, hungover look in the mirror right now, while the 2-2 teams are motivated to position themselves for a strong October. So, this game meant more than just getting a divisional win on the road, for a lot of reasons. But before I get into why that is, I’ll own my blatant sports fan hypocrisy by admitting that I would have spin-zoned the hell out of this game if Buffalo had won it. Drake Maye looked more poised. They hung with one of the best teams in the AFC. Lots to build on. Maybe they win if everyone is healthy. It’s a long season. This was the best the team has looked. We all know the platitudes. Luckily, though, I don’t have to do any of that, as New England outcoached and outplayed Buffalo to find themselves half a game out of first place in the AFC East. And this iteration of the Bills has never, at any point, defeated a defending AFC Champion. Let’s start with the offense, because that has been the team’s biggest weakness thus far. Sure, Maye had a fumble and a pick, but in a nice change of pace neither of them were on him. He probably should have felt the pressure on the strip sack and tucked the ball instead, but that was a strong pass rush against a new member of the offensive line. For the most part, Maye was decisive, poised, and clutch when he needed to be. I also have to point out that if T.J. Parker’s hands had been any more illegally to the face on that strip sack, he would have found himself on a split screen on MSNBC at some point this week being asked some questions. He also outrushed Josh Allen by 50 yards, which I didn’t expect (more on Allen’s legs and the defensive strategy surrounding that in a minute). And all of his runs were the right kind: receivers were covered, or the protection broke down, so he tucked and ran. He also got out of bounds or went right to the ground in the face of contact, which was even more enjoyable than watching him scramble. As for his leading receivers, it was a nice mix of old and new. Hunter Henry finally got involved in the passing game, and Romeo Doubs is getting more and more comfortable by the week. The bobble-to-interception wasn’t the best look for him, and he seems good for one drop per game. But if he can make up for it with two scores per game, I’ll certainly allow it. It’s wild to me how excited I was about the New England wide receiver room coming into this season. Brown, Doubs, Boutte, Douglas, Hollins, Chism, Williams… there just seemed to be so many weapons. Then Brown got hurt right away, Boutte got traded, Williams continues to be an absolute ghost, and a guy who should be thriving as WR4 was somehow pulling WR1 duty. And then that guy goes down too. “Man, if Mack Hollins can’t play for an extended period, this offense is really screwed” 100% went through my head yesterday. Football. What a ride! But in Hollins’s absence, seven different Patriots notched at least one reception. And Kyle Williams got two whole targets! I don’t want to get into too much turd in the punchbowlery in the wake of a big win. But what in the name of Tebow do the Patriots have to do to take a receiver early in the draft and have that receiver work out? And while I appreciate the universe balancing things out by consistently gifting the team with short, explosive, white slot receivers in the later rounds or through free agency, it would be nice if Kyle Williams could join the likes of Deion Branch and… um… Deion Branch… instead of Bethel Johnson, Chad Jackson, Brandon Tate, Taylor Price, Aaron Dobson, N’Keal Harry, Tyquan Thornton, and Ja’Lynn Polk. That said… I don’t want to pull the plug on Kyle Williams yet. He still has value and a skillset that could make him a strong contributor. But I also kind of feel like I’m at the point where, from this moment forward, if the Pats are thinking about targeting a WR in the draft, instead they should just trade that draft pick for a receiver who has already proven that he can produce at the NFL level. Speaking of producing… poor Tyquan Thornton. He had carved himself out a nice role in that Chiefs offense, which is a point in favor of the “it ain’t the player, it’s New England’s development” side of things. Hopefully that injury looks a lot worse than it is and he’ll be back on the field before too long. OK, enough with the negativity. One receiver being nonexistent just opened the door for the latest New England folk hero, Efton Chism III, who has made the catch of the year so far. This was shortly after high-pointing a crosser for a 19-yard gain to move the ball into Bills territory. There wasn’t anything complicated about the route; it looked like a simple out-and-up. Maye had to throw it a little earlier than he probably would have liked as the pressure came around the left side, and the coverage was perfect. Chism just made an absolutely absurd catch, and the legend was born. I was a little surprised to see that New England rushed for 143 yards yesterday. But then you realize that it’s less than 100 without Maye’s scrambles, and since TreVeyon Henderson seems to eat primarily off of long runs, it makes a lot more sense. Which means that this game was more or less won on the shoulders of the QB who had really been struggling through three weeks. And if he had laid another huge egg yesterday, there would be some conversations happening right now. Of that, I have no doubt. But this whole thing was just what everyone needed. There’s still a ton to clean up. This game could have gotten out of hand late in the first half with all the shenanigans that went down. But I’d rather need to clean up than start thinking about cleaning house. Speaking of cleaning house, the cupboard was pretty bare for the Patriots defense, who were without both Christians and a wildly depleted LB corp. They still held Allen to four yards rushing and should have recorded a safety. Seriously, what the hell was that? I guess a random, no-look throw to nobody while both still in the pocket in the end zone doesn’t meet the standards for grounding somehow. The best part about that play, though, was Gabe Jacas, who steamrolled Dion Dawkins and created immediate pressure. He’s still raw, but given the serious questions he was raising for everyone during the preseason, Jacas has been a beast. My only real gripe with the defense is that, at times, they seemed so concerned with Allen running that they broke into a lot of soft zone, which gave Allen plenty to choose from. But it was mostly effective, so hard to get too mad. I absolutely love it when the defense, any defense, celebrates an open receiver dropping a pass. As someone who has taken more than my fair share of credit for group projects in which I did zero work, it resonates with me on a personal level. I still remember being in 10th grade and, having done exactly nothing for our group report on FDR’s New Deal,…

title: Mike Vrabel fires back at Bills safety after postgame rant
summary: If you ask C.J. Gardner-Johnson, the better team lost during Sunday’s New England Patriots game against the Buffalo Bills. It was one of several dubious claims the Bills safety made in the postgame locker room following his team’s 29-26 defeat. Gardner-Johnson complained about the Patriots’ apparent lack of confidence, about their offensive output, and about […]
full_text: If you ask C.J. Gardner-Johnson, the better team lost during Sunday’s New England Patriots game against the Buffalo Bills. It was one of several dubious claims the Bills safety made in the postgame locker room following his team’s 29-26 defeat. Gardner-Johnson complained about the Patriots’ apparent lack of confidence, about their offensive output, and about the game-winning touchdown being scored by an apparent practice squad player who won’t be able to repeat that feat any time soon. For New England head coach Mike Vrabel, that final part was particularly interesting. “For a guy who’s been on eight teams in four years, I guess he knows the drill,” Vrabel said about the Bills defender during an appearance on WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show on Monday. As with the totality of Gardner-Johnson’s statements — the Patriots outperformed Buffalo by multiple statistical metrics — there also was no truth to the practice squad player claim. The pass catcher in question, after all, was second-year wide receiver Efton Chism, who has been on New England’s active since joining the organization as an undrafted free agent in 2025. While Chism only saw extended playing time after fellow wideout Mack Hollins exited with a calf injury, he made the most of his opportunity. The sophomore caught two passes for 42 yards on the Patriots’ game-winning drive, including the 23-yard touchdown on third down to cap it off. For Vrabel, that was more noteworthy than any trash talk coming out of Buffalo. “Nobody works harder,” he said about Chism. “You love to see players take advantage of opportunities and help the team win. He is very well-respected. He practices — on show team, he takes a million reps. Nobody runs more miles or yards or whatever we track than Chiz.” With Hollins’ injury status unclear as of right now, and with A.J. Brown ineligible to return from injured reserve until next week, Chism might find himself playing more snaps on offense this week against the Las Vegas Raiders. If so, there is a chance he will put more big plays on tape for Gardner-Johnson and the Bills defense to study ahead of the rematch in early December.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Real Drake Maye shines through in Patriots’ win over Bills
summary: There was talk about a shoulder injury. There was talk about a rift with head coach Mike Vrabel. There even were comparisons with Mac Jones. And yet, when he left the field at Highmark Stadium on Sunday, all the speculation and exaggeration surrounding Drake Maye was suddenly a thing of the past. At least for […]
full_text: There was talk about a shoulder injury . There was talk about a rift with head coach Mike Vrabel . There even were comparisons with Mac Jones . And yet, when he left the field at Highmark Stadium on Sunday, all the speculation and exaggeration surrounding Drake Maye was suddenly a thing of the past. At least for one game, the New England Patriots’ third-year quarterback looked like the MVP candidate again that he was just last season. Maye had just led his team to a 29-26 upset win over the previously-unbeaten Buffalo Bills, and doing so in style. He was efficient as a passer, productive as a runner, and most importantly avoided the back-breaking mistakes that cost the Patriots in their previous losses to the Seahawks and Jaguars. He looked like vintage Drake Maye. “I think it’s relieving a little bit,” the 24-year-old said during his postgame press conference. Entering 2026 off a Super Bowl berth and one of the best individual seasons in Patriots franchise history — a history, mind you, dominated by the greatest quarterback of all time — Maye and the team had high expectations. The first three games, however, tempered those expectations. Maye looked insecure, made questionable decisions, and was one of the least effective QBs in the NFL. In those three games, two of them losses, the turned the ball over a league-worst seven times. But while he did add two more giveaways to his tally on Sunday in Orchard Park, his performance as a whole was much more in line with the pre-season expectation. Not only did he go toe-to-toe with one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks, Josh Allen, he statistically out-performed his Bills counterpart. Welcome back, good Drake Maye. — Bernd Buchmasser (@berndbuchmasser.bsky.social) 2026-10-05T10:43:28.202Z Maye looked particularly good during the Patriots’ game-winning drive in the late fourth quarter. Taking possession of the ball down five points with 4:27 left on the clock, he completed passes to Hunter Henry, Romeo Doubs and Efton Chism before again connecting with Chism on a 23-yard touchdown; he also added two more points on a subsequent conversion to Rhamondre Stevenson. In total, Maye went 4-for-7 for 68 yards and a touchdown on the final possession. “We definitely got to build off it,” he said after the game. “I’m just proud of the way the guys fought. Nobody blinked when we were over there on the sideline and they scored and went up 26-21. We just did what we do and just thankful for those guys stepping up. Everybody’s stepping up.” For his head coach, Maye’s performance on Sunday did not come as a surprise even after his slow start to the season. “He’s extremely prepared and focused and had a good week of practice for the most part,” Mike Vrabel said. “I thought that there was some protection. I thought he was decisive.” There was a lot to feel good about for the Patriots coming out of Sunday’s game. But despite playing his best football of the season in a hostile environment and without two of his top targets — A.J. Brown (IR), Mack Hollins (third-quarter calf injury) — Maye was not entirely happy with the performance on Sunday. Besides the two turnovers, he lamented missed opportunities to close out the game sooner than the late fourth quarter. “We still have some work left out there. We left our defense in some bad positions. We got the ball back twice in that third quarter, where we got a chance to really put it on them,” he said. “You’re 1-2, we come to this game and just earned a second win, 2-2. You can’t hang your hat. This is the league, and I know I have to play better and still left some stuff out there today. So, we have to build on it and know that this isn’t a point in the season where you can end the season on this. You have to get back and keep going.”
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Craig Woodson, Patriots defense step up in upset win over Bills
summary: The New England Patriots bounced back on Sunday. And while it was Drake Maye’s late 73-yard fourth-quarter drive that resulted in the game-winning touchdown to Efton Chism III, putting New England ahead in its Week 4 upset on the road against the previously unbeaten Buffalo Bills, its defense helped seal the victory nearing the final […]
full_text: The New England Patriots bounced back on Sunday. And while it was Drake Maye’s late 73-yard fourth-quarter drive that resulted in the game-winning touchdown to Efton Chism III, putting New England ahead in its Week 4 upset on the road against the previously unbeaten Buffalo Bills , its defense helped seal the victory nearing the final minute of regulation. On 2nd-and-6 from his own 40-yard line, Josh Allen stiff-armed his way out of a would-have-been Dre’Mont Jones sack before uncorking a deep ball down the left sideline towards his receiver Joshua Palmer. But second-year safety Craig Woodson cut in front of Palmer and high-pointed the ball, intercepting Allen. That turnover put the Patriots’ offense back on the field, where Maye found Hunter Henry for a first down to end the contest. However, earlier in the quarter, Buffalo wide receiver Keon Coleman scored the Bills’ go-ahead touchdown, slipping past Woodson and cornerback Charles Woods by running a post on his way to the end zone. “I trust Craig (Woodson) with everything we got,” head coach Mike Vrabel said. “He’s very mature, and I just love his demeanor. I love the way that he prepares, and that’s what happens. We choose our ability to respond and how we’re going to do it. I’m sure he was disappointed in the play before, and [he] came back to make a huge play to seal [the game]. “So all the credit to him, and being able to understand that the game isn’t over, and we’re going to come back and we’re going to need [him].” Woodson was just one player from an entire defensive unit that stepped up amidst crucial injuries, leaving key players absent from the matchup. Though outside linebacker Dre’Mont Jones returned, both standouts Christian Gonzalez and Christian Barmore sat out. After New England regained its advantage 21-17 shortly after halftime, the offense grew stagnant, with its next three drives resulting in punts through half of the final frame. Still, it took Buffalo four offensive series to find Coleman in the end zone, punting twice and only notching a field goal on its third drive. Though allowing 26 points isn’t labeled a “shut down” defensive performance, it could be considered as such against a Bills offense that led the league averaging 33.7 points per game entering the divisional matchup. Buffalo’s production also includes a statistically top-five rushing offense. Even though their run defense bent a little more in the second half, the Patriots held that unit 64 yards below its weekly average and running back James Cook to just 16 yards on the ground in the first half. “I thought we were excellent against the run … So, [I’m] extremely proud of the way the defensive staff, but most importantly, the players,” Vrabel said. “All the credit goes to those guys for being out there.” With players like recent practice squad elevation Kindle Vildor contributing and making appearances on the field that afternoon, Woodson described the team’s approach as a “next-man-up mentality” before adding that the group was “ready today.” “Everyone has to believe they are going to be the answer for why we’re going to get back in this thing,” Vrabel said of his messaging heading into the contest. “… That’s what the message will continue to be … You have to prepare every week as a starter, and you have to believe that you are the reason. Whether you make one play or 15 plays, that you’re the reason we’re going to win.” New England, heading into Highmark Stadium 1-2 on the season, now adds another tally to the win column, placing itself just one game behind the Bills in the conference standings. “We knew that we were in a little bit of a storm when it came to our record, losing games and especially how we last [to the Jacksonville Jaguars],” Woodson said. “I think we all just wanted to rally together … We know we can go make plays, and that was the only thing we told each other, like, ‘Go be you out there and go make a play.’ We already put it on tape before. Just go do it again, and that’s what happened today.”
author: Andrew Guindon

title: 10 things we learned from Patriots vs. Bills
summary: The New England Patriots celebrated a massive win in Buffalo on Sunday, beating their division rivals 29-26 and improving to 2-2 on the year. It’s still early and a lot will happen, but this one victory may have just saved their season. Let’s get into the lessons we learned from the game. This is a […]
full_text: The New England Patriots celebrated a massive win in Buffalo on Sunday, beating their division rivals 29-26 and improving to 2-2 on the year. It’s still early and a lot will happen, but this one victory may have just saved their season. Let’s get into the lessons we learned from the game. This is a mentally tough team The Patriots heard all the talk this week, they couldn’t have missed it. People say they were done. They said Drake Maye was broken. They claimed that there was a rift between him and Mike Vrabel . They said the team hated Vrabel. They had the Patriots ranked 31st in the league. None of it mattered. When the Patriots’ backs were against the wall, they responded with a huge win in Buffalo — becoming the first road win to celebrate a victory at the new Highmark Stadium. From the 97-yard drive to start the game to the fourth-quarter drive to win it, the Patriots competed their posteriors off, and won despite four of their best players — CB Christian Gonzalez, DT Christian Barmore, WR A.J. Brown, RG Mike Onwenu — being out with injury. In doing so, they might have pulled their season back from the brink of collapse. A 2-2 record looks a lot better than 1-3, and with a win over the Bills, and only being one game behind them now, they have a shot at competing for the division once again. There is a long way to go, as mentioned above, but this win last year served as a springboard for the team. Maybe it does the same this season. Drake Maye answers the critics Of all the people who were criticized this week, no one was criticized harder than Drake Maye. For him to play the way he did on Sunday was therefore impressive. It wasn’t perfect, and I didn’t like the fumble just outside the red zone, but he played his best game of the season and did it all for the team, running for 54 yards as well as passing for 269 and three touchdowns. If Maye continues to play the way he did in Buffalo on Sunday, the critics are not going to have much to say. In fact, if he plays this way every week, he’ll be back in the MVP conversation in no time. EF-Yeah Chism When Mack Hollins went down with an injury in the third quarter, the Patriots were left with a hole on their wide receiver depth chart. Efton Chism stepped up to fill that hole, and he made two monstrous catches on the final drive, the second one being a one-handed touchdown on third down that won the Patriots the game. The severity of Hollins’ injury remains to be seen, and it will be seen how effective Chism can be if asked to step into his role on a full-time basis. At least on Sunday, however, the second-year wideout stepped up when the Patriots desperately needed him to. It was exciting to see, and potentially a sign of good things to come from him. Injuries are piling up Speaking of guys who are injured, the depth at the receiver position is being tested with Hollins now banged-up as well. Add the fact that A.J. Brown is also not eligible to return until Week 6 against the Jets, and the team might have to rely on the likes of Efton Chism and Kyle Williams — or rookie tight end Eli Raridon — at a higher rate than normal. Young edges continue to impress The Patriots are banged up along the defensive line right now, but they have gotten some solid play out of their two young edge defenders, Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas. Both of them showed some real flash and power, and they constantly seem to be around the ball making plays. Jacas helped force what could have been a safety, while Ponder had a sack and a fumble recovery. They are not blue-chip players at this current moment, but they both look to be competent starters, and that’s huge considering that Ponder was a UDFA last season and Jacas looked awful in camp and preseason. The Patriots needed them to play well with Harold Landry out and will continue to count on them until the team captain is able to return from the PUP list. Romeo Doubs has a good day, but leaves more to be desired Since we are talking about the receivers, let’s talk about the guy who has been New England’s default WR1 since A.J. Brown went down, Romeo Doubs. On the one hand, he had two touchdowns and two fourth-down conversions on Sunday; on the other, he dropped a pass that ended up being an interception that gifted the Bills three points before the end of the half. The throw was not a perfect one by Drake Maye, but you would still like to see a $68 million receiver bring it down. Doubs needs to continue to improve if the Patriots are going to continue to win games with A.J. Brown on IR and Mack Hollins’ outlook unclear, but he took a step in the right direction on Sunday. In total, he finished with six receptions for 58 yards and those two TDs. Defensive masterclass on Josh Allen Josh Allen is one of, if not the very best quarterback in the NFL. He had an okay day throwing the ball on Sunday, but the Patriots were able to almost completely shut him down as a ball-carrier. He did have a tush push touchdown, but finished with only 4 rushing yards for the day. Every time he broke the pocket or stepped up, there were multiple guys waiting for him to stop him from running. The Patriots also did a nice job not leaving guys open while doing that, honing in on the “second play” element that makes Allen such a dangerous player. They made it difficult for the Bills to generate explosive plays — at least when they weren’t throwing to Keon Coleman — and forced them to string together long drives to score. Considering the injuries the Patriots were dealing with, it was an impressive performance. The Patriots look better running the ball, but still can’t run with big personnel The Patriots want to establish the run, and they brought in a bunch of players this offseason to help them do just that. They have already lost Julian Hill for the season, and Reggie Gilliam has been banged up as well, but you would still like the Patriots be able to run the ball more effectively especially out of heavy personnel. The good news is that the Patriots were able to run fairly efficiently out of lighter packages. The bad news is that they still can’t line up and run it down your throat like they would seemingly like to do. They need to simply accept what they are, and what injuries to multiple players, including Mike Onwenu, have made them. That might mean that they are going to have to pass the ball more, and run out of some lighter formations, but based on what we saw Wednesday, that is perfectly fine and might be a recipe for success for this team. Not a banner day for officiating It was far from a banner day for the refs around the league, with multiple bizarre interactions between players and coaches and the officials. One of those came in the Patriots game. Seemingly without warning, Mike Vrabel was hit with an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for arguing over a ticky-tack holding call on Marcus Jones. In addition, the holding call on Will Campbell was suspect as well, and that the Bills had worse calls that were missed, including an egregious hands-to-the-face flag that should have been thrown on the Drake Maye strip sack. Based on what we saw around the league, the officiating should be called into question, and the way that some of them have been acting leaves quite a bit to be desired. Raiders up next, in the throwbacks The Patriots are hoping to build off of the momentum of their win in Buffalo next week, when they welcome the Las Vegas Raiders to Gillette Stadium. The Raiders are coming off a season where they were the worst team in the league, but are playing very well right now and look like they are for real. They are 3-1 and almost pulled off the upset of the Chiefs on Sunday. This looked to be an easy win when the schedule came out in May, but it’s not looking so easy anymore. The Patriots are going to look good in their red throwback jerseys, and the hope is that the old Deion Sanders quote proves true, and that they play as well as they look.
author: Pat Lane

title: Patriots vs. Raiders odds: Opening lines for Week 5 matchup

title: Saints and Falcons Prediction: MNF Superdome Showdown
summary: The New Orleans Saints will return to the Caesars Superdome on Monday night for their first NFC South matchup of the season as they host the Atlanta Falcons on Monday Night Football. New Orleans enters Week 4 looking to bounce back from a frustrating 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, while the Falcons come […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - JANUARY 04: Head coaches Raheem Morris of the Atlanta Falcons and Kellen Moore of the New Orleans Saints meet after the Falcons beat the Saints 19-17 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints will return to the Caesars Superdome on Monday night for their first NFC South matchup of the season as they host the Atlanta Falcons on Monday Night Football. New Orleans enters Week 4 looking to bounce back from a frustrating 35-27 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, while the Falcons come to town for another chapter in one of the NFL’s longest and most heated rivalries. Monday night’s matchup carries even more significance as the Saints and the NFL commemorate the 20th anniversary of the historic “Domecoming” game. On Sept. 25, 2006, New Orleans returned to the Superdome for the first time following Hurricane Katrina and defeated Atlanta 23-3 in a night that became about much more than a football game. Now, 20 years later, the Saints and Falcons will once again meet again in primetime with a national audience watching. For the Saints, their focus will be to put last week’s loss behind them and get back on track. Tyler Shough has continued to show promise through the first three games of the season, but the offense needs to be more consistent and avoid the mistakes that proved costly against the Raiders, WR Chris Olave remains one of Shough’s most dangerous weapons and will once again play an important role against Atlanta. Establishing an offensive rhythm early will be especially important as New Orleans looks to take advantage of what should be an energetic home crowd. Defensively, the Saints will face another difficult test against a familiar division opponent. Games between these two teams have rarely been predictable, and limiting explosive plays while creating pressure will be key if the Saints hope to slow down a Falcons offense led again by quarterback Michael Penix Jr. The Saints must capitalize on their opportunities. In a rivalry where games are often decided by only a few plays, turnovers and red-zone execution could ultimately make the difference. But Monday night will have a different feel inside the Superdome. Between the national spotlight, the rivalry and the emotions surrounding the anniversary of one of the most important nights in franchise history, the atmosphere should be electric. The Saints will have a loud and proud home crowd behind them as they look to bounce back, earn their first NFC South win of the season and add another memorable game to the Saints and Falcons history. Prediction: Saints 34 – Falcons 27 It’s Monday Night Football, the Saints are back in primetime, and the Superdome will be rocking. With all of the emotions surrounding the 20th anniversary of “Domecoming”, I think the atmosphere gives New Orleans an extra edge. In what will be a close game, I think the Saints can feed off that energy and come away with the win. title: Week 4 Film Preview: Highlights from the All 22
summary: Falcons 35 – Packers 14 The Packers couldn’t do much on the offensive side of the ball last Thursday night and it led to Atlanta’s first win of the season. In Michael Penix first game of the season back from injury, Atlanta was able to control the line of scrimmage on both sides of the […]
full_text: Falcons 35 – Packers 14 The Packers couldn’t do much on the offensive side of the ball last Thursday night and it led to Atlanta’s first win of the season. In Michael Penix first game of the season back from injury, Atlanta was able to control the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball and dominate the Packers for most of the game. While Atlanta deserves the credit for going into Lambeau and getting the win against the favored Packers, this game was more about the Packers not executing than Atlanta doing something special. For the Saints to get a win this Monday night, it must start with taking control of the line of scrimmage, something they couldn’t do in the 4th quarter against the Raiders. Set the Edge Atlanta’s offense starts and ends with their ability to get their best player, Bijan Robinson, the ball with room to run. Their playbook is centered around their ability to run outside zone with Robinson and the Packers never found a solid answer for this as Robinson rushed for 194 yards and 2 touchdowns on Thursday night. Outside zone is a very hard play to stop as it is tiring for the defensive line and offers many possible cut-back options for the running back so defenders must be discipline in their gap assignments. If the Saints can set the edge and limit Atlanta’s ability to let Robinson round around the edge, the Falcons will not have similar success on the ground that they had in Green Bay. Take Advantage of Personnel Mismatch The Falcons defensive response to 12 personnel can be seen below and will be an area the Saints can take advantage. When the Packers put 2 tight ends on the field, the Falcons reacted by getting into a bear front (Image below) out of a base personnel package that include 3 lineman and 4 linebackers. This is an area where the Saints offense can take advantage as they can present having 2 tight ends in their personnel package while using either Noah Fant or Juwan Johnson in more of a receiver role. While they Packers weren’t able to take advantage of the mismatches the Falcons 12 personnel response would create due to poor OLine play, the Saints seem very comfortable so far this season with 2 tight ends on the field. This leads me to believe we will see another big day for Juwan in the receiving game and more effective in the run game as the Falcons front 7 on paper is the weakest one they have faced yet. Limit Drake London Explosives Similar to the Ravens, the Falcons offense will give the Saints defense a hefty sample of boot action to stop on Monday night as they use the play as a compliment to their zone rushing scheme. The Falcons boot play is unique as they move Drake London (most dangerous receiver) around to involve him in the concept in multiple ways. Unlike the Ravens, London will run every route in the concept and offers a unique ability to be dangerous at every level of the defense. The Packers where never able to reach a real answer for the Falcons zone rushing which led to London gashing them on boot and play action plays. While I trust Staley’s ability to stop the Zone/Boot combo teams after his showing against the Ravens, Drake London will be the best receiver he has been tasked with stopping yet this year in that type of scheme. Though I don’t expect London to be running wide open across the field, the Saints must have an answer for when he catches the ball on short flat routes that can be found as check downs – which is where the Raiders constantly found easy yards for their tight ends. This area is where London is most dangerous as he can turn a short competition into an explosive play for the Atlanta offense. Keys to Victory Set the Edge (Stop Outside Zone) Take Advantage of Personnel Mismatch (Utilize 2 tight end packages) Limit Drake London Explosives (Stop Boot)

Carter, 23, recorded 14 pass rush wins off the edge, the most by any player in any game this season, per ESPN analytics, plus three tackles and three quarterback hits. He also generated a career-high nine pressures on 37 pass rushes, per NextGen Stats. Eight of those pressures came within 2.5 seconds, which is the most quick pressures created by any player in a game this season. “It was pretty good today,” Carter said of the Giants’ pass rush, which recorded two sacks. “But I feel like we can get even more than we had today. Gotta keep going, keep getting after it.” Accompanied with a #BaldyBreakdown Reese & Carter were all over the field 😤 pic.twitter.com/biRezxnkSL — New York Giants (@Giants) October 5, 2026 Why Giants didn’t use the ‘J.J. McCarthy package’ after manipulating roster | New York Post By activating McCarthy instead of declaring him the emergency No. 3 quarterback, the Giants could have inserted him into the game at any point rather than only if their first two quarterbacks were out for the game. “We had enough guys playing special teams, and it just gave us an option in case we wanted to put J.J. out there to run certain plays that we had prepared for him,” head coach John Harbaugh said. “But to think that he was going to be the backup for the whole game was unrealistic. So we had Jake up, too, and that was our thinking. We just felt like we needed three guys for kind of the two roles.” NFL Week 4: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday’s games | ESPN.com Did Jameis Winston do enough to keep the starting job? This is the up-and-down Winston experience that is expected. Yes, there were two ugly interceptions. But there were also some “Wow!” throws and three touchdown passes. It was his 20th career three-touchdown game. He went 18-of-29 for 250 yards. It wasn’t pretty, but it was enough to produce a victory for the second straight week. Winston has been adamant about being judged on wins and losses. This probably bought him some more time with J.J. McCarthy waiting in the wings. QB Report Cards for 2026 NFL Week 4 | Bleacher Report Grade: C+ . Jameis Winston isn’t like other backup quarterbacks. He’s a former No. 1 overall pick, with extensive starting experience. His performances can be a wild ride, but he has the ability to make all of the throws and move an offense. He’s also the type of quarterback, who loves to live on the edge and attempt throws that will hurt his team as often as they help. The full “Jameis Winston experience” occurred Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals. In the end, the Giants found a way to win and improve to 3-1. Meanwhile, Winston’s confidence is building. “I’m heating up. And I’m starting to get better, better and better,” said Winston. “Last week, I was questioning if I can even throw. title: NY Giants to place KR/WR Braxton Berrios on IR, per report
summary: Braxton Berrios is being placed on injured reserve by the New York Giants after suffering a foot injury in Sunday’s 36-24 victory over the Arizona Cardinals, according to a report from ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter. It is unclear when Berrios was injured, though his last play was a late-second quarter punt return on which […]
full_text: Braxton Berrios | Getty Images Braxton Berrios is being placed on injured reserve by the New York Giants after suffering a foot injury in Sunday’s 36-24 victory over the Arizona Cardinals, according to a report from ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter . It is unclear when Berrios was injured, though his last play was a late-second quarter punt return on which he lost 2 yards. Berrios was just added to the 53-man roster last week after the Giants released Odell Beckham Jr . Considering Beckham’s weekend rant after his release, he may have taken himself out of the running for a return to the Giants. The Giants have wide receivers Dalen Cambre and Jalin Hyatt on the practice squad. They cut ties with veteran wide receiver Darius Slayton, now a member of the Indianapolis Colts, early in the season. Berrios has returned five kickoffs for an average of 27.6 yards and four punts for an average of 2.5 yards this season. Charlie Jones , an experienced NFL kick returner, replaced Berrios on kickoff returns Sunday. He averaged 23.0 yards on three returns. He took over for Berrios on punt returns after the injury, averaging 14.5 yards on two returns.
