title: Giants-Cardinals ‘things I think’: First-place Giants just keep ‘throwing punches’
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The flawed but feisty New York Giants woke up Monday morning with a 3-1 record and sole possession of first place in the NFC East. That is a pleasant, but absolutely unexpected development. Just for fun, and because we know it may not stay this way over the next 13 games, […]
full_text: John Harbaugh and Giants players talk to an official during Sunday’s game. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The flawed but feisty New York Giants woke up Monday morning with a 3-1 record and sole possession of first place in the NFC East. That is a pleasant, but absolutely unexpected development. Just for fun, and because we know it may not stay this way over the next 13 games, a look at the Week 4 NFC East standings: New York Giants — 3-1 Dallas Cowboys — 2-2 Philadelphia Eagles — 2-2 Washington Commanders — 1-3 How did this happen? Let’s take a look. The John Harbaugh effect The veteran head coach’s impact has been central to the Giants’ early-season success. Harbaugh made players — many of them used to losing with the Giants — believe they could win if they earned the right to win. He drove them hard during the spring and especially in the summer, harder and longer than most were accustomed to as NFL players. Harbaugh made them believe that the hard work, and the bond they developed through their shared effort, would callous them and help build the toughness to earn the opportunity to win. Be truthful, Giants fans. Would the team have won either of the Week 3 and Week 4 games it was victorious in last season? Almost certainly not. A year ago, the Giants blew five fourth-quarter leads. In each of the last two weeks, they have won games that felt as though they were about to be lost. That maybe should have been lost. “You have to play the next play, which is what they do. You gotta keep believing, and then you got to do. Keep believing, keep doing, keep believing, keep doing, keep believing, keep doing,” Harbaugh said after Sunday’s game. “That’s really what life is. Football is a metaphor for life, and that’s the way a football game goes. Sometimes it doesn’t go your way. But the last two times it did go our way, and they were rewarded for that.” Defensive tackle D.J. Reader is in his 11th season in the NFL. He knows what he sees and feels. “We fightin’, man. We out there throwing punches, and we know our brother beside us is throwing punches with us,” Reader said. “That’s all that matters. “It might not be as conventional as everybody’s looking for it to be, but shoot, we care about each other. There’s nothing really you can do to replace camaraderie. When people care about each other, a lot of things can happen.” The Giants are not the most talented team in the NFL. They are not the most talented team in the NFC East. They have lost their young star quarterback for the season in Jaxson Dart. They have lost their defensive leader in Brian Burns for the season. There are plenty of flaws to pick at. Yet, they believe. It is, again, resilience and toughness born from the work they have done. “You shouldn’t be out there playing if you don’t believe,” Reader said. “We put a lot of work in in camp. New coaches, new coordinators, new systems. If you believe in the work you put in, you just gotta keep believing.” Significantly, the winning plays were made the past two weeks by players who are having resurgent seasons. A week ago it was Jevon Holland, who was disappointing in his first season with the Giants in 2025, but earned NFC Defensive Player of the Month honors after getting three interceptions in three games. Sunday, it was Tae Banks , who looked like a bust three years after the Giants made him a first-round pick. Harbaugh gave Banks a shot at redemption, and from the beginning, Banks has taken advantage of it. Teammates lauded Banks’ resilience on Sunday, making two plays on the final goal line stand after a questionable pass interference call against him put the Arizona Cardinals at the Giants’ 4-yard line with :22 to play. Banks said after the game that the important thing is to “keep going.” He and his teammates have been doing that. “That’s real hard,” said Arvell Reese . “After you make a mistake like that, some people would probably get down. He still held his head high, chest up. Man made a play; he won us the game. That’s very hard. Tip my hat to him.” Abdul Carter is another player who had a rough rookie season in 2025, but who had a big hand in Sunday’s victory. “I think it just shows what we’re made of,” Carter said. “In those critical situations, that’s where you’ve gotta be at your best. The last two weeks we’ve been at our best in those situations. “It’s really hard to win in this league. It just reminds me of last year so much because in these situations we didn’t get it done, but obviously this year has been a change. I credit the coaches, I credit the players, I credit everybody in the building. It takes everybody.” It started with Harbaugh setting the standard, and convincing the players they could do it if they worked hard enough to earn it. The Jameis-coaster I think that is what we have to call the Jameis Winston Experience. There is great. There is ugly. There is everything in between. In some cases, all at the same time. I don’t know about anyone else, but every time Winston drops back to throw, my immediate thought is “Oh, God, what is going to happen this time?” Sometimes it is great. Sometimes it is disastrous. Every time he starts to move around in the pocket or his feet start to bounce around, I cringe. Yet, some of his best plays occur when that happens. Some of his worst, too. If I’m an offensive lineman, sometimes I love Winston. Sometimes, I hate him for making me look bad. Winston threw three touchdown passes. He threw two interceptions. He made plays that kept the Cardinals in the game. Yet, in the end, he made plays the Giants don’t win the game without. The Giants are 2-0 with Winston starting games. It isn’t pretty with Winston, and never will be. Still, could this be the start of a heater like the one Winston was on when he went 5-2 as a starter for the New Orleans Saints in 2021? Even Winston’s post-game press conference sounded like Jameis being Jameis. “I’m just grateful for the opportunity I have now. And right now, I get to smile and say I’m the starting quarterback for the New York Football Giants,” Winston said. “So, focusing on what I would love is winning games with my team, being the best that I can be. And I just feel like that, man, I’m heating up and I’m starting to get better, better, and better. “Last week, I was questioning if I could even throw. This week, I’ve got people talking about the Jameis Winston experience again. So, I’m just still so curious, and I’m so inspired to be the best me every single day. And that alone pushes me. Not another man, not another teammate, just my desire to be what I would love.” Honestly, I’m not exactly sure all of that makes sense. But sometimes watching Winston doesn’t make sense. Which, right now, with the way things are going for this Giants team, might make him the perfect quarterback for an imperfect team that has so far turned the NFC East upside down. A monster is rising In retrospect, it seems appropriate that the first question Arvell Reese was asked after Sunday’s game was about playing so well in front of Lawrence Taylor as the Giants honored the 1986 Super Bowl team. I’m kind of mad that I didn’t think to ask the question. “Oh man, that means a lot, bro,” Reese said. “With a guy like that in the building, him setting the standard for how that position is supposed to be played back in the day. It definitely means a lot to play a decent game like that.” Let’s not put Reese in the same category as Taylor just yet. Actually, not for a long while. Maybe never. Still, the 21-year-old rookie had a Taylor-esque game on Sunday. He had nine tackles. He had a pressure that led to an interception when he hit Jacoby Brissett’s arm. He had an interception of his own. He had a tackle for loss. He had three passes defensed. He made one-on-one tackles in the open field. Still, he only called his play “decent,” because there were “a bunch of plays I left out there.” Reese said in the celebratory post-game locker room that he wants to…

title: 3 NY Giants players injured in victory over Arizona Cardinals
summary: The New York Giants suffered a trio of injuries during Sunday’s 34-26 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. Bryan Hudson starts at center Bryan Hudson played well in his first NFL start at center. Head coach John Harbaugh said that Hudson started in place of John Michael Schmitz because the latter missed practices at the end […]
full_text: Jason Pinnock | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants suffered a trio of injuries during Sunday’s 34-26 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. Safety Jason Pinnock , splitting time early in the game with Tyler Nubin , left the game with a concussion. Pinnock played 17 snaps. Kick returner/reserve wide receiver Braxton Berrios left the game with a foot injury. Berrios had been replaced on kickoff return at the beginning of the game by Charlie Jones . Jones took over as the punt returner after Berrios was injured. Defensive lineman Chauncey Golston left the game with a neck injury. That led to an uptick in snaps for Darius Alexander . Bryan Hudson starts at center Bryan Hudson played well in his first NFL start at center. Head coach John Harbaugh said that Hudson started in place of John Michael Schmitz because the latter missed practices at the end of the week due to the birth of a child. Per Pro Football Focus, Hudson was the fourth-highest graded center in Week 4, and had a perfect 100.0 pass-blocking efficiency score in 33 pass-blocking snaps. Harbaugh did not anoint Hudson as the new starting center. “JMS had missed a couple days of practice, and Huddy had been doing so well,” Harbaugh said. “We kind of felt like he’s got the reps. He’s made the calls, and we were kind of thinking about starting to work him in a little bit here and there, even some extra line stuff, if possible. And it just made sense. I mean, JMS, he’d been up, his wife had the baby. He didn’t have a lot of rest. It just made sense, and I think it paid off. It’s not a long-term thing. I mean, we just have two centers we really like.” 3-0 at home Sunday’s victory marked the first time since 2008 that the Giants have started a season 3-0 at home. MetLife Stadium opened in 2010, so that is the first time in their current building. “It means a lot. I think all of us, all of us, the players, coaches, we’re all very, the organization,” Harbaugh said. “I know Mr. Mara, talked to him after the game, everybody’s very proud of that, very proud of that. All right, now, next time we come back home, we got to extend it. We got to win the next one.”

title: Giants-Cardinals: 5 plays that led to the Giants’ victory
summary: The New York Giants defeat the Cardinals 36-24 in an exciting, sloppy game that showcased a resilient defense that dialed up the pressure. Arizona set the tone early, taking a 14-3 lead with a heavy rushing attack that exploited the Giants’ edge. However, Dennard Wilson’ unit stabilized and only allowed 138 total yards after those […]
full_text: Arvell Reese | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants defeat the Cardinals 36-24 in an exciting, sloppy game that showcased a resilient defense that dialed up the pressure. Arizona set the tone early, taking a 14-3 lead with a heavy rushing attack that exploited the Giants’ edge. However, Dennard Wilson’ unit stabilized and only allowed 138 total yards after those first two Cardinals’ possessions. Both teams turned the football over three times. Both teams were sloppy with consequential penalties throughout the game. It was a wild experience, but New York is now 3-1 at the top of the NFC East; here are the five plays, or sequence of plays, that got them there. Play(s) 1: Goal line stand Deonte Banks played a HUGE role in the Giants’ win over Arizona. 1 INT, 1 TD, 4 PD, 3 AST vs Cardinals A huge win for New York as they try to stay right in the NFC East race. https://t.co/03EtvopKuc pic.twitter.com/zvcIU9pS0k — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) October 4, 2026 I’m here for the Tae Banks redemption arc. The Giants relied heavily on man coverage, including at the end when Arizona had a fresh set of downs with 22 seconds on the Giants’ four-yard line. Banks made TWO elite plays: a pass break-up against Tre McBride and the epic pick-six to secure the Giants’ victory. Banks was beaten earlier in the game for a touchdown, but bounced back with game-saving work, as you can see in the post above. Below is just the pick-six, which capped a resilient effort by the defense: PICK SIX TO SEAL THE GAME! 🤯 Deonte Banks intercepts Jacoby Brissett and takes it to the house to secure the win for the Giants pic.twitter.com/xlEssRkJcq — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 4, 2026 DOTS of the Deonte Banks game-winner pic.twitter.com/KDnI8qIWkI — Doug Analytics (@Doug_Analytics) October 4, 2026 Play(s) 2: Controversial — or correct — call! ? Dominic Zvada booted his third field goal of the game, as yellow laundry found its way onto the field. It was a defensive holding penalty that extended the Giants’ drive: Refs said this was a hold on Dante Stills 😭😭😭😭😭😭😭😭😭 pic.twitter.com/YmCTSpaoUn — mervin (@MervinBusanut) October 4, 2026 Mike LaFleur was upset, and the Giants took advantage of the call with another peak of the Jameis Winston roller coaster: Theo Johnson up the seam for the go ahead score! pic.twitter.com/y7ThBuOmC5 — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 4, 2026 Out of an EMPTY formation, Winston found Theo Johnson up the seam for a touchdown in tight coverage, which gave the Giants a 25-24 lead. New York went for two by running the football off-tackle to the left; Najee Harris punched it in, and the Giants took a three-point lead. Play(s) 3: Reckless and sloppy football The Giants seized momentum with two touchdowns in two minutes of game time. However, the Jameis Winston experience can be quite reckless. Winston threw two interceptions on the next two Giants’ drives: We see you 29 ‼️ 📺:CBS pic.twitter.com/d2ABjyKyGD — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) October 4, 2026 Budda Baker interception! 🙌 AZvsNYG on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/fSRBXz7KKr — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 The Giants got the ball to start the second half, and they responded by committing a false start penalty and throwing an interception – this is not winning football. The Winston interception led to the Cardinals scoring a go-ahead touchdown at the tail end of a 10-play, 37-yard drive, where Greg Newsome II was called for a defensive holding penalty in the end zone against Marvin Harrison Jr. Brissett 🎯 Higgins for the TD AZvsNYG on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/zm1iLz07Rw — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 The touchdown and extra point gave the Cardinals a five-point lead with 7:20 left in the third quarter. The Giants may have put the Cardinals away early, but the reckless, sloppy football made for a much more competitive — and exciting — game. Play(s) 4: Arvell Reese continues to impress Arvell Reese has established himself as one of the better young defensive weapons in the NFL, after some coverage lapses in the first two weeks of the season. Wilson mentioned Reese’s development when talking with the media, and he had his best game to date. Reese was heavily involved in Wilson’s blitz package. He hit Jacoby Brissett’s arm, which resulted in this Greg Newsome II interception: Arvell Reese on the blitz hits Jacoby Brissett's arm, which led to this Greg Newsome INT… The #Giants defense NEEDED this. pic.twitter.com/kgaIzFQ5Hn — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 4, 2026 Winston and the Giants offense went three-and-out, but Winston found Malik Nabers in the end zone after Reese secured his own interception toward the end of the second quarter: Excellent turn around by the #Giants defense, led by rookie Arvell Reese. Shelby Harris gets his paw on a pass and Reese is there to secure the INT. pic.twitter.com/8JCBR0y22p — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 4, 2026 Malik Nabers scored a few plays later to give the Giants a lead. Reese also had several big tackles and knocked other balls out of the air: Arvell Reese is putting the Giants' defense on his back. Blitz PBU to force a third-and-long where the #Giants got off the field. pic.twitter.com/9zpNn5zVKo — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 4, 2026 Reese finished with nine tackles, a tackle for a loss, and three passes defensed. Play (s) 5: Abdul Carter is a stud The Giants felt the loss of Brian Burns early, as Arizona averaged nine yards per play on their first two drives. The Cardinals had a lot of success rushing outside, but Carter’s presence was felt on the third drive with a tackle for loss. He then took over the game in the second half, but no sequence of plays was more important for Carter than his two quarterback hits: Abdul Carter with TWO QB hits on consecutive plays to force a Cardinals punt. Both Carter and Arvell Reese have put the defense on their backs at different points of the game. Great effort by the young #Giants defenders. pic.twitter.com/rXczrhL85L — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 4, 2026 Najee Harris fumbled the football after the Giants’ defense forced a four-and-out. Arizona received the ball near midfield, down by three with 11:08 left in the game. Carter hit Brissett on second-and-12, but the pass was incomplete and well covered by Newsome. Carter then rushed Brissett and hit him on a third-and-12 pass that went for just five yards. Arizona was forced to punt, as New York’s defense kept the momentum. Carter also had his hand in on Tremaine Edmunds play vs. Brissett in the second half: Abdul Carter wins inside and forced Brissett into the arms of Tremaine Edmunds. Dennard Wilson has DIALED up the blitz/pressure against the Cardinals. pic.twitter.com/7qSo77fZvi — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 4, 2026 It was excellent to see both Reese and Carter play as well as they did against Arizona. Both young players were integral parts of this Giants’ victory.

title: The Jets, the Rabbit-Duck Illusion, and Why Fan Perceptions Are Shifting Again
summary: The picture below is known as the rabbit-duck illusion. Depending on your perception, you might see a rabbit or a duck. The illusion first appeared in a German magazine in the 1890s, and it has been dissected by scholars in numerous academic fields since. Fans of the television series How I Met Your Mother may […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 4: Roschon Johnson #23 of the Chicago Bears reacts during the fourth quarter against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 4, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The picture below is known as the rabbit-duck illusion. Depending on your perception, you might see a rabbit or a duck. The illusion first appeared in a German magazine in the 1890s, and it has been dissected by scholars in numerous academic fields since. Fans of the television series How I Met Your Mother may recognize the illusion as it played a central role in an episode that aired in 2010. This speaks to something basic. Our perceptions of a person, event, or place can change even if little has changed on the surface about that entity. It’s tough to believe, but there was a brief window in 2024 when the Aaron Rodgers-Robert Saleh Jets seemed to be right on track. The team lost its opener in San Francisco to the 49ers, a game few expected them to win. The Jets followed that loss up to back-to-back wins against the Titans and the Patriots. The team was 2-1 heading into Week 4. Of course that year nobody thought Tennessee or New England would be very good, but the Jets were doing what good teams did. They took care of business against bad opponents. Then came Week 4. The Jets lost to a Denver Broncos team they were supposed to beat. The next week they lost in London to the Vikings, and their head coach was fired. Next up was a loss to the Buffalo Bills. The team made a desperation trade for Davante Adams, but that didn’t help the Jets avoid a loss to the Steelers and then the next week that same Patriots team. After the third week of that season, it was perfectly reasonable to look at the Jets’ 2-1 record and feel like they took care of business against bad teams. A few weeks later, those games looked different. The Titans were on their way to earning the number one overall pick, but they had outgained the Jets in Week 2. The Jets needed a late goal line stand to secure a win against a dreadful team. The Week 3 win against the Patriots was more decisive, but New England was indeed awful in 2024. Still they were able to avenge their loss to the Jets a few weeks later. It quickly had become clear that the 2024 Jets were also a very bad team. They would win only three more games the rest of the way, one of which was against a Jaguars team that also earned a top five pick. Another was against a Dolphins team in Week 18 playing its backup quarterback. I’m not sure which one of duck or rabbit represents a good team on its way and which represents a really bad team that had a soft early season schedule, but it’s fair to say perceptions changed about that Jets team. An NFL season is a fragile thing. A team can seem to be on a good trajectory and then completely fall off and have a disastrous season. The 2026 Jets weren’t playing spectacular football heading into Week 4, but they more or less had looked like a professional team, which was something to be appreciated. The record might have only been 1-2, but this team looked a cut above your recent Jets club. They were coming off a Week 3 game where they stood toe to toe with a quality Lions team. Up against a backup quarterback in Chicago, I don’t think a win was an unreasonable ask. At the very least, the Jets should continue to look professional. Instead fans were treated to a catastrophic loss. The Jets were horrible in all phases of the game. In recent years this team has had an uncanny way of becoming a footnote like this. And there’s this:￼ The Bears had more 1st downs (34) than the Jets had plays (32). It's the 2nd game in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) in which one team had more first downs than its opponent had plays. H/t ESPN Research #jets ￼ — Rich Cimini (@RichCimini) October 5, 2026 This was the kind of game that makes you question whether the progress of the first four weeks was actually progress. Maybe that win over the Tennessee Titans that seemed promising in the moment was just this team’s version of the Week 3 2024 game against New England, catching a horrific opponent at the perfect moment on the schedule. Blowing a 10 point lead to Green Bay in the fourth quarter in a game they otherwise dominated perhaps could be excused since the Jets did play at a high level. Losing a back and forth road game to the Lions because Detroit made one more play? It happens. But when you combine these results with that ghastly effort in Chicago, you get a 1-3 record. You could be excused for wondering how real the progress of the first three weeks really was. When I say progress, I’m not talking about merely being better than the Brady Cook Jets of the final five games from 2025. That legitimately might have been the worst five game stretch of football a team has played in NFL history. The Jets could have done literally anything this offseason and been improved from that. The question is whether the Jets are on track to become a genuinely good team within the next year or two. You could be forgiven if your answer today is different from what it would have been yesterday. One critical area where fan perceptions might change is on the team’s head coach. It isn’t exactly a secret that Aaron Glenn has struggled in his year and change in charge of the Jets. His 4-17 record is a clear enough indicator of that. Of course Glenn inherited a true nightmare situation, one few coaches could have navigated successfully to this point. There’s nothing wrong with trying to talk yourself into a head coach. Glenn was a legendary player for this franchise. Hoping for the best for him is the right thing to do. So we can point out the horrendous condition the team was in when he took the job. We can talk about focusing on the long-term. We can try to absolve Glenn of the blame. But when you face the Bears, you face Ben Johnson. There is a clear display of what a genuinely good head coach is capable of doing. Johnson, of course, took over a much better situation in Chicago. Still, it isn’t all about his talent. In a six day stretch he just produced two wins with two different quarterbacks playing well. Neither of those quarterbacks is his starter. Compare that with Glenn. Ask what Glenn is doing to make this team better. Your perception of Glenn slowly making progress building this team might change faster than you can say, “Rabbit to duck.” The best thing about the NFL is there’s a game the next week. A victory over the Browns can change perceptions back. But for one week, the Jets have left many of us wondering whether the early stages of 2026 actually represent a meaningful step forward. They earned that through this performance.

title: Eagles Injury Tracker: List of players grows after Week 4 loss
summary: We are just about a quarter of the way through the 2026 NFL season already, and while the Eagles seemed to avoid injury issues in the first two weeks, they’ve really stacked up in their last two games. Heading into the Week 4 matchup against the Rams, the Eagles had six players inactive due to […]
full_text: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images | Getty Images We are just about a quarter of the way through the 2026 NFL season already, and while the Eagles seemed to avoid injury issues in the first two weeks, they’ve really stacked up in their last two games. Heading into the Week 4 matchup against the Rams, the Eagles had six players inactive due to injury: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) Dallas Goedert (knee) Hollywood Brown (ankle) Fred Johnson (knee) Zack Baun (concussion) Marcus Epps (groin) And then, things spiraled completely out of control during the Rams game, with Saquon Barkley suffering a hamstring injury early in the first quarter. Heading into their Week 5 matchup, these are some of the newer injuries to keep an eye on: Saquon Barkley ( UPDATE : Week-to-week hamstring injury ) Quinyon Mitchell ( knee ) Jonathan Greenard ( UPDATE : Day-to-day ankle injury ) Tank Bigsby ( UPDATE : On IR — having core muscle surgery ) Cam Jurgens ( UPDATE : Self-reported concussion symptoms Monday morning ) It wasn’t due to injury, but Lane Johnson was inactive for Sunday’s game too due to personal reasons , so his status moving forward is also questionable. There are also a handful of players sitting on IR, with some uncertainty about when they’ll be back with the team: Landon Dickerson (knee) Eli Stowers (hamstring/quad) Grant Calcaterra (back) Jakorian Bennett (knee) Andre’ Sam (foot) Johnny Wilson (knee — unable to return this season) All-in-all, the Eagles will have a lot of questions to answer as far as the roster goes moving forward, and hopefully some of these starters will be able to return soon.
author: Alexis Chassen

title: Saquon Barkley injury: Eagles running back is week-to-week with hamstring
summary: Injuries are quickly becoming a problem, and the Eagles could be without more than a handful of offensive starters for their Week 5 game in London. One player they might not have with them is running back Saquon Barkley, who is reportedly week-to-week with a hamstring injury he sustained on the first drive against the […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images Injuries are quickly becoming a problem, and the Eagles could be without more than a handful of offensive starters for their Week 5 game in London. One player they might not have with them is running back Saquon Barkley, who is reportedly week-to-week with a hamstring injury he sustained on the first drive against the Rams . #Eagles RB Saquon Barkley is unlikely to play Sunday vs. the Jaguars in London because of the hamstring injury he suffered vs. the Rams, an NFL source said. @RapSheet and @MikeGarafolo report it’s considered a week-to-week injury, so Barkley will avoid being placed on short-term… — Jeff McLane (@Jeff_McLane) October 6, 2026 It could have been worse for Barkley, and for the Eagles, and thankfully it doesn’t look to be a longterm injury. Still, the team placed RB Tank Bigsby on IR earlier in the day , leaving Will Shipley as the only running back on the active roster. The team does have three backs on the practice squad, Jaydon Blue, Dameon Pierce, and Carson Steele, but for an offense that’s already struggling to find their footing, having to rely on the guys so deep on the roster is less than ideal. Maybe being forced to do things differently will help head coach Nick Sirianni and OC Sean Mannion find a spark they’ve so badly missed through four games this season. And hopefully Barkley is back sooner rather than later to help establish the ground game.

title: Eagles injury list grows: Cam Jurgens enters concussion protocol
summary: The list of injured Eagles players continues to grow, and things are getting particularly dicey up front with the offensive line. It was reported Monday night that former center turned left guard Cam Jurgens self-reported concussion symptoms earlier in the day, and is now in the protocol, according to NFL insider Mike Garafolo. Sunday’s game […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images | Getty Images The list of injured Eagles players continues to grow, and things are getting particularly dicey up front with the offensive line. It was reported Monday night that former center turned left guard Cam Jurgens self-reported concussion symptoms earlier in the day, and is now in the protocol, according to NFL insider Mike Garafolo . Sunday’s game against the Rams really highlighted what a bad position the Eagles are in with their OL depth, and Jurgens being sidelined only adds to the issue. The new left guard stepped into Landon Dickerson’s spot when the original LG went to IR after Week 1, but Jurgens really struggled in his new role. Head coach Nick Sirianni was asked on Monday if they had considered benching Jurgens, but he publicly stated he was pleased with Jurgens. Heading into training camp, the Eagles offensive line was Jordan Mailata, Landon Dickerson, Cam Jurgens, Tyler Steen, and Lane Johnson. Heading into their Week 4 game against the Rams, the starting OL was Jordan Mailata, Cam Jurgens, Drew Kendall, Tyler Steen, and Markel Bell. Lane Johnson missed Sunday’s game due to personal reasons, and Fred Johnson was inactive due to injury. Drew Kendall went into the medical tent at one point during the game, but was thankfully able to return and finish the game, but there’s a chance he’s not fully healthy either. Heading into the week the team had just Willie Lampkin and Micah Morris as active backups, and they’ll have to turn to one of them to replace Jurgens if he’s unable to travel to London.

title: Monday Night Football: Falcons vs. Saints

title: Tank Bigsby injury: Eagles running back to injured reserve
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are placing No. 2 running back Tank Bigsby on injured reserve, according to a report from NFL insider Ian Rapoport. Bigsby is set to core muscle surgery with the hope that he’ll be able to return in “six weeks or shorter.” He was previously listed on the injury report with an abdomen […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 4: Tank Bigsby #8 of the Philadelphia Eagles is helped off the field after sustaining an injury during an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on October 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are placing No. 2 running back Tank Bigsby on injured reserve, according to a report from NFL insider Ian Rapoport. Bigsby is set to core muscle surgery with the hope that he’ll be able to return in “six weeks or shorter.” He was previously listed on the injury report with an abdomen injury that apparently worsened during the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Bigsby saw increased playing time on Sunday due to Saquon Barkley suffering a hamstring injury early in the game. With Barkley in danger of missing more game(s), the Eagles could be without their top two running backs against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 5. That would leave them with just Will Shipley, who’s also appeared on the injury report in recent weeks, as the only player at his position on the active roster. The Eagles do have three running backs on their practice squad: Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele, and Jaydon Blue. Pierce seems like the most likely candidate to be signed to the Eagles’ roster, if they want to go that route. Pierce looked good in training camp and preseason when he wasn’t dealing with injury issues of his own. Preseason fan favorite Steele could then be temporarily elevated from the practice squad to give the Eagles at least three running backs for game day. Blue only joined the team back in September. Losing Bigsby, especially while Barkley might also be out, isn’t ideal. And neither is the Eagles’ bleak offensive outlook at this point in time.
author: Brandon Lee Gowton

title: Eagles-Rams snap counts: Darius Cooper overtakes Makai Lemon
summary: The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams are in. Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE DEFENSE SPECIAL TEAMS DID NOT PLAY INACTIVE: Lane Johnson, Fred Johnson, DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert, Zack Baun, Marcus Epps, Hollywood Brown, Cole Payton ACTIVE: Tanner McKee, Andy […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 04: Darius Cooper #80 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates after making a catch for a touchdown during the second quarter of the game against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on October 04, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams are in. Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE Jordan Mailata, Tyler Steen, and Cam Jurgens are the only players on offense who’ve played 100% of the Eagles’ offensive snaps this season. And Jurgens probably shouldn’t be playing at this point. Markel Bell made his first career NFL start with Lane Johnson unavailable to play. Dontayvion Wicks played the most snaps of any Eagles receiver but ranked third in targets with five. Interesting to see that Darius Cooper outsnapped Makai Lemon as WR2 … while also playing a significant role on special teams, where he logged a tackle on punt coverage. Good! We’ve been calling for Cooper to get more playing time. His team-high seven targets produced three catches for 33 yards and two touchdowns. Johnny Mundt playing 80% of the Eagles’ offensive snaps is a failure in both roster construction and personnel usage. He’s not even that great of a blocker (he had a drive-killing holding penalty) and he basically offers nothing as a pass-catcher. I get the Eagles are without Dallas Goedert and Eli Stowers (who doesn’t look very ready to be a meaningful contributor) but that’s just way too much playing time for Mundt, who is ideally more of a third tight end. Mundt played more than the Eagles’ 2026 first-round pick!!!!!! What are we doing here. Lemon saw the second-most targets with six. He logged three catches for 27 yards. Curiously, all three receptions came on the Eagles’ third drive. Somehow never got another touch after that. Will Shipley and Tank Bigsby were forced into bigger roles with Saquon Barkley suffering a hamstring injury. And then Bigsby got banged up later in the game. Zach Ertz saw a smaller workload in this game (21% snaps played) than he had in Week 3 (38% snaps played). Elijah Moore was a healthy scratch as WR7 in the first two games. Injuries allowed him to suit up for the last two games but he’s yet to touch the ball. Perhaps in part because he apparently doesn’t know what to do out there. Jalen Hurts yelled at him to line up off the ball early in the game. Moore also doesn’t help on special teams at all. Nice use of a roster spot. The Eagles brought Willie Lampkin in for a tush push (that failed in part because it was a long 4th-and-1) and as an extra blocker in a jumbo package on 3rd-and-goal from the 2-yard line. They should consider playing him more … at left guard. Micah Morris made his NFL debut on offense by coming into the game with Lampkin on that goal line jumbo package. DEFENSE Miss me with putting major blame on the defense for this loss. They had to play 84 snaps. Part of that is because they couldn’t get off the field at the end, sure, but they were exhausted at that point because this pathetic offense gives them little rest. 84 snaps is ridiculous. It’s just three fewer than the Eagles’ defense faced in last year’s loss to the Chicago Bears. And this defense had to play 70 snaps in Week 1 and 72 in Week 3. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. was very active in his first career regular season where the Eagles weren’t resting starters. He had 15 total tackles. Entering this game, Cooper DeJean and Quinyon Mitchell were the only Eagles defenders who had played 100% of the team’s defensive snaps. But they both missed time due to injury in this one. DeJean was able to return to action while Mitchell was not. As you can see, Trot Jr. played the entire game while Jihaad Campbell did not. Hmm. Michael Carter II got the start at safety with Marcus Epps and seemed to play relatively well. He tipped a pass to create DeJean’s intercetion.The Eagles should probably stick with him there. The Eagles continue to manage Jalen Carter’s workload more than normal as he plays through a hairline fracture in his wrist. Nolan Smith was the Eagles’ top edge rusher in terms of both playing time and performance. He logged just one more snaps than Jalyx Hunt, who didn’t get the start in this game while behind Smith and Jonathan Greenard. Jonathan Jones had to play a good deal with Mitchell getting hurt. Jordan Davis played a season-low snap count percentage at 34.5%. He ranks 60th out of 177 interior defenders in total snaps played this season. Davis is the eighth-highest paid player at his position on an annual basis. Arnold Ebiketie saw a bigger role than normal with Greenard getting hurt. Mac McWilliams came in to play nickel cornerback while DeJean was briefly unavailable due to injury. Kenny Moore made his Eagles debut by playing just one snap on defense. SPECIAL TEAMS Kelee Ringo had an active game with three special teams tackles. Josiah Deguara was limited to special teams duty after being temporarily elevated from the practice squad as a fourth tight end. Britain Covey helped to set up one of the Eagles’ two touchdowns with his 41-yard punt return. DID NOT PLAY INACTIVE: Lane Johnson, Fred Johnson, DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert, Zack Baun, Marcus Epps, Hollywood Brown, Cole Payton ACTIVE: Tanner McKee, Andy Dalton Hopefully Lane and his family are OK. Fred Johnson missed his second game in a row. DeVonta is expected to miss at least one more game due to his hamstring injury. Goedert might miss another game. Baun might be able to return from concussion protocol this week. TBD. Epps might not get his starting spot back even when he is healthy. Brown missed his second game in a row. With Cooper rising, there isn’t really room for him in this receiver rotation. Payton will continue to be a healthy scratch as QB4. McKee is reportedly QB2 now with Dalton being demoted to QB3. The Eagles should just cut Dalton. There’s no point of him being on the roster. There never was. The roster spot is more valuable than he is.
author: Brandon Lee Gowton

title: Eagles-Rams Takeaway: Injuries complicate search for identity
summary: DeVonta Smith. Saquon Barkley. Lane Johnson. Landon Dickerson. Dallas Goedert. Tank Bigsby. Quinyon Mitchell. Jonathan Greenard. Zach Baun. Marcus Epps. Nine starters and one vital back-up. All injured either coming into the Eagles’ fall-from-ahead 24-20 loss to the Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday or hurt during an excruciating afternoon that dropped the Birds […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 4: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles screams prior to an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on October 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images DeVonta Smith. Saquon Barkley. Lane Johnson. Landon Dickerson. Dallas Goedert. Tank Bigsby. Quinyon Mitchell. Jonathan Greenard. Zach Baun. Marcus Epps. Nine starters and one vital back-up. All injured either coming into the Eagles’ fall-from-ahead 24-20 loss to the Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday or hurt during an excruciating afternoon that dropped the Birds to 2-2 on the still-young-but-getting-older season. Even if the Eagles came into the game with an offensive system that had been in place for four or five years and knew what they wanted to be, losing that many players in one game would be difficult to overcome. But when you’re under yet another first-time offensive coordinator and playcaller, and when you’re going up against one of the most high-powered offenses in the NFL, sometimes the attrition and misfortune of injuries is too much to overcome. For most of three-and-a-half quarters yesterday, the story of the day was “resilience.” No, the Eagles had not played well on offense, but it was somewhat understandable without Smith, their No. 1 wideout, and Johnson and Dickerson, both of whom anchor the offensive line. When Barkley went down on the first series of the game, Bigsby, Will Shipley and Darius Cooper stepped up and made enough plays to take advantage of L.A. mistakes and put up a 20-10 lead. Their depth was being tested but they were hanging in there. The numbers, including a ghastly 0-for-12 on 3rd downs, would be less important than the grit showed by Jalen Hurts and an offense trying to cobble things together while short-handed. But with Sean Mannion calling plays in just his fourth NFL contest, it became clear he, and Hurts, are still searching for easy-button set of layup plays that can help them convert short distances in pressure situations. In seven of their 12 failed third down opportunities, they needed less than five yards, and on the all-important 4th-and-goal from the 2 in the fourth quarter, there was nothing dependable or reliable in the playbook for Mannion and Hurts to turn to. No security blankets. Even without Smith in the lineup, there should still be at least 2-4 plays the offense can choose from in order to pick up five yards, or give themselves a real shot at the goal line. But there is nothing in the bag they feel good about yet. It all comes down to forming an identity. The Eagles searched for one all last year under Kevin Patullo and never found one. That search continues through four games under Mannion. And while some patience should be reserved for the new OC, it is reasonable to expect some improvement as the weeks move along. Nick Sirianni is correct that progress is not always linear, but it also should look better than it has over the last two weeks. Their struggles in the second half of football games is truly concerning. One week after being outscored 17-0 after halftime, the Eagles were shut out 14-0 in the second half against the Rams. That’s 31-0 over the last two weeks. Now, it’s fair to wonder how things might have gone had Hurts not bobbled the snap on 3rd-and-2 at the goalline late in the 4th quarter and managed to hand the ball off to Bigsby, who was still in the game at this point. It looked as though Bigsby would have at least been able to get it close to the goal line, if not score. Had he done so, the game would have been over. But if wishes were horses, then beggars would ride. Mannion was supposed to craft an offense that would put defenses into conflict, never knowing when the Eagles were going to run or pass. But so far, it’s pretty much a guarantee that if Hurts is under center, they’re handing it off to a running back. They’re only going to pass out of the shotgun, and that’s problematic. Is that a function of Hurts’ comfort or a lack of imagination from Mannion? We asked many of these same questions last year under Patullo. Those questions, and the quarterback, remain. It is difficult to find an identity without a competent offensive line and, right now, they don’t have one. They haven’t had one since the Super Bowl 59 squad walked off the field. Dickerson’s absence forced a reshuffling of the offensive line that pushed Cam Jugens to left guard and Drew Kendall to center. Kendall has been fine, but Jurgens has struggled. And with Lane Johnson out and Tyler Steen also finding difficulty, as well as a predictable pattern for defenses to hone in on, it’s been almost impossible for the Eagles to form the kind of run-first identity Mannion would ideally like to have. As such, there is no play-action. Nothing to put defenses in conflict. Should Hurts have been able to do a little more against the Rams in the second half? The film grinders will watch on All-22 and let us know if meat was left on the bone, but it didn’t look as though Hurts had much of a chance in the passing game on Sunday. The makeshift offensive line couldn’t hold up to a superior Los Angeles pass rush and, with the game on the line, wilted. The search for an identity on offense will clearly be hampered by the loss of star players and key offensive linemen. Defensively, even without Mitchell, Greenard, Baun and Epps, the defense should have been able to hold a 10-point lead with 6 minutes left and the Rams backed up to their own 2-yard line. Quick aside: Sirianni’s decision to go for it at the goal line was the right call. Had he kicked the field goal, the Rams still could have gone ahead with two touchdowns, which is what happened anyway. Sirianni had to believe that, even if the Eagles fell short there, the defense would at least force a struggling Matt Stafford to take more time off the clock to travel 98 yards than they did, and he had to believe they would be able to prevent the Rams from scoring twice in that short amount of time. But Vic Fangio’s unit, who had played admirably to that point, was unable to get the job done. Mitchell’s absence in the secondary was felt, as was Baun’s play-making and ability to cover receivers out of the backfield. The pass rush, which had been so effective all day, suddenly ran out of gas. Jalen Carter’s name was barely uttered on Sunday. Ultimately, the losses on defense were too much to overcome. Moving forward, the concern is how long these missing players will be out. Reports indicate Smith’s hamstring injury is one that could keep him out for multiple weeks. The injuries to Barkley and Biggs didn’t look good. No one knows, as of this writing, what forced Johnson to miss the game on Sunday, and even when Dickerson comes back, no one is sure how he’s going to look. Will the defense be without Mitchell long-term? How about Greenard? Baun’s concussion? There is a real danger of this football season looking like the 2005 Eagles who, coming off a Super Bowl, ran into a calamity of injuries (and Terrell Owens’ nonsense) and suffered a lost season under Andy Reid. Sirianni and Hurts have never had a losing season. This Eagles roster is top-heavy and, when the top is hurt, there’s not much there waiting in the wings to replace them. It is in situations like these that Mannion has to prove that he can be a creative problem-solver and Hurts can be adaptable. They must work together to find an identity or, at the very least, a collection of plays they can rely on to get them 5-7 yards throughout a game. Perhaps that’s easier said than done but, that is why the Eagles hired Mannion, after all. The NFL season is one-quarter of the way done. The training wheels need to come off now. If we’re going to see a fully functional Mannion offense, it has to start now, even if they are under-manned. Yes, injuries complicate the search for an identity. But an identity still must be found if the Eagles want to avoid…
author: John Stolnis

title: Eagles News: “The Nick Sirianni hot seat is real, or at least it should be”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! There’s plenty of blame to share but the head coach is lacking answers and that’s a pretty big problem. The team isn’t that far off from 0-4; they narrowly won their first two games. Of course, you can also say the […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 4: Head Coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts after a play during the fourth quarter of an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on October 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! There’s plenty of blame to share but the head coach is lacking answers and that’s a pretty big problem. The team isn’t that far off from 0-4; they narrowly won their first two games. Of course, you can also say the Eagles were close to being 3-1. But that record would be masking a team that’s just not playing very well right now. We might be heading down a path where a reset is needed. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … NFL winners and losers: Nick Sirianni sucks – SB Nation The Sirianni hot seat is real, or at least it should be. This team has churned through offensive coordinators since its Super Bowl win, routinely causing them to get blamed when things go wrong and the offense doesn’t reach its potential. This has to come back to Sirianni at some point, and it’s fair to question whether or not he’s lost control of the offensive side of the ball. One of the best traits the Eagles had at their zenith was a perfect understanding of who they are, their strengths, and not getting outside of that rubric. Lately it’s felt as if Philadelphia is playing aspirational football, forcing what they want to be, rather than accepting who they are right now — and playing to those strengths. It’s a weird situation, because Sirianni actually does have a lot of fantastic traits. He’s an excellent motivator, he developed a locker room culture that had more of a swagger an edge, but he’s sorely needing someone to assist with the strategic elements of the game. It’s not that Sirianni is incapable, but more that he looks like a coach who is underwater right now, trying to do too much at once. If he doesnt find a way of swimming soon, it’ll sink this entire season. Roob’s Observations as Rams take advantage of injury-riddled Eagles – NBCSP Second half. Again. Good lord. The Eagles have now been outscored 54-20 in the second half this year, 31-0 the last two weeks and they’ve been outgained by an average of 202-103. That’s insane. The Cowboys scored more second-half points today (28) than the Eagles have all year. The Rams outgained them 260-72 Sunday. How does an NFL team not understand you have to play 60 minutes to beat a good team? How can an entire team just fall to pieces when the game is on the line? How can so many players just stop making plays at crunch time? The Eagles on Sunday had four first downs in the second half and the Rams had 16. Seriously? Come on. And I put the blame for this squarely on the coaching staff, Nick Sirianni in particular. He’s responsible for everything we see on the football field. And what we’re seeing after halftime is a football team that’s inept, unprepared, overmatched and embarrassed on a weekly basis. Pathetic. Eagles vs. Rams: 9 winners, 9 losers, and 4 IDKs – BGN The Philadelphia Eagles didn’t really deserve to beat the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday afternoon. The Birds were outgained by 243 yards. That’s typically not a recipe for success. Neither is failing to convert a single third down despite having 12 chances to do so. Despite these struggles … and despite entering this game with a lot of key absences and only suffering more injuries during the day … the Eagles almost managed to steal this game. Almost. They were two yards away from going up 17 points with about 7.5 minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. If they score a touchdown in that spot, the conversation is a lot different than it is right now. But that’s not our current reality. The Eagles lost their second game in a row and one can only wonder if there are more losses on the way. Handing out 10 awards from the Eagles-Rams game – PhillyVoice They were 2-for-9 last week against the Bears. Add it up, and they are 2-for-21 on 3rd downs the last two games. #Math. Is it execution? Play calling? Scheme?”Everybody contributed to that,” Nick Sirianni said. “Everybody. There’s execution errors. There’s coaching errors. Everybody contributes to that.” It feels like “Everybody contributed to that” is a common answer too often, from the back half of the 2025 season, carrying through into 2026. What made the third-down ineptitude so egregious was that they weren’t even in a lot of third-and-long situations. […] They were in 3rd and 5 or less on seven of those 3rd-down opportunities. Other than the Tush Push (which also failed today), the Eagles just don’t seem to have anything they can go to to sustain drives. Good Start Goes Bad – Iggles Blitz I don’t know how to feel about the Eagles right now. I was impressed with the first half. I was depressed by the fourth quarter. And I’m definitely concerned by all the injuries. While I’m not confident in them, I don’t want to dismiss the positive signs from the Rams game. The safeties played well. The pass rush was good at times. The STs gave the team a big boost. Rookie Markell Bell did some good things in his first NFL start. But the offense…yikes. Regardless of who is out, the offense must handle the blitz better. That is on the OL, Hurts, the skill players and the coaches. Everyone owns some of the blame for those struggles. Teams will continue to attack until the Eagles show they can block it and/or burn it. Sean Mannion, or Nick Sirianni, or Jalen Hurts has to decide on offensive identity after ugly Rams loss – Inquirer After nearly reaching the quarter pole of the season, it’s become evident that Sean Mannion’s Eagles offense is disjointed, unimaginative, and ultimately, ineffective. Or is it Nick Sirianni’s offense? Or Jalen Hurts’? Or does it even matter who is given ownership of a unit that failed to capitalize on an impressive defensive performance against the Los Angeles Rams? Of course, everyone played a part in a 24-20 loss on Sunday. Vic Fangio’s defense could have gotten a stop on the Rams’ two late fourth-quarter touchdown drives. The Lane Johnson-less offensive line could have opened more holes and given Hurts more time. The wide receivers, running backs, and tight ends could have done something to convert just one third down. But the offense has reached an inflection point after its regression in each of the first four games, and it’s on the figureheads at the top to decide where to go from here. Should Sirianni allow Mannion to fully implement the Kyle Shanahan scheme that was at the core of his hiring? Or should they just abandon the under-center heavy system that has been woefully unproductive thus far? What is the Eagles’ offensive identity? Not ‘good enough,’ says Nick Sirianni after loss to Rams | The Early Bird – PHLY Eagles An optimist’s view would also point to the fact that the Eagles have been here before with Hurts under center and Sirianni at the helm. You might remember the team also got off to a 2-2 start in 2024. The offensive line implored Sirianni to pivot toward more of a run-first approach, Sirianni shaved his head, and the Eagles went on a magical run to Super Bowl LIX and left Caesars Superdome with the organization’s second Lombardi Trophy. That page doesn’t seem to be in Sean Mannion’s 2026 playbook, though. The Eagles ranked fifth in EPA/rush through the first four games of 2024. This season, they’re 24th. They’ve had moving pieces along the offensive line in three of the first four games and Barkley has now suffered a stinger and a hamstring injury already this season. Backup running back Tank Bigsby also suffered an apparent injury late in the fourth quarter. What is apparent is that the Eagles now have an urgency to figure out what this year’s about face is going to look like. A training camp spent harping on under-center formations and play-action passing…

title: Eagles vs. Rams: 9 winners, 9 losers, and 4 IDKs
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles didn’t really deserve to beat the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday afternoon. The Birds were outgained by 243 yards. That’s typically not a recipe for success. Neither is failing to convert a single third down despite having 12 chances to do so. Despite these struggles … and despite entering this game with […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 4: Darius Cooper #80 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the second quarter of an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on October 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles didn’t really deserve to beat the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday afternoon. The Birds were outgained by 243 yards. That’s typically not a recipe for success. Neither is failing to convert a single third down despite having 12 chances to do so. Despite these struggles … and despite entering this game with a lot of key absences and only suffering more injuries during the day … the Eagles almost managed to steal this game. Almost. They were two yards away from going up 17 points with about 7.5 minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. If they score a touchdown in that spot, the conversation is a lot different than it is right now. But that’s not our current reality. The Eagles lost their second game in a row and one can only wonder if there are more losses on the way. Time to hand out winners, losers, and I don’t knows. For even more analysis, check out my appearance on the PHLY Eagles postgame show along with Brandon Graham, Bo Wulf, and others! WINNERS DARIUS COOPER September 21, 2026 : “I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again: good things happen when Hurts throws the ball to Cooper.” My love for Cooper isn’t just a bit! He’s proving to be a useful player. Three of his five receptions this season have resulted in touchdowns. On his first touchdown, Cooper made a great effort to snag the ball out of the air to prevent an interception and put points on the board for the Eagles instead. Cooper then managed to get wide open in the back of the end zone for Hurts for his second score. Cooper finished this game with a team-high seven targets. That volume speaks to Hurts’ trust in him. It’s pretty silly that this guy saw zero targets in Week 1. And that he played the fifth-most snaps of any Eagles receiver in Week 3, when he also logged zero targets. Cooper can make plays as a pass-catcher. He’s the Eagles’ best blocking receiver. He’s among the NFL leaders in special teams tackles. The Eagles need to stop messing around and get him more regularly involved. It’s really a shame they lost this game because Cooper would be getting much more shine if they won. MARKEL BELL Bell graded out better as a run blocker than a pass protector. The rookie tackle was able to use his size and strength to pancake some defenders. Bell wasn’t perfect. But he had to start this game on short notice after Lane Johnson did not play due to personal reasons. It’s not like he got a full week in practice to prepare for this situation. Bell did not look totally lost out there. He did not wreck the game. That might sound like a low bar but it’s an encouraging starting point. ANDREW MUKUBA Mukuba has drawn a lot of ire but he made a really nice diving interception for a 21-yard return that allowed the Eagles’ offense to set up at the plus 28-yard line and ultimately score three points. Mukuba’s playmaking ability is part of his purported appeal, so, that was good to see. He did was charted for two missed tackles, which isn’t ideal. But those mistakes are a little more easy to live with if he’s generating big plays. COOPER DEJEAN DeJean has bounced back since a rough Week 1. Impressive focus to stay with a tipped ball and make the grab for a pick and 25-yard return to set up an Eagles touchdown right before the end of the first half. JEREMIAH TROTTER JR. Tackles aren’t a perfect stat but Trot Jr. led the team with 15 total, 10 of which were solo. A team-high three of his tackles were classified as “stops,” which are tackles that constitute a failure for the offense. Trot Jr. did miss a key tackle on Kyren Williams’ touchdown run that gave the Rams the lead. Shame, too, because he had the running back lined up for either no gain or a loss. Didn’t make the play. Still, more good than bad from a player making his first NFL start in a game where the Eagles weren’t resting their starters. NOLAN SMITH Smith timed up the snap count well to get to Matthew Stafford unblocked for a sack. His second sack of the season accounts for the Eagles’ total of four sacks through four games. Smith also had two “stops. One of them was a TFL. Also worth noting that Smith officially started this game as one of two edge rushers … with the other being Jonathan Greenard. MICHAEL CLAY Part of the reason why the Eagles were in position to steal this game was because their special teams unit played well. We’d be ripping Clay if his group had a rough day, so, it’s only fair to give the Eagles’ special teams coordinator credit here. JAKE ELLIOTT Including training camp practices (28/31), preseason games (7/7), and the 2026 regular season thus far (13/13), Elliott is 48/51 on all kicks dating back to the offseason. That’s pretty good. Elliott drilled a 56-yarder in the rain and wind today. He has two makes from 50+ yards on two tries this season. He was 5/15 from 50+ in the past two seasons combined. Elliott also did his part to help pin the Rams back deep with a kickoff that hit the landing zone and bounced into the end zone to force LA to take over at their own 20-yard line instead of the standard touchback at the 35-yard line. BRITAIN COVEY Covey set the Eagles up at the plus 17-yard line with his 41-yard punt return. Two plays later, Hurts hit Cooper for Philly’s first touchdown of the game. Covey is logging 13.5 yards per punt return this season. That figure would rank eighth among qualified punt returners from last season. Good stuff. LOSERS TEAM HEALTH The Eagles have a long list of players who are injured coming out of their Week 4 loss. Far from ideal. Especially with an international trip coming up this weekend. SEAN MANNION This offense flat out sucks. Is that entirely Mannion’s fault? No. We all know there are major injury issues. We can allow some room for growing pains. But he is the offensive coordinator and the results were very, very bad. The Eagles have failed to convert their last SEVENTEEN third down attempts. 0/17! They were 0/12 in this game. One year after leading the NFL in three-and-out percentage, the Eagles continue to look pathetically inept. A bunch of stats to back up the eye test: The Eagles have 15 three-and-out drives this season, the most in the NFL. 11 of their 15 three-and-out drives have come in the 2nd half, 3 more than any other team in the NFL. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Steelers could be getting some help in their defensive backfield soon, with head coach Mike McCarthy telling reporters Monday that safety DeShon Elliott is “getting close” to a return off of injured reserve. “DeShon is making progress,” McCarthy said. “Had a chance to watch him work last week, so he’s definitely getting close. title: Steelers Week 4 grades in loss to Browns
summary: After four weeks, the Pittsburgh Steelers find themselves in third place in the AFC North, holding a tiebreaker over the Cincinnati Bengals, who lost on Sunday to the Jacksonville Jaguars. It makes it that much more frustrating that the Steelers were unable to take care of their own business and get to 3-1. Instead, Pittsburgh […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images After four weeks, the Pittsburgh Steelers find themselves in third place in the AFC North, holding a tiebreaker over the Cincinnati Bengals, who lost on Sunday to the Jacksonville Jaguars. It makes it that much more frustrating that the Steelers were unable to take care of their own business and get to 3-1. Instead, Pittsburgh dropped their Week 4 game to Cleveland 27-24 on Thursday. With Week 4 wrapped up, we give our grades for the Steelers. Let’s dive in. Aaron Rodgers Jarrett Bailey: It was a mixed bag for Rodgers. On one hand, he had a great fourth quarter that featured two touchdown passes. On the other hand, he failed to pull the trigger on a pair of throws that would have changed the outcome. DK Metcalf got behind the Browns defense for what would have been an easy score, but Rodgers didn’t see it. Metcalf was also open on the Steelers’ final play in regulation that could have put them in range for a potential game-tying field goal. He also held the ball too long, which made him responsible for more than one of the five sacks he took. Grade: C+ Joey Bray: This is a very tough grade for me. On the one hand, Rodgers brought the team all the way back down 14 in the 4th quarter by making one impressive throw after another. His quarterback sneak on the 2-point conversion attempt late in the contest capped off one of the best quarters of football Rodgers has played in a Steelers uniform. With that being said, it was quite obvious throughout this game that Rodgers’ lack of mobility put the Steelers in tough situations too often. The veteran quarterback was sacked 5 times and took 10 hits. While some of that is on the offensive line, the lack of mobility makes Rodgers an easy target for teams that love to blitz like Cleveland. There is only so much Rodgers can do at his age, as he is simultaneously digging the Steelers out of holes that he puts them in. Grade: C Offensive Line Jarrett Bailey: The offensive line wasn’t perfect. Max Iheanachor made Sam Williams look like Lawrence Taylor, and Rodgers was sacked five times. However, the fault can’t all go on the shoulders of the guys up front. The Steelers’ receivers couldn’t gain any separation, which led to Rodgers having to try and create. When you hold the ball longer all night, naturally more sacks will happen. They could have been better, but could have been worse, as well. Grade: C+ Joey Bray: After an impressive game from the offensive line with Max Iheanachor and Brock Hoffman making their Steelers debuts, it was a bit of a different story in Week 4. As we talked about with Rodgers, I think it is more than fair to say the offensive line is responsible for some of the sacks and quarterback hits that Rodgers endured. However, Rodgers’ immobility does his line absolutely no favors. The run blocking was more than fine, as the Steelers averaged just under five yards per gain. The important thing to keep in mind is that this offensive line is incredibly young and still gelling together. There will be plenty of ups and downs with this unit in the early stages of the season. Grade: C Jaylen Warren Jarrett Bailey: Warren continues to show that the offense should run through him by putting up a second consecutive game of 100+ scrimmage yards. He averaged 5.5 yards per carry and continues to be a strong receiver out of the backfield. More of No. 30 will lead to more wins. Grade: A- Joey Bray: Are you kidding me? Jaylen Warren is having a career year in 2026. With fellow back Rico Dowdle still nursing a toe injury, Warren once again took care of the Steelers’ rushing duties. Coming fresh off a game in which Warren averaged over seven yards per carry, the running back once again proved why he deserves to be the Steelers’ feature back even when Dowdle is fully healthy. Warren used his 17 carries to pick up 93 yards and added 33 yards on three receptions. He should, and will continue to be, the engine of the Steelers offense. Grade: A+ Pass Coverage Jarrett Bailey: If only the Steelers gave a fair contract offer to their good press-man cornerback and didn’t lowball him on guaranteed money. For a group that came into the year very deep, they are all of a sudden very thin, and struggled immensely to slow down the Browns passing game. With Jamel Dean dealing with an ankle injury, they need to bring in someone from the outside. Grade: D- Joey Bray: This secondary desperately needs a bump. I find it hard to be on Daylen Everette like most are right now, given the fact that the play in which Denzel Boston ran by him for a chunk gain downfield was a miscommunication and not all on the rookie corner. Jaylen Ramsey came into the contest playing on a broken wrist on just three days’ rest, and Jamel Dean aggravated an ankle injury that kept him out for most of the contest. All of that said, this is not a strong unit right now, but they are nowhere near healthy. However, this was a rough showing from them. Deshaun Watson was quite efficient, with a 94.0 passer rating, but he was far from perfect. There were often receivers open downfield as Watson extended the play. There is a little bit of hope, as safety DeShon Elliott is eligible to come off of injured reserve as early as next week, which would be a massive boost to a secondary that needs help fast. Grade: D ​Pass Rush Jarrett Bailey: The Steelers had the seventh-worst pressure percentage in Week 4 entering Monday before the Saints and Falcons could be considered. That said, when they did get pressure, they got to Watson quick, ranking seventh in time to pressure. I don’t blame the pass rushers for a largely down night as much as I blame the lack of blitzes. The Steelers only sent five or more rushes on 18.9 percent of snaps, and the Browns got rid of the ball in an average of 2.42 seconds, which was the fifth-fastest rate in the league in Week 4. Grade: C+ Joey Bray: I thought the pass rush got home and pressured Watson quite a bit on Thursday, but Watson’s legs allowed him to escape more often than not. TJ Watt continued his Defensive Player of the Year-caliber start to the season with a sack and a forced fumble in the contest. Jack Sawyer got his hand on a pass that ended up causing an interception. I am becoming just a tad worried about Nick Herbig, who has yet to record a sack this season after signing a massive extension in the offseason. Herbig did make several plays in the run game on Thursday Night, so there is no real reason to panic just yet. Grade: B- Tackling Jarrett Bailey: A big part of waiting to put out our grades was because I wanted to see where the Steelers ranked in terms of miss tackles in Week 4. Entering Sunday night, they missed the most tackles of any team with 14. Inexcusable performance from the defense. Grade: F Joey Bray: According to Pro Football Focus, the Steelers missed 14 tackles in Week 4. Comparatively, the unit missed seven tackles in their Week 3 contest against the Bengals. This was not an isolated issue for one position group, as just about every unit on the defense missed several opportunities to bring Cleveland down at some point in the game. This was an overall poor showing from the defense who is still struggling with basic things like communication and tackling. Grade: F Let us know what you think in the comments . (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks are making more moves at the running back position, and this signing involves a practice squad poach. Jordan Schultz reported on Monday that undrafted rookie Robert Henry Jr, who’s been on the Washington Commanders practice squad all season, is joining the Seahawks active roster. At 5’9 and 196 pounds, Henry is on the smaller side for a running back and he’s not a burner with his 4.52s 40-yard dash, but he’s still a running back and Seattle only has two career RBs on the active roster. It’s reasonable to think that if Henry is on the active roster, Velus Jones Jr would be cut and subsequently re-signed to the practice squad, as he does not have to clear waivers. He’d also get three new elevations by returning to the PS. Seattle also intends to sign Joe Mixon to the practice squad , so with Jadarian Price on injured reserve and Zach Charbonnet not back for Week 5 against the San Francisco 49ers, Seattle seemingly has two other options at its disposal to handle the next couple of weeks.

title: Seahawks fan chat: Falcons vs. Saints rivalry renewed on ‘Monday Night Football’
summary: The Atlanta Falcons and New Orleans Saints wrap up Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season. Outside of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the NFC South actually looks at least entertaining to watch. The Falcons got Michael Penix Jr back and lit up the Green Bay Packers, while the Saints have been in nothing but thrillers […]
full_text: The Atlanta Falcons and New Orleans Saints wrap up Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season. Outside of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the NFC South actually looks at least entertaining to watch. The Falcons got Michael Penix Jr back and lit up the Green Bay Packers, while the Saints have been in nothing but thrillers despite their 1-2 record. There is a special reason why Monday Night Football picked this matchup for this week. It’s 20 years ago that the Saints returned to New Orleans after being displaced for the entirety of the 2005 season due to Hurricane Katrina. Their temporary homes were San Antonio and (predominantly) Baton Rouge. One of their “home” games was against the New York Giants… at Giants Stadium. When the Superdome re-opened in 2006, it was on MNF against the Atlanta Falcons. Steve Gleason blocked Michael Koenen’s punt, and Curtis DeLoatch fell on the ball for one of the more emotional touchdowns in NFL history. THE SAINTS BLOCK THE PUNT!! Steve Gleason came flying in for a perfect block leading to Curtis DeLoatch falling on it in the end zone. The Superdome is as loud as it’s ever been right now. What a moment for the city of New Orleans! https://t.co/BkvdiNtcgx pic.twitter.com/V0tiSO7D1k — 20 Years Ago Sports (@20YearsAgoSport) September 25, 2026 The Saints won 23-3 to improve to 3-0, ultimately making the NFC Championship Game for the first time in franchise history. Here we are 20 years later, and it’s Falcons at Saints again, but thankfully not in the wake of a horrific hurricane. We’re hoping it’s a fun game, plus the winner improves to .500 in a division where it probably won’t take too many wins to be the leader. Chat about it here on Field Gulls starting at 5:15 pm PT on ESPN!

full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - JANUARY 18: Joe Mixon #28 of the Houston Texans carries the ball on a running play during the second half of the AFC Divisional playoff game against the Kansas City Chiefs at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium on January 18, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Help is on the way for a banged up Seattle Seahawks backfield. After Sunday’s report from Jay Glazer that running back Joe Mixon would work out for the Seahawks on Monday — something that was confirmed as a formal tryout on the league’s transaction wire — the other shoe has dropped in the form of a deal between the team and the veteran. NFL reporter Jordan Schultz was first to report the signing, with ESPN’s Adam Schefter providing the information that Mixon would join the team’s practice squad, not 53-man roster. Seattle’s plan is to sign Joe Mixon to its practice squad when he completes his medical exam, which he still is doing, per sources. https://t.co/lUuchpJzN4 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 5, 2026 Mixon, 30, is back in the league after he missed the entire 2025 season with a foot injury that led him to tell former teammates he was done in the NFL. Prior to his year away, the two-time Pro Bowler was a 14-game starter for the Houston Texans in 2024, rushing for 1,016 yards on 4.1 yards per carry, while adding another 309 yards through the air. The long-time Cincinnati Bengal has broken the 1,000-yard mark in five of his eight seasons, with a career-high 1,205 yards coming in 2021. While Mixon will get his start in Seattle as a part of the practice squad, he’ll presumably feature on gameday in short order. Rookie Jadarian Price is on injured reserve with a chest injury, while Zach Charbonnet — whose practice window is open as he looks to come off the PUP list — won’t play in Week 5 . Though Emanuel Wilson’s 81-yard performance on Sunday helped the Seahawks get by with a win while their backfield was in a tough spot, further help is on the horizon in the form of Mixon.
