title: Co-defendant in Terrion Arnold case will testify against Arnold following plea deal
summary: Two months ago, the Seattle Seahawks made the controversial decision to sign cornerback Terrion Arnold, whose Detroit Lions career abruptly ended after he was arrested and charged with numerous felonies, including kidnapping and armed robbery. Arnold is currently on the commissioner’s exempt list, which means he doesn’t count toward Seattle’s 53-man roster, but he otherwise […]
full_text: Two months ago, the Seattle Seahawks made the controversial decision to sign cornerback Terrion Arnold , whose Detroit Lions career abruptly ended after he was arrested and charged with numerous felonies, including kidnapping and armed robbery. Arnold is currently on the commissioner’s exempt list, which means he doesn’t count toward Seattle’s 53-man roster, but he otherwise cannot play or practice with the team until further notice. The latest update to this case doesn’t sound particularly encouraging for Arnold. Boakai Hilton, Arnold’s childhood friend and co-defendant, pleaded guilty in court on Monday to three counts of kidnapping, three counts of robbery with a firearm, conspiracy to commit kidnapping and conspiracy to commit robbery with a firearm. He was sentenced to 10 years in prison, and part of his plea agreement includes testifying against Arnold. Here’s part of the statement from the Hillsborough County (FL) state attorney’s office : Boakai Hilton has pleaded guilty and been sentenced to 10 years in Florida State Prison for his role in the violent robbery and kidnapping case that also involves NFL player Terrion Arnold. This plea requires him to testify truthfully in any future proceedings related to this case. Hilton pleaded guilty to three counts of kidnapping, three counts of robbery with a firearm, conspiracy to commit kidnapping, and conspiracy to commit robbery with a firearm. Investigators say Hilton, Arnold, Lyndell Hudson, Freddie Hughes III, Christion Williams, Arianna Del Valle, and Jasmine Randazzo lured three men to a Tampa apartment, where the victims were robbed at gunpoint, beaten, and held for more than an hour. Arnold is accused of coordinating and directing the plan after believing the victims had stolen more than $200,000 worth of his personal property at an AirBNB rental. Investigators found no evidence linking the victims to that theft. It’s worth noting that Del Valle and Randazzo have also pleaded guilty. Arnold was drafted in the first round by the Lions in 2024 but was waived days after his arrest. When the Seahawks signed Arnold, they pointed to “overwhelmingly positive” feedback they received about his character, including from former Alabama teammate Jalen Milroe and defensive backs coach Karl Scott, who recruited but never coached Arnold at Alabama. It’s TBD on the next major date in Arnold’s case, but in the meantime Arnold isn’t going to be on the field for the Seahawks anywhere in the near future.

title: Snap Reactions: Emanuel Wilson capitalizes on Jadarian Price’s absence
summary: On Sunday afternoon at Lumen Field, the Seattle Seahawks moved to 3-1 on the season by holding on to defeat the Los Angeles Chargers 30-23 after having jumped out to a three-touchdown lead in the third quarter. When the Seahawks had the ball, Emanuel Wilson saw the bulk of the work at running back, playing […]
full_text: Oct 4, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson (23) runs for a touchdown against the Los Angeles Chargers during the first half at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On Sunday afternoon at Lumen Field, the Seattle Seahawks moved to 3-1 on the season by holding on to defeat the Los Angeles Chargers 30-23 after having jumped out to a three-touchdown lead in the third quarter. When the Seahawks had the ball, Emanuel Wilson saw the bulk of the work at running back, playing 60 percent of the offensive snaps, with George Holani at just 37 percent and Velus Jones seeing the field for his first two offensive snaps of the season. Wilson turned those snaps into 21 carries for 81 yards and a touchdown, to go with three receptions for 39 yards and a receiving touchdown. Wilson’s 81 yards marked the fourth time in his career he’s broken the 75 yard rushing mark in a game, including the second time in the past three weeks. At right guard the rotation between Christian Haynes and Beau Stephens continued with yet another week of a roughly 60/40 split. At times Stephens has looked good, and at other times he has looked like a rookie fifth round pick. However, perhaps the most notable stat from the rotation is the fact that of the eight pressures credited to Seattle offensive linemen Sunday, four of them were allowed by Haynes. Whether it was simply a poor matchup, opponents have enough tape to know the weaknesses to exploit when Haynes is in pass blocking or some other reason, whatever the reason for the struggles Sunday, with Anthony Bradford out for at least two more weeks right guard will continue to be a spot to keep an eye on. Lastly, while fans call for more Tory Horton, the coaching staff seems to have other ideas. After missing the season opener, Horton’s snap counts and the percentage of offensive snaps played has decreased in each of the past two weeks: Week 2: 22 snaps, 31.4% of offensive snaps Week 3: 15 snaps, 22.4% of offensive snaps Week 4: 10 snaps, 16.7% of offensive snaps The most likely culprit to point a finger at would likely be the simple fact that even as some receivers are producing more at a younger age, wide receiver remains one of the slowest to develop positions in the NFL due to the complexity of NFL route trees compared to most college systems. Whether that is what is preventing Horton from seeing more snaps or not is something to which fans are almost certain to be paying attention in the coming weeks. On defense, the secondary looked revitalized with the return of Julian Love, who played every snap. Notably, Trevon Diggs saw his first regular season action of the season after earning an elevation from the practice squad, while Nehemiah Pritchett played less than he had in any game so far this season. In spite of that limited playing time against the Chargers, with just five more snaps over the remaining 13 regular season games Pritchett will set a career high. And, as always, special teams continues to belong to Brady Russell, as he led the Seahawks with 30 special teams snaps played. Interestingly, though, former wide receiver turned defensive end turned linebacker Connor O’Toole finished right behind Russell with 29 special teams snaps. From there Mike Morris, A.J. Finley, Patrick O’Connell and Tyrice Knight all played 24 special teams snaps, with Julian Neal right behind them with 23. And now it’s on to Week 5 and an opportunity to take over first place, via tiebreaker, in the NFC West.
author: John Gilbert

title: Seahawks won’t have Zach Charbonnet, Leonard Williams a maybe versus 49ers
summary: Sunday the Seattle Seahawks defeated the Los Angeles Chargers 30-23 at Lumen Field to keep pace with the San Francisco 49ers, who sit alone atop the NFC West at 4-0. And now comes Week 5 and a matchup against those undefeated 49ers, which means an opportunity for Seattle to take over first place in the […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 04: Leonard Williams #99 of the Seattle Seahawks receives medical attention against the Los Angeles Chargers during the fourth quarter at Lumen Field on October 04, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sunday the Seattle Seahawks defeated the Los Angeles Chargers 30-23 at Lumen Field to keep pace with the San Francisco 49ers, who sit alone atop the NFC West at 4-0. And now comes Week 5 and a matchup against those undefeated 49ers, which means an opportunity for Seattle to take over first place in the division by knocking the Niners out of the top spot. However, when the teams face off Sunday, the Seahawks will once again be without 2026 first round pick Jadarian Price, who is on injured reserve for at least another three weeks. That brings the discussion to 2023 second round pick Zach Charbonnet and a potential return from injured reserve, but any hopes for that were shot down by head coach Mike Macdonald Monday. Mike Macdonald injury updates on @SeattleSports "Zach Charbonnet will get team reps this week, and that’s exciting. He will not play this week." Leonard Williams: “ It’s an ankle; we are optimistic, and we will see this week.” @CascadiasportsN @Seahawks — MazvitaMaraire (@MazvitaMaraire) October 5, 2026 Thus, barring the addition of a veteran free agent, such as Joe Mixon, it appears as though Seattle fans have another week of the former undrafted duo of Emanuel Wilson and George Holani, with Velus Jones seeing situational spot snaps. However, what could be even more important news on the injury front is the availability of All-Pro defensive lineman Leonard Williams. Williams suffered an ankle injury in the second half against Los Angeles and Macdonald was noncommital regarding Williams’ availability for the showdown against San Francisco. Williams is a huge piece of the Seattle defense, and while Macdonald says he is optimistic, Macdonald is a dad, and “we will see” more often than not tends to be dad speak for “no.” Should Williams be unable to play against San Francisco it would be a big blow for a defense that has given up far more points than they would prefer the past couple of weeks to opponents of a far lower caliber than the 49ers offense the Seahawks defense will face in Week 5. And now it’s on to the Wednesday injury report.

title: Seahawks-Chargers post-game recap: NFL at last completes decades-long transition to flag football
summary: In the last 120 minutes of their young season, we’ve seen the worst the 2026 Seattle Seahawks have to offer. The three turnovers in Washington that sank an offensive renaissance. Then, early defensive domination was undone by untimely mistakes and lack of discipline back at home. Sloppiness in all three phases on critical downs gifted […]
full_text: Oct 4, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh greets Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike MacDonald after the game at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In the last 120 minutes of their young season, we’ve seen the worst the 2026 Seattle Seahawks have to offer. The three turnovers in Washington that sank an offensive renaissance. Then, early defensive domination was undone by untimely mistakes and lack of discipline back at home. Sloppiness in all three phases on critical downs gifted points to opponents in close games, repeatedly. In their last 120 minutes, more things went wrong than a fan can count, even a Sea-soned Hawks fan, and still Seattle earned a split. Depending on your point of view, that’s either a reason to rejoice or to worry. Ah, who am I kidding — been doing a bit of both myself and I’ll guess you have too. It’s reassuring to be able to win even playing under your talent level. These aren’t the Dolphins or Cardinals, who have basically room for error if they want to post the W. Speaking of inferior teams, whooping the winless Los Angeles Chargers 30-13 as the fourth quarter begins is usually the recipe for a final quarter of self-congratulations, toasts in the crowd, and everyone in Seahawks Nation looking ahead to a Week 5 clash with the 49ers. Instead, one near-meltdown later, on the heels of stubbing your toe the week prior, the whole enterprise suddenly feels shaky. Seattle converted exactly one third down on the ground, did not sustain drives after building a three-score lead, and did not defend well enough to slam the door well before the final minute, but at least they did that. Uchenna Nwosu provided the capper on a big revenge game (those are real): Stay for the last split second though — John Fraley (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-10-04T23:46:31.168Z LA was in position to win because of Justin Herbert’s excellent second half, implausible toughness, and a veritable plague of personal fouls — seven in total for Seattle. One early soft call on Brady Russell stomped on a drive before it had a chance to bloom. Connor O’Toole drew one for a borderline helmet-to-helmet when the punt returner unwisely declined to make a fair catch. Nick Emmanwori’s inexplicable headbutt with five seconds before half left stopped the clock and put the Chargers in comfortable field goal range. Devon Witherspoon tackled a dude four steps out of bounds, Emmanwori grabbed a facemask in the open field, DeMarcus Lawrence hit Herbert low and Derick Hall hit him late on the same drive. And that’s not counting the offsetting personal fouls somewhere in that first quarter, well before the game descended into a parody of itself. The 150 yards in penalties were a new franchise record. (More than any Raiders game back in the AFC West days, even.) Fortunately, the Chargers arrived with an entire case of beers, and at the contest’s most critical moments, they’d casually pull one out and ask the Seahawks to hold it. When Los Angeles was perfectly poised to conduct a proper game-winning drive with all three timeouts, Justin Eboigbe landed on Sam Darnold after his slide, freshening the downs for Seattle and forcing longtime Seahawks sufferer Jim Harbaugh to burn them after all. There’s a sequence in the third quarter that captures the essence of this flagfest better than any. Do note the expressions on Jason Myers’ and Michael Dickson’s faces — “What are we even doing, guys.” You probably saw these at your watch party, in your row at the stadium, or on your own face at some point Sunday afternoon. Putting this whole Seahawks-Chargers sequence on tape because it's emblematic of the day — John Fraley (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-10-05T00:11:57.867Z You can watch the video, but just in case you don’t: Greg Zabel isn’t on the field until the play clock hits 10, so he hurries to his assignment. The kick is snapped at zeroes, Myers pushes it right, giving LA excellent field position EXCEPT NO, there’s a late leverage call against the defense, first down Seattle instead. (The drive would end soon thereafter in three points, which seemed superfluous at the time but ended up pretty dang important.) Anyway. It’s fun to complain about a win, sure beats the alternative. Thirty penalties and countless bullet wounds in everybody’s feet later, the Seahawks had emerged with their third victory of the year. Truly, ‘bout the only surprise is their victory formation went off without a flag. The recap will omit most of the fouls, if possible. Before we get there! It would be criminal to not mention Emanuel Wilson’s big day. Not by choice entirely, Mike Macdonald and Brian Fleury traded their explosive but risky running attack for a more reliable, albeit boring dose of Wilson and George Holani. It frickin’ worked. (I will never stop quoting Pete Carroll no matter how many Super Bowls [four] Macdonald wins here.) Wilson rewarded his coaches, teammates and himself with a tough, tough 21-81-1 line and that first-quarter touchdown reception that sent the Chargers chasing the hosts for the rest of the afternoon. Factor in 51 more yards from Rashid Shaheed and Holani and you have the makings of a respectable running game. Which you’ll need. Q1: Seahawks 7, Chargers 3 Predator: The officiating crew Prey: Anyone watching How: We didn’t know it yet, but maybe we should’ve. Like when the officials found offsetting personal fouls that instant replay couldn’t locate. That should’ve alerted viewers. Then, Russell was dinged 15 for this “offense”: First quarter recap: this is a 15 yard penalty — John Fraley (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-10-04T21:19:15.564Z Later, O’Toole’s personal came for leading with the helmet but you can see him pull up. Maybe it’s a flag but that exact hit is performed on every drive and Derius Davis never put his hand up. I don’t know what a crew can do when a team like the Seahawks repeatedly toes the line with over-aggressiveness some might call dirty. But it was hard to watch the parade of yellow. Action: In the most mulligan-y of starts conceivable, Herbert and Darnold traded interceptions on successive plays. What to say about that, except you’d like to win the turnover battle from there on out, and the Seahawks did. The Chargers offense settled in first though, with two rapid-fire first downs, one semi-explosive pass play and one questionable offsides against Nwosu to creep into field goal range. An eight-play, 30-yard drive off the pick resulted in three points. And when Seattle’s real opening possession ended in an awkward intentional grounding, the hangover from that Commander got real rear view mirror-like: objects are closer than they appear. No matter, O’Toole reached into his special toolebox and pulled out a timely fumble recovery. First O'Toole in the right place at the right time since Lawrence of Arabia — John Fraley (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-10-04T20:48:08.068Z The game was barely five minutes old, and each possession was a whiplash. Add Weeks 3 and 4 together and a fan could be forgiven for believing they were watching the 2010s Chaoshawks again. (Recite the Kevin Clark tweet from memory, if you know what I mean.) Yet the pattern of this particular meeting had already manifested: the Chargers were happy to beat themselves, the Seahawks happy to oblige. Off the giveaway, it took exactly one play for Wilson to tilt the field. Little screen to the right, and with ball in hand he turned and went north-south with more determination than a Blackpoll warbler (safe to Google it, go ahead). Seattle ended up six points richer. The next seven possessions ended in punts. Emmanwori and Lawrence helped kill drives with tackles for loss, and as the second quarter took off, so did the Seahawks pass rush. Q2: Seahawks 20, Chargers 6 Predator: Byron Murphy Prey: Interior linemen, assuming they existed at all How: Living in the backfield. In the first clip,…

full_text: The San Francisco 49ers may be one of the few undefeated teams around the league, but as they head north to face the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, they’ll do so as underdogs. According to the current line at FanDuel Sportsbook , the Seahawks are a 3-point favorite (-110), and -164 on the moneyline, with the 49ers coming back at +138. Despite another injury plagued campaign already well underway in the Bay, San Francisco has put together a pair of high-quality wins, famously blowing away the L.A. Rams in Australia in Week 1 and seeing off the Denver Broncos at home on Sunday. The resilient 49ers will provide a great test for a Seahawks team who, despite a 3-1 mark, are yet to face a quality opponent. That’s going to change in rapid fashion, however, with the NFC West clash kicking off a four-week stretch in which Seattle will face the Niners, Broncos, Chiefs (one of the other remaining undefeated teams), and Bears. With Brock Purdy and San Francisco’s offense in good form, and the Seahawks’ questions in the secondary, it’s easy to see the divisional foes being dragged into a back-and-forth affair, with the total of 47.5 looming. title: Seahawks Droppings: Uchenna Nwosu mercifully ends repulsive game vs old team
summary: A win is a – hold on, there’s a flag. As I was saying, you can’t complain – wait, did I just see yellow fly again?  Let me try this again, beggars – oh for the love of God, there’s another one?!? That’s what the entire game felt like today…a sloppy, disjointed mess. It was […]
full_text: A win is a – hold on, there’s a flag. As I was saying, you can’t complain – wait, did I just see yellow fly again? Let me try this again, beggars – oh for the love of God, there’s another one?!? That’s what the entire game felt like today…a sloppy, disjointed mess. It was like preseason with the amount of stupid penalties committed by the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Chargers as each team tried to give the game away. However, the Seahawks were just a little smarter about being less dumb, barely holding on to a 30-23 win that had no right being as close as it was. Los Angeles came in with an 0-3 record, and played like it for the first three quarters. The Seahawks took advantage of turnovers, racing out to a 21-point lead in the third quarter. That should’ve been a comfortable cushion with the Dark Side defense, but it wasn’t. Seattle continued to commit asinine penalties and allow long third and fourth down conversions. Los Angeles had the ball with over 1:30 left only down seven points. Luckily, former Charger Uchenna Nwosu strip-sacked Justin Herbert with Derick Hall recovering the ball to preserve the win. It was pretty ugly. Seahawks Droppings The refs were flag happy, but I thought all of the calls were legit. That means that the Seahawks have a penalty – and by extension – a discipline problem right now. Many of those penalties were personal fouls. Many of those extended drives. You just can’t do that against good teams and win. Seattle racked up 14 penalties for 150 yards which is inexcusable. This is a pattern that has been relatively consistent this season going back to preseason. It will need to turn around or Seattle will lose games because of it. Jason Myers missed an extra point, got bailed out by a penalty after missing a long FG, and had another kickoff out of bounds penalty . I’m trying not to get too concerned, and give him the benefit of the doubt, but that’s becoming more difficult each week. The defense wasn’t up to its standard today in the second half. That late 4th and 7 conversion was the stuff of nightmares. Yes, they forced four turnovers…yet to do that and only win by seven points isn’t ideal. Part of the reason for the defense running out of gas was the offense taking their foot off of it in the fourth quarter . Seattle had 30 points prior to the final frame, adding none in the final 15 minutes. Even an extra field goal or long drive would’ve made this game much more comfortable. Seattle had the ball twice in the last 5 minutes and couldn’t close out the game. Emanuel Wilson was quite good as the feature back today with over 100 total yards and 2 TDs . He always seems to finish forward and has shown decent hands out of the backfield. Seattle will need him to hold down the fort until Zach Charbonnet can play. Sam Darnold had only 13 completions, and was under pressure quite a bit . He made a few plays with his legs which was nice to see coming off of his injury. The slant throw to Tory Horton was a thing of beauty. His boneheaded INT on the first offensive play was not. Jaxon Smith-Njigba didn’t get to the 100-yard mark for the first time in 2026, yet was still a factor in the game with a huge early third-and-long conversion . He led the team with 76 yards, followed by Emanuel Wilson’s 39 yards. Rashid Shaheed was more active today, especially out of the backfield where he contributed 33 yards a TD. Shaheed also fumbled again on a kickoff, but got the ball back. I don’t like to see that. What I would like to see, however, is Tory Horton getting more run. All he does is seemingly catch TDs, with another one today. I feel like he could be a much bigger weapon with all the attention that JSN, Shaheed, and Cooper Kupp get. Maybe Horton will be a bigger part as the season rolls on. Ernest Jones IV had a pretty awesome game with 12 tackles, 1 TFL, 1 Sack, and 1 INT . Nick Emmanwori also had a nifty sack…and a dumb penalty that helped the Chargers have an even more makeable FG . I thought DeMarcus Lawrence had a much bigger impact than his 3 tackles and 2 TFL stat line suggests. I’m not too mad at him for his low hit on Herbert since he was already going down to the ground and there wasn’t much he could do about it. Plenty of players took turns being boneheads on defense. Seattle has a hell of a lot to shore up prior to playing the San Francisco 49ers next week. You better believe that the undefeated Niners will be a much bigger test than anyone the Seahawks have faced thus far in 2026. Hopefully Leonard Williams’ ankle injury isn’t serious, as the team will need him in a big way. Coming off of a terrible loss last week, it would’ve been nice to see the Seahawks make a statement and close the Chargers out in the fourth quarter. Oh well, it could’ve been – oh get the f— out of here with the flags, the game is over!!

Rashid Shaheed got involved in the offense finally, but not through the air. The Dark Side gave up some points, but closed it out in the end. Not perfect. Oh, well. title: 49ers News: We’re on to Seattle
summary: I was watching some of the Seattle-Washington game today, trying to get a sense of how the Commanders managed to beat the defending champs.  One factor was Sonny Styles. He dominated from the linebacker position, making game-changing plays in pass coverage. You could tell he played high-level basketball, this wasn’t just “good coverage for a […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - DECEMBER 15: Fred Warner #54 of the San Francisco 49ers makes a tackle during the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on December 15, 2022 in Seattle, Washington. The 49ers defeated the Seahawks 21-13. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images I was watching some of the Seattle-Washington game today, trying to get a sense of how the Commanders managed to beat the defending champs. One factor was Sonny Styles. He dominated from the linebacker position, making game-changing plays in pass coverage. You could tell he played high-level basketball, this wasn’t just “good coverage for a linebacker”. He intercepted JSN, got a PBU against Jadarian Price, and forced a fumble. If the 49ers beat the Seahawks this week, Fred Warner will need to play a major role. He’s one of the few players in the NFL that could cover JSN just as well as any running back or tight end. That factor feels repeatable. Another factor was that Seattle was down several defensive backs against Washington, against a healthy Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs. Julian Love came back last week and Ty Okada was borderline, so the 49ers will face a healthier Seattle secondary with a more injured receiving corps. That factor feels a bit less repeatable. The real x-factor, in my opinion, will be the Seattle run offense against the 49ers run defense. The 49ers, to their credit, seemed to tighten things up against Denver. Fans should be locked in on any Mykel Williams news, he could matter a lot. Sunday can’t come any sooner! 49ers’ game review: How Brock Purdy is making his offensive line look great (paywall) “But it wasn’t just his scrambles. On Purdy’s 1-yard touchdown pass to Deebo Samuel in the third quarter, Colby, at left guard, was knocked backward by defensive tackle Eyioma Uwazurike, forcing Purdy to drift left to buy extra time before making his flip to Samuel. Three plays before the touchdown, the Broncos quickly collapsed the pocket and Purdy didn’t hesitate to give up on a passing play, sprinting 11 yards around left end on 2nd-and-11 from Denver’s 18-yard line. In the fourth quarter, Purdy was chased to the left sideline by All-Pro defensive end Zach Allen. Just before he ran out of real estate, Purdy slammed on the brakes, backpedaled to get distance from the 6-foot-5 Allen and fired a 16-yard completion off his back foot to fullback Kyle Juszczyk. The 49ers entered Sunday as one of four teams in the Super Bowl era to start a season 3-0 without allowing a sack. The group includes Manning and the 2005 Colts, along with the 1984 Dolphins and Dan Marino, whose lightning-quick release explains how he once went an NFL-record 19 straight games without being sacked. The point: Great QBs can help make their offensive linemen look statistically great.” 49ers’ George Kittle is not only back to full speed. He looks like he did in 2018 (paywall) “ Kittle said he felt off during the Week 1 game in Australia, his first game since tearing his Achilles in January. From that point on, however, he’s felt like the Kittle of old. “I trained, and in July I was hitting 20 miles an hour,” he said. “I knew that if I could just do it consistently — I think the biggest part was, like, the acceleration, getting that back. From Week 2 on, I had so much confidence in it and haven’t looked back since.” 49ers minutia minute: Deebo Samuel’s YAC is back — just ask Talanoa Hufanga (paywall) “If Kittle was going nearly 20 mph, how fast was left guard Colby moving? His GPS readout registered 18.5 mph on the play, which checks out considering he appeared to be keeping pace with Kittle and his pursuer, Hufanga, as they raced downfield.” 49ers vs. Broncos PFF grades: Best and worst from the game, plus snap counts “Despite playing through a rib injury, wide receiver Mike Evans earned the game’s highest overall grade with an 88.9 offensive grade.” 49ers grades: Raheem Morris colt-pletely shuts down Bo Nix and the Broncos “Jacob Cowing’s reverse did not go as planned. He is still running too many Senior Bowl routes that may work in practice, but it’s taking too long to get open within the offense’s structure and timing. Brandin Cooks found out that the 49ers motions aren’t as easy as they look. He was flagged for an illegal shift, and also had a target go through his hands. On that same play, Cooks drifted on his route. Jordan Watkins regressed as a blocker. He also strictly ran “clear out” routes. On one play, Watkins didn’t hustle to dig out safety Talanoa Hufanga, and Hufanga made a play at the line of scrimmage. That explains why Watkins only ran nine routes. ….This was the best Romello Height has looked this season. As you can see from those clips, Keion White flashed quite a bit, too. I thought the defensive line was even better on the rewatch. Denver couldn’t accomplish anything on the ground. J.K. Dobbins had a 27.3% success rate. R.J. Harvey had a 28.6% success rate. Naquan Jones and Sebastian Valdez have been pleasant surprises. Gracen Halton and Osa Odighzuwa have been better than expected against the run, and the latter two continue to generate pressure. Matt Judon only played 14 snaps. Khalid Kareem was in for 19 snaps. In a dream world, that’s Mykel Williams’ workload next week. But the fact that the Niners didn’t get pushed against the run and won when Denver dropped back should be encouraging since they were without Nick Bosa.”

full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan provided injury updates on Monday afternoon. He confirmed Kyle Juszczyk has a hyperextended knee . Juice is expected to miss 2-3 weeks. Shanahan said Luke Farrell and Brayden Willis will take over Juszczyk’s role. “They’re all pretty interchangeable, but it’ll definitely get Brayden some more ops.” Safety Marques Sigle has a high ankle sprain. He’ll miss some time. How much remains to be seen. Sigle is expected to miss multiple weeks. Malik Mustapha will slide into Sigle’s role. Cornerback Upton Stout will be day-to-day with an AC issue in his shoulder. If Stout can’t play, Shanahan said Ephesians Prysock is a candidate to play for Stout. That’s interesting. On Sunday, Deommodore Lenoir played nickel, with Jack Jones moving to the outside. Staying with cornerbacks, Nate Hobbs is “getting close” and could return to practice soon, depending on where he is in rehab. Mykel Williams will participate in team drills this week. The 49ers hope to activate him Sunday against Seattle, pending a good week of practice. The 49ers are not anticipating Nick Bosa or James Thompson Jr. to play against the Seahawks. Wide receiver Christian Kirk is still on track to return to practice in Week 6, as this week isn’t an option. Based on how the wideouts have performed to date, outside of Mike Evans, Kirk will be relied on in the passing game. Speaking of Evans, he had no setbacks on Sunday after playing through a rib injury.

title: 49ers grades: Raheem Morris colt-pletely shuts down Bo Nix and the Broncos
summary: The San Francisco 49ers beat the Denver Broncos by double digits at home. After a slow start, the offense finished the game with three consecutive touchdown drives. But the defense kept the Broncos in their stall all game. They responded well after a shaky fourth quarter in Week 3. Here are my positional grades for […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers beat the Denver Broncos by double digits at home. After a slow start, the offense finished the game with three consecutive touchdown drives. But the defense kept the Broncos in their stall all game. They responded well after a shaky fourth quarter in Week 3. Here are my positional grades for the 49ers’ Week 4 report card. Quarterback: B QB Performances, Week 4 (pre-MNF) 1. Drake Maye 91.0 Total QBR 2. Bryce Young 85.4 3. Dak Prescott 85.3 4. Tyson Bagent 75.1 5. Kirk Cousins 72.7 pic.twitter.com/SErnq4kF4o — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) October 5, 2026 To give you an idea of where Purdy ranked among his peers in Week 4. Hat tip to the Broncos for making things tough on the passing game early on. It was difficult to tell whether they had the 49ers stumped, if the Niners were the ones making mistakes, or a combination of both. Purdy was hovering around a 50% completion percentage before finishing the game 9-of-10. He didn’t make any of the “wow” plays that we’ve seen so far this season, but it never felt like Purdy needed to. This never felt like a Purdy game. He didn’t lose or win the game. He scrambled for a first down, ran out of a couple of sacks, and used his legs to find Kyle Juszczyk for a much-needed first down. But Purdy was also on target on only 70% of his throws, which was 17th for the week. Running backs: B+ Christian McCaffrey made Talanoa Hufanga miss on his first carry. Christian McCaffrey made Talanoa Hufanga miss on his first carry. He had a 10-yard gain on 3rd and 1 in the second quarter, where 90% of running backs gain one yard. McCaffrey was stuffed four times, but those came when the Broncos had the perfect run blitz on, or in short-yardage/goal-line situations where Zach Allen did Zach Allen things. McCaffrey finished with a pair of missed tackles and only a 26% success rate, but my eyeballs tell me he ran well. Next Gen Stats has McCaffrey for +7 in rushing yards over expected in Week 4. I feel like that number is low. Kaelon Black only had six carries. He bounced a run when he shouldn’t have on third-and-short. Black did not pick up the first down. Black looked indecisive on half his carries. It wouldn’t be surprising to see Deebo Samuel see an uptick in carries. Deebo’s first carry was a 22-yard counter where he ran through Hufanga’s tackle attempt. He took a reverse for 20 yards after Hufanga and cornerback Riley Moss stopped Samuel for a gain of three-ish. The 49ers trust Kyle Juszczyk to block defensive ends and linebackers. They’ll miss that level of trust, even if it’s only for two games. Juszczyk made himself available on his second reception after sprinting across the field. Kyle Juszczyk is one of those guys that you can't replace. The 49ers ask him to do everything. The trust level is through the roof. Last week they had him covering punts. Watch Juszczyk's (bottom of the screen) effort on this scramble drill vs. everybody else. pic.twitter.com/Fy5KsSk4Ea — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) October 5, 2026 That type of effort is not something you can replace. Wide receivers: C We will never speak ill of Mike Evans for gutting it out. He had no business being on the field. Yet, Evans still produced like a typical WR1. As for the rest of the wide receiver room, they have work to do. Let the record show this doesn’t include Deebo, who was more of a running back in this game. Jacob Cowing’s reverse did not go as planned. He is still running too many Senior Bowl routes that may work in practice, but it’s taking too long to get open within the offense’s structure and timing. Brandin Cooks found out that the 49ers motions aren’t as easy as they look. He was flagged for an illegal shift, and also had a target go through his hands. On that same play, Cooks drifted on his route. Jordan Watkins regressed as a blocker. He also strictly ran “clear out” routes. On one play, Watkins didn’t hustle to dig out safety Talanoa Hufanga, and Hufanga made a play at the line of scrimmage. That explains why Watkins only ran nine routes. The passing game revolves around Evans, and for good reason. Demarcus Robinson is missed over the middle, while De’Zhaun Stribling’s blocking could come in handy for the running backs. Tight ends: B- Before George Kittle took a screen to the house, the tight ends were unspectacular. Denver put Patrick Surtain on Kittle to begin the game, which is the ultimate sign of respect. Kittle’s targets were largely underneath, save for a seam pass against Surtain. Kittle and Luke Farrell only had one pass-blocking snap against Denver. They combined to miss three blocks when the 49ers ran it. Outside of the screen, there were a lot of stalemates where most of the plays didn’t result in a positive or a negative. They did their jobs. I will say it never gets old watching Kittle manhandle a defensive lineman. That’s what he did on his lone pass-blocking rep. It’s a luxury for the 49ers. Offensive line: B Kyle Shanahan may never spend another dime on a left guard if the 49ers continue to get this kind of production from Connor Colby. To give you an idea of Colby’s athletic level, he reached 18.54 miles per hour while trying to chase down Kittle. Colby allowed a team-high three pressures and had two players he’d want back against the run. But that ignores the other plays where Colby either held his own or, like on one McCaffrey run, drove his man 11 yards downfield. McCaffrey ran into a stacked box 53% of the time. Denver went out of its way to plug gaps. Hufanga made several plays. Jake Brendel had three negative plays against the run out of 31. Colton McKivitz, Colby, and Dominick Puni had two, while Trent Williams had one. It’s a preventative position, and each player was just as effective in pass protection. Purdy’s average time to throw was 2.86 seconds, and Denver’s average time to a pressure was 2.61 seconds. Those are great marks for the offensive line. Zach Allen was a nightmare, as expected. But Nik Bonitto was held in check, and the Broncos didn’t get many, if any, clean wins up front. Defensive line: B+ When the opposing quarterback isn’t looking beyond ten yards, sacks are hard to come by. Denver came into the season boasting one of the NFL’s best offensive lines. This was easily the toughest test to date for the 49ers. This was the best Romello Height has looked this season. Best game to date for Romello Height. He finished with the 6th-highest pass rush win % among all EDGE rushers with at least 20 PR snaps in Week 4. This is why the 49ers drafted him. FWIW, Keion White was 13th. They were winning. The ball was just coming out hot. pic.twitter.com/Ny2SlSvlCI — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) October 5, 2026 As you can see from those clips, Keion White flashed quite a bit, too. I thought the defensive line was even better on the rewatch. Denver couldn’t accomplish anything on the ground. J.K. Dobbins had a 27.3% success rate. R.J. Harvey had a 28.6% success rate. Naquan Jones and Sebastian Valdez have been pleasant surprises. Gracen Halton and Osa Odighzuwa have been better than expected against the run, and the latter two continue to generate pressure. Matt Judon only played 14 snaps. Khalid Kareem was in for 19 snaps. In a dream world, that’s Mykel Williams’ workload next week. But the fact that the Niners didn’t get pushed against the run and won when Denver dropped back should be encouraging since they were without Nick Bosa. Linebackers: A- Jaden Dugger only saw the field for 15 snaps. Garret Wallow continues to rotate in occasionally in obvious passing situations for Dre Greenlaw. But Raheem Morris wasn’t going to leave Greenlaw on the sideline for long. Not against the Broncos. Greenlaw has to be exhausted the day after the game. He had 12 tackles, but he was involved in so many more plays that freed up his teammates. Greenlaw hasn’t impacted a game like this since he returned against the Rams late in the season a couple of years ago. Greenlaw…

title: Dre Greenlaw and Deebo Samuel used same motivation to help 49ers past Broncos
summary: The 49ers knew what to expect from their Week 4 matchup with the Denver Broncos, and it played out exactly as they anticipated. San Francisco’s 24-14 win over Denver was a rock fight. An ultra-physical battle of wills in which the 49er offense had to be very patient in grinding down the Broncos’ vaunted defense, […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 04: Deebo Samuel Sr. #19 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates after scoring a touchdown in the third quarter against the Denver Broncos at Levi's Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 49ers knew what to expect from their Week 4 matchup with the Denver Broncos, and it played out exactly as they anticipated. San Francisco’s 24-14 win over Denver was a rock fight. An ultra-physical battle of wills in which the 49er offense had to be very patient in grinding down the Broncos’ vaunted defense, and which turned on a key special teams play from Siran Neal in the third quarter. They were able to pull out win in no small part thanks two players whose physicality was missing from the roster last season after they each made the decision to explore pastures new, only to find their way back to the 49ers this year. Dre Greenlaw and Deebo Samuel each opted to leave the 49ers in 2025. Greenlaw signed with the Broncos as a free agent, while Samuel requested a trade and was dealt to the Washington Commanders. Neither move worked out, and the 49ers made the decision to reunite with both players on one-year deals. Doing so is looking like an increasingly astute call by San Francisco, with their value to the team laid bare as they both produced key performances brought on by the same motivating factor. Greenlaw successfully channels extra emotion For Greenlaw, the motivation was obvious. The Broncos cut him in March, one year into a three-year deal, seemingly put off by an injury-affected 2025 season for the linebacker who infamously tore his Achilles running onto the field in the second quarter of the 49ers’ Super Bowl 58 defeat to the Chiefs. This was a revenge game for Greenlaw, and he made sure to make his presence felt. Greenlaw was everywhere against his former team, making 12 tackles, forcing a fumble and recording three pressures, all while regularly talking trash to Broncos head coach Sean Payton, whom he had to held back from confronting at the end of the game. Being deemed expendable by the Broncos lit a fire under a player who needs excuse to play with aggression, though the 49ers were happy he was able to keep it in check enough to avoid any costly unsportsmanlike penalties. Said head coach Kyle Shanahan of Greenlaw: “We knew he’d be excited going into this game. Dre’s excited going into every game, but this one meant a little more to him. I was a little nervous there in the first half. We told him, ‘You can get close, but don’t be so excited you give them an explosive with 15.’ And I really thought someone was going to get one in the second half of one of the teams, just challenged our team to make sure it wasn’t us. I don’t think anyone ended up getting one, but Dre held his emotions good enough today and led the team in tackles and had an unbelievable game. He’s had an unbelievable season so far and we’re so happy to have him back at home.” Fellow linebacker Fred Warner added: “There was definitely something a little extra for him this week. He got banged up last game. Everybody was asking him, ‘Hey, are you going to be able to make it?’ And he said, ‘I wouldn’t miss this one.’ He had extra emotion going into this game. I told him just to use it wisely, which he did. I was proud of him and he played a heck of a game. He’s played great all year. He’ll continue to play great for us. I’m glad he’s on our side now.” Greenlaw heeded those words, his display was full of emotion and energy, channeled in the right way, and it provided the 49er defense with something it arguably lacked last season when he was in Denver and Warner missed most of the season to an ankle injury. Pressed to elaborate on his feelings about Greenlaw, Shanahan replied: “I think people know, but like if I had to wear a jersey, I’d probably wear his. Just the way he plays, what he’s done for us over these years, going back to his rookie year and getting us the number one seed in Seattle with the play he made on the goal line. Just the way he inspires people because the way he plays. I think he’s an intimidation factor for the other side of the ball because of the way he plays, and it’s hard for us not to be as aggressive as possible with how he is out there. So, we missed him for the year, but it was good to, as we feel, get a family member back.” That intimidation factor was clear for all to see on Sunday and, in Samuel, the 49ers had a playmaker providing it on the other side of the ball. Samuel produces vintage display Greenlaw was given additional fire from the emotion of being doubted by one franchise. For Samuel, his impressive start to the season — which has seen him score three receiving touchdowns already — looks to have stemmed from a desire to dispel the notion that he had lost a step. After an indifferent 2024 with the 49ers, Samuel looked a long way from his devastating best during his sojourn with the Commanders, and San Francisco fans would have been forgiven for being somewhat skeptical about the idea of a second spell with the Niners. But his signing on a one-year, $7 million deal already looks like one of the best moves of the offseason, and left tackle Trent Williams believes the success Samuel has enjoyed through four games is a product of the wideout’s abilities being questioned. “I think knowing him as well as I do, this offseason was probably the first time in his career that he was doubted,” Williams said. “He’s always been supremely talented, always been a playmaker, and this league, it turns on you quick. I think him having to feel that doubt for the first time, I think it lit a fire in him.” Deebo breaking tackles and picking up 20 yards 😤 DENvsSF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SiAgd5A8eB — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 The 49ers are reaping the benefits of Samuel’s desire to prove the skeptics wrong. There is an evident explosiveness to his play and, against the Broncos, his trademark bruising style of running with the ball in his hands was crucial to the Niners wearing Denver down. Samuel’s most tangible contribution to the win was, of course, his touchdown reception in the third quarter that gave the 49ers a lead they did not relinquish. But he also had a 22-yard run in the first quarter, a 20-yard rush in the second on a drive that led to a game-tying field goal, and an eight-yard reception that set up third-and-short on a scoring drive that ended in a Christian McCaffrey touchdown. In doing so, Samuel displayed the tackle-breaking ability that has underpinned his success in the NFL, leading to significant praise from Shanahan after the game. Kyle Shanahan is paying homage to Bill Walsh Shift & Motion to a Split Back Pro Set to run Counter Solid with Deebo Samuel👌 pic.twitter.com/oOaQt8GZGo — Coach Dan Casey (@CoachDanCasey) October 4, 2026 “I thought Deebo was huge today,” Shanahan said. “Those two runs in the first half that he had, I don’t think many people get the amount of yards that he got on that. I think both of them, I think they were about eight yards, but he does something amazing to get over 20 on both of them. “He was really big at the end on a couple. They’re all less than 10-yard catches, but they were big catches that kept us ahead of the sticks. Then Brock finding him to get in the end zone was huge too.” In bringing back Greenlaw and Samuel, the 49ers took calculated, low-risk bets on players they developed and whom they trust. Four games into the season, both bets are paying significant dividends, with Sunday’s hard-fought victory perhaps the best illustration yet of their worth to this team. Greenlaw and Samuel have had very similar journeys in recent times. On Sunday, they both thrived amid the same urge to silence those who doubted what they had left in tank. Now, back with the team that never lost faith in them, their shared desire has the chance to help make their reunion season with the 49ers a very…

full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that the San Francisco 49ers will be without Kyle Juszczyk for a ‘couple of weeks’ due to a hyperextended knee. Those were the initial tests. Juszczyk will undergo an MRI on Monday to confirm whether those initial tests were accurate. Juszczyk has played a pivotal role for the 49ers this season. They ask him to do everything . He caught a slant route from Brock Purdy that led to a first down, and the other reception also moved the chains for the offense. But it’s been the blocking and usage on dash motion that have helped the running game take off this season. Juszczyk is a big reason why. In Week 3, the 49ers had Juszczyk covering punts. If the team is short on depth in one area, Juszczyk is probably the backup. Short on wide receivers and with Jake Tonges going down, Juszczyk has lined up everywhere on offense. Here’s a look at his snap alignment through four weeks: Tight end – 44 Slot/stack WR – 35 FB -23 Wing (attached off-tackle) – 14 WR – 6 RB – 3 It’s a huge loss for an offense that prides itself on multiplicity. Brayden Willis played 10 snaps and ran three routes for Juszczyk. Willis missed one of his 7 run-blocking snaps. And now he’ll go against the best defense in the league. We’ll see whether he is the fullback or they ask more of Luke Farrell. Kyle’s update, 11:47 a.m. PT: Ian Rapoport shared that Juszczyk has a bone bruise that will keep him out for 2-3 weeks. Juszczyk is also dealing with a knee sprain.

It’ll also be the first time the 49ers are underdogs in a game since Week 1. San Francisco is a 3-point underdog in Week 4 on FanDuel […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images We move into Week 4, where the San Francisco 49ers will face their rival Seattle Seahawks. It’s the first time the Niners will hit the highway in three games. It’ll also be the first time the 49ers are underdogs in a game since Week 1. San Francisco is a 3-point underdog in Week 4 on FanDuel Sportsbook, with the total set at 47.5. That’s a relatively high total, considering how the 49ers offense fared in the final two matchups against Seattle last season. But there are some differences. George Kittle didn’t play in the Divisional round. Trent Williams didn’t suit up in the final regular-season game. Mike Evans wasn’t on the team. Faithful, take 49ers game day wherever you go! Stay connected to the action and share every reaction with fellow 49ers fans on the SB Nation app. Join the live game-day chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Over four weeks last year, the 49ers offense was 22nd in EPA per play at -0.04, but fourth in success rate at 47.2. Through four games this season, the Niners lead the league in EPA per play at 0.25, with a league-leading 53.1% success rate. A dominant defense is difficult to sustain year over year. Look no further than the Houston Texans. Mike MacDonald has bucked that trend so far this season. Seattle was historically good at stopping the run last season. Their defense is still elite, ranking second in EPA per play and success rate. They’re tied for a league-high six interceptions and have allowed the second-fewest yards before contact. The final score for the 49ers over the Broncos was not indicative of how the game went. It was 3-3 late in the third quarter, and Brock Purdy had about 100 passing yards. On the flip side, the Seahawks won 30-23, but the score was 27-6 midway through the third quarter. The Chargers had nine possessions and had turned it over twice without scoring a touchdown up until that point. Brock Purdy isn’t Justin Herbert, and Kyle Shanahan isn’t Mike McDaniel. Familiarity will play a factor, but Shanahan joked last Super Bowl that you shouldn’t interview him about Seattle after his offenses failed to find the end zone. Will this time be any different? Let us know below in the comments.

title: 3 stars from the 49ers win over the Broncos: Siran Neal saves the day
summary: It wasn’t the most convincing of wins, but it was a win nonetheless, as the San Francisco 49ers withstood the Denver Broncos and the heat, moving to 4-0 on the season with a 24-14 victory. A slow first half for both sides ended with a blocked Eddy Pineiro field goal, which added to the slow […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images It wasn’t the most convincing of wins, but it was a win nonetheless, as the San Francisco 49ers withstood the Denver Broncos and the heat, moving to 4-0 on the season with a 24-14 victory. A slow first half for both sides ended with a blocked Eddy Pineiro field goal, which added to the slow start, but things woke up late in the third quarter to San Francisco’s advantage. And with such a close game, it only took a couple of big plays to swing the momentum the 49ers’ way. We use two of Sunday’s stars to acknowledge who made those game-changing plays: 3rd star: TE Georgie Kittle It wasn’t the big momentum swing, but it was the play that put things to rest for the 49ers. Kittle was held to a relatively quiet game up until the 2:25 mark in the fourth quarter. Until then, he was targeted five times for three receptions and 14 yards before the 49ers took a three-point lead late in the game. Facing a second-and-8 with a chance to run the clock down to the two-minute warning, the 49ers went to Kittle. A slow-developing screen gave the tight end oodles of space, and after making the first man miss, it was a footrace to the end zone. Kittle outpaced Talonoa Hufanga for a 56-yard score and gave the 49ers an insurmountable 10-point lead. The speed looked good for a player nine months removed from an Achilles injury. Kittle’s day was boosted by the big catch, finishing with 70 yards on four receptions and a touchdown. 2nd star: DB Siran Neal Kittle’s play might have sealed the win, but Neal’s special teams play first swung the momentum toward the 49ers. The third quarter started the way the first half did for the 49ers offense: slow. San Francisco opened the third quarter with two drives totaling six plays for four yards. That’s when Corliss Waitman was called onto the field for his fourth punt of the game and second of the third quarter with Marvin Mims back to return. Waitman launched a 61-yard punt with Neal gunning down towards Mims. Mims decided to take the return even with Neal closing in, and the decision was a poor one. Neal held Mims to just a one-yard return, but before Mims’ elbow could hit the ground, the impact of his wrist hitting the ground jarred the ball loose, and Neal was able to recover. After a quick review, the call was confirmed, and the 49ers regained possession at the Denver 28-yard line. Nine plays later, the 49ers took the lead 10-3 with their first touchdown of the afternoon. The 49ers offense was floundering, but the field-position swing of Neal’s forced fumble changed things. Before Neal’s heroics, the offense had scored only three points through nearly three quarters. After the forced fumble, the 49ers scored 21 points in a little over a quarter. Neal’s takeaway completely flipped the game in San Francisco’s favor, and for that he earned Sunday’s No. 2 star. 1st star: WR Mike Evans Maybe his ribs are broken, maybe they aren’t, but you could tell that Evans was in pain on Sunday. And despite the pain, Evans still led all pass-catchers in receiving yards. In the gutsiest performance since Mac Jones in Los Angeles last season, Evans hauled down five passes for 76 yards, wincing and hobbling his way through Sunday. Evans was responsible for some of the biggest plays in the 49ers’ offense, with three receptions for 15 or more yards. He started his day with a big 18-yard gain to open the 49ers’ fourth drive. The catch-and-kick started what turned out to be the 49ers’ first scoring drive of the game, resulting in an Eddy Pineiro field goal. His next catch was his longest reception of the game. With 38 seconds left in the first half and the offense inside its own 20-yard line, Evans flipped the field with a 26-yard reception, getting the ball near midfield. This catch also led to a Pineiro field goal, but this kick was blocked, holding the drive without points. Evans’ last big play led to the game-winning score, after starting the 49ers’ first drive of the fourth quarter with a nine-yard grab to move the offense into plus territory. Several plays later, Evans almost got into the end zone, but a 17-yard reception moved the ball to the goal line, setting up a Christian McCaffrey touchdown to put the 49ers up 17-6. It’s not the most eye-popping line we’ve seen from Evans, but with the ribs obviously bothering him, it boosts the performance that much more. Throughout the season, we will track the three stars of the season by tallying points for each star award using a complex scoring system: three points for being the first star, two for the second, and one for the third. Through Week 4, the standings are: QB Brock Purdy – 7 points LB Fred Warner – 3 points WR Deebo Samuel – 3 points
author: Andrew Pasquini

title: NFC West Recap: 49ers remain in first place, Rams and Seahawks win
summary: 4-0. That’s all. The San Francisco 49ers are 4-0 and look like a 4-0 team. The Denver Broncos were the first big test for the 2026 offense, and they passed with flying colors. Yes, there were injured defensive backs with the Broncos, but the 49ers don’t have their starting wide receivers 100 percent healthy either. […]
full_text: (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images 4-0. That’s all. The San Francisco 49ers are 4-0 and look like a 4-0 team. The Denver Broncos were the first big test for the 2026 offense, and they passed with flying colors. Yes, there were injured defensive backs with the Broncos, but the 49ers don’t have their starting wide receivers 100 percent healthy either. The 49ers were nearly mistake-free, with a single penalty for five yards all game. Brock Purdy’s numbers were a bit more pedestrian with 19 for 30 and 218 yards, but his 107.4 passer rating has him now four games in without dropping below 100 for the metric. Oh, and another streak? Brock Purdy has yet to be sacked in 2026. Every game isn’t going to be pretty, but Purdy delivered where it mattered, especially that final touchdown to George Kittle. Unfortunately, the 49ers play in a competitive division, and two of the other three teams also notched wins. Arizona Cardinals (1-3) When the score had the Cardinals with a 14-3 lead over the New York Giants toward the end of the first quarter, I was going to repeat how the Cardinals were much better than their record was—and also that the Los Angeles Rams beating up a Giants squad without their starting quarterback wasn’t near as earth-shattering as some may want to believe. Then the Giants came back. At the end of the half, it was 19-17; the Giants and the Cardinals would be trading leads before the game ended. While Giants quarterback Jameis Winston did Jameis Winston things, like throwing two interceptions and taking four sacks, Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett threw three interceptions and only averaged 4.7 yards per completion. Ick. Arizona put up 123 yards of total rushing. And 166 yards of total receiving. I don’t mean to make this math class, but that’s under 300 yards of total offense. It’s very hard to win football games with that and three interceptions to boot. The sad part is, the Giants weren’t exactly efficient either, getting 337 yards of offense. Once they had a successful two-point conversion near the end of the third quarter, it was pretty much all over, even if up by two points. The good news? The Cardinals are no longer tied. They now have last place in the NFC West all to themselves. Seattle Seahawks (3-1) Well, this is a weird way to start a football game: First Chargers play: Interception First Seahawks play: Interception Wild scenes in Seattle! 🤯 Watch Chargers v Seahawks on Sky Sports and NFL Game Pass on DAZN 📺 pic.twitter.com/qx5DVZfWFl — NFL UK & Ireland (@NFLUKIRE) October 4, 2026 Sure, when the first plays from both offenses are interceptions, that’s a sign of the weirdness to come. The commentating team said it best: “Two plays, two picks.” And I say: “ Endless possibilities .“ Funny thing is, for the next three quarters this was all Seahawks. Then the fourth quarter rolled around, that’s when they let their foot off the gas. How did this happen? Well, the Seahawks getting 14 penalties for a franchise-record 150 yards through the game certainly doesn’t help. This batch of laundry includes a facemask call and some roughing-the-passer flags, allowing the Chargers to sustain drives and get back into the game in the fourth quarter. The Chargers also o utgained the Seahawks 138 yards to 11 in that same quarter. Yes, you read that right. 11 yards in the final quarter of the game for the Seahawks offense. With under a minute left, the Seahawks managed to sack Justin Herbert and force a fumble to end the game and get out of there. Had the Seahawks not played such a tremendous three quarters, that game could have been a disaster. Then again, that was a hell of a three-quarters. Regardless, that was not four quarters of football from the Seahawks. It was, however, a win that puts them to 3-1. Los Angeles Rams (2-2) This marks the first game the Rams played on a Sunday afternoon. Four weeks into the season, they play a game that isn’t on prime time. After this, I think I’ll take the prime time games since the Rams have only won one of those. And for a bit, they may have had no business winning this one. I mean when you have a catch like this, it’s just a bad sign for the visiting team: OH MY DARIUS COOPER 🤯 pic.twitter.com/adE7VVSDSo — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 4, 2026 I don’t care who you root for—that catch was awesome. So how did the Eagles blow this? Beyond the points, the Rams dominated in several areas, including time of possession, third-down conversions (the Eagles didn’t convert a single one), first downs, and more. The Eagles had two turnovers, but they also suffered from some bad playcalling. And when you have that on top of you not converting a third down, two touchdowns seems more like a gift. The first half had the Eagles up 20-10. The Rams were not going away, but the Eagles had their turnovers and their lead. Just no mistakes, no getting cute, and manage the game. Just manage the game. Make good play calls: The Rams stop the tush push‼️ 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/7siNXhy8D4 — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) October 4, 2026 That was not managing the game or making a good play call. Credit to the Rams for stopping a play that is rarely stopped. But no credit to the Eagles for running that. That looks like a looooong fourth and 1, to the point that it’s fourth and 2. Call me crazy, but that doesn’t seem like a good time to run that when you are on your own side of the field. Reminds me of another failed QB sneak I saw Sunday that probably should have been left on the playsheet. But even with that blunder, the game stayed 20-10. Until the four-minute mark of the fourth quarter. That’s when the Rams scored not one but two touchdowns to take the lead and the win. That’s right, with four minutes left in the game, the Rams scored 14 unanswered points. And their second touchdown came with nearly a minute remaining. So in reality, the Rams scored two touchdowns in three minutes. When you are up 10, and that happens? Is that the Rams or the Eagles? Who knows. Even with the differential in stats, I’m wondering how the Eagles managed to meltdown in five minutes. Onto Week 5 The Rams go back to prime time in Week 4. This time they host the Buffalo Bills. The Bills lost to the New England Patriots Sunday, so don’t expect them to be too happy with life a week later. Maybe the Bills can use the Rams to get right and hand them another prime-time loss. The 49ers have their second test of the season against the Seattle Seahawks and that Seahawks defense. They are in Seattle and much healthier than they were last time, in the NFC Divisional. The Seahawks defense has given Kyle Shanahan fits in the past, but if the 49ers offensive line can keep Brock Purdy upright when the Seahawks rush four, then there could be an opening. The Seahawks are favored by three points this time, which is practically the “home-field” points. If the 49ers manage to win here, they are 3-0 in the division, and you could not ask for a better start. Also, can we keep Brock Purdy at 0 sacks into Week 5? Please? The Cardinals host the Detroit Lions. The Lions are favored by five points, so that should tell you what to expect. Given the defenses, I expect this to be a pretty high-scoring one. The over/under is at 52.5 points—so the oddsmakers tend to agree with me. The Lions lost to the Panthers Sunday night so expect them at 2-2 to come out with their hair on fire. 1st: San Francisco 49ers Next at Seattle Seahawk s 2nd: Seattle Seahawks; Next: vs. San Francisco 49ers 3rd: Los Angeles Rams; Next: vs. Buffalo Bills (Monday Night Football) 4th: Arizona Cardinals; Next: vs. Detroit Lions

title: 49ers prove age is just a number with unique piece of NFL history
summary: In recent years, 49ers GM John Lynch has spoken regularly about San Francisco’s roster needing to get younger, and the front office has made plenty of moves with that goal in mind. But four weeks into the 2026 season it is the still plentiful old heads on the San Francisco offense that have powered the […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images In recent years, 49ers GM John Lynch has spoken regularly about San Francisco’s roster needing to get younger, and the front office has made plenty of moves with that goal in mind. But four weeks into the 2026 season it is the still plentiful old heads on the San Francisco offense that have powered the 49ers to a 4-0 start. The 49ers were made to work very hard for their 24-14 win over the Denver Broncos, with their experienced cast of skill-position players coming through when it mattered. Deebo Samuel caught his third touchdown of the season to give the 49ers a 10-3 lead in the third quarter, before a Christian McCaffrey goal-line plunge and a spectacular 56-yard catch-and-run from George Kittle on a screen clinched the victory for the 49ers. The scores by Samuel and Kittle sealed a unique piece of history for a 49er offense that, with the likes of De’Zhaun Stribling and Ricky Pearsall sidelined, is hugely reliant on ageing veterans. Indeed, per CBS Sports’ Doug Clawson , the 49ers have 11 receiving touchdowns scored by players aged 30 or over. That is the most through four games in NFL history. Kittle has accounted for four of them, with Mike Evans scoring two in addition to Samuel’s treble. Demarcus Robinson and Kyle Juszczyk each have one. Of course, in an ideal world the 49ers would love to have Stribling, who was injured in his NFL debut and is likely looking a late November return, and Pearsall (out for the season) making key contributions and developing into long-term assets. But this is still a team very much focused on the now and, for the time being, the 49ers’ veteran pass-catchers are a huge reason why they look like the best team in football through four weeks. You’re only as old as you feel, and the 49ers are feeling very good heading into their Week 5 matchup with the Seattle Seahawks.
author: Nicholas McGee

summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their initial injury report Monday ahead of Thursday night’s matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, and the biggest news involves star safety Antoine Winfield, Jr. Winfield did not participate due to a rib injury suffered late in Sunday’s 17-14 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Head coach Todd Bowles revealed Monday […]
full_text: Oct 4, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (31) cannot complete the interception against the Green Bay Packers during the game at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their initial injury report Monday ahead of Thursday night’s matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, and the biggest news involves star safety Antoine Winfield, Jr. Winfield did not participate due to a rib injury suffered late in Sunday’s 17-14 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Head coach Todd Bowles revealed Monday that Winfield suffered a slight rib fracture and is expected to miss two-to-four weeks, dealing another significant blow to an already banged-up Buccaneers roster. Winfield has recorded 24 tackles through Tampa Bay’s first four games and remains one of the most versatile and important pieces of Bowles’ defense. His absence will begin Thursday against Dallas and could potentially keep him sidelined for several additional games depending on his recovery. Quarterback Baker Mayfield also remained out with his dislocated right thumb, while cornerback Benjamin Morrison and linebacker SirVocea Dennis were non-participants. Rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter was limited with a knee injury, while first-round pick Rueben Bain Jr. was estimated as a full participant despite groin and shoulder injuries. For Dallas, cornerback Cobie Durant, linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and tackle Drew Shelton were listed as non-participants. Guard Tyler Smith, who has missed the first four games with a thumb injury, was limited as Dallas opened his practice window. Monday’s participation levels were estimations because Tampa Bay conducted a walkthrough. The full initial injury report for Monday is below. title: The Day After: Buccaneers vs Packers Week 4 Reactions
summary: The Buccaneers are 0-4. Hoo boy. I don’t think even the most pessimistic Bucs fan expected the season to be trending this way and right now there don’t seem to be many answers on offense or defense. Tampa Bay’s ship is taking on water at a rapid pace. When a team is struggling, social media […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - OCTOBER 04: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Head Coach Todd Bowles waits for the challenge call to be confirmed during the regular season game between the Green Bay Packers and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on October 04, 2026 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida.(Photo by Cliff Welch/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Buccaneers are 0-4. Hoo boy. I don’t think even the most pessimistic Bucs fan expected the season to be trending this way and right now there don’t seem to be many answers on offense or defense. Tampa Bay’s ship is taking on water at a rapid pace. When a team is struggling, social media can sometimes be a brutal place to be but it can also provide some more insight and context to what is actually happening. Bucs defense making it too easy for opposing offenses Tampa Bay’s defense did some good things on Sunday and even forced two turnovers in the fourth quarter to keep the team in the game, but they also had their shortcomings, specifically when facing first and long situations. In this game, the Bucs defense had: 1st and 20–> allowed a 4-yard gain next play 1st and 19 –> allowed a 16-yard gain next play 1st and 20 –> allowed a 13-yard gain next play 1st and 20 –> allowed a 19-yard gain next play — Evan Closky (@ECloskyWTSP) October 4, 2026 That is simply too easy for NFL offenses. When you have those situations, you need to take advantage of it and too often on Sunday the Bucs were allowing the Green Bay offense to overcome long yardage situations. Making it look easy has started to become a theme not just for the defense, but for the entire team so far this season. This pass rush… yikes Heading into this season, the Bucs pass rush was expected to be much improved. The team put a lot of resources into improving it with signing veterans Al Quadin Muhhamad and A’Shawn Robinson as well as drafting Rueben Bain Jr in the first round. There were clear expectations for this group with the likes of Yaya Diaby, Vita Vea and Calijiah Kancey already in place. The production, however has been lackluster to say the least. Pressure Allowed Vs. TB @PFF LT: Jordan Morgan: 3 LG: Laken Tomlinson: 0 C: Sean Rhyan: 1 RG: Travis Glover: 1 RT: Anthony Belton: 0 — Jacob Morley (@JacobMorley) October 5, 2026 Coming into Sunday the Packers offensive line was a huge issue and a really hinderance to their offensive production. Don’t worry though, they played the right team this week. Jordan Love gets the ball out quickly which doesn’t help, but to not have any semblance of pressure on Sunday is just not going to cut it. Tampa Bay’s offense has been ugly for a long time The Bucs offensive struggles this season have been well documented, but this is an issue stemming from last year as well. Watching this team operate an offense just feels like pulling teeth at this point. Most games for NFL teams scoring 20 points or less since Week 12 of last season: Bucs 9 (2-7) Jets 8 (0-8) Cardinals 7 (0-7) — Greg Auman (@gregauman) October 4, 2026 Tampa Bay is on that list with the Jets and the Cardinals who have been two of the worst teams in the NFL over the past year respectively. This is a serious issue, and the worrisome part is that there are no signs things are getting better. In fact, the Bucs points scored as an offense has decreased each week this season, scoring a season low 14 points against the Packers on Sunday. Something needs to change and change fast before things get even uglier for this football team.
author: Evan Wanish

title: Dan Quinn: Commanders plan to start Jayden Daniels vs. Giants
summary: The Washington Commanders flew home from London after their 30-13 loss to the Indianapolis Colts, without a bye week in its near future despite the international contest. It was a somber flight as the team fell to 1-3, in another game finished by a backup QB. This time is was 7th-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis filling […]
full_text: The Washington Commanders flew home from London after their 30-13 loss to the Indianapolis Colts , without a bye week in its near future despite the international contest. It was a somber flight as the team fell to 1-3, in another game finished by a backup QB. This time is was 7th-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis filling in for Marcus Mariota who suffered another MCL sprain in the first quarter. Quinn said the Commanders plan to give franchise quarterback a full week of practice and to have him start the Week 5 contest against the New York Giants, a formal return after suffering a dislocated left elbow during Week 2 at Dallas. Head coach Dan Quinn didn’t hold his day-after press conference until Monday evening (ET) due to the extraordinary travel, but still had some news to address in his meeting with the media. He touched on injuries to Marcus Mariota and Jaylin Lane and a lot more, as the Commanders move on from the latest loss and toward a Week 5 clash with the rival New York Giants. He also said that safety Nick Cross (illness/internal), guard Sam Cosmi (concussion) and running back Rachaad White (should) should at least retur to practice. Here’s everything Quinn had to say on Monday, plus some highlights to single out: Dan Quinn Injury updates Expected to practice this week: QB Jayden Daniels (elbow) S Nick Cross (internal injury) RG Sam Cosmi (concussion) RB Rachaad White (shoulder) Timetable unclear: QB Marcus Mariota (MCL) WR Terry McLaurin (hamstring) DE Charles Omenihu (groin) Eligible, but unsure of IR return:… — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) October 5, 2026 Jayden Daniels getting ready Dan Quinn on Jayden Daniels for Week 5: “The goal is for him to have a full week of practice and start on Sunday.” — JP Finlay (@JPFinlayNBCS) October 5, 2026 ‘Frustrated and pissed’ Dan Quinn: We’re frustrated and pissed. Ready to be back home and playing the NFC East leading Giants pic.twitter.com/AJ1m9c8CoN — JP Finlay (@JPFinlayNBCS) October 5, 2026 Marcus Mariota update Dan Quinn said they don’t have exact timetable for Marcus Mariota’s return. Said he’d work off to the side and they’ll continue to assess his progress. — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) October 5, 2026 Jaylin Lane done for the year #Commanders HC Dan Quinn confirmed WR Jaylin Lane will be out for the season with a fractured and dislocated ankle. He also confirmed QB Marcus Mariota suffered a sprained MCL, but didn't have a timetable for his return. — Tashan Reed (@tashanreed) October 5, 2026

title: Washington Commanders injury update: Jaylin Lane done for the season
summary: Commanders receiver and primary return man Jaylin Lane has suffered an ankle injury that will end his season, head coach Dan Quinn announced during his Monday press conference.   Lane suffered what Quinn considered a “serious” injury during Sunday’s loss to the Indianapolis Colts, where it was obvious that he would not return to the […]
full_text: Commanders receiver and primary return man Jaylin Lane has suffered an ankle injury that will end his season, head coach Dan Quinn announced during his Monday press conference. Lane suffered what Quinn considered a “serious” injury during Sunday’s loss to the Indianapolis Colts, where it was obvious that he would not return to the game or to football in any capacity in the near future. Lane dealt with a dislocation and a fracture of the ankle. The fourth-round NFL draft pick has been one of the best return men since entering the league, with two punt return touchdowns during his rookie season in 2025. He was a special team stallion but lightly used on the offensive end both in this season and the last one. Even still, his loss is a significant one that will hold weight over the campaign. It’s fair to expect that Luke McCaffrey will take over returning kicks and punts from now on through the end of the year. That also means that McCaffrey will be active when he has not in recent weeks, allowing for his inclusion in the offense.
