title: Washington Commanders Whiteboard: Notes and observations from Week 4
summary: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and […]
full_text: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and observations from the Washington Commanders’ 13-30 loss to the Indianapolis Colts in London. Personnel decisions are still a problem After interior offensive lineman Nick Allegretti struggled in the first two games, Sam Cosmi’s absence in Week 3 gave the Washington Commanders an opportunity to replace him at center and move the journeyman over to the guard position. Lucas Patrick played surprisingly well in his place, and in London it looked like the team would go with the same starting lineup. The team went a step further and benched Allegretti for sixth-round rookie Matt Gulbin . After playing all of four snaps the week prior, Gulbin lined up across All-Pro defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to start Sunday’s game. Predictably, things did not go well for the rookie and he was beaten badly on the play that resulted in Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota’s injury. After repeatedly emphasizing their faith in Allegretti this summer, four weeks into the season, he was benched. #Commanders GM Adam Peters says that the team is comfortable with Nick Allegretti & Matt Gulbin as “two good starting level centers” https://t.co/iUBQmzaYit — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) September 4, 2026 Gulbin beat cleanly on the sack pic.twitter.com/i0mEDXJoRt — Grant Paulsen (@GrantPaulsen) October 4, 2026 Unfortunately, Commanders general manager Adam Peters also chose not to sign a veteran quarterback following Jayden Daniels injury and the team gave backup Athan Kaliakmanis few repetitions in practice this week while getting Daniels work. The seventh-round selection performed admirably given the situation, but you have to wonder if the game would have gone differently with a veteran behind center. Following the game, Dan Quinn justified the decision by indicating Allegretti was banged up and would have been limited to start, despite being listed as a full participant in Friday’s practice. #ICYMI #Commanders HC Dan Quinn on the change at RG and if it’s a long term change. From the transcript: pic.twitter.com/A5NOZveEBg — CWallSports (@cwallse) October 5, 2026 The Commanders running game is on life support Running back Bill Croskey-Merritt received the bulk of the team’s carries on Sunday with nine attempts for fifteen yards and a 1.7-yard per carry average. Merritt has struggled so far this year and currently holds a 2.8-yard per carry average on the season, which ranks 82nd amongst all running backs in the league, according to SumerSports . In fact, Marcus Mariota’s 35-yard scramble produced more rushing yards than Croskey-Merritt’s, Craig Reynolds’ and Kaytron Allen’s 14 rushing attempts combined. If you remove the quarterback rushing completely, the Commanders had 18 rushes for just 49 yards on Sunday. Those kinds of results aren’t going to win many games. So who is at fault? Croskey-Merritt isn’t running with good vision so far and Ekeler and White both boast better yards per carry averages, coming in at 7.3 yards and 4.5 yards, respectively. However, their combined rushing attempts are half of Bill’s total, and they haven’t had a chance to experience the negative runs that happen running behind the current offensive line. Heading into the game, Washington’s running backs had been hit at or behind the line of scrimmage on 53% of their runs, which was the second highest rate in the league, according to Sharp Football Analysis . Things didn’t get much better in London, and the much-maligned fourth-and-1 call to Craig Reynolds was doomed to fail no matter which back was behind center, as Brandon Coleman missed a key block. Every Bill Croskey-Merritt Week 4 carry (don't ask why Casper the Ghost was standing in the way at the start) Poor blocking and poor vision on the few plays that had some space. He finished with 15 yards and is now averaging 2.8 yards per carry for the season #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/fDE91JBm8v — Full Command (@FullCommandShow) October 5, 2026 I dare y'all to say Craig Reynolds was the problem, or that Buckner blew this up. Coleman is one of their best run blockers, and he completely wet the bed. It left Bates vulnerable, this is supposed to be 3 true DBLs at the snap for a short yard. https://t.co/bxE1xlVGdT pic.twitter.com/Ih6U5Pus7C — Jamual (@LetMualTellit) October 5, 2026 Overall, the current offensive line isn’t a fit to effectively run a zone scheme, with guys like Chris Paul, Nick Allegretti, and Matt Gulbin playing the majority of the snaps on the interior. In Week 2 of preseason, the Whiteboard focused on the need to establish the starting offensive line so the unit could develop familiarity with one another. Since then, Allegretti took his first game snaps in Week 1, Cosmi went out in Week 2, the center and right guard were both changed in Week 3, and the right guard was replaced on Sunday. While talent is a big factor, zone blocking also requires scheme fit and cohesion, and this offensive line doesn’t have it. The defense is better but still isn’t preventing their opponents from scoring After allowing Seattle to score over 30 points last week, the Commanders defense once again gave up another 30 points to the Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts. The defense held strong through much of the first half but, after the failed fourth-down attempt in the second quarter, the Colts went on to score on their next drive and wouldn’t relinquish their lead for the remainder of the game. As the game wore on in the second half, the offense and special teams didn’t do them any favors, and Jonathan Taylor eventually wore the defense down for 95 rushing yards and two touchdowns. The Colts 5 possessions before Dan Quinn's 4th down attempt: Fumble, punt, punt, punt, interception. After the failed 4th down attempt: TD, FG. Indy never trailed again. pic.twitter.com/mpmK7jxnfV — JP Finlay (@JPFinlayNBCS) October 5, 2026 I see a lot of people mad at the defense for allowing 30 points, but context is NEEDED. This is how the Colts scored their TDs: •1st-Drive started on WSH46 after Washington went for it on 4th down. Defense had a stop on 3rd and 14, and refs called that awful Roughness call on… — Josh Taylor (@JoshTaylorFB) October 4, 2026 While the details matter, the inability of the defense to stop opposing offenses from scoring has been a persistent problem for the Commanders. According to FoxSports , Washington’s defense now ranks 25th in passing defense, 30th in red zone defense, and 31st in scoring defense after Sunday’s game. While the run defense, turnovers, and pressures are all improvements, those rankings call to mind last year’s defense under Joe Whitt Jr. The calls didn’t go the Commanders way… Like many, I rarely point to the officials as the reason for a team losing a game, but, for this one, they deserve a mention. While some of the calls were legitimate, others were decidedly questionable or not called against the Indianapolis Colts. Both definitely impacted the game at several key moments, and while the officiating may not have definitively changed the outcome, there is no questioning the disparity we saw in Sunday’s game. It’s been 9years since an NFL game had a 10-1 penalty disparity pic.twitter.com/Xh4NmsdURk — Chuck Sapienza (@chucksapienza) October 4, 2026

title: Commanders injury update: Marcus Mariota dealing with knee injury
summary: UPDATE: Mutliple reports have confirmed what Dan Quinn stated after Sunday’s loss to the Colts, that Marcus Mariota suffered an MCL injury to the same knee that got hurt during the preseason. He missed roughly a month with the last ailment, and it’s fair to expect he’ll miss the same amount of time this time […]
full_text: UPDATE: Mutliple reports have confirmed what Dan Quinn stated after Sunday’s loss to the Colts, that Marcus Mariota suffered an MCL injury to the same knee that got hurt during the preseason. He missed roughly a month with the last ailment, and it’s fair to expect he’ll miss the same amount of time this time around. Commanders QB Marcus Mariota suffered an MCL sprain Sunday in London, per source. This is his second MCL sprain, the first coming in the preseason. pic.twitter.com/GHYVOTApqP — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) October 5, 2026 Here’s the play where Mariota got hurt: #Commanders rookie RG Matt Gulbin gets manhandled here on the play that Marcus Mariota got injured on pic.twitter.com/hOEiNE3lcX — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) October 5, 2026 As previously mentioned, it’s expected that top Commanders QB Jayden Daniels will start and play in a Week 5 contest against the Giants after suffering a left elbow dislocation in Week 2. Jayden Daniels was formally ruled out of Sunday’s game against the Indianapolis Colts, yet they felt good about their quarterback situation. That was due to veteran backup, Marcus Mariota, a proven commodity capable of winning games at this level. We saw proof of that last week, when he was darn near perfect in a Week 3 victory over the Seahawks. He validated that point over the first few drives, until he went down awkwardly during a quarterback sack. Here’s the play that Marcus Mariota got hurt on. He’s now headed to the locker room. pic.twitter.com/DszMaJu5mq — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) October 4, 2026 Mariota went into the blue medical tent and then into the locker room and did not return to the game. Rookie Athan Kaliakmanis entered the game and ended up playing out what became a 30-13 loss to the Colts. After the game, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said that Mariota suffered an MCL injury, and would be evaluated, with additional imaging, once the team returned to the DMV. “I’m just gutted for him,” Quinn told on-site reporters in his postgame press conference . “…The team thinks it’s an MCL injury and he’ll have scans tomorrow (Monday) and we’ll have further knowledge with the length (of absence) and all those things.” Mariota missed a few weeks when he injured his MCL in the same knee during the preseason , so it’s probably fair to expect the veteran to miss some weeks (at least) in this case. Quinn said that Daniels expects to be a full participant in practice leading into a Week 5 contest against the New York Giants, creating the belief that he’ll be able to return for that contest. If Mariota will miss some weeks, as expected, the Commanders still have some depth issues at quarterback. Kaliakmanis was 15-for-33 passing for 186 yards , one touchdown and one interception despite taking few reps during the practice week. Does that influence whether the Commanders add another quarterback to the roster? Mariota’s prognosis will impact that, but it seems likely they’ll add someone should Mariota miss some time. The Commanders have Sam Hartman on the practice squad, and it will be interesting to see if they consider him a viable option. Should the Commanders sign another quarterback? title: Commanders vs. Colts (London) – Studs and Duds
summary: Washington took on Indianapolis over the pond and, although they hung tough early on, the injuries (playing their third-string quarterback), inconsistent play calling, poor coaching and having to play not only against the Colts but also the refs, ultimately doomed the Commanders in the end and resulted in a 30-13 loss. full_text: Washington took on Indianapolis over the pond and, although they hung tough early on, the injuries (playing their third-string quarterback), inconsistent play calling, poor coaching and having to play not only against the Colts but also the refs, ultimately doomed the Commanders in the end and resulted in a 30-13 loss. Washington is now 1-3 on the season with a division game against the Giants on the horizon. Dan Quinn’s seat continues to get even hotter and Adam Peters’ draft and free agency strategy have fans questioning their qualifications. Although there is a great chance both quarterback Jayden Daniels and receiver Terry McLaurin return next week, it’s going to take a miracle for Washington to make the postseason at this rate. Below are my Studs and Duds of the game, followed by some notes. Studs: CB Amik Robertson: Mik led the team in tackles (nine total, seven solo) and had a beautiful pass defended on a deep shot down the left sideline, allowing just two passes completed in coverage. He continues to be the bright spot on this defense. He recorded an interception on an errant pass by Jones and had a big hit to prevent a first down on a third-and-short. He had six tackles and a pass defensed. But it wasn’t just what was called. It’s also what wasn’t called, including two pretty blatant pass interference calls against the Colts defensive backs. The “crew” needs to be investigated by the NFL. This is who the @NFL sent to ref the game in London. Alan Eck (Williamsport, PA native) grew up an Eagles fan and despised Washington. summary: The Daily Slop – 5 October 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. full_text: The Daily Slop – 5 October 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles NFL.com Commanders QB Marcus Mariota suffers knee injury in loss to Colts Mariota suffered the knee injury on a third-down sack midway through the first quarter when Indy defensive end Laiatu Latu landed on the veteran QB’s right leg. Mariota went to the locker room and was replaced by Kaliakmanis, with Washington leading 6-0. This was Kaliakmanis’ first NFL regular-season game appearance. The 23-year-old is the first QB drafted out of Rutgers to attempt a pass in the NFL since the 2005 season (Mike McMahon). Kaliakmanis is also the first rookie QB from the 2026 draft to take a regular-season snap; he was the eighth QB taken at No. 223 overall. Commanders coach Dan Quinn said after the loss that Mariota is feared to have aggravated an MCL injury that sidelined him in 2022. The vet QB will undergo testing to confirm the nature of the injury. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Download the SB Nation app Commanders fans, take command of game day! Follow the action and share every cheer, question and instant reaction with fellow fans on the SB Nation app. Chat live during every game Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly move between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . JP Finlay Making sense of the London mess The Commanders went to England for a weird week and came back 1-3 But as bad as the refs were, they did not lose Washington the game. Washington lost the game, and a major portion of that belongs to Quinn. The decision in the first half to go for it on 4th down from about midfield, with a third-string rookie QB in the game and a defense that was dominating, was curious. It was an aggressive call at a time when discretion might have been the move. To go for it not just with Kaliakmanis under center but with practice squad call-up Craig Reynolds at running back made even less sense. Quinn did his best to explain the decision, yet, it still lacks clarity. Dan Quinn on the 4th down attempt to Craig Reynolds – we have to be able to get that. It was less than a yard. We can’t overthink it. pic.twitter.com/TUhTAdIP0c — JP Finlay (@JPFinlayNBCS) October 4, 2026 The failed 4th down attempt completely swung the momentum of the contest. Quinn’s decision in that spot gave the Colts life. For Commanders fans the offensive line moves provide whiplash. After the team cut Tyler Biadasz last winter and tried to sign Tyler Linderbaum with no success, that’s when the Allegretti hype train began from AP and DQ. They love Nick. Nick is the smartest guy in the room. Nick can get the job done. Well, to the Commanders brass, don’t pee on our leg and say that it’s raining. And by the way, Gulbin was quite bad against the Colts and got his lunch money taken by DeForest Buckner . It’s quite possible Sam Cosmi returns next week and the Allegretti/Gulbin conversation dwindles but that doesn’t mean the process was correct. Benching Allegretti made no sense against the backdrop of months of praise, and makes even less sense after watching the Colts defensive line hurt Mariota, abuse Kaliakmanis and shut down the Commanders run game. So to add it all up: bad refs, bad injuries, bad 4th down decision, bad personnel decision, and a loss to a Colts team that doesn’t seem very good. The result? An 8-hour flight home and a 1-3 record. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Too Deep Zone 3rd-string QB renders all other injury conversations a little asymmetrical Sunday’s Week 4 action began in London, where the Colts faced a Commanders team without Jayden Daniels and Terry McLaurin, among many others. Marcus Mariota got hurt early in the first quarter, entrusting the Commanders offense to seventh-round Rutgers rookie Athan Kaliakmanis, previously best known for sometimes looking halfway decent while tossing RPOs in the first quarter against Ohio State. Kaliakmanis, the Piscataway Popgun, spent the first half being treated like a blueberry scone by Laiatu Latu and other Colts defenders. In the third quarter, however, he completed bombs to Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown – with Sauce Gardner in coverage on both plays – to throw a scare into the listless-since-2016 Colts. The Colts were also banged up, most notably at wide receiver, where Alec Pierce, Keenan Allen and Darius Slayton were unavailable on Sunday. But a third-string quarterback renders all other injury conversations a little asymmetrical. Also, a team that’s relying on Keenan Allen and Darius Slayton to play significant roles in 2026 is just asking for trouble. Fortunately for the Colts, Jonathan Taylor can carry their offense against weaker opponents, Laquan Treadwell is having the best season of his decade-long career, and it’s only a matter of time before Marquez Valdes-Scantling, Dante Pettis, Denzel Mims and Jalen Reagor all find their way to Indianapolis. The Colts prevailed in a 30-13 victory against Kaliakmanis’ Upside-Down Golden Gophers (the Commanders rookie also played for the University of Minnesota) to achieve their preferred flavor of unsweetened tapioca .500 blandness. Mariota may be out a while, but Daniels will return next week To read more of this article, CLICK HERE A quick reader poll ESPN NFL Week 4: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday’s games Can the Commanders recover from all these injuries? As the saying goes, it’s getting late early for the Commanders. They were already playing minus their top four offensive players — tackle Laremy Tunsil, receiver Terry McLaurin, quarterback Jayden Daniels and guard Sam Cosmi — and then they lost backup QB Marcus Mariota. The good news for them? They’re hopeful Daniels can return in Week 5, but they need McLaurin ( hamstring ) and Cosmi (concussion) and their returns remain uncertain. And the worst part for Washington: After facing the Giants next Sunday, they play at San Francisco and then host the Eagles and Rams. Injuries plus that schedule equals trouble. What to make of the QB performance: Athan Kaliakmanis, who was filling in for Mariota, has a big arm and plays with poise, but he’s also inexperienced and playing behind a patchwork line. Bad combo. He completed 15 of 33 passes for 186 yards, with a touchdown and an interception. With Mariota injuring the same knee that sidelined him multiple weeks in training camp, the Commanders need to consider signing a veteran to back up Jayden Daniels. However, the line needs to provide more help or it won’t matter. — John Keim To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Film Room: Run Game Struggles vs Colts The Washington Commanders fell to perhaps their most disappointing defeat of the season so far. In London, the Commanders faced off against a very beatable Colts team and they started off well but things quickly fell apart as Marcus Mariota was injured on the second drive and seventh round rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis, the Commanders third string quarterback, was forced into the game. Kaliakmanis performed admirably in his first NFL action, but the team struggled to support him. The obvious thing to do with a young and inexperienced quarterback in the game is to run the ball and take the pressure off him. However, the Commanders run game struggled massively against the Colts defense. The Commanders ended the game with 100 yard rushing on 22 carries at 4.5 yards per carry according to the box score. However, that’s heavily influenced by Mariota’s read-option keeper for 35 yards and Kaliakmanis scrambling for a further 16 yards. If you take out the quarterbacks and just look at the running backs, the Commanders had 18 rushes for just 49 yards in this game, an average of 2.7 yards per carry. That’s not…

title: NFL Week 4's best arrivals, led by Saints DE Cam Jordan
summary: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
full_text:
Week 4 of the NFL season has arrived, and the calendar has officially flipped to October. But sweater weather hasn't quite followed everywhere. 

 Unseasonable heat out West could keep layers light for another week, while cooler temperatures settling in across the East are opening the door for more fall-ready fits. That means players have plenty of options as they make their Week 4 entrances. With three weeks of looks already in the books, personal styles are also starting to take shape around the league. Some players have leaned into statement pieces, while others have kept things clean and understated.

 From warm-weather looks to seasonal layers, Week 4 brings another round of game-day style as the calendar officially turns to fall.

 

 Monday night drip 
 New Orleans Saints defensive end Cameron Jordan opted for Saints colors in his look before "Monday Night Football." He rocked a gold and black checkered jacket and black pants on arrival. His quarterback, Tyler Shough , paid homage to the annual Bayou Classic held at Caesars Superdome with a clean shirt. Meanwhile, Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . wore an all-black fit with a gold chain necklace.

 

 

 Primetime fashion 
Ahead of the Detroit Lions and Carolina Panthers tilt on "Sunday Night Football," Aidan Hutchinson donned a fuzzy color-block sweater vest with black jeans and boots. And, of course, he had his signature gallon water jug in hand. 
 Sunday style 
 
The best design is in the details. Super Bowl champion Uchenna Nwosu and his celebrity stylist Ini Ikpe prioritize weekly custom game-day looks from Black and Brown designers.

 This week, Ikpe took us inside the Abasi x Jagne denim fit Nwosu is displaying this Sunday -- a partnership with Baba Jagne, a Senegalese Gambian designer based in Los Angeles who is known for silhouettes and patterns that make you look twice.

 "It's a cropped jacket and wide-leg trousers in dark indigo raw denim with copper contrast stitching. The jacket takes the classic trucker and rebuilds it," Ikpe said. "Its front panels snap on and off so they can be rearranged, which leaves an open U-shaped cutout down the front. Panels curve around the body, a buckled strap sits at the hem, and the sleeves sweep down from the shoulder. The trousers have a tan leather belt that dips and curves down the front, darted knees and a long, flared leg. Cognac leather JAGNE patches finish both pieces."

 Nwosu's favorite part is that nobody else has this look; he's the first to wear it and feels unapologetically authentic to his style.

 It's a small glimpse into just how much attention some of the best-dressed NFL players, like Nwosu, put into their game-day tunnel fit. -- Cameron Wolfe 

 
 Sunday's Best 
 Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai arrived in a custom matching jacket gifted to him by Brenda, a Bears fan and breast cancer patient at Advocate Health Care. 
 
 Thursday night's fashion 
Players and coaches aren't the only ones showing off their pregame style. Mascots get in on the tunnel fits, too. This week, Brownie the Elf was ready to rock for Cleveland's Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Game, channeling Prince in a purple jacket with a matching guitar.

title: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
summary: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces active players making their moves among the greats.
full_text:
Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns . 
 
 This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams  after a blockbuster trade  in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season. 
 
 Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players --  Von Miller  (No. 9), Cameron Jordan  (No. 17), Calais Campbell  (No. 25), T.J. Watt  (No. 26), Danielle Hunter  (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack  (T-29th) -- in the top 30.  
 
 Joining the top 30 soon could be  Aaron Donald ,  who unretired  to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th.  
 
 As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach career top-five territory. 
 
 
 
 Miller, who signed with the  Dallas Cowboys  in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him.   
 
 But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks heading into the season was 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982. 
 
 If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the career list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White's.  
 
As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape 
 We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season. 
 

 

 Week 4 update 

 Watt kicked off things in Week 4 on "Thursday Night Football" in an impactful way. He had one sack, one forced fumble and a fumble recovery to move his total to 4.5 sacks on the season. Other than that, there wasn't much activity with Garrett continuing to be on IR. 

 Week 3 update 

 There wasn't much movement on the list this week with only Mack (1) and Hunter (.5) recording sacks. Watt, Campbell, Hunter and Mack (in that order) now make up 25 to 28 on the all-time list. Along with Campbell, the three top active leaders -- Miller, Jordan and Garrett -- have yet to record a sack this season.  

 Week 2 update 

 The second week of the season saw little movement near the top of the career list, but Watt's hot start continues, with the defensive end recording 1.5 sacks to now put him at 3.5 through two weeks (No. 2 in the NFL this season) and break a tie with Campbell to move to 25th. 

 Hunter (27th) and Mack (29th) also recorded one sack apiece over the weekend to break ties and move up one spot on the list. 

 Donald (33rd) made his  season debut on "Monday Night Football" against the Giants after taking two years off. He finished with three tackles, one for a loss, but did not record a sack. 

 

 

 Week 1 update 

 Of all the active sack leaders, Watt was the only one to record a sack, finishing the game with two to move to a tie with Campbell for 25th. 

 And while Donald was held out of the Rams' Week 1 game, Garrett will be out for at least the next four after failing to record a tackle in Australia and landing on injured reserve after having to have arthroscopic surgery on his knee.

 After the Rams' opening loss, Garrett said this was " the worst version of myself that I've put out there."

 What follows is not the current draft order based on records. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

title: Atlanta's jabs at New Orleans after MNF top Week 4 trolls
summary: The calendar shifted to October, and the trolls are becoming a little more impactful, led by the Atlanta Falcons.
full_text:
Welcome to the first weekend of October, when the games get a little more meaningful and the trolls follow suit. Week 4 of the NFL season was further proof of that.

 

 The Atlanta Falcons dominated the New Orleans Saints 45-24 on "Monday Night Football," thanks to a standout performance from their backfield.

 Atlanta put up a whopping 420 yards, led by 145 rushing yards by Bijan Robinson , who also added two scores. His fellow running back Brian Robinson Jr . put up three touchdowns. The Falcons' five rushing touchdowns tied a franchise record. They are the sixth pair of teammates who each had multiple rushing touchdowns in a "Monday Night Football" game. The Falcons' lone passing touchdown occurred when quarterback Michael Penix Jr . connected with wide receiver Jahan Dotson for a 31-yard score. 

 With the Falcons-Saints rivalry being one of the fiercest in the league, it only made sense that Atlanta poked fun after the victory -- multiple times. The Falcons captioned their post: "Marched in," a nod to the Saints' anthem, "When the Saints Go Marching In."

 The Falcons then resurfaced a video in which a Saints fan motioned a choking sign at Falcons players as they entered halftime with a lead, indicating that Atlanta would eventually lose. The original video had the caption: "This Saints fan potentially could have an all-time clip for the second half," to which the Falcons quipped postgame with: "He did not." 

  

 Here are the other top trolls from Week 4.

 

 Dallas Cowboys 34, Houston Texans 30 
 The Dallas Cowboys defeated the Houston Texans  on the road. Facing a four-point deficit with 2:23 left, Dallas went on an 11-play, 74-yard drive that concluded with a 12-yard touchdown catch by wide receiver CeeDee Lamb .

 It put the Cowboys up for good and capped a stellar performance from Lamb. He had a whopping 17 catches -- second most in franchise history -- for 189 yards. It's the most receptions by any player since Keenan Allen had 18 in Week 3 of the 2023 season, according to ESPN Research.

 Dallas had clever jabs lined up for the in-state matchup. The Cowboys referenced country star Ella Langley's hit track, "Choosin' Texas," in a social media post, adding "Dallas" ahead of "Texas."

 Then, Dallas put a spin on the opening sequence from the sitcom "King of the Hill," which is set in Texas. The illustration featured Lamb, Dak Prescott , wide receiver George Pickens and safety Caleb Downs hanging out together with "Kings of the State" written above them.

 

 
 Carolina Panthers 32, Detroit Lions 26 
 It required one final stop, but the Panthers survived for a "Sunday Night Football" win against the Lions.

 Carolina held a six-point lead when Detroit regained possession with 2:06 left. Four plays later, the Lions turned it over on downs, clinching the Panthers' victory. Panthers quarterback Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns -- both to wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan , who had 14 catches for 192 yards. Their teammate, running back Chuba Hubbard , had 122 yards on the ground and two scores.

 Carolina understood the assignment postgame when poking fun at Detroit. It shared an image of a Panther standing on a ledge and growling over a lion, writing in the caption: "The Lion's king."

 

 

 Seattle Seahawks 30, Los Angeles Chargers 23 
 Seattle held on to beat Los Angeles in a bounce-back victory.

 The Chargers had a chance to tie the score with 1:42 remaining, but the Seahawks sacked quarterback Justin Herbert to force a fumble, which they recovered to secure the win. Seattle forced four turnovers -- three came from Herbert and two led to touchdowns.

 The Seahawks had multiple lightning- and charging-related trolls after the win.

 Their first post was simple with the caption: "Lights Out," a reference to the nickname of Chargers legend Shawne Merriman. Seattle's victory comic included a robot out of charge. Seahawks defensive end Leonard Williams  was labeled "The Lightning Thief," the title of a popular Rick Riordan novel. Then there was an image of a charging cord with tattered wires, captioned "0% battery," and another of a charging error with safety Nick Emmanwori sacking Herbert in the background. 

 

 

 Los Angeles Rams 24, Philadelphia Eagles 20 
 Los Angeles stormed back late to beat Philadelphia on the road.

 The Rams outscored the Eagles 14-0 in the second half. The winning touchdown came on a 7-yard run by Kyren Williams  with 1:10 left. The Eagles then had a turnover on downs, giving the Rams the ball and the win.

 Even though the result was still up in the air, Los Angeles soft launched its troll with a post earlier in the day. The Rams shared an image of their players with "Rams in Philadelphia" written above them in a font evoking the hit comedy "Abbott Elementary," which is set in Philadelphia.

 Just over five hours later, Los Angeles posted a test paper with scantron bubbles filled in to spell out "W."

 

 
 San Francisco 49ers 24, Denver Broncos 14 
 The 49ers remain undefeated following a win against the Broncos.

 San Francisco's defense shined, allowing just one touchdown and 296 total yards to Denver. The 49ers' offense played its part, too, specifically the offensive line -- the team has yet to give up a sack this season. The Niners are the first team to allow zero sacks through four games since the 2005 Indianapolis Colts , according to ESPN Research.

 The Broncos' home stadium is Empower Field at Mile High, and even though the 49ers won at home, they highlighted the "mile high" component with a jab.

 

 
 Jacksonville Jaguars 22, Cincinnati Bengals 17 
 Jacksonville's wire-to-wire win over Cincinnati prompted a simple, yet effective, troll.

 Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence had 223 passing yards and one score, and Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow threw for 428 yards, one touchdown plus two interceptions. Cincinnati put up a whopping 437 yards of offense but had only two touchdowns to show for it.

 In a battle between Jaguars and Bengals, Jacksonville highlighted its win by writing "Jungle Cats" in its postgame caption.

 

 
 Cleveland Browns 27, Pittsburgh Steelers 24 
 The Browns have won three straight games for the first time since 2023 after defeating the Steelers on "Thursday Night Football."

 Pittsburgh tied the score with 1:42 remaining, but Cleveland responded by kicking a winning field goal with 10 ticks left. As a result, Deshaun Watson became the second Browns quarterback since 1970 to lead three straight winning drives in the fourth quarter or overtime, according to ESPN Research.

 At first glance, Cleveland's Minecraft-themed post after the win seemed something ordinary. But it was a reference to former Pittsburgh head coach Mike Tomlin revealing his Minecraft world  Wednesday. The Browns capitalized on the moment by building out an "L" in Minecraft blocks and writing: "Pittsburgh was defeated by the Dawg Pound."

title: How the sportsbooks adjust after high volume of early-season NFL injuries
summary: With several players out for an extended time (some for the entire season), sportsbooks have reacted quickly.
full_text:
Injuries play a key role in the (mis)fortunes of every team over the course of the NFL season. Nearly a quarter of the way through the 2026 campaign, the list of star players facing significant injuries is staggering, leaving bettors and bookmakers alike scrambling to adjust.

 Quarterbacks play the most important position in the game and are, naturally, perennial favorites for Most Valuable Player. Thus far, five quarterbacks who began the season as starters have sustained serious injuries: Jayden Daniels , Lamar Jackson , Baker Mayfield , Caleb Williams and Jaxson Dart (who is out for the season). 

 A sampling of names from other offensive skill positions include Saquon Barkley , Travis Etienne Jr ., A.J. Brown , Ja'Marr Chase , Justin Jefferson , DeVonta Smith and De'Von Achane (who is also out for the season ). There have been several big names to go down on the defensive side of the ball as well, though those generally have less impact for betting purposes.

 Individual games are usually a starting point for sportsbooks when adjusting for injuries. Every player has a value that plays into any given game's line, so when an injury occurs -- whether before a game or during it -- sportsbooks take into account how many points to the spread that player is worth. 

 

 For example, the Chicago Bears opened as 1.5-point home favorites in lookahead lines for their Week 3 matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles , but when Williams sustained his hamstring injury in Week 2 , the line ultimately moved to Bears +4.5, a five-point swing based essentially on one player.

 That said, sportsbooks can sometimes overrate a player's importance or underrate a team's resilience in those situations: The Bears are 2-0 straight up and against the spread with Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent under center.

 "One of the biggest lessons from this season has been that we've probably undervalued the backups," Caesars Sportsbook's head of football Joey Feazel told ESPN over email. "Time and time again, reserve quarterbacks and 'next men up' have stepped in and performed above expectations, and the book has found itself on the wrong side of more than a few of those results."

 Feazel says that a star player leaving a game injured means the sportsbook has to adjust its numbers "immediately." The Baltimore Ravens , for example, ended up not covering their pregame line of -11.5 after Jackson left injured against the Tennessee Titans , meaning a confident bettor could have gotten nice value on the Titans spread in the second half, when the Ravens offense scored zero points.

 Most of the major sportsbooks also now offer some form of injury insurance -- a more popular feature in recent seasons -- that refunds player props should a player leave hurt. However, it often only covers the first half unless bettors pay a premium to cover the whole game.

 Looking towards futures, a major injury will have an obvious effect on the given player's season statistical props, as well as their odds to win awards. 

 

 For players that have already been ruled out for the season, like Dart and Achane, their chances to hit their preseason yardage or touchdown props as well as win any awards are already zero. Unfortunately for bettors, those are generally not the type of wagers sportsbooks offer insurance policies on. 

 But then there are players like Williams, Jackson and Chase, who have not been ruled out for the year and will still have their season-long props affected. For yardage and touchdown props, it amounts to another case of bad luck, as players facing a multi-game absence will have a very hard time hitting their preseason numbers. 

 DraftKings sportsbook director Johnny Avello told ESPN that bookmakers clearly cannot account for injuries happening, but rather have to work under the assumption that a player is going to play the whole season and create his props accordingly. From there, all they can do is rework awards and team futures.

 "For us, adjustments galore on awards, adjustments on week-to-week propositions, adjustments on team futures when we know that a quarterback is going to be out an extended period of time. Even if he's out a couple of games and depending on who they're playing, that's probably going to hurt their chances a little," Avello said. "But as far as the season-beginning stuff that we put up, those things are closed and whatever the bettors bet at that point they get."

 Williams was one of the most popular picks for MVP, showing 12-1 odds coming into the season and shortening to +600 after a dazzling Week 1 performance. His preseason action made him a serious sportsbook liability, but he is now out to 50-1 as he remains sidelined. 

 On the flip side, the Bears' Super Bowl odds immediately fell from 21-1 to 30-1 upon Williams' injury, but they've shortened to 18-1 after consecutive strong showings without him.

 Jackson -- an MVP favorite -- and Chase -- an Offensive Player of the Year liability -- were both just injured in Week 4 and while their awards odds did take an immediate hit, it's probably too early to tell how the maladies might affect the bigger picture.

 "The traders only react to injuries once the timeline for the absence is confirmed, although small adjustments are made, it's 'let's see what the doctor says' first before making any significant changes," said Feazel.

title: 'Unacceptable': Ravens steaming after most penalty yards in 6 years
summary: The Ravens were flagged 13 times Sunday for 131 yards, which was their most in a game in six years.
full_text:
BALTIMORE -- After the Baltimore Ravens ' 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans , coach Jesse Minter didn't hide his frustration when asked about his team's increasing number of penalties. 
 
 "It's obviously unacceptable," Minter said, shaking his head. "At the end of the day, we have to get out of our own way." 
 
 The Ravens were flagged 13 times Sunday for 131 yards, which was their most in a game in six years and repeatedly kept Baltimore from pulling away from winless Tennessee.  
 
 In the first quarter, Nate Wiggins ' illegal contact penalty gave a first down to the Titans in the red zone on the opening drive, which resulted in a touchdown. 
 
 In the second quarter, Lamar Jackson 's 29-yard scramble was reduced to a 7-yard gain because of wide receiver Elijah Sarratt 's holding penalty. 
 
 In the third quarter, Baltimore cornerback Chidobe Awuzie 's 39-yard pass interference penalty was Tennessee's biggest play on a drive that ended with a field goal making it 24-10. 
 
 "It's very frustrating," offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley said. "And drives here, drives there got stopped by penalties or miscommunications. Those things can't happen. And I think those things kind of get overlooked because we're up two possessions, but those drives are very important." 
 
 Minter said two weeks ago that reducing penalties was a "major point of emphasis." But the problem has gotten worse. 
 
 The Ravens' 39 penalties are tied for the most by a Ravens team through four games since 2000. Baltimore's 329 penalty yards this season rank behind only the Green Bay Packers (344). 
 
 The Ravens' offense has accounted for 61% of the team's penalties with 24. Baltimore's 11 false starts are the second most in the NFL. 
 
 This shouldn't come as a major surprise. In early August, the Ravens were called for eight false starts in a two-hour training camp practice because quarterbacks were working on a different cadence. 
 
 Ravens left guard John Simpson said the issues with penalties are being addressed in practice. 
 
 "We've been doing as much as we can, just trying to bring it up on film and just talk about it," Simpson said. "For instance, our cadences, just reminding each other when we break the huddle what our cadence is and stuff like that so we're all on the same page." 
 
 
 The Ravens have chalked up some penalties to being either questionable or unfortunate. Last week, Wiggins was called for pass interference on Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb when it looked like Lamb was the one who interfered with Wiggins. 
 
 On Sunday, Baltimore safety Kyle Hamilton was flagged for unnecessary roughness when he sacked Titans quarterback Cam Ward after the play clock had run out. But the officials blew the whistle just before Hamilton hit Ward. 
 
 "That's just one of those plays. It is what it is," Minter said. "I do respect the fact that the league wants to protect the quarterbacks, so I want to start with that, because if that happened to our quarterback, I'd be sitting there saying the same thing." 
 
 This marked the 12th time since 2000 that the Ravens committed 13 or more penalties in a game. 
 
 "When you have penalties, you shoot yourself in the foot, and that lowers your chances," middle linebacker Roquan Smith said. "It takes all of us, not just one of us. It takes all of us, play in and play out, to play [with] clean technique and fundamentals. When we do that, things normally go in our favor. But obviously if we do not, we allow teams to stay around." 
 
 A high rate of penalties have produced mixed results for Baltimore. In the six seasons where the Ravens have totaled over 120 penalties, they didn't have a winning record three times (2005, 2015 and 2016) and they won the AFC North three times (2003, 2012 and 2024), including a Super Bowl title in 2012. 
 
 "If we can get out of our own way," Minter said, "I think there's a high ceiling for us."

title: NFL Week 4: CeeDee Lamb, Joe Burrow and more fuel best quotes
summary: From family reunions to postgame trash talk, here are some of the sharpest sound bites and one-liners from around the league in Week 4.
full_text:
Week 4 in the NFL wasn't short on entertainment.

 Before "Monday Night Football" between the Atlanta Falcons and New Orleans Saints , the week featured 10 games decided by one score. 

 The close finishes provided plenty of fuel for trash talk and sharp sound bites as some of the game's best moments come from what's said before or after the whistle.

 Players and coaches carried their teams' momentum from the field to the podium, delivering standout lines in their postgame sessions.

 From bold statements to perfectly timed one-liners, here are the best quotes from around the NFL in Week 4.

 

 

 "My grandma came out here, which was really good to see." 

 Dallas Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb 

 Delivering a dominant performance in his adopted hometown, Lamb guided the Cowboys to a dramatic triumph Sunday afternoon.

 The wideout had a career-high 17 receptions for 189 yards, capped by a go-ahead 12-yard touchdown grab with under a minute remaining to seal a 34-30 decision over the winless Texans.

 Originally from Louisiana, Lamb relocated to the Houston region following Hurricane Katrina in 2005. A large contingent of family members, including his grandmother, traveled to watch Lamb on Sunday.

 

 

 "Obviously, we had our opportunities in the last two weeks, but this isn't Armageddon or anything." 

 Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow 

 Addressing his team's consecutive defeats following a 2-0 opening stretch, Burrow openly acknowledged his frustration while maintaining perspective on Cincinnati's outlook.

 "You can't ride the roller coaster week-to-week," Burrow added. "You're going to win some; you're going to lose some. Obviously, you want to win every single one [and] you're going to fight like hell to make it happen, but we're not going to ride that roller coaster."

 

 

 "We're not going to get into any bulletin board material. ... An elevated guy made a hell of a catch -- probably won't hear from him again. ... A practice squad player made a hell of a play." 
 Buffalo Bills CB C.J. Gardner-Johnson 

 Wide receiver Efton Chism III hauled in a sensational one-handed touchdown reception Sunday, sealing the Patriots' 29-26 comeback victory over the Bills. The play marked just the seventh career reception for Chism, an undrafted free agent in 2025 who, Gardner-Johnson's quip notwithstanding, has spent his entire tenure on the active roster rather than the practice squad. After signing with New England as an undrafted rookie in 2025, Chism secured a place on the 53-man roster out of training camp. Across 11 regular-season appearances in his young career, the receiver has remained on the main squad without ever being relegated to practice team status.

 After the game, Gardner-Johnson downplayed the clutch moment . 

 

 

 "For a guy that has been on eight teams in four years, I mean, I guess he knows the drill." 
 New England Patriots  coach Mike Vrabel 

 Upon hearing Gardner-Johnson's remarks Monday during an interview with Boston radio station WEEI, Vrabel offered a sharp response to the well-traveled defensive back, who has played for five franchises over the past two seasons.

 

 

 

 "You see the 'bink bink'?" 

 Jacksonville Jaguars CB Jarrian Jones 

 Positioned across the field, Jones lacked a vantage point for fellow cornerback Travis Hunter 's takeaway and subsequent juke against Cincinnati Bengals wideout Tee Higgins on Sunday. After snagging the pass, Hunter jabbed left before selling a head feint, dropping Higgins onto the turf prior to a 30-yard return to Cincinnati's 36-yard line.

 Although a penalty on defensive lineman Arik Armstead erased the highlight from the official play-by-play, the electric moment generated genuine excitement in Jacksonville's locker room. 

 

 

 "It was a goofy game." 

 Tennessee Titans  coach Robert Saleh 

 Even with Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson sidelined throughout the second half due to an ankle issue, Tennessee could not recover from a 24-7 halftime deficit.

 The 24-18 defeat dropped the Titans to 0-4, marking their third consecutive loss decided by a single possession. Following the contest, Saleh addressed the team's inability to capitalize after holding the Ravens scoreless over the final two quarters.

title: Pat Surtain II out with an ankle injury: How will the Denver Broncos adjust?
summary: While Surtain was able to avoid a long-term, season-ending injury, the loss of him and Riley Moss puts the Broncos in a short-term bind.
full_text:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Before the season began, Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II penned a first-person offering in the Players' Tribune that closed with the phrase "Let me just tell you straight up: You're making a big mistake if you're trying to write off Denver."

 Less than a month later, Surtain's season, the Broncos' defensive plan and the team's overall fortunes have taken a hit -- though not as big of a hit as originally feared. Surtain, who left Sunday's loss to the  San Francisco 49ers just before halftime, could miss multiple games with a right ankle injury , according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler . But even though Surtain avoided a season-ending injury, even a missed series would impact the Broncos, who have an AFC West matchup Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers in SoFi Stadium followed by a short turnaround for a Thursday night affair against the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

 Surtain is a two-time first-team All Pro and was the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year in 2024. And his status as the game's best cornerback and one of the linchpins of the Broncos' defensive plan means the proverbial "next man up" will have one of the most difficult assignments in the NFL.

 

 "Of course, [on Monday] and throughout the week, really we'll stay away from any updates,'' Broncos coach Sean Payton said Monday. "Guys were all in getting work and rehabbing."

 Surtain's absence, no matter how long, would impact how the Broncos construct their pass rush and coverage plans along with their ability to match a cornerback on the league's best wide receivers as often as they do with him. With fellow outside cornerback Riley Moss also leaving Sunday's game with a rib injury shortly after Surtain went down, the Broncos' pass defense could look vastly different in the weeks ahead.

 "You'll go 16 weeks, and that might happen once every two years, but you have to be ready," coach Sean Payton said of the timing of the two CB injuries. "It affects if you can get into dime ... it may take you out of some packages."

 On a first-and-10 play from the 49ers' 42-yard line with 30 seconds left in the first half, 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy completed a 4-yard pass to Christian McCaffrey . But away from the play, Surtain pivoted in coverage and began to hop on his left foot, keeping his right foot off the ground. He was taken to the locker room and evaluated, then underwent additional tests Sunday night and Monday by the team's medical staff.

 Jahdae Barron  (2025 first-round pick) and  Kris Abrams-Draine  (2024 fifth-round pick) played outside corner for the remainder of Sunday's game. They held their own in most individual matchups with the 49ers' wide receivers in the 24-14 loss , but Purdy accumulated 129 of his 218 passing yards in the second half, along with both of his touchdown passes.

 After the game, teammates expressed confidence in Barron and Abrams-Draine. Said wide receiver Jaylen Waddle on Abrams-Draine: "KD can hold his own. He's elite, he's here for a reason. I'm excited for him to get a shot."

 "I thought they came in and did a real good job,'' Payton said. "It was good to see. I think it's a position we have depth at, and those guys both kind of got thrown into the fire and I thought they handled it well.''

 

 But the Broncos' ability to do some of their favorite things on defense -- like add defensive backs to their varied pass rush approach and use Surtain in solo matchups on the league's best receivers so they can be flexible with coverage plans elsewhere -- would be impacted by the All-Pro's absence.

 That's a "no-duh" assessment on the surface, but the Broncos had the most sacks in the league by defensive backs last season (7.5) and were one of only two teams to get at least 25 pass-rush snaps from three different defensive backs (safety Talanoa Hufanga , nickel cornerback  Ja'Quan McMillian  and safety Brandon Jones ). Hufanga showed his pass-rushing chops in Week 3, coming up with a key drive-stopping sack in a victory over the Rams. Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph has said that how often he sends five or more rushers at the quarterback can be dictated "by what we do with Pat and how we create the rush and coverage plan around that."

 According to ESPN tracking, the Broncos have played the fifth-most man-to-man snaps in the league over the first four games of the season (57.9%) and have three of the top 12 players in the league -- Surtain, Moss and Jones -- in man coverage snaps. While Joseph says the Broncos' zone-match concepts in coverage are often confused with man-to-man in some advanced metrics, the absence of Surtain, as well as Moss, will impact how they cover.

 "He's a big part of our defense," Abrams-Draine said of Surtain on Sunday. "... There's no question about that, we just have to find a way to play. We've put in the work, me and Jahdae, we have to be ready to do what we need to do."

title: With Edgerrin Cooper out, Evan Williams shines for Packers
summary: The Packers lost one of their two young defensive stars in Cooper (Achilles), but Williams delivered a big game.
full_text:
TAMPA, Fla. --  Evan Williams has had interceptions before. Four of them in his first 32 NFL regular-season games before Sunday to be exact. So while the Green Bay Packers safety would like the football he inadvertently discarded after interception No. 5 came early in Sunday's 17-14 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , it was the sack -- his first in the NFL -- on the final series that might have been more meaningful.

 Three times on the final three defensive plays of the game, coordinator Jonathan Gannon called blitzes. Three times, he sent Williams. On the first, Williams came unblocked and sacked rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels . The second forced a quick pass for a short completion. And on the third, Williams got home again and had Daniels in his grasp when the quarterback flung the ball away.

 Game over.

 

 Not only did the Packers (2-2) come away with a much-needed win, but they might also have found a way to make up for the loss of linebacker Edgerrin Cooper , who left the game in the second half with a likely season-ending Achilles injury .

 Yes, the Packers have leaders such as linebacker  Zaire Franklin and safety  Xavier McKinney . And eventually they will get star edge rusher  Micah Parsons back. But Cooper and Williams were the young stars on this defense, both members of the 2024 draft class, and now one of them is likely out of the picture.

 Gannon might not rush Williams as much from the safety spot as he did with Cooper as a linebacker, but for Gannon to give Williams that responsibility -- and for Williams to deliver -- could be a sign of what's to come without Cooper.

 "Shoutout to that guy just because he always preaches players not plays in the biggest situations," Williams said of Gannon. "For him to call my number in that type of situation, it means a lot to me. To understand the coach has that type of trust in you in the big situations, when you have to make a play, that you're the number he calls, that means everything. Moving forward, yeah, it means everything."

 

 It capped the kind of performance by Williams that the Packers are going to need. Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper took over for Cooper at linebacker Sunday, but Williams took over as playmaker. He already had that first-quarter interception, which wasn't granted until replay overturned the call of incomplete on the field, but Williams finished with seven tackles, the sack (which was one of two QB hits) and two pass breakups.

 "Hell of a game," McKinney said.

 Williams' two pressures on the final drive gave him six for the season after recording two in his first two seasons. Part of that is opportunity. But with opportunity comes responsibility.

 "He can be really f---ing good," McKinney said. "I think just the progression that I've seen him make from when he first came here to where he's at now, he's a mature player. He goes out there and he's versatile and can play different things, and I think you're just going to keep see him progressing. My job is to make sure that he keeps going towards where I know that he's capable of being as a player in this league. I love to see it, and it's good to see it, too."

 

 It didn't surprise tight end Tucker Kraft , who has gone up against Williams as much as anyone in practice.

 "Evan's shown up in critical moments this season -- deep PBUs, fitting the box," Kraft said. "So having a guy as dynamic as Evan on your team, it really alleviates a lot of issues because he brings that physicality and he's a ballhawk."

 As much as the Packers will need someone to make up for the loss of Cooper, Williams must be conscious of one thing: Don't try to do too much. And he knows it.

 "As soon as you start to do too much and feel like you've got to make plays or fill in for somebody that's gone, that's when there's holes in the defense and explosives start to show," he said. "So it's just about doing your job and trusting the man next to you, even though that's not going to be Coop. I've got trust in all the guys in this locker room. We put in a lot of time in training camp to get to this point right here. Regardless who it is, we're going to ride with him all the way."

 Williams said he had a feeling he might be in position to make some plays Sunday, especially the interception, which was his first of the season after he had one taken away by a penalty in Week 1.

 "The ball found me in practice a couple times," he said. "That's always a good sign coming into a game."

 Speaking of finding the ball, Williams would like the ball from the interception. He discarded it after the side judge initially ruled he caught the ball out of bounds.

 "I tossed the ball back to the ball boy," Williams said. "They didn't even review it. I think a challenge flag came out and then like 15 seconds after, they said it's an interception. After that, I was just focused on my celebration. Went to the end zone and started celebrating. And then about 3 seconds later, I'm thinking, 'What did I do with that ball?'"

title: 2026 NFL Power Rankings: How all 32 teams stack up for Week 5
summary: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 5? We made our 1-32 list and sized up each franchise's performance so far.
full_text:
After four weeks of the  2026 NFL season , there are only three undefeated teams left: the 49ers, Chiefs and Vikings. And last season's 14 playoff teams are off to a rocky start, with a combined record of 30-26 this season. That's the lowest winning percentage through four weeks by the previous season's playoff teams in the past 15 years, per ESPN Research.

 So why are those teams struggling -- and how are San Francisco, Kansas City and Minnesota still unbeaten? We're stacking all 32 teams entering Week 5. And in addition to our 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to reflect on the first month of the season. Which teams are meeting or exceeding expectations? Which teams are already in jeopardy of a failed season? 

 To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another, ranking them from No. 1 to 32. Here are a few highlights from this week's rankings:

 
 The Jaguars secured their second straight win over an AFC opponent Sunday to move into the top five of our rankings. That was despite 125 penalty yards in Cincinnati , which marked their most in a single game since Week 7 of 2019, per ESPN Research. And the Jaguars saw some positive play from third-year receiver  Brian Thomas Jr ., who scored on his first red zone target this season. 
 The Eagles are out of the top 10 after a shocking defeat to the Rams at home. According to ESPN Analytics, Philly had a 97.4% chance to win when it led by 10 with a third-and-goal at 8:17 in the fourth quarter. The loss marked their second straight game with no points in the second half. 
 The Browns climbed into the top 20 of our list after their third straight win -- a 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday night. Cleveland won three games as an underdog for the first time since 2021, per ESPN Research. And it is tied with Baltimore for No. 1 in the AFC North, though the Ravens could run into some trouble after QB  Lamar Jackson   injured his ankle  Sunday. 
 
 Let's get into the full list, starting with a different No. 1 team from last week.

 Previous rankings: Week 2 | Week 3  | Week 4 

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 1. San Francisco 49ers (4-0) 
 Week 4 result: Beat the Broncos 24-14 
 Week 4 ranking: 2 

 Four words to describe the first four weeks: Not surviving but thriving.

 

 The 49ers have again been hit by a slew of injuries. On the defensive line, star defensive end  Nick Bosa is out because of a calf issue . At receiver, they've lost Ricky Pearsall ( knee ) for the season and promising rookie De'Zhaun Stribling ( ankle ) for 10 weeks. And yet, the Niners are one of three undefeated teams. Quarterback Brock Purdy has emerged as an early MVP candidate, as the offense has done most of the heavy lifting. But Sunday's win showed the Niners can lean on their defense and special teams when they aren't lighting up the scoreboard. -- Nick Wagoner 

 
 

 

 2. Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) 
 Week 4 result: Beat the Raiders 30-27 
 Week 4 ranking: 3 

 Four words to describe the first four weeks:  In Walker we trust.

 

 Coach Andy Reid and offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy have no excuses to ever abandon the running game as long as running back Kenneth Walker III is healthy and on the field. Walker has completely transformed the Chiefs' offense, allowing quarterback Patrick Mahomes to make more deep completions. Walker leads the NFL with 537 rushing yards and the team with six total touchdowns. The Chiefs should continue to rely on Walker following the bye week after injuries to receivers  Tyquan Thornton (dislocated left ankle) and Rashee Rice (right hamstring).  -- Nate Taylor 

 
 

 3. Seattle Seahawks (3-1) 
 Week 4 result: Beat the Chargers 30-23 
 Week 4 ranking: 4 

 Four words to describe the first four weeks: Eventful -- not always positive.

 

 Quarterback Sam Darnold sustained a glute injury  on the season's fifth play and missed most of the first two games. No. 1 running back  Jadarian Price , Seattle's first-round pick, lost fumbles in consecutive weeks and is now on IR because of a chest injury . The Seahawks won in Week 4 despite a franchise-record 150 penalty yards. Throw in coach Mike Macdonald's interview mishap -- which resulted in an apology to Broncos coach Sean Payton -- and the reigning champions haven't traveled the smoothest road so far. But the first month was also defined by some stellar performances, such as  Drew Lock 's fill-in stint and Jaxon Smith-Njigba continuing to make his case as the league's best receiver. -- Brady Henderson 

 
 

 4. Buffalo Bills (3-1) 
 Week 4 result: Lost to the Patriots 29-26 
 Week 4 ranking: 1 

 Four words to describe the first four weeks: Might've established unsustainable expectations.

 

 The Bills opened the season with 77 points and 855 yards in two weeks. Quarterback Josh Allen looked unstoppable against Houston and Detroit , two teams with Super Bowl aspirations. Now the Texans and Lions are a combined 2-6, and the Bills are coming back down to earth. Coach Joe Brady's offense has been held to 25 points per game over the past two weeks and turned the ball over seven times. There's no question the Bills can compete in the AFC. But the steamrollers who looked poised to break NFL scoring records seem like an artifact of the season's first 10 days. -- Nick Suss 

 
 

 5. Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1) 
 Week 4 result: Beat the Bengals 22-17 
 Week 4 ranking: 10 

 Four words to describe the first four weeks: Defense is getting overlooked.

 

 Heading into this season, there was plenty of hype around Year 2 of the Liam Coen offense. But defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile has made a name for himself early in the season, which could lead to attention in next year's head-coaching cycle. The Jaguars rank among the top eight in the NFL in sacks, run defense, turnovers, red zone efficiency and third-down defense. The run defense is second in the NFL (74.3 yards per game), and Jacksonville has given up just nine first-half points. -- Michael DiRocco 

 

 
 

 6. Baltimore Ravens (3-1) 
 Week 4 result: Beat the Titans 24-18 
 Week 4 ranking: 5 

 Four words to describe the first four weeks: First place but hurting.

 

 The Ravens are meeting expectations with their best start in three seasons, which puts them in a first-place tie with the Browns atop the AFC North. But it has come at a cost. Quarterback Lamar Jackson is considered  day-to-day after injuring his ankle Sunday , and his offensive line isn't faring much better. Injuries have left Baltimore with its No. 4 option at center ( Olaivavega Ioane ) and its third-string right guard ( Emery Jones Jr .). "We're not going to make excuses," coach Jesse Minter said. "We're going to figure out the guys that we have and put them out there and give ourselves the best chance to be successful." -- Jamison Hensley 

 
 

 7. Los Angeles Rams (2-2) 
 Week 4 result: Beat the Eagles 24-20 
 Week 4 ranking: 7 

 Four words to describe the first four weeks: Not a superteam ... yet.

 

 The Rams came into the season with sky-high expectations after adding defensive end Myles Garrett , cornerback Trent McDuffie and defensive tackle Aaron Donald to a team that already had the reigning MVP in quarterback  Matthew Stafford . But Los Angeles needed an improbable comeback victory Sunday to avoid a 1-3 start. The Rams have been inconsistent and missed significant players because of injuries, including Garrett (three games), Donald (one game) and wide receiver Puka Nacua (two games). Los Angeles might not be playing like a Super Bowl contender right now, but it could be later in the season, especially once Garrett is back from knee surgery . -- Sarah Barshop

title: Why a Tyreek Hill-Chiefs reunion makes so much sense
summary: The Chiefs had been monitoring and receiving updates on Hill's rehab and training sessions even before the injuries to Tyquan Thornton and Rashee Rice.
full_text:
LAS VEGAS -- For weeks, Tyreek Hill has posted videos of himself during training sessions. Many of them have featured Hill on a South Florida beach displaying his speed, quickness and ability to change directions. Hill posted another clip Monday, this one with him on a bench working on his footwork and catching a football while wearing a helmet.

 "Smooth like butter," Hill said on his Instagram story.

 Hill, who hasn't played in an NFL game in more than a year, has demonstrated -- in video after video -- his eagerness to return to the league. Over the past few months, Hill has observed the encouraging responses from a particular group of players: his former teammates with the Kansas City Chiefs , the team with which he became a three-time All-Pro before being traded to the Miami Dolphins .

 

 "Keep going brotha!" quarterback Patrick Mahomes wrote on Hill's Instagram post in late July.

 Tight end Travis Kelce responded, too -- posting four cheetahs (in reference to Hill's nickname) and three fire emojis.

 Even as far back as February, defensive tackle  Chris Jones used his X account to send a message to Hill: "Cheetah it's time."

 Jones wasn't afraid to mention Hill's name again Sunday in the locker room after the team's comeback win over the Las Vegas Raiders , offering support for a reunion between Hill and the franchise. The Chiefs and Hill, who is a free agent, could restart their partnership later this week . During his recovery from a dislocated left knee and multiple torn ligaments, including the ACL, in Week 4 of 2025, Hill has remained fond of the Chiefs, according to multiple sources with knowledge of his situation. The sources say he knows the Chiefs are a logical team with which he can begin the third chapter of his career.

 The Chiefs are in need of a receiver, especially after Sunday's game. Tyquan Thornton is out indefinitely after suffering a dislocated left ankle. Rashee Rice  sustained a right hamstring injury and left the game in the first quarter. Thornton and Rice have been the Chiefs' best receivers through the first four games, combining for 24 receptions on 31 targets for 409 yards and three touchdowns. And Thornton had his best game before the injury, catching five passes for 111 yards and two touchdowns.

 "Hm," Hill wrote on his X account Sunday after the game.

 Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Monday that he planned to begin negotiating a deal for the 10-year veteran with multiple teams. The Chiefs have maintained contact with Hill and are among the options.

 "I would anticipate Tyreek potentially signing with a team over the next few days," Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

 Hill has watched each of the Chiefs' four victories this season. At times, he has been willing to publicly flirt with rejoining the Chiefs. He used his Snapchat account early in the offseason to show that he was back in Kansas City to visit family members and to continue his rehab. His profile photo showed him in a Chiefs uniform. In June, Hill made an appearance in Jefferson City, Missouri, autographing items for Chiefs fans.

 

 "KC I missed you," Hill wrote on his Snapchat account. "See you soon."

 Even before the injuries to Thornton and Rice, a team source said the Chiefs had been monitoring and receiving updates on Hill's rehab and training sessions. The team believes Hill is targeting a November return to the field. With an in-season signing, the Chiefs' deal with Hill could be a one-year contract with incentives. Entering Monday, the Chiefs had just over $3 million salary cap space.

 "Tyreek Hill would like to come back [to Kansas City]," Schefter said on Monday's episode of "Get Up." Schefter later added: "The players support Tyreek Hill coming back."

 Hill began his career in Kansas City, playing alongside Mahomes and Kelce for six seasons, and helped the Chiefs become one of the league's most potent offenses. Known for his speed and tracking the ball on deep passes, Hill was the perfect receiver for Mahomes' rare arm strength. He scored 62 total touchdowns during his time with the Chiefs, playing a major role in the team's comeback victory over the San Francisco 49ers in Super Bowl LIV, the franchise's first championship in 50 years.

 

 If the Chiefs and Hill agree to a deal, he will be reunited with coach Andy Reid and offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy, who joined the team in the offseason. The familiarity with Reid, Bieniemy and the Chiefs' offense -- including its terminology -- could help ease Hill's transition back onto the field. Without Thornton's production, the Chiefs could use Hill's route-running ability to help give Mahomes an answer to man-to-man coverage from opposing defenses, an issue the offense has struggled with in the past.

 Several analysts have argued that the Chiefs offer Hill the best chance -- considering playing time, a defined role within the offense and the opportunity to help a contender -- to reestablish himself in the league. A one-year deal would allow Hill to be a free agent again next year to potentially earn a more lucrative contract.

 In 2022, the Chiefs traded Hill to the Miami Dolphins for five draft picks. The Chiefs have not had a 1,000-yard wide receiver since.

 After signing a four-year, $120 million extension with the Dolphins, Hill was one of the league's most productive receivers in 2022 and 2023. He was able to record more than 1,700 yards in both seasons and scored 21 total touchdowns during that stretch. In February, the Dolphins released him -- a decision that cleared significant salary cap space -- as part of their rebuild under a new coach and general manager.

 Last September, Hill's estranged wife, Keeta Vaccaro, alleged eight incidents of domestic violence in filings related to the couple's divorce case, according to documents obtained by TMZ. Hill has denied the claims.

 Prior to his injury last season, Hill was still able to account for more than half of the Dolphins' air yards (53.5%). His three deep receptions -- of 20 air yards or more -- almost matched his total from 2024 (four), according to NFL Next Gen Stats.

 At age 32 and after the most significant injury in his career, Hill is confident he can still be an impactful player.

 "Bro 32 is not old," Hill wrote on his X account last week. "Still prime years."
