title: Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 5: Jaguars are the AFC's best, more
summary: Has Jacksonville climbed to the top of its conference? Get ready for Week 5 with takes on the Jaguars, Bengals, Rams, Bears, Texans, Eagles and Lions.
full_text:
Week 4  of the 2026 NFL season is in the books. It was flag week in the NFL! I love a flag week. Who doesn't love a flag week? Referees threw 293 flags in Week 4, the most in a single week this season and in any season since 2019. My favorite flag thrower is Nathan Jones, the field judge for Carl Cheffers' crew -- I know, I know, normie pick -- but he kills it every time.

 Every Tuesday of the NFL season , I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions; those come later. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

 
 Subscribe: 'ESPN's Leaguewide' 

 
 This week, I'll start with the crowning of a new top team in the AFC, discuss why another top AFC team needs to ignore their quarterback and wonder where all the play-action went in the Rams' offense.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Jaguars are the class of the AFC 
 Bengals don't need to pass more 
 Rams need to rediscover play-action 
 Johnson is Coach of the Year 
 Stroud is finally back 
 Eagles' offense is unrecoverable 
 Lions' defense has no quick fix 
 Four extra inklings 

 

 
 

 I think ... the Jaguars are the class of the AFC 
 Here are the current odds to represent the conference from DraftKings:

 

 The market has the Jaguars (3-1) in a weird spot right now. They don't like them enough to plant them atop the conference with the longstanding big three -- that's the Chiefs (4-0), Bills (3-1), and Ravens (3-1). But they think they're clearly better than the second tier of AFC contenders -- the Bengals (2-2), Patriots (2-2) and Broncos (2-2). They're not entirely sure what to do with the Jaguars.

 I know what to do. Stick 'em in the top tier.

 If I've said it once, I've said it a thousand times: Look at what the Jaguars have been since their Week 9 bye last season. They're 12-2 over 14 regular-season games, tied with the Seahawks for the best such record. Offensively, they are second in points per drive, and defensively they are third in points per drive.

 Fourteen games is a pretty big sample, but we can check for easy pitfalls just in case. The Jaguars are third in turnover margin over that time at plus-11 with only 14 giveaways in 14 games -- that feels suspicious. But we have a better metric for turnover impact than margin, and its turnover EPA -- it helps us put a weight on turnovers, as some interceptions (thrown in the red zone, for example) hurt more than others (thrown on third-and-long 40-plus yards downfield). The Jaguars are 16th in turnover EPA per game over this stretch of games -- bang on league average.

 What about strength of schedule? Have they been treading over cupcakes? That was a legitimate concern throughout the 2025 season -- they played a stretch of bad offenses, including the Daniel Jones -less Colts twice, the  Cam Ward  Titans twice and the  Brady Cook  Jets. To start 2026, the defense had faced Deshaun Watson 's Browns, the  Bo Nix  Broncos -- a worryingly good game for Nix, if you're a Jaguars believer -- and a disastrous game from the  Drake Maye  Patriots.

 Then they played the Bengals and Joe Burrow on Sunday -- a stiffer test.

 It was a solid team 22-17 win across the board. The Jaguars had a 34.5% pressure rate against Burrow. The pass rush, which I had lamented as a potential Achilles' heel for a contender not two weeks ago, showed up in a huge way. Arik Armstead had more pressures in this one game (six) than the entire Jacksonville defensive tackle room had produced through the first two weeks of the season. Burrow threw two picks on the day, and both were the result of pressure in the pocket.

 Defensively, the Jaguars accounted for the absence of outside corner Montaric Brown (hamstring) with a full menu of Travis Hunter coverage snaps. He played 71 defensive snaps, not sitting out a single play . He had seven targets in 48 coverage snaps and surrendered only four catches for 30 yards -- most of them underneath completions in zone coverage. He had two pass breakups on the day and another interception wiped out by a roughing the passer penalty.

 

 On offense, the Jaguars had one of the most impressive days rushing of coach Liam Coen's tenure. Indeed, the Jaguars averaged 4.7 yards per carry (seventh-best game) with 2.4 of those yards coming before contact (second-best game). Second-year man Bhayshul Tuten had two big runs called back for penalties, and the Jaguars suffered a few stuffs at the hands of the Bengals' Dexter Lawrence II . But it was a balanced approach. Also, don't forget about Cam Little 's big leg -- he nailed two 50-plus-yard field goals. The Jaguars are a complete team.

 If you feel as if you've noticed a theme in the summary of Jacksonville's success against Cincinnati ... the Jaguars were swimming upstream against their own miscues. Jacksonville ate 125 yards worth of penalties in this game, its worst single-game number in the past six seasons. This scoreboard could have and should have been more lopsided with better discipline across the board.

 In the Coen tenure, the Jaguars have risen well against AFC contenders. They split with Cincinnati over the past two seasons and split the series with Houston last season in a weird loss to Davis Mills . They took Buffalo to the final bell in the postseason and beat Kansas City in the regular season at a final bell of their own.

 The only thing this team doesn't have is a recent, deep postseason run -- they haven't made the divisional round since 2022 -- to give them a sense of tenure and legitimacy. The Ravens and Lamar Jackson were in the divisional round in 2024 and the conference championship in 2023. The Bills were in the divisional round last year and the conference championship in 2024. I don't need to explain the Chiefs' experience. We've seen all of them there, so it's easier to imagine seeing them again.

 We've also seen those quarterbacks win MVP trophies. Five of the past eight, to be exact.

 Continued doubt in the Jaguars is borne only by suspicion in Trevor Lawrence , who didn't immediately reach his billing as the next generational quarterback when he was selected with the No. 1 pick in 2021. Because he was shaky to start his career (under Urban Meyer and on a dreadful roster, mind you), his blossoming now must be fraudulent.

 

 If Lawrence is less trustworthy than Jackson, Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes  as the difference-making passer on a top tier contending team because of his lack of MVP trophies and deep postseason experience, then there's nothing I can say now to change your mind. You have to wait to see what awards he wins this season and how deep his team goes.

 

 But if I can convince you that sometimes, gifted quarterbacks don't land with the right playcaller at first -- that sometimes, Matthew Stafford has to sit and toil in Detroit for seasons before he can find his Sean McVay, and Matt Ryan must do the same -- then perhaps we can reframe this moment for Lawrence. I wrote it Week 3 and still believe it in Week 4: The guy looks like an MVP. He doesn't play like a middling quarterback propped up by an elite playcaller -- nor does Coen coach him that way. Too much of this offense is built on his arm, his throw on the move, his pre-snap acumen. He is what we were promised. Not insufficient, just delayed.

 Don't buy the Jaguars yet if you don't want to. I understand your hesitancy. Just don't forget that you were offered a chance to buy in on the ground floor.

 

 

 I think ... the Bengals need to ignore Joe Burrow  about their pass-heavy approach 
 The Bengals threw the football on 81.7% of their offensive snaps against the Jaguars. Of course, they largely trailed in this game,…

title: Vikings make history at 4-0 -- without a scoring offense
summary: Minnesota sits atop the NFC North despite its special teams outscoring its offense the past three weeks.
full_text:
MINNEAPOLIS -- The Minnesota Vikings are 4-0, one of three teams in the NFL without a loss, and they've gone about it in a way the league hasn't seen for more than 100 years. 

 Sunday's 15-10 victory over the Miami Dolphins was the Vikings' second game this season without a touchdown. The other was a 9-3 victory in Week 2 at the Chicago Bears . 

 The last time an NFL team started its season 4-0 despite having multiple games without a touchdown was in 1923. The only other time it has ever happened was in 1922, in both cases by the Chicago Cardinals. 

 No team would realistically expect to be undefeated over such a stretch, but the explanation for the Vikings' success is clear. Their defense has limited opponents to an NFL-best 12.8 points per game this season, and over the past three weeks, their special teams have accounted for six times as many points (42) as their offense (seven). 

 That formula hardly seems sustainable, but under coach Kevin O'Connell, the Vikings have demonstrated a knack for stacking wins in unusual and sometimes unprecedented ways. 

 "We've got to own our role in our own aspect of not moving the football more consistently," O'Connell said, "and then go from there. But excited to get back to work at it. Excited to be 4-0 as a team."

 

 In 2022 the Vikings set an NFL record by going 11-0 in one-score games and became the first team ever to win 13 or more games despite having a negative point differential. They have now put together an NFL-best nine-game regular-season winning streak, dating back to Week 14 of the 2025 season, despite averaging 272.8 yards per game, fourth lowest in the NFL over that period. 

 This season's team has had a level of personnel shuffle that merits appropriate context. New quarterback Kyler Murray suffered a concussion on the 11th play of the season, and receiver Justin Jefferson sprained his left ankle seven plays into Murray's return in Week 3. In other words, they have played only 18 snaps together this season. 

 Sunday, they played almost half of the game without left tackle Christian Darrisaw (neck/concussion exam) and left guard Donovan Jackson (knee). In addition, the offense still appears to be adjusting to Murray, who took roughly half of the team's offensive snaps in spring practices and the first portion of training camp while competing for the job with J.J. McCarthy , who was traded  to the New York Giants  on Sept. 28. 

 Right tackle Brian O'Neill said last week that linemen wouldn't have "internal clocks" any longer because of the way Murray can extend plays out of the pocket. The Dolphins sacked Murray three times in the first half Sunday  (marking Miami's first three sacks of the season), and by halftime the crowd at U.S. Bank Stadium was booing the offense with vigor. All told, the Vikings committed five pre-snap penalties on offense, including two false starts, and O'Connell noted there "were some cadence things going on that we have to continue to figure out what the root of that is."

 

 Murray shouldered the blame for those mistakes, which both he and O'Connell called "unacceptable."

 Said Murray: "Obviously all 11 guys have got to be on the same page, but it starts with me. So we'll be better at that."

 An optimist could find reasons to be encouraged by Sunday's fourth quarter, during which Murray completed 12 of 13 passes for 113 yards. He found receiver Jordan Addison on a 27-yard deep crossing route and repeatedly fed tight end T.J. Hockenson , who tied his career high with 13 receptions. That helped the Vikings kill the final 5:41 of the clock while holding a one-score lead.

 To be fair to history, it should be noted that Hockenson smartly decided to slide at the 2-yard line instead of scoring a touchdown on the Vikings' final pass of the game. But O'Connell said: "I told our guys if we want to score, we should do it earlier."

 As they work through their offensive issues, it is reasonable to expect the rest of the team to continue producing at high levels. Their defense limited the Dolphins to one snap on their side of midfield in the first half, and emerging pass rusher Dallas Turner recorded two more sacks to raise his season total to 5.5. 

 

 Kicker Will Reichard , meanwhile, converted all five of his field goal attempts to raise his season total to 12-for-12. In a darkly humorous moment near the end of the game, the crowd at U.S. Bank Stadium gave him a standing ovation when the big screen showed video of him on the sideline. "A stone-cold killer," safety Harrison Smith called him. 

 The crowd let out its frustration frequently, even when O'Connell called kneel-downs from the 2-yard line rather than try to score to end the game. 

 "We want to score points too," Hockenson said, "and it is what it is. We love our fans here. We love playing in front of them. We're frustrated too sometimes, but we're getting it rolling and that is what it is. I understand it, and we're moving forward."

 Will it be any better in Week 5, when the Vikings go on the road Sunday to face the New Orleans Saints ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox )? It's not yet clear whether Jefferson will be ready, and the Vikings might also play without Darrisaw and/or Jackson. But with arguably the NFL's best defense, and a perfect kicker, who needs touchdowns anyway?

title: Bijan Robinson sparks Falcons' rout of division rival Saints
summary: The Falcons rolled over the Saints with Brian Robinson and Bijan Robinson combining for five rushing TDs.
full_text:
NEW ORLEANS -- It took Bijan Robinson exactly three plays to make a statement Monday night, and the Atlanta Falcons spent the rest of the game adding an exclamation mark in a 45-24 victory over the New Orleans Saints .

 Robinson opened the scoring with a 59-yard touchdown run as he continued his primetime excellence, finishing with 145 yards and two touchdowns on 19 carries.  Brian Robinson Jr . scored three touchdowns. The duo averaged 3.7 yards before contact and broke 11 tackles.

 It was a history-making performance as the Falcons became the first NFL team to win consecutive games on the road, in primetime and by 20-plus points.

 The Saints couldn't get much going on either side of the ball.

 Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

 

 

 

 Atlanta Falcons (2-2) 
 What to make of  Michael Penix Jr . 's performance:  Penix was efficient and managed a good game as the ground attack led the way. He was 15-of-20 passing for 223 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions. Atlanta was 4-of-8 on third downs, a major negative for Penix in the past. In just two games since returning from a torn left ACL, Penix has looked like he could develop into the quarterback the Falcons envisioned.

 

 Trend to watch: Bijan Robinson's dominance in primetime games continued. He rushed for more than 100 yards and two touchdowns before halftime. Robinson was the first player with at least 75 rushing yards and two touchdowns in a single quarter on "Monday Night Football" since DeAngelo Williams of the  Carolina Panthers  did it in 2008. Since the 1970 NFL/AFC merger, no player has more scrimmage yards per game in primetime than Robinson (145.5 in 12 games) with a minimum of five games, per ESPN Research.

 Stat to know:  The Falcons had multiple players score multiple rushing touchdowns in a single game for the first time since Oct. 21, 1973, according to ESPN Research. Dave Hampton and Eddie Ray did it against the Chargers back then.

 Surprising performance : Brian Robinson Jr. had three rushing touchdowns for the first time in his career. He became the first nonstarter to rush for three touchdowns in a single game since Gus Edwards for the Baltimore Ravens in 2023. He also became the first Falcons running back with three touchdowns in a game since Devonta Freeman in 2016.

 Next game:  vs.  Baltimore Ravens  (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET)

 
 

 

 New Orleans Saints (1-3) 
 The Saints came into the game with high emotions and optimism as they revisited the 20th anniversary of their return to the Caesars Superdome following Hurricane Katrina's devastation. They left searching for answers after losing to their bitter rival in a performance that included eight penalties, a missed field goal and yet another slow start on offense.

 The defense came into the game without starting linebacker Kaden Elliss and several players on the defensive line, and it showed. New Orleans gave up 207 yards on the ground and a number of explosive plays through the air.

 The Saints had a chance to make some noise in the NFC South with a win. Now they'll need to climb out of a 1-3 hole with an undefeated Minnesota Vikings team coming to New Orleans next week.

 What to make of  Tyler Shough 's performance:  Shough has been a bright spot this season, but he didn't have his best game against the Falcons, completing 30 of 48 passes with one touchdown and no interceptions. He was sacked twice and was under constant pressure, getting pressured on 35% percent of his snaps, according to ESPN Research. His only touchdown pass came with 1:13 left on a 3-yard pass to  Devaughn Vele .

 Stat to know:  The Saints' eight turnovers this season are tied for fourth most in the NFL and part of a larger problem of sloppy play that has contributed to a 1-3 start.

 Trend to watch:  Slow starts. They have been a problem since the start of the Kellen Moore regime last year. The Saints have scored six points in the first quarter this season, and their 35 total first-quarter points dating back to the start of last season ranks last in the NFL during that period.

 Next game: Minnesota Vikings  (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)
